abstract: Climate tipping points present significant long-term challenges, with critical thresholds at risk of being crossed within this century. Crossing these thresholds would lead to widespread self-perpetuating changes, from unprecedented sea-level rise to inhospitable weather extremes, for which humanity is inadequately prepared. title: From air quality forecasting to integrated and intelligent urban prediction systems
abstract: Air quality forecasting has evolved into a multi-component enterprise integrating chemical transport models, emissions, observations, data assimilation, and artificial intelligence. We argue that future progress will depend less on refinement of individual components than on integrating their interfaces across urban physics, atmospheric chemistry, machine learning, dense observation networks, human activity, and decision-making systems. We outline ten emerging directions that together constitute a transition towards integrated and intelligent urban prediction systems.

abstract: Anthropogenic nutrient pollution drives coastal eutrophication, but distinguishing physical transport from internal biogeochemical processing along the land-sea continuum challenges linear models. abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and edge computing has increased the demand for accurate and low-latency remote sensing image classification; however, conventional cloud-centric approaches face challenges related to processing latency, communication overhead, and efficient analysis of diverse land-cover scenes. abstract: In this paper, we propose a three-stream ocean radiative transfer module as an extension of the Nucleus for European Modelling of the Ocean (NEMO). This module solves in-water irradiance fields in 1D water columns, discriminating between two downward streams, direct and scattered, and a backscattered upward stream. The module solves 33 wavebands between 250 and 4000 nm, with a resolution of 25 nm in the visible range. abstract: Monitoring-data-driven reliability assessment of bridge infrastructure uses structural health monitoring, inspection, load testing, bridge weigh-in-motion, visual/non-destructive testing (NDT) data and digital twins to characterize evolving condition and failure risk. abstract: Abstract The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a significant vector-borne threat; however, few models successfully integrate rigorous theoretical guarantees with efficient, reliable predictive tools. title: Salt Marsh Mapping from Landsat Multispectral Data Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Salt marshes are crucial coastal ecosystems that support biodiversity and provide a range of ecosystem services, including nutrient retention, shoreline erosion protection, and carbon storage, through the processes they maintain. However, their dynamic nature, combined with human pressures, has led to their rapid decline, making ongoing monitoring essential. abstract: The East Antarctic Ice Sheet (EAIS) is often considered less vulnerable to climate change than the West Antarctic or Greenland ice sheets, but some regions of the EAIS have been losing mass over recent decades. abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. abstract: Biofertiliser formulations, comprising free-living and symbiotic bacteria, mycorrhizal and saprotrophic fungi, and associated microfauna (protozoa and bacterivorous nematodes), offer a viable alternative to synthetic fertilisers for restoring soil health, yet field efficacy remains inconsistent. abstract: Abstract Although significant N 2 fixation rates (NFRs) have been observed throughout mid‐Atlantic coastal waters, studies have been limited in their temporal coverage, and the methods used to detect nitrogen fixers (diazotrophs) and their findings have varied. abstract: The segmentation of spectral domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) images for diabetic macular edema (DME) using deep learning technology has key challenges such as data privacy, computational cost, and information uncertainty. abstract: Maritime unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly transforming ocean, coastal, port, and offshore operations through rapid sensing, intelligent communication, autonomous perception, and cooperative decision support. abstract: This study aims to determine university students’ levels of artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and to examine the patterns of variation of this competence across individual and educational variables. Conducted within the Turkish higher education context, where empirical evidence on AI literacy remains limited, this study addresses a gap in the regional literature by providing large-scale, multidimensional evidence on how AI literacy competencies are distributed among undergraduate students. abstract: Continuous underwater ecological observations generate massive volumes of visual data from heterogeneous systems. abstract: Changes at the land–sea interface reveal whether mangrove systems advance seaward, retreat landward, or undergo coastal squeeze as their seaward and landward boundaries converge. abstract: Monitoring marine turbocharger condition under real-ship operation is complicated by operating-condition variability and limited labelled maintenance data. abstract: In recent years, multimodal deep learning has made great progress, enabling artificial intelligence to learn across text, audio, images, video, and other data. abstract: Nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions from marine diesel engines remain a major environmental concern in the maritime industry, requiring effective monitoring strategies under actual operating conditions. This study proposes a Random Forest-based approach for detecting anomalous operating conditions associated with NOx emissions using operational data collected from an actual merchant vessel during an 11-day voyage. abstract: Reliable prediction of chloride convection-zone depth is important for service-life assessment of tidal-zone concrete, but most data-driven chloride studies focus on surface concentration or diffusion-related indicators. This study proposes a data-driven prediction and explainability framework for chloride convection-zone depth. abstract: Climate change has accelerated the deterioration of aging coastal bridges by increasing chloride exposure and environmental variability, creating significant challenges for long-term Structural Health Monitoring. abstract: Underwater polarization imaging (UPI) remains challenging due to the unique physical properties of underwater environments, where images typically suffer from severe degradations. abstract: Coastal cities face increasing climate risks as rising mean and extreme sea levels interact with dense exposure, critical infrastructure, land subsidence, and drainage limitations. abstract: The North Sea is among the largest and most productive shallow marine ecosystems, heavily influenced by historical and ongoing exploitation. Monitoring of North Sea biodiversity is vital for a better understanding of ecosystem responses to ongoing anthropogenic pressures and for informing effective management and conservation strategies. abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping hydrogeological modeling. The question is whether hybrid physics–AI approaches can reconcile the explanatory power of process-based models with the flexibility and speed of machine learning. abstract: Abstract Marine numerical forecasting is susceptible to complex spatiotemporal systematic errors, particularly during extreme weather events, such as typhoons, which majorly impede its efficacy in disaster prevention and mitigation. abstract: Abstract This work focuses on an educational project for third-year students in Italian classical high schools, integrating generative artificial intelligence (AI) into the study of Latin. title: From shoreline delineation to reservoir storage: benchmarking Sentinel-2 methods for fixed-basin bathymetry
abstract: Accurate shoreline delineation is critical for converting satellite imagery into reservoir bathymetry and storage products, yet its downstream consequences remain poorly quantified. abstract: Nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO2) are air pollutants primarily emitted from anthropogenic sources, however, bottom-up anthropogenic NO x emission inventories often suffer from update delays. The TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) provides near-real-time, high-resolution NO2 column densities, offering new opportunities for timely NO x emission prediction. title: A neuroevolution-driven agent-based model of coral larvae settlement
abstract: Coral reefs face significant threats due to climate change and human activities, which require innovative approaches to study and protect these ecosystems. Successful settlement is the bottleneck linking a reef's free-swimming larvae to the benthic community, ultimately determining the next generation of corals and the long-term resilience of the entire ecosystem. abstract: Visual impairment constitutes one of the primary barriers to social inclusion, affecting over 285 million individuals experiencing low vision or blindness, while assistive devices are frequently costly or lack accessibility. Consequently, the present study conducted a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the main objective of identifying the most efficient artificial intelligence models in the domain of text, color, and object recognition—specifically concerning items such as fruits, banknotes, and facial expressions. abstract: Based on satellite altimetry, GRACE space gravimetry and Argo-based steric data down to 2000 m, recent studies have shown that the North Atlantic sea level budget (i.e., altimetry-based sea level minus sum of components) of the past two decades is not closed, with strong regional residuals in the North Atlantic. title: Taxon‐specific community structure partitions marine particle size spectra into stable and dynamic components
abstract: Abstract Oceanic particle size distributions (PSDs) link plankton community structure to biogeochemical cycling. Although the influence of community composition on size spectra is well recognized in theoretical approaches, long‐term empirical evidence connecting taxon‐specific variability to bulk PSD structure remains limited. Despite public policy narratives highlighting grassroots sustainability and the inclusion of small enterprises, the underlying political-economic processes and structural barriers that dictate their execution remain insufficiently understood. title: Comparative analysis of the applicability of artificial intelligence models for code generation
abstract: This article analyses the potential for using selected artificial intelligence models in the code generation process during the development of a web application. The analysis was conducted in the Windsurf environment using the Open Data Explorer project as a case study. These models were compared in terms of functional effectiveness, implementation efficiency, the quality of the generated code, project stability, and the types of errors that occurred during subsequent iterations. title: PINN-Sed: Interconnected Physics-Informed Machine Learning Model for High Resolution Suspended Sediment Transport in River Network
abstract: Abstract There is growing demand for river-network models that can estimate sediment transport at fine temporal resolution. Although coupling physically based sediment modules with hydrological and hydrodynamic models is a logical path forward, these approaches require intensive calibration and substantial computing power, limiting their practical use. title: Interpretable multi-branch physics-informed neural networks for structural health assessment of reinforced concrete beams
abstract: The relationship between observable damage and residual shear performance remains unclear. This study proposes an interpretable multi-branch Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to predict the residual shear capacity of Reinforced Concrete (RC) beams using 583 experimental samples. The model uses a physics-guided multi-branch architecture to separate concrete, reinforcement, and crack-induced effects, improving both accuracy and interpretability. abstract: The connecting rod is a critical mechanical component that transmits reciprocating motion from the piston to rotational motion in the crankshaft. Although connecting rods are traditionally manufactured from aluminum alloys, titanium alloys, or alloy steels, the demand for higher power-to-weight ratios has motivated the exploration of alternative materials supported by advanced computational validation methods. title: Probabilistic corrosion prediction of marine steel under future climate change scenarios using physics-informed Gaussian process regression
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a framework of corrosion prediction by utilizing physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PI-GPR) and future climate change simulation. Long-term corrosion prediction of marine steel structures is routinely based on stationary environmental assumptions; however, future sea surface temperature (SST) changes should be taken into account as it may affect corrosion degradation over structural service life. title: Behavioral Patterns and Identity Expression in University Students’ Uniform-Wearing: A Quantitative Study
abstract: Despite growing scholarly interest in the sociocultural functions of student uniforms, empirical research on uniform-wearing Behavior in Southeast Asian higher education remains limited, particularly regarding the interplay between digital self-presentation and institutional dress norms. This study investigated the Behavior and motivations behind student uniform wearing at Kasetsart University, Kamphaeng Saen Campus. abstract: The early detection of production anomalies in petroleum wells is critical for optimizing operational efficiency, reducing downtime, and mitigating environmental risks, particularly in complex and prolific regions like the Niger Delta. This study investigates the application of both unsupervised and supervised artificial intelligence models for anomaly detection using historical well production data. abstract: Abstract This study investigates and enhances the Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm, a novel neural network training approach recently introduced by Geoffrey Hinton. abstract: This study investigates how university history lecturers in Vietnam, the Philippines, and Indonesia perceive and integrate technology into history instruction within diverse socio-cultural and institutional contexts. The study was conducted in response to persistent challenges in history education, including lecture-dominated instruction, students’ perception of history as a memorization-based subject, and the limited pedagogical use of digital tools in humanities education. College students are socially active and often live or study in congregate settings, which may place them at continued risk of upper respiratory tract infection (URTI). title: Ecological recovery, maintenance-dependent protection: a synthesis of three nature-based solutions for coastal resilience in New Jersey
abstract: Hurricane Sandy in 2012 led to an extensive deployment of coastal nature-based solutions (NbS) in New Jersey, providing a unique opportunity to evaluate their physical and ecological performance under multi-year monitoring programs. This study presents a comparative synthesis of documented outcomes across three NbS categories implemented in New Jersey, including beach nourishment and dune restoration on the Atlantic coast, thin-layer placement (TLP) of dredged material for estuarine salt marsh restoration, and living shorelines based on constructed oyster reef systems in Delaware Bay. title: How heterogeneous environmental regulations shape marine sustainable development: evidence from coastal China
abstract: Marine sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, making the design and selection of effective environmental regulatory instruments increasingly important under tightening marine ecological constraints. In this study, marine sustainable development is measured by marine green total factor productivity (MGTFP). abstract: Marine environments contain plastic debris that potentially elicits adverse effects in aquatic organisms. In Egypt, microplastic pollution has been recognized as a significant issue; however, risks associated with human consumption have not been fully elucidated. Here, we evaluated the frequency of occurrence, abundance, and distribution of microplastics (MPs) in edible marine invertebrates (mussel, shrimp, and crab) sold at markets along the Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts of Egypt. title: Eavesdropping on Whales: Hydrophones, Noise and Asymmetrical Listening in the Ocean
abstract: This article concerns the practice of using hydrophones to listen to sperm whales, a species that emits the loudest biological sounds on the planet, in an era of worsening oceanic noise pollution. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork with a whale tourism company in the Norwegian Arctic, the article describes how trained guides track sperm whales with hydrophones that work by amplifying their clicking sounds within a given range. title: Research on Copyright Governance and Security Challenges of Training Data for Generative Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Generative AI depends on training with very large volumes of data, and the acquisition and use of that data has become a focal point for copyright infringement and for privacy and security risks. This paper examines how generative AI training data is governed and what security problems it raises. title: Environmental Controls of Soil Inorganic and Organic Carbon Revealed Through Multivariate Analysis and Machine Learning in the Eastern Black Sea Region of Türkiye
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the controls of soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil inorganic carbon (SIC) in humid mountainous landscapes is challenging because of strong topo‐climatic and land‐use heterogeneity. abstract: Global climate models are essential tools to simulate past and potential future pathways of climate change, as well as associated climate impacts. Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) describe a range of future scenarios of global economic and demographic development. abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. title: Performance of Two Beginner-Accessible AI Image Classifiers for Marine-Debris Identification on Beaches of the Texas Gulf Coast
abstract: Marine debris poses persistent environmental and human-health risks, while recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the accessibility of image-classification tools. This study investigated the extent to which two beginner-accessible AI image classifiers, trained by a high school student, could distinguish between oceanic debris and natural marine objects on beaches along the Gulf of Mexico coast in southern Texas. abstract: Marine radioactive contamination can cross national boundaries, limiting the effectiveness of legal responses confined to a single jurisdiction. China has responded by progressively developing its legal framework through successive revisions to the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China and the consolidation of relevant rules in the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China (EEC). abstract: Accurate reconstruction of three-dimensional ocean current fields is critical for understanding ocean dynamics and real-time conduct of modern oceanographic field campaigns, particularly for mesoscale eddy surveys. We propose a physics-guided modeling and learning framework for multi-source data fusion to estimate the three-dimensional (3D) current structure of oceanic eddies by integrating satellite altimetry and temperature data, ocean reanalysis data, and in situ drifting buoy observations. In such systems, predictability is not uniform in time but instead depends on the trajectory of the system through its underlying phase space. abstract: Artificial intelligence has expanded its presence in education by offering resources capable of personalizing activities, supporting formative assessment, generating content, and fostering more interactive learning experiences. This study aims to analyze the potential of artificial intelligence within the educational context, the key ethical challenges associated with its use, and its contributions to active teaching and learning methodologies. title: Few Annotations, High Accuracy: Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation Improve Passive Acoustic Monitoring of the Vulnerable African Manatee
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring elusive and threatened species remains a major challenge in ecology and conservation, particularly in turbid aquatic environments. The African manatee ( Trichechus senegalensis ), listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN, remains difficult to survey using visual methods, limiting reliable assessments of its distribution and population status. abstract: The conservation of endangered anadromous fishes depends on understanding their full-lifecycle habitat requirements, yet the marine phase of Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ) remains a critical knowledge gap despite over 90% of its lifespan occurring at sea. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric aerosols play critical roles in climate and air quality. Accurately assessing their environmental impacts requires understanding aerosol abundance, distribution, and the key factors and processes that control them. abstract: Potentially Polluting Wrecks (PPWs) represent a critical global threat to marine ecosystems, requiring proactive risk management aligned with the Precautionary Approach of international environmental law. abstract: Abstract Lightning‐ignited wildfires (LIWs) are a major contributor to burned area in Northern California and have increased substantially in size over recent decades. Predicting LIWs remains challenging because ignition depends on both lightning occurrence and fuel‐meteorology interactions. We develop a two‐step convolutional neural network (CNN) framework to conjunctively predict (a) lightning occurrence from meteorological conditions and (b) wildfire ignition conditional on lightning using both meteorological and fuel‐related predictors. abstract: Earthquakes represent one of the most destructive natural hazards, causing severe social and economic losses, particularly in tectonically active regions. In this context, estimating the short-term probability of earthquake occurrence is of critical importance for disaster preparedness and risk mitigation. This study focuses on Istanbul province, located along the North Anatolian Fault Zone in the Marmara Region, which is considered one of the most seismically active areas in Türkiye. title: Digital economy, green innovation, and high-quality development of the marine economy: evidence from China’s coastal regions
abstract: This study examines the association between the digital economy and high-quality marine economic development using panel data for 11 coastal provincial-level regions in China from 2014 to 2023. title: Remotely sensed vegetation resilience in the four major estuarine ecosystems of eastern China
abstract: Introduction Estuarine wetlands are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth, but they have been experiencing severe degradation induced by human activities and climate change worldwide. Traditional assessments of degradation mostly rely on static indicators, which are insufficient to reflect dynamical ecosystem properties such as systemic resilience. abstract: ABSTRACT Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are promising for harvesting low‐frequency, stochastic ocean‐wave energy, yet their limited power output and inefficient energy utilization hinder practical marine applications. title: Advancing data integration in marine citizen science: insights from a collaborative workshop
abstract: The ocean remains critically under-observed, particularly in coastal zones where traditional monitoring is limited by cost, logistical constraints, and competing regulatory priorities. Marine citizen science offers an emerging and powerful complementary approach to addressing these gaps; however, data management challenges currently limit its full integration into scientific and policy data infrastructures. abstract: Sea level rise, combined with extreme coastal flooding, poses a significant threat to the socio-economic development of coastal areas. abstract: Particulate matter (PM2.5) concentration is a critical air quality indicator with severe health impacts. This study evaluates long short-term memory (LSTM) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) networks to identify the most accurate forecasting architecture. title: Deep learning driven smartphone system for fish disease diagnosis in Indian major carps
abstract: Abstract Fish disease poses a substantial threat to the productivity and sustainability of Indian major carps (IMCs) in aquaculture. Early and accurate fish disease detection is crucial to minimizing economic losses and ensuring fish health management. In this study, we developed a lightweight deep learning model, FishMoViT, for real-time detection of seven major IMCs diseases. This article presents the design and implementation of an intelligent surveillance system based on the YOLOv8nano architecture for real-time detection of sharp objects, specifically knives, in images and video streams. abstract: Abstract Changes in ice sheet mass manifest as changes in ice flow, ice thickness, and gravitational attraction. These parameters can be measured from space and used to track Greenland's contribution to sea level rise independently from each other. abstract: Abstract Many coastal regions around the world face increasing risks from both natural and anthropogenic drivers, including climate change, rising sea levels, and rapid, unauthorized urbanization. This study proposes an end-to-end edge-cloud hybrid artificial intelligence (AI) system that addresses these constraints jointly. abstract: This article examines the regulatory power of algorithms and businesses from an organizational perspective. abstract: Ecotourism is increasingly promoted as a conservation financing mechanism in developing coastal regions, yet empirical evidence linking visitor activity to ecosystem outcomes remains limited. This study examined the relationship between ecotourism visitation and land cover change across three Tanzanian coastal sites over 11 years (2012-2022). abstract: The obligate coral-symbiotic crab Trapezia septata is a key mutualist in Pocillopora coral holobionts, providing essential services such as predator defense and sediment removal. abstract: ABSTRACT The Indian white prawn ( Penaeus indicus ) is the dominant shrimp species in the northern Oman Sea and plays an important role in the economy of coastal communities in the region. abstract: Monitoring environmental challenges such as landfill expansion and marine debris accumulation requires high-resolution satellite imagery with enhanced spectral, spatial, and temporal details. abstract: Accurately monitoring lake water levels is critical for identifying potential hazards and developing sustainable water management strategies. title: Wheat yield prediction using machine learning, proximal sensing, nitrogen and climate data for Oklahoma
abstract: Purpose Accurate in-season yield prediction is a practical prerequisite for informed nitrogen (N) management decisions in winter wheat production, yet no rigorous framework has been established and tested against the tools producers currently rely on. Our study developed and evaluated machine learning (ML) models for pre-application wheat yield prediction to support in-season top-dress N management in Oklahoma. abstract: The operational reliability of marine chiller units is critical for maintaining the thermal stability of shipboard systems; however, the harsh and variable maritime environment frequently leads to complex mechanical failures. While Deep Belief Networks (DBNs) offer powerful diagnostic capabilities, their ‘black-box’ nature often hinders the trust of marine engineers in making critical maintenance decisions. abstract: Cocoa swollen shoot disease (CSSD) is a major threat to cocoa production in West Africa, and its early detection remains difficult because current molecular methods are often destructive, costly, and time-consuming. This study investigated whether chlorophyll fluorescence spectral indices could discriminate healthy (SA, n = 361), asymptomatic infected (AS, n = 284), and symptomatic infected (SY, n = 161) cocoa leaves. abstract: Abstract Tornado climatologies over the contiguous United States have traditionally relied on report‐based data sets, which are subject to biases related to population density, time of day, and evolving observational practices. This study presents an object‐based machine learning framework for constructing a tornado climatology using storm cluster data derived from a radar reanalysis data set within the Multi‐Radar Multi‐Sensor framework spanning 2005–2011. abstract: This article studies the causes of biofouling and methods to combat it. The problem under consideration is relevant to the development and operation of marine structures (ship hulls, underwater vehicles). abstract: Unintended pregnancy remains a major reproductive health challenge in Benin Republic, with adverse consequences for women’s health and socio-economic wellbeing. This study aimed to identify and profile women at elevated risk of unintended pregnancy in Benin using machine learning techniques to support equity-driven interventions. We analyzed data from the 2017–2018 Benin Demographic and Health Survey for women aged 15–49 whose most recent birth was live. abstract: Abstract Underwater soundscapes are critical indicators of marine ecosystem health, but traditional passive acoustic monitoring with hydrophones is spatially limited and logistically challenging for long-term observations. This study investigates the potential of distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) to overcome these limitations. A field trial was conducted using a bespoke fiber-optic cable deployed off the coast of Monaco, focusing on three sound-producing Mediterranean species: Ophidion rochei , Sciaena umbra , and Epinephelus marginatus , all known for their distinct acoustic signatures. title: Multi-source remote sensing approach for monitoring the Caspian Sea shoreline dynamics
abstract: This study presents a scalable methodology for the semi-automated extraction of the Caspian Sea shoreline and water surface based on medium-resolution satellite imagery and cloud computing within the Google Earth Engine environment. The input datasets included very high-resolution PlanetScope imagery, Harmonized Landsat–Sentinel products, and DAHITI satellite altimetry data. The proposed approach consists of three stages: generation of reference and working shoreline datasets, validation-based selection of the optimal extraction algorithm, and its subsequent scaling to the entire Caspian Sea.

abstract: Algal overgrowth on coral reefs threatens reef fish species richness worldwide, yet the variation in this pressure across gradients of coral cover remains unclear. abstract: Extreme climate events associated with climate change pose a growing threat to forestry production efficiency, yet systematic empirical evidence on their effects on ecological total factor productivity in forestry (forestry TFP) and the underlying transmission pathways remains limited. Effective management of these resources is vital to mitigating the risks of floods, droughts, and other hydrological hazards. abstract: Abstract This study developed a spatially explicit framework to estimate household water consumption (HWC) and the number of household water subscribers in each consumption class (NHWSCC) using land surface temperature (LST), land value, and elevation. abstract: The increasing occurrence of natural hazards, either individually or in combination, has intensified disaster risk worldwide, with the Chattogram Region of Bangladesh representing a prominent multi-hazard hotspot where earthquakes, landslides, and floods frequently coexist. title: AI-Enabled Cultural Heritage Preservation and a Browser-Based Virtual Museum: Design and Implementation of a Kenya Coastal Heritage Platform
abstract: Coastal Kenya holds a wide-ranging cultural heritage expressed in material artefacts, oral traditions, indigenous and local languages, historical knowledge, and everyday community practices. Yet these resources are increasingly strained by modernisation and global circulation, shifting modes of cultural transmission, and gaps in systematic documentation. This study reports the design and implementation of the Kenya Coastal Heritage Digital Platform produced under the Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for the Preservation and Promotion of Coastal Cultural Heritage in Kenya (LAIPCH-K) project.

abstract: Accurate estimation of crop aboveground biomass (AGB) and aboveground carbon (AGC) across growth stages is pivotal for evaluating agroecosystem carbon sequestration. abstract: Background Fast and accurate identification of tea pests and diseases with lightweight, efficient, and resource-friendly computation is a key challenge in smart tea gardens. abstract: Accurate prediction of the initial cracking time (ICT) of reinforced concrete (RC) bridges is critical for durability assessment and maintenance planning. Conventional ICT models, predominantly calibrated on laboratory data, often fail to capture the complex degradation of in-service bridges in subtropical coastal environments. Although Fe oxyhydroxides are recognized as major geochemical hosts of contaminants, their long-term mineralogical evolution and relationships with PTE partitioning in tropical fluvial–estuarine systems remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater‐based artificial leaves are fundamentally constrained by anodic surface poisoning and insufficient photovoltage for bias‐free reaction under complex electrolytes. From metric to model: a five-stage pipeline for building and sustaining valid AI predictive systems in consumer neuroscience
abstract: The application of machine learning to consumer neuroscience has made it possible, in principle, to predict consumer responses from media assets alone. However, the pursuit of model sophistication has outpaced attention to a foundational constraint: the quality of any predictive artificial intelligence (AI) system is bounded by the quality of the neurophysiological and biometric data used to train it, and by the rigor of the modeling procedures applied to those data. title: Viral diversity and ecological functions in the world’s largest deep-sea mineral exploration region
abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodule provinces host distinct benthic prokaryotic communities, yet viruses that regulate them remain largely unknown. Here, we established the viral genome dataset of the Clarion-Clipperton Fracture Zone, the world’s largest deep-sea mineral exploration region, to investigate viral diversity and ecological functions. title: Holocene-like summer climate during Marine Isotope Stage 11 in northwestern Greenland
abstract: Determining the climatic conditions under which the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) was smaller than present is important to quantify GrIS sensitivity to climate change. We use biomarkers in sediment collected beneath the GrIS at Camp Century, northwestern Greenland, to reconstruct summer temperature and atmospheric circulation 416 000 ± 38 000 years ago, at some point during Marine Isotope Stage 11 (MIS 11). abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming university life and the way educators and students engage with knowledge. Generative assistants, intelligent tutors, and adaptive systems offer opportunities to personalize learning, provide immediate feedback, and address diverse educational needs. However, their use also raises concerns regarding privacy, academic authorship, algorithmic bias, and technological dependency. abstract: The report examines the evolution of risks and threats within the security environment of the Black Sea region, in the context of the shifting geopolitical landscape and the transformation of international relations. It analyses the processes shaping security dynamics -ranging from traditional military risks to contemporary hybrid, cyber, and cognitive threats. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine protective coatings often fail prematurely under the coupled effects of mechanical damage, UV irradiation, microbial fouling, and corrosion, because conventional barrier‑type systems lack adaptive interfacial regulation and integrated protective functions. Herein, a GO‑HHU‑CuPN‑EP coating is fabricated via a room‑temperature aqueous supramolecular self‑assembly strategy. title: Covalent Organic Frameworks in Smart Food Packaging: Advances, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Food preservation challenges have positioned packaging as a rapidly evolving, innovation-driven field, with smart packaging offering transformative solutions. Among advanced materials, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted growing attention due to their permanent porosity, structural tunability, high surface area, and chemical stability. These features allow COFs to address critical needs in food packaging, including active barrier protection, antimicrobial action, and smart sensing of food freshness and spoilage. abstract: The high-dimensional Fokas model can describe a wide range of complex nonlinear wave phenomena; however, traditional analytical methods struggle to obtain a diverse set of exact analytical solutions, which limits the theoretical analysis and engineering applications of such models. In this paper, we address the problem of finding exact solutions for the high-dimensional Fokas model by combining Maple’s automatic bilinearization technique with an exploratory method using bilinear neural networks. abstract: To address the pressing demand for autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied environments, this paper systematically reviews the development status and future trends of multi-domain geomagnetic navigation and positioning technologies. title: Broadband underwater acoustic regulation composite metasurface based on pentamode scattering-dissipation synergy
abstract: Abstract Traditional directional regulation metasurfaces redirect reflected waves into prescribed directions, limiting their effectiveness in broadband and multistatic underwater detection. To address this issue, a diffuse scattering–dissipation composite metasurface based on pentamode materials is proposed, in which impedance matching, viscoelastic dissipation, and phase-gradient diffusion are synergistically coupled to attenuate acoustic energy and suppress directional echoes. title: Satellite-based vessel detection under turbulence and jitter: a degradation-aware comparison
abstract: Maritime domain awareness increasingly relies on satellite-based Earth observation (EO) for wide-area vessel monitoring. Low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms enable flexible acquisition, but optical imagery can be degraded by atmospheric turbulence and platform jitter. This paper presents a degradation-aware evaluation of deep learning-based maritime vessel detection that links algorithmic performance to the physical constraints of spaceborne optical imaging. title: A Silk Nanofiber‐Mediated Controlled Swelling‐Locking Strategy for Tough, Anti‐Swelling Hydrogels Toward Underwater Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive hydrogels are promising for wearable sensors in human motion detection owing to their skin‐like softness, strain sensitivity, and biocompatibility. However, their practical application in aqueous environments is severely hindered by swelling‐induced mechanical deterioration and electrical instability. Herein, a tough, anti‐swelling conductive hydrogel for underwater sensing is reported, enabled by a “silk nanofiber‐mediated controlled‐swelling‐locking” (SNF‐CSL) strategy. title: Comparison of biological matrices for the quantification of blood protein fractions in sea turtles Caretta caretta
abstract: Caretta caretta is the predominant sea turtle nesting along the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea. It is listed as a vulnerable species in the IUCN red list, because it is threatened by human activities. Protein electrophoresis is an important diagnostic tool in sea turtles rehabilitation, providing information on inflammatory, nutritional and epatic status. title: Multi source Earth observation and machine learning framework for mapping land degradation vulnerability in salinity- and hydrothermal-stressed regions of the southern main Ethiopian Rift
abstract: Soil erosion and land degradation are the main environmental challenges disturbing ecosystem services, agricultural productivity, and community livelihoods in Ethiopia. The Southern Main Ethiopian Rift is one of the regions experiencing high levels of soil erosion and land degradation, driven by active geological processes and anthropogenic activities. However, the contribution of these geological processes to salinization and their subsequent impact on soil erosion and land degradation in the region remains poorly understood and insufficiently studied. title: Construction and Practice of a Faculty Teaching Innovation Team for Cruise Interior Outfitting Technology Co-driven by Industry-Education Integration and Digital-Intelligence Empowerment
abstract: In response to the successive construction of domestically built large cruise ships and ongoing reforms in vocational education, conventional approaches to faculty development and organizational structures are no longer sufficient for cultivating interdisciplinary professionals in cruise interior design and outfitting technology. Taking the faculty team at Jiangsu Maritime Institute as a case study, this research employs policy analysis, occupational task analysis, and comparative case study methods to explore pathways for team building and pedagogical reform. title: Coastal Community Empowerment and Environmental Conservation Through the PALUH ASRI Social Innovation Program
abstract: Coastal ecosystems face increasing challenges due to environmental degradation, declining community welfare, and limited local capacity to manage natural resources sustainably. Social innovation-based empowerment programs are needed to integrate environmental conservation with social and economic development. This study aimed to describe the implementation of the PALUH ASRI Social Innovation Program as a model of coastal community empowerment through mangrove conservation and sustainable development approaches. title: Implementing the BBNJ Agreement: shaping and being shaped through institutional interaction with RFMOs
abstract: With the entry into force of the Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (the Agreement), its interaction with existing institutional bodies has become an immediate governance challenge. Regional fisheries management organizations (RFMOs), as the primary institutions regulating high seas fisheries, represent one of the earliest and most consequential arenas in which this interaction will unfold. title: Closing the gap between micro- and nanoplastics science and policy
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly being identified across environmental matrices, the food chain, and drinking water, with documented effects on human health, yet policy on how to translate this evidence into pollution-reduction action lags well behind the pace at which the underlying data are being generated. title: Renewable Energy for Rural-Coastal Development: Integrating Blue Economy Strategies with Faith-Based Climate Action
abstract: Rural-coastal settlements in developing nations suffer from immense energy poverty, climate vulnerability and lack sustainable livelihood options. If problems of the blue economy are resolved, renewable energy deployment can be a viable solution. Through this study, we want to integrate blue economy strategies with renewable energy initiatives and faith-based climate actions for sustainable development of rural-coastal sector. title: A review of responsible use of AI in remote sensing and cartography
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into remote sensing (RS) offers profound capabilities in data analysis, interpretation, and knowledge discovery. While AI applications offer immense potential for addressing global challenges such as environmental monitoring, disaster management, and urban planning, their rapid increase necessitates a critical examination of responsible development and deployment practices. title: Investigating climate-phenology relationships among the most common Italian forest species using Sentinel-2-derived vegetation phenology and productivity products
abstract: Climate change is profoundly altering forest phenology and productivity across Europe, particularly in Mediterranean regions characterized by high climatic heterogeneity. Understanding how climatic and site-specific drivers regulate the start, end, and length of the growing season, and how these phenological shifts translate into productivity responses, remains a key challenge for predicting forest carbon dynamics. Laser‐induced graphene (LIG) thermoacoustic sound source (TASS) is integrated with an aqueous cooling environment, while a hydrophobic styrene–ethylene–butylene–styrene (SEBS micromesh is introduced as a multifunctional interlayer. abstract: The performance of the Weather Research and Forecasting model coupled with chemistry (WRF-Chem) depends on the accuracy of input data and parameterisation schemes. This study examined the sensitivity of WRF-Chem version 4.4.2 to various domain configurations, chemical mechanisms, and physics parameterizations. abstract: This study presents a data-driven hydrodynamic optimization framework for toroidal propellers. As a representative engineering application of artificial intelligence (AI), the framework offers an efficient route toward the advanced design of underwater propulsion systems. The framework is based on an experimentally validated high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model, where open-water test data are used to validate the numerical methodology. abstract: Citizen science has experienced exponential growth since 2010, now contributing over 80% of data to global biodiversity repositories and fundamentally transforming biological inventory systems. abstract: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) has developed rapidly for ocean scatterometry over the past three decades. However, residual signal calibration errors, arising from inaccuracies in some key parameters and the complex space environment, degrade its performance. title: Integrating climate adaptation initiatives for coastal resilience: governance lessons from the Catalan coast
abstract: Mediterranean coastal regions face increasingly interconnected climate risks that require adaptation across sectors and governance levels. Despite growing policy commitments and a widening portfolio of adaptation initiatives, implementation often remains fragmented. This study examines the governance conditions under which diverse climate adaptation initiatives can be integrated to support coordinated regional and local resilience. abstract: Metaheuristic tuning of depth controllers for remotely operated vehicles is usually performed against a generic error integral, which does not encode mission priorities such as battery use, actuator stress from chattering, direction-dependent overshoot risk and post-event recovery. abstract: Abstract Control of agile and highly maneuverable underwater vessels is fundamental to explore complex maritime environments including survey closed to ocean structures and shallow waters. Currently, traditional autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and remote operated vehicles (ROVs) can encounter challenges navigating through these tight spaces. abstract: Plastic pollution is a global challenge, yet life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) methods lack spatially explicit transfer coefficients to quantify macroplastics distribution between terrestrial and aquatic environments. Current LCIA models focus on marine impacts, leaving terrestrial and inland aquatic pathways poorly characterized and limiting the integration of land-based plastic emissions into environmental assessment frameworks. abstract: This study investigates the techno-economic feasibility of coupling a reverse osmosis (RO) desalination plant with a nuclear-renewable hybrid energy system (Nu-R HES) consisting of a 150 MWe small modular reactor (SMR), a 100 MWe solar photovoltaic (Solar PV) plant, and a 600 MWe hydroelectric power plant (HPP) for the seaport region of Durrës, Albania. abstract: This study examined hook-size effects on catch characteristics, maturity composition, selectivity, and management performance in red tilefish ( Branchiostegus japonicus ) longline fisheries off Jeju Island, Korea. abstract: Deep-tow magnetic surveys deploy magnetometers close to the seafloor to obtain high-spatial-resolution magnetic anomaly data, yet such datasets are inevitably contaminated by complex noise. This study adopts the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to denoise deep-tow magnetic data and systematically evaluates the denoising performance of four wavelet families (Haar, Daubechies, Symlet, and Coiflet). abstract: Abstract The Solotvyno salt mine in West Ukraine presents significant environmental and infrastructural risks due to uncontrolled salt dissolution following mine flooding, causing ground subsidence, sinkhole formation, and transboundary contamination of the Tisza River. abstract: Recent landscape transformations resulting from the replacement of natural areas with anthropogenic uses have had an impact on the semi-arid region of Brazil. The objective of the research was to evaluate a land use and land cover classification model in the Caatinga biome, using machine learning techniques integrated with multiple environmental and climatic covariates. abstract: Timely pavement condition assessment is essential for maintaining road safety and optimizing maintenance planning; however, conventional inspection methods remain labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often lack the capability for continuous large-scale monitoring. abstract: This study investigates rainfall and temperature extremes across six agricultural blocks in the Cauvery Delta Zone (CDZ), Tiruchirappalli district, Tamil Nadu, using daily meteorological data from 1981 to 2023. abstract: In the cybersecurity domain, a drastic increase in threats affects the security of network and users. Particularly, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack poses a challenging issue because of its ability to inundate and debilitate targeted systems via distributed networks. Recently, deep learning (DL) based intrusion detection systems (IDS) are employed for detecting network intrusions and identifying anomalies in the network traffic. abstract: Utility-scale wind energy conversion systems are subjected to highly stochastic aerodynamic loading profiles, making drivetrain components—particularly high-speed gearbox shaft bearings and generator stator windings—susceptible to premature failure. abstract: Carotenoids play a crucial role as accessory pigments in plant photosynthesis and are closely associated with physiological responses to environmental stress. abstract: Applying the historical materialist principle of the dialectical relationship between infrastructure and superstructure, this study examines the development of Vietnamese elite sports from 2011 to 2026. abstract: Tidal flooding has become an increasingly significant environmental hazard in coastal areas. abstract: Graduates of maritime technical educational institutions must demonstrate proficiency in English for Specific Purposes (ESP) when performing their functional duties as part of a multinational crew. abstract: Magma reservoirs commonly exist in clusters and situate within complex fault networks, yet sequential triggering of unrest at multiple reservoirs and faults is rarely observed. abstract: This study proposes a novel Pruned Meta-Fuzzy Functions (PMFF) framework to forecast nationwide air temperatures across 81 cities in Türkiye. While existing literature often focuses on single models or standard hybridizations, these approaches frequently struggle with noise inherent in meteorological datasets and lack the necessary generalizability to perform across diverse topographical and climatic regions. abstract: Marine governance should be understood as a form of global governance because of the systemic nature of marine challenges. title: Sustainable seaweed aquaculture development in the Mekong Delta under climate change
abstract: This structured narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on the development of seaweed aquaculture in the Mekong Delta under climate change. Literature searches were conducted through 30 June 2026 using Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, followed by screening and thematic synthesis. The Mekong Delta is increasingly exposed to sea-level rise, salinity intrusion, and extreme weather events, which are undermining the viability of conventional agricultural systems and rural livelihoods. title: Why April Stands Out: Monthly Impacts of Internal Variability on Arctic Amplification
abstract: Abstract Observed Arctic amplification (AA), defined as the ratio of Arctic‐mean to global‐mean surface air temperature (SAT) trends, peaks in April, a feature not captured by climate models. Here, we quantify the impact of internal variability on Arctic‐mean SAT trends in March, April, and May from 1980 to 2022 using multiple approaches, including machine learning algorithms—convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and partial least squares (ML‐PLS)—as well as dynamical adjustment and wind‐nudged experiments. title: Marine-Derived Bioactive Peptides as Immunomodulatory Agents: Organoid-Based Platforms and Translational Perspectives
abstract: Marine environments harbor immense biodiversity that yields peptides with potent immunomodulatory, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory activities. These marine-derived immunomodulatory peptides act as molecular mediators of host defense and immune homeostasis across taxa ranging from fish to humans. title: Linking landscape structure and resource availability to coastal bird responses under Spartina alterniflora invasion
abstract: The invasion of Spartina alterniflora has profoundly altered habitat composition, landscape patterns, and resource availability in coastal wetlands. However, the large-scale mechanisms through which these changes affect birds with different habitat requirements remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Fast and accurate river flow simulations are essential for designing efficient hydraulic structures and establishing reliable safety policies under climate change. Traditional numerical methods are frequently computationally expensive for simulating nonhydrostatic river flows, which is important under extreme flow scenarios. Single-strain inoculants often perform inconsistently because they do not persist or compete well in resident soil microbiomes. abstract: Accurate solar radiation prediction is essential for integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems into power systems and supporting supply–demand management. However, many regions lack on-site irradiance measurements due to limited sensor deployment. To address this, this study investigates domain adaptation (DA)-based transfer learning for solar radiation prediction under zero-label conditions, where solar radiation measurements are unavailable in the target region. abstract: The accelerating global transition toward renewable energy has fundamentally altered the relationship between meteorology and electrical engineering. As power systems incorporate increasing proportions of weather-dependent solar and wind generation, meteorological data have evolved from peripheral inputs into indispensable operational assets for grid planning, dispatch, resilience management, and infrastructure protection. abstract: ABSTRACT Ruthenium (Ru)‐based materials are promising catalysts for alkaline water electrolysis; however, their practical application is severely limited by insufficient activity and poor stability. abstract: The digitalization of industrial facilities, driven by Industry 4.0 technologies, is fundamentally changing how production assets are monitored, modeled, and managed, and its strongest effect is felt in maintenance management, where traditional corrective and time-based practices are giving way to data-driven, condition-based, and predictive maintenance strategies. abstract: Offshore flowlines connect subsea wells, manifolds, and processing facilities, but any loss of containment can quickly escalate into environmental, operational, or reputational incidents. This review explores how smart leakage detection can mitigate environmental risk in Saudi Arabia’s offshore oil and gas flowlines by integrating process-based monitoring, distributed sensing, subsea robotics, machine learning, and environmental surveillance. abstract: Introduction Recreational activities such as birdwatching, or “birding,” are among the most commonly studied cultural ecosystem services. However, the benefits these services provide, particularly within avian-estuarine habitats, remain mostly under characterized. abstract: Minimizing casualties and property losses from maritime emergencies requires a timely and reliable search and rescue (SAR) logistics network. Unlike conventional emergency logistics, maritime incidents are not only stochastic but also involve demand locations that evolve over time under ocean environmental influences. title: Lake sediments uncover glacier change on the Kerguelen Islands during the past 1500 years
abstract: Climate change is driving the rapid retreat of glaciers across the sub-Antarctic zone. Using continuous lake sediment-based records of past glacier changes, the recent trends can be evaluated in a long-term context. Here, we analyse sediments from two glacier-fed lakes: Lake Athéna II and Lake Héra, located downstream the Chamonix Glacier on the sub-Antarctic Kerguelen Islands in the Indian Southern Ocean. abstract: Coastal schools possess ecological, social, cultural, and economic resources that can become authentic learning contexts, yet classroom practice may remain textbook-centered and detached from local environmental problems. This community service program aimed to design and implement Coastal Innovative Learning (CIL) for teacher capacity building on Salemo Island. abstract: Global fisheries face an urgent crisis of biodiversity loss due to the unintentional capture of non-target species, known as by-catch. Traditional Electronic Monitoring (EM) systems rely on manual review of video footage, often resulting in data backlogs and delayed management responses. abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are spreading fast through higher education, reshaping how students learn. abstract: Regional climate modelling plays a central role in understanding and projecting climate change across Australasia, a region characterised by complex topography, diverse climate regimes, and high exposure to climate extremes. abstract: This article argues that contemporary Western military innovation has become a strategic dead end. In turn, reduced reservoir inflows limit the water available to hydroelectric power plants for optimal hydroelectric generation. abstract: The exponential growth in IoT gadgets has made the attack surface in contemporary. Deep learning models fail to generalize to novel attacks, and biological models lack the contextual understanding required to capture complex relationships within network data. abstract: Introduction Maritime chokepoint disruptions can substantially degrade shipping services even when the underlying network remains structurally connected. This study examines the Red Sea–Suez disruption and evaluates alternative recovery strategies. abstract: Between 2019 and 2025, as part of the National Geographic and Rolex Perpetual Planet Everest expeditions, a team of National Geographic Explorers, scientists, and elite climbing Sherpas installed a network of Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs) to improve understanding of the climate at high altitudes in the Nepal Himalaya. title: MEDSLIK-II v3.00: an improved oil spill transport and fate model for surface oil releases
abstract: A revised version of the MEDSLIK-II oil spill numerical model software is presented. MEDSLIK-II is a free, open-source numerical model for oil spill transport and fate from surface oil releases, simulating the slick evolution. This paper describes the restructuring of the model workflow and setup, done by the introduction of new tools to pre-process the input data and post-process the output. Satellite images are used to validate the model for two test cases, and new quality indices are established. title: Integrated assessment of Dakhla (Southern Morocco) groundwater suitability for irrigation: Combining hydrochemical, microbiological, and multivariate analyses
abstract: Groundwater from the deep aquifer of Dakhla (Southern Morocco) is used as the main water source for developing agriculture in the arid coastal region. In order to determine its suitability for irrigation purposes, this study combines hydrochemistry, microbiology and multivariate analyses on samples collected from 13 boreholes during two years (2024–2025). Hydrochemical facies predominantly were (Na-Cl) type with high levels of mineralization (Average Electrical Conductivity = 2676 μS/cm), and FAO standards-exceeding levels of chlorides. abstract: Fungi play pivotal roles in terrestrial ecosystems as decomposers, pathogens and endophytes, yet their significance in marine environments is often understudied. Seagrasses, as globally distributed marine flowering plants, have critical ecological functions but knowledge about their associated fungal communities remains relatively limited. Previous amplicon surveys of the fungal community associated with the seagrass, Zostera marina, have revealed an abundance of potentially novel chytrids. title: Adaptive residual-gradient sampling PINNs for unsteady wake reconstruction around offshore cylinder arrays
abstract: Accurate reconstruction of unsteady wakes around offshore cylindrical structures is important for assessing wake interference, flow-induced loads, and the hydrodynamic environment of pile groups, marine risers, and related systems. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free surrogate modelling approach for such unsteady flows, but their accuracy depends strongly on collocation-point placement in evolving wake and boundary-layer regions. title: Investigation on flow and heat transfer characteristics of the once-through cooling system in a nuclear power plant under cold source disturbance
abstract: This study investigates the flow and heat transfer characteristics of the Once-through Cooling System (OCS) in a nuclear power plant under cold source disturbances. Based on an energy transport model of the Cold-End System it systematically analyzes the influence of various cold source disturbance factors on system operation, including seawater temperature, tide level, and condenser cleanliness coefficient. title: Implications of inter-observer variability for image-based monitoring of salmon lice (Lepeophtheirus salmonis) in commercial aquaculture
abstract: Image-based counting is increasingly used for automated monitoring of parasitic salmon lice ( Lepeophtheirus salmonis ) in salmon aquaculture. Machine-learning models for detection and classification of lice are trained using human annotations and thus ultimately depend on human judgement. Yet the extent to which observers agree in their assessment of image material, particularly under changing environmental conditions, has not been investigated. title: Revolutionizing Women’s Health with AI?
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is often portrayed as radically transforming healthcare. Such hyped expectations, however, contrast with actual outcomes, which include well-documented harms to minoritized patients. In this paper, we critically question the idea that AI will revolutionize women’s health by advancing sex-specific medicine. We present a qualitative analysis of twenty-three recent publications, sourced from medical databases, that discuss the use of AI in relation to gender/sex health disparities. abstract: Antarctic ice mass loss has intensified in recent decades. However, short-term glacier velocity variability in Victoria Land, East Antarctica, remains poorly documented. This study used Sentinel-1 SLC data and environmental records from 2017 to 2025 to quantify glacier-velocity variability in Victoria Land and examine its model-based statistical associations with selected atmospheric and oceanic variables using XGBoost–SHAP. An AI-driven evidence ecosystem for cardiometabolic nutrition: bridging the gap from multiomics to patient empowerment
abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases remain a primary global health challenge, with nutritional interventions serving as a critical pillar of management. However, the rapidly expanding volume of nutritional research, spanning high-dimensional multiomics, real-world continuous monitoring, and highly heterogeneous clinical trials, has created fragmented knowledge silos, leading to a profound translation lag between scientific discovery and clinical practice. abstract: This study develops an integrated multi-algorithm spatial simulation framework for large-scale urban expansion analysis by combining a Back Propagation Artificial Neural Network (BP-ANN), the Future Land Use Simulation (FLUS) model, Cellular Automata (CA), the standard deviational ellipse, Neighborhood Aggregation Analysis, and landscape metrics within a unified data flow. title: A hybrid method for winter road surface temperature prediction using improved LSTMs and stacking-based ensemble learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of road surface temperature (RST) is essential for proactive winter road maintenance and traffic safety management. However, existing approaches – ranging from physics-based models to data-driven methods – either require detailed pavement thermal parameters that are rarely available at operational road meteorological stations, or lack the capacity to simultaneously exploit local meteorological analogues and long-range temporal dependencies in an interpretable ensemble framework. title: Niche differentiation and functional complementarity between rare and abundant taxa sustain grassland soil bacterial diversity
abstract: Soil bacterial communities are central to grassland ecosystem functioning, yet how abundant and rare bacteria taxa differ in ecological strategies, community formation, and environmental responses remains unclear. Here we show, using 278 soil samples from grasslands across China, that these groups have contrasting but complementary ecological roles. Abundant taxa are mainly adapted to nutrient-poor conditions, tolerate a wider range of environments, and are shaped largely by random ecological processes. title: Effects of Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise and deep-sea water consumption on metabolic syndrome: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: [Purpose] The increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome poses significant health risks, particularly for cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes. Exercise interventions have shown promise in improving the components of metabolic syndrome, including blood pressure, lipid profiles, and glucose metabolism. Kinect-based mixed-reality exercise provides real-time feedback and personalized guidance, making it suitable for unsupervised training. abstract: Introduction Land-based cultivation using alternative water resources, such as saline groundwater (brine), offers a promising strategy for the sustainable production of the green macroalga Ulva compressa . Because Ulva growth and morphogenesis depend strongly on associated bacteria, understanding microbiome dynamics during acclimatization to brine is essential for stable biomass production. title: Using nuclear technology to change how we explore icy Ocean Worlds: examples from nuclear powered mission concept designs
abstract: Icy ocean worlds represent some of the most compelling targets in the search for extraterrestrial life, yet their exploration is constrained by significant logistical challenges including long transit times, limited solar power availability, and demanding radiation environments. Nuclear power and propulsion systems can offer a transformative capability by providing high specific impulse, continuous high-power availability, and mission flexibility. abstract: Introduction Characterizing Critical Zone processes requires high-frequency, spatially distributed environmental data. Environmental wireless sensing networks (WSNs) can meet this need, but few researchers currently implement this infrastructure themselves, instead relying on legacy data loggers that require manual data retrieval or commercial telemetry systems that are too often hindered by financial and logistical constraints, e.g., sensor lock in, proprietary data models, recurring cellular fees, and lack of programmatic data access (e.g., APIs). title: An Integrated AHP–Entropy Weighted GOD model with K-Means Clustering for Groundwater Vulnerability Mapping in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater resources in the coastal sedimentary basins of sub-Saharan Africa face severe anthropogenic threats. Conventional groundwater vulnerability overlay models, such as the GOD index, are frequently constrained by subjective parameter weighting and arbitrary index thresholding, which can produce spatial over-smoothing and broad, homogeneous vulnerability classifications. title: Dissecting land subsidence along United States coasts through hazard characterization and exposure disparities
abstract: Land subsidence is a widespread coastal hazard that exacerbates flooding and infrastructure degradation. Here, we present the first national-scale characterization of land subsidence hazard and exposure of population groups and infrastructure systems across 20 United States coastal states, explicitly accounting for spatial dependence. Using more than 190 million vertical land motion measurements derived from radar satellite imagery and ground observations, we develop a national-scale map that classifies subsidence into low-, moderate-, and high-hazard levels. title: Icing detection on wind turbine blades using a dual-attention CNN-BiLSTM model optimized by the hawkfish optimization algorithm
abstract: In cold offshore regions, blade icing on wind turbines can cause abnormal loads, elevated failure risk, and reduced power generation efficiency. Accurate detection of icing states is therefore crucial for ensuring safe operation. This study presents a detection method for icing states that combines feature engineering, deep learning, and intelligent optimization. title: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces: Construction principles, microscopic characterisation and biomedical functions
abstract: Engineered probiotic biointerfaces are the dynamic boundaries through which modified bacteria interact with their biological surroundings. They can improve bacterial survival, mucosal retention and therapeutic delivery, but the structural basis of these effects is often unclear. This review groups biointerfaces by their dominant role: barrier protection, recognition, responsiveness, interaction and renewal by living cells. title: AI-Enabled Technology Project Governance Framework for Early Risk Detection, Performance Forecasting and Adaptive Intervention
abstract: This work addresses a common problem: technology projects often run late, go over budget, or fail because risks are found too late. Before this framework, managers relied on manual reports and gut feeling, which meant problems were spotted only after damage was done. We built a system that reads project data (like progress, defects, and team speed) every two weeks, uses machine learning to predict which projects are likely to delay, and explains why using simple scores. journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: A critical review of industry 5.0-enabled nano-catalysts for synergistic air, water, and soil pollution abatement toward environmental sustainability
abstract: Environmental remediation has started to take advantage of all the advantages of Industry 5.0: sustainabililty, resilience and human-centric techologies. The role of nanocatalysts has a privileged part on it, as they allow the remediation of numerous pollutants present in atmosphere, water or soils. title: Adjoint-based shape optimization of a ship hull using a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) assisted propulsion surrogate model
abstract: Adjoint-based shape optimization of ship hulls is a powerful tool for addressing high-dimensional design problems in naval architecture, particularly in minimizing the ship resistance. However, its application to vessels that employ complex propulsion systems introduces significant challenges. They arise from the need for transient simulations extending over long periods of time with small time steps and from the reverse temporal propagation of the primal and adjoint solutions. title: A Probabilistic multi-objective optimization framework for offshore wind turbine jacket substructure under aero-hydrodynamic loading using surrogate models
abstract: The significant inherent uncertainties in the design and optimization of offshore wind turbines make it necessary to adopt a probabilistic approach to ensure structural reliability and performance. This study proposes a probabilistic multi-objective optimization approach for the offshore wind turbine (OWT) jacket based on dynamic responses predicted by surrogate models. title: Membrane crystallization for water sustainability: Scientific paradigms reshaping technology
abstract: Membrane Crystallization (MCr) is an emerging hybrid water separation technology that combines membrane processes with crystallization to generate controlled supersaturation via selective solvent or antisolvent transport, enabling precise control of crystal nucleation and growth kinetics. This study utilizes bibliometric analysis, machine learning, and data mining to systematically investigate scientific trends, publication patterns, key contributors, linguistic features, and technological developments in the MCr field. abstract: To address the difficulty of feature point extraction and insufficient matching robustness in weak-texture environments, which degrade visual localization accuracy, this paper proposes an improved visual SLAM framework integrating multi-scale deep features and adaptive filtering. title: Spatial heterogeneity of precipitation trends in the interior of northern Northeast Brazil: role of Atlantic and Pacific SST variability (1979–2020)
abstract: Abstract Precipitation variability in the MATOPIBA region, located in northern Northeast Brazil, exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity and is strongly influenced by large-scale ocean–atmosphere interactions. This study investigates trends, non-stationarity, and ocean–atmosphere teleconnections of daily precipitation over the period 1979–2020 using CPC/NOAA rainfall data and sea surface temperature (SST) fields from the Tropical Atlantic and Equatorial Pacific. title: Investigating terrestrial water storage change in a western Canadian river basin with GRACE/GRACE-FO and fully-integrated groundwater – surface water modelling
abstract: As hydrological trends shift in response to a warming climate, accurate characterization of hydrologic conditions and hydrologic change are imperative for water resources management, which is particularly important in the Canadian Prairies. abstract: Introduction Municipal solid waste (MSW) management significantly contributes to urban greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Optimizing MSW classification and treatment is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality, especially in coastal cities with unique waste streams. abstract: Abstract Introduction Ecological restoration projects are rapidly expanding in size, complexity, and frequency globally, driven by international agreements and an increased recognition of the efficacy of actions for biodiversity. Upscaling restoration will increasingly necessitate the restoration of multiple physically or functionally connected habitats concurrently, including across ecological realms (i.e. marine, freshwater, and terrestrial). title: Algorithmic Governance and International Law: Reconciling Sovereignty and Cross-Border Accountability
abstract: Abstract This article interrogates the concept of artificial intelligence (AI) sovereignty as an emerging site of normative tension within international law. As states increasingly assert jurisdiction over AI technologies and digital infrastructures, established doctrines, particularly those concerning territoriality, jurisdiction, and accountability, are under strain. abstract: The Asiatic black bear (Ursus thibetanus), a large and vulnerable mammal in northern Pakistan, faces increasing threats from habitat loss, tourism, human disturbance, and human–bear interactions. However, spatially explicit information on its potential habitat remains limited. The data were computed from earthquake rupture forecasts (ERFs) supplying initial generation conditions and a linear long‐wave Green's function approach to efficiently calculate tsunami propagation. abstract: In an increasingly digitalized business environment, microbusinesses face significant barriers to competing effectively in digital markets, including economic limitations, lack of marketing knowledge, and a pronounced technological gap. abstract: ABSTRACT Materials manufacturing has entered into a new era with the rapid development of technologies. title: Visual narratives of disaster on Instagram: a multimodal AI-assisted analysis
abstract: This paper explores Instagram as a platform for visual and emotional narratives of disaster across the response and recovery phases. Focusing on the extreme flooding that affected western Germany in July 2021, the study analyzes approximately 2,700 Instagram posts collected over a three-year period. It employs a mixed-methods approach combining generative artificial intelligence with qualitative and quantitative analyses.
