title: Contact lens with stretchable distributed-feedback laser for intraocular pressure monitoring
abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. Smart contact lenses are an attractive platform for continuous IOP tracking, and optical strain sensors are particularly promising thanks to their high sensitivity and natural readout. title: Strategic Environmental Assessment for the Ukrainian Community Development Strategies: European Union Practice
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is an important tool for integrating environmental considerations into territorial planning and sustainable development. This study compares SEA practices in the United Kingdom, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine to identify best European practices and formulate recommendations for Ukraine. The study used a comparative approach based on analysis of legal frameworks, consultation systems, and official SEA reports. abstract: Covering about 20 % of the global ocean, the polar ocean areas are among the most sensitive regions of the Earth climate system, where today climate change is reshaping processes that influence global circulation, sea level, and climate far beyond the poles. Here, we develop an ocean narrative that integrates physical, ecological, and societal indicators, to illustrate polar ocean change. abstract: The Arctic Ocean (AO) is experiencing declining sea ice extent and thickness and increasing sea surface temperatures, with cascading consequences for the entire ecosystem. abstract: Abstract The observed sensitivity of the Arctic summer sea‐ice area (SIA) to changes in the external forcing is a key quantity for understanding and projecting sea‐ice loss. abstract: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS) are now central tools forland resource mapping, administration and environmental management worldwide. title: Temporal evolution of the Petermann Ice Shelf estuary constrained by satellite remote sensing observations
abstract: Supraglacial rivers may reduce ice-shelf instability by draining meltwater from the ice-shelf surface, limiting loading-induced stresses from ponded meltwater. However, if a supraglacial river incises to below sea level at the ice-shelf front, forming an estuary, this effect may be negated. Water flow reversal in the estuary loads the ice shelf, which induces flexural stress, limits meltwater export, and enhances melting. title: Sustainability put to the test: environment and regional spatial planning in Chilean public policy (1994–2021)
abstract: This article reconstructs and analyzes the evolution of sustainability in regional-scale spatial planning in Chile between 1994 and 2021. It identifies four phases of normative evolution, from the first legal frameworks to the incorporation of Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and recent policies, using a qualitative–quantitative mixed design that combines content analysis of 11 instruments with exploratory visualization through MDS and clustering and inferential testing through PERMANOVA. title: Strengthening strategic environmental assessment through ecosystem service valuation and public preferences: evidence from Ireland
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is a key instrument for integrating environmental considerations into plans and programmes at an early stage of decision-making. However, effectiveness reviews highlight a significant gap in the systematic quantification of SEA benefits, particularly regarding non-market values and ecosystem services (ES). title: Efficient hydrogen peroxide synthesis from seawater via Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe under moderate temperature gradient
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) plays a crucial role in environmental remediation, chemical synthesis, and energy storage. Nevertheless, its industrial production is energy consuming with significant environmental burdens. Here we show a proof-of-concept thermoelectrocatalytic strategy for H2O2 production directly from seawater, driven solely by low-grade waste heat. A low-temperature thermoelectric (TE) material, Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe, is designed as a catalyst that enables efficient H2O2 generation under a moderate temperature gradient (ΔT). abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a pilot project exploring the integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into geography education in Zanzibar, Tanzania. Responding to systemic challenges such as overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, and limited resources, the study developed and implemented a localized, GenAI‐assisted teaching platform. Using a mixed‐methods approach, this study involved 133 teachers who experienced both traditional teaching and GenAI‐assisted teaching via a platform featuring interactive maps, a multilingual chatbot, and customized video content. title: Spatial variability in seawater chemistry across an intertidal mangrove–coral reef boundary
abstract: Context Edge effects at habitat boundaries can generate strong physicochemical gradients that structure coastal ecosystems. Although environmental gradients within coexisting mangrove–coral habitats are well documented, spatial variability in seawater chemistry across intertidal mangrove–reef boundaries remains under-characterised. Aim We examined fine-scale spatial variability in seawater chemistry across a mangrove–reef ecotone to assess how nearshore physicochemical conditions vary with proximity to mangroves. title: Geographic information systems, practical experiences in higher education
abstract: Geographic information systems (GIS) are technological tools for capturing, storing, analyzing, and visualizing geospatial data. This study presents the development and educational implementation of the Sistema de Información Geográfica para el desarrollo Sostenible (SIGDS) or geographic information system for sustainable development, an open-source geoportal integrating renewable energy assessment, smart-grid monitoring, and disaster-risk management at the Technical University of Manabí, Ecuador. title: Flash nanoprecipitation of monodisperse luminescent nanosensors for simultaneous oxygen and flow imaging
abstract: Understanding mass transfer in aquatic biological systems requires simultaneous measurements of velocity fields and transported scalar fields. Such scalar fields, including spatial distributions of dissolved oxygen concentration, can be measured using luminescent sensor particles that also function as flow tracers, but their performance is affected by particle size and dispersity. title: Widespread estuarine fishes drive long-term spatial beta diversity across a subtropical marine-estuarine gradient
abstract: Coastal lagoons and estuaries are characterized by strong marine-estuarine gradients, yet it remains unclear whether long-term spatial heterogeneity in fish assemblages primarily reflects species replacement, ordered species loss, or interannual changes in species occurrence and environmental responses. title: Overlooked contribution of organic alkalinity in Arctic Ocean margins biases ocean acidification estimates
abstract: Organic alkalinity has been recognized as a potentially substantial fraction of total alkalinity in coastal waters. However, conventional assessments of ocean acidification typically neglect its contribution when calculating pH and aragonite saturation state, potentially biasing the derived values. Here, we present elevated organic alkalinity in Arctic margins, and show that failure to account for it introduces substantial biases in calculated [H+] (1% – 51%) and aragonite saturation state (1% – 117%) in the Svalbard fjords, Tanafjorden, and the Barents Sea Opening, with potential implications

title: Species-specific responses of zooplankton to intermittent seawater intrusion in a re-opened estuarine system
abstract: This study evaluated zooplankton community dynamics under an intermittent seawater intrusion regime following the partial re-opening of the Nakdong River Estuary Barrage, South Korea from 2022 to 2024. Environmental variables and zooplankton distributions were monitored across vertical water layers (surface, middle, and bottom) at five upstream and three downstream sites relative to the barrage. title: Plastic bottles as marine litter tracers: evidence of illegal disposal in the Indian Ocean sector of the Southern Ocean
abstract: Abstract Marine litter is a major global concern, and identifying its origin is crucial to developing adequate and effective management strategies to curb pollution. Although the Southern Ocean is remote, with limited shipping activity and strong latitudinal frontal systems separating it from other oceans, pollution is an increasing problem in this region. Marine litter has been collected on sub-Antarctic Marion Island (part of the Prince Edward Islands in the Indian Ocean sector of the Southern Ocean) since 1993. title: A GIS-based approach for assessing island landscape visual character: Reciprocal land–sea visual characterization in the Zhoushan Archipelago, China
abstract: Coastal tourism, port expansion, and land reclamation are intensifying pressures on island landscapes, highlighting the need for systematic visual assessment to support sustainable planning and management. To address this need, this study develops a GIS-based approach for the Zhoushan Archipelago that uses character mapping as the spatial organizing basis and examines reciprocal land–sea viewing conditions, from the sea toward land and from land toward the sea, across foreground and background zones. title: Consistent drivers of coastal biodiversity across the tree of life
abstract: Coastal ecosystems are threatened by global change but remain understudied despite their importance for biodiversity and human society. For instance, most coastal studies and monitoring programs focus on a few groups of organisms owing to methodological limitations. However, high-throughput sequencing of environmental DNA (eDNA) now facilitates taxonomically broad studies of coastal biodiversity. title: Genomic insights into the metabolic complementarity of a synthetic marine consortium for hydrocarbon degradation in coastal sand microcosms
abstract: Microbial consortia are essential for the degradation of complex hydrocarbon mixtures in coastal environments, yet the functional basis of consortium performance rarely resolved at strain level. In this study, we employed a Plackett–Burman experimental design to rationally assemble and optimize a synthetic consortium for the degradation of medium-grade crude oil in a sand–seawater microcosm. Six strains were selected: Stutzerimonas stutzeri CBC1 and CBC2, S. balearica GOM11, Pseudomonas sp. CBC3, Halomonas litopenaei GOM23 and Enterobacter kobei GOM24. title: Comparing Strava and survey-based data for coastal recreation accounting
abstract: Coastal zones provide recreational ecosystem services across land and sea, yet spatial data for ecosystem accounting is limited. We compared Strava activity data with survey-based public participation GIS (PPGIS) data across the Oslofjord, Norway, to assess spatial and sociodemographic biases in crowdsourced recreation accounting. Strava over-represented activities along the coastal belt and across marine areas, while under-representing island visitation and leisure-oriented activities. title: Status of Sea Bamboo (Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758) in Bunaken National Park, North Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758, commonly known as sea bamboo, is a gorgonian octocoral of the family Isididae that plays a vital structural and ecological role in coral reef ecosystems. It is also recognised for producing unique bioactive secondary metabolites, particularly hippuristanol, which exhibits potent antiviral and cytotoxic properties. Despite its conservation and pharmacological importance, baseline demographic data for I. hippuris across North Sulawesi marine protected areas remain scarce. This study assessed the distribution, abundance, and population density of I. hippuris within B

title: Silicate accumulation in taxonomically diverse seaweeds: morphology, uptake, visualization and environmental responses
abstract: Abstract Silicon is required by some microalgae but use and accumulation by seaweeds has been quantified in few taxa. This study aimed to examine biogenic Si (bSi) in taxonomically and morphologically diverse seaweeds, measure Si uptake rates, assess the effects of environmental conditions on bSi, and visualize Si within seaweed tissues. bSi was determined in 57 seaweed taxa across 17 taxonomic orders collected around Tasmania, Australia. title: Abrupt pH changes overestimate the responses of Chaetoceros muelleri to ocean acidification
abstract: Ocean acidification, characterized by a gradual seawater pH decline, influences marine primary producers such as diatoms, which contribute substantially to oceanic carbon fixation. Experimental studies aiming to project climate change impacts often simulate acidification via abrupt pH shifts, potentially misrepresenting ecological and evolutionary responses. Here we conduct a long-term evolution experiment with the marine diatom Chaetoceros muelleri, comparing abrupt and gradual CO2 increases from 440 to 1000 ppm over 1100 generations. title: Projecting Impacts of Marine Heatwaves and Their Effects on Long‐Term Changes in Marine Ecosystems Over the 21st Century
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasing in frequency, duration and intensity under climate change. Although current MHWs trigger broad ecological impacts, such as coral bleaching, mass mortality of seagrass meadows, and declines in important fish stocks, the cascading effects of MHWs on ecosystem structure and functions in the 21st century remain unclear. In this study, we utilise a global biomass flow modelling framework to analyse these impacts. title: Navigating coastal futures: Harnessing GIS and multi-criteria decision analysis for sustainable resilience in Kerala's vulnerable Shores
abstract: Extreme weather occurrences, particularly in densely populated coastal places like India, cause loss and devastation, hindering disaster preparedness and long-term viability of vulnerable populations. Research shows that hybrid models, such as Bayesian Networks and Coastal Vulnerability frameworks, outperform traditional methods for measuring coastal vulnerability to Sea Level Rise (SLR). However, their extensive geographical coverage has considerable limitations, including data scarcity and challenges in effectively capturing differences in tiny locations. title: ANOVATS: a subsampling-based test to detect differences among short time series in marine studies
abstract: Assessing marine ecosystems is important for understanding the impacts of climate change and human activity, as well as for maintaining healthy oceans and ecosystems. In marine science, it is common for biologists and geologists to identify regional differences based on expert knowledge, frequently through data visualization. However, time series data collected through surveys in marine studies typically span only a few decades, limiting the applicability of classical time series methods. title: Where do the monsters come from? Visualizing marine pollution through biological mutation and game threat design
abstract: Marine pollution is difficult to communicate because much of it is gradual, distributed, and hidden below the surface. Plastic fragments, chemical residues, and damaged habitats may be present long before the sea looks visibly different. This creates a problem for games: players need to understand danger quickly, while the process itself is slow and difficult to see. This paper examines biological mutation as a design language for making that hidden damage visible. title: Environmental Factors Have a Stronger Influence on the Coral Holobiont in Comparison to Geographic Distance Along a 15,000‐km East‐to‐West Transect Through the Coral Triangle, Pacific and Indian Oceans
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim To determine the factors that structure coral‐associated microbial communities (bacteria and Symbiodiniaceae). These microbial communities play critical roles in reef ecosystem function, yet the relative importance of environmental versus geographic drivers in structuring these communities across large spatial scales remains poorly understood, particularly across broad Indo‐Pacific gradients that include biodiversity hotspots such as the Coral Triangle. title: Tecnologías de información geográfica y gerencia pública en salud: hacia una vigilancia epidemiológica territorial de la enfermedad diarreica aguda en Perú y América Latina
abstract: La enfermedad diarreica aguda (EDA) persiste como problema prioritario de salud pública en Perú y América Latina. Mediante una revisión sistemática PRISMA de 30 estudios (Scopus y SciELO, 2000-2026), se analizó cómo las Tecnologías de Información Geográfica (TIG) —autocorrelación espacial e indicadores LISA— identifican clústeres de riesgo de EDA. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen activos estratégicos de gerencia pública en salud, con potencial para optimizar la planificación territorial, la asignación presupuestaria y la capacidad de respuesta institucional ante brotes.

title: A validated methodology for the accurate determination of anthropogenic microparticles in sea salt: Application to Mediterranean Sea and Eastern North Atlantic Ocean salterns
abstract: Anthropogenic microparticles (AMPs) are ubiquitous contaminants of increasing environmental concern, and sea salt represents a potential route of human dietary exposure. This study developed and validated an analytical workflow for the accurate determination of AMPs in sea salt from Mediterranean Sea (MED) and Eastern North Atlantic Ocean (ATL) salterns, with particular emphasis on prevention of external contaminations. title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. title: Constraint-Based Adaptive Grids for Compact Representation of Marine Scalar Fields
abstract: Fixed-block representations can obscure heterogeneous local variability in marine scalar fields. We present a deterministic adaptive representation in which anchored dyadic tiles merge under a field-normalized local-range rule and a realized-tile diameter cap. Area-weighted tile values provide lossy reconstruction, whereas exact tile-to-cell membership preserves the link to the authoritative source grid. title: Mapping Coastal Resource–Environment Carrying Capacity in an Intensively Developed Coastal Area: Evidence from Rui’an, China
abstract: Abstract Coastal zones are dynamic land–sea interfaces where development pressures often approach ecological and environmental limits. Here, we operationalize a pressure–condition–response (P–C–R) framework to deliver a customized, high-resolution ( 30 × 30 m ) assessment of coastal resource–environment carrying capacity (RECC) for Rui’an (Zhejiang, China) using 2017 multisource geospatial, environmental, socioeconomic, and planning data sets. title: Mapping Physical Education Research in Southeast Asia: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends and Productivity
abstract: Physical education (PE) research in Southeast Asia has expanded rapidly, yet its regional distribution, leading contributors, and conceptual development have not been mapped in a single study. This bibliometric analysis examined 470 English-language Scopus-indexed publications issued from 1955 through 2024. Descriptive performance analysis and science-mapping procedures were conducted with Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to assess annual output, country and institutional productivity, authors, sources, collaboration patterns, keyword structure, and thematic change. title: Comparable temperatures but different microbiomes: long-term time series exposes seasonally divergent Baltic Sea prokaryotic communities
abstract: Abstract Marine microbiomes exhibit seasonal dynamics in many ocean regions. While we can characterize the biodiversity and composition of ocean microbiomes, we lack a systematic understanding of how environmental drivers shape the seasonal succession of marine microbes. title: Landscape of Targetable Genetic Alterations in Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma among Patients in Southeast Asia
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a heterogeneous form of biliary tract cancer, for which treatment options remain limited; however, molecular profiling technology has helped in uncovering genomic mutations that can be used in precision oncology. This molecular profiling study has been carried out retrospectively in order to investigate the genomic alterations that are targetable in advanced cholangiocarcinomas of Southeast Asia. title: Modeling of near-source conditions of alkalinity injection in marine environment for precipitation assessment
abstract: The permanent sequestration of carbon dioxide via Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement offers a promising pathway for large-scale climate mitigation. However, the operational safety of alkaline discharges is contingent upon avoiding secondary calcium carbonate precipitation, which occurs when the seawater aragonite saturation state exceeds critical thresholds. This study investigates the near-field mixing dynamics of bicarbonate-enriched effluents using high-resolution Large Eddy Simulations across various seasonal stratification and buoyancy regimes. title: Human pressure, habitat heterogeneity and species traits jointly determine the level of dark diversity in coastal fish communities
abstract: Understanding how anthropogenic pressures and environmental gradients shape coastal fish communities is a central question in biogeography and marine conservation. Yet, the set of species expected to occur at a site given ecological conditions but being absent – the so‐called dark diversity – has received far less attention than observed species, even if they hold key information about local extirpations and conservation effectiveness. title: Current knowledge of marine crustaceans in Mauritius and their global importance in a changing climate
abstract: Abstract Marine crustaceans are ecologically and socio-economically important components of coastal and marine ecosystems; however, in Mauritius, knowledge of their biodiversity, functional roles, and responses to climate change remains limited and fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes available information on Mauritian marine crustaceans, with particular emphasis on the class Malacostraca, while identifying key knowledge gaps and research priorities relevant to their ecological importance and climate-change vulnerability at both local and global scales. title: Benthic communities on recent and historical volcanic lava flows of an oceanic island
abstract: Understanding how benthic communities develop on newly formed marine substrates is essential for explaining ecological succession after large natural disturbances. However, different benthic components may respond at different temporal scales. Here, we examined successional patterns in selected components of shallow benthic communities across three submarine lava flows of contrasting ages on La Palma Island (Canary Islands, Spain): less than 1 year, 73 years, and 473 years old. title: Three decades of marine bioregions evolution through analysis of phytoplankton phenology
abstract: Ocean biogeochemistry is undergoing significant modification in response to climate change. To better track these evolutions, we present a novel ocean monitoring indicator that follows the temporal evolution of marine bioregions of similar phytoplankton phenologies. Chlorophyll a concentration observations from remotely sensed ocean color describe seven distinct marine bioregions characterized by their unique patterns of phytoplankton biomass seasonality. title: Winter disturbances drive community change in subarctic eelgrass meadows
abstract: The dynamics of winter sea ice and icefoot play a fundamental role in structuring intertidal ecosystems in subarctic environments. However, ongoing climate warming is altering ice regimes across northern shorelines. In the St. Lawrence marine estuary (Canada), reduced formation of icefoot increasingly exposes benthic habitats to winter-related disturbances. title: Balancing blue growth and the ecosystem approach: policy coherence in Sweden’s Marine Spatial Plan for the Baltic Sea
abstract: There is growing expectation within the European Union (EU) that Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) – the public process for allocating marine space among competing uses – can support environmental restoration and economic development through the Ecosystem Approach (EA), which seek to balance ecological, social, and economic objectives. This article examines how effectively MSP implements the EA in practice, using Sweden’s Baltic Sea plan as a case study. Pyropia haitanensis cultivation enhances water quality and reshapes microbial communities in coastal water and connected aquaculture ponds
abstract: Seaweed cultivation offers nature-based bioremediation for aquaculture effluents, yet its cascading effects on microbial ecosystems remain poorly understood. This study evaluated Pyropia haitanensis cultivation impacts across four phenological stages in nearshore marine (Cultivation Area, PS; Control Sea, CS) and connected aquaculture ponds (Influenced Pond, PA; Control Pond, CA). abstract: Artificial coastal defences simplify, linearize, and homogenize the coast, leading to reduced species diversity, ecological functioning, and ecosystem services. Previous active management research has shown that greater habitat complexity at millimeter to decimeter scales increases the diversity of fauna and flora living on constructed shores, however, little is known regarding the potential effects of increasing the scale of complexity on larger marine species. title: Global triazine herbicide pollution impairs marine phytoplankton nutrition through disruption of acetyl-CoA-related metabolism
abstract: Herbicide contamination impairs marine primary productivity, yet its subcellular impact on phytoplankton carbon allocation remains poorly understood. Global monitoring (1990–2023) revealed triazine herbicides as the dominant coastal pollutants, with atrazine and simazine exceeding 80% detection frequency; their combined toxicity corresponded to a median atrazine-equivalent concentration of 0.68 nmol L −1 . title: Climate trends in the Azerbaijani Caspian Sea sector and associated atmospheric circulation indices
abstract: ABSTRACT This study analyzes recent climatic changes in the Azerbaijani Sector of the Caspian Sea (ASCS) and their relationships with large-scale atmospheric circulation. Long-term changes in meteorological variables, river runoff, and sea level were assessed using data from 33 hydrometeorological stations and gauging posts for 1981–2024. title: Dietary shift from marine to agriculture in coastal Lower Yangtze Delta during Neolithic revealed by isotopic evidence from Jingtoushan
abstract: Neolithic agriculture is considered to have reduced marine food reliance among coastal populations, yet whether this dietary transition occurred in Neolithic China remains unclear. The lower Yangtze River Delta, central to both marine adaptation and rice agriculture origins, provides key evidence. In this study, stable isotope data from human and faunal bone collagen from the Jingtoushan site (8300–7800 BP), combined with published regional data, were used to investigate the dietary patterns and shifts. title: Biomass and Carbon Allocation in Tree Components of Beech-Chestnut Mixed Forests in Coastal Western Black Sea Region
abstract: Aim of study: Estimating C storage using biomass data is a widely used method for forest ecosystems. In most studies, the content of biomass is calculated by destructive methods such as cutting and sampling of trees on sampling plots. However, tree biomass can be estimated using diameter and height data without disturbing the site. The aim of this study is to determine the content of above-and below-ground biomass and their carbon (C) stocks in an eastern beech (Fagus orientalis Lipsky) and Anatolian chestnut (Castanea sativa Mill.) mixed forest. title: Wind and turbulence conditions encountered by vessels and wind-assisted propulsion systems at sea
abstract: Time-resolved measurements of the open-ocean marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) are essential for characterizing wind conditions encountered by wind-assisted propulsion systems (WAPS). A unique dataset obtained using two upward-facing continuous-wave profiling lidars during four trans-Atlantic crossings of a tanker is presented. abstract: Seaweed aquaculture offers a scalable route to food production and marine carbon sequestration, yet expansion into open oceans is limited by strong currents that prevent stable attachment and destroy the low-velocity conditions needed for growth, while nutrient scarcity adds a further constraint. title: Environmental Security of the Gulf During Armed Conflict: Marine Pollution Risks, GCC Preparedness, and a Regional Emergency-Response Framework
abstract: The Gulf is a strategically crucial and environmentally vulnerable semi-enclosed marine system supporting petroleum industries, international shipping, desalination facilities, coastal ecosystems, and urban centers. Alongside chronic industrial and maritime pressures, armed conflict introduces severe risks via direct military operations, targeting of energy infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, hazardous material releases, and disruption of monitoring networks. title: Hidden Ecosystems of an Endangered Giant: Microbiomes of Leatherback Sea Turtles
abstract: Abstract The leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) is a migratory, globally endangered marine species whose associated microbiota remain understudied. Characterizing these communities may inform animal health and conservation. We hypothesized that different turtle body sites and nests host distinct microbial communities. To test this, we analyzed 76 samples from five animals and seven nests, comprising nest sand (surface and bottom layers), eggs, and turtle-associated microbiota from the cloaca, mouth, tears, and carapace, collected during the nesting and hatching periods. title: Long-Term Shoreline Dynamics and Their Implications for Coastal Spatial Management
abstract: Coastal development increasingly takes place in environments where dynamic shoreline processes undermine the permanence of spatial planning and infrastructure. This research investigates long-term shoreline change along the Tanjung Pandan coast, Indonesia, and assesses its implications for coastal management, with Tanjung Pendam serving as a strategic urban waterfront. A quantitative spatial-descriptive methodology, combined with planning interpretation, was employed using multi-temporal shoreline data from 2000, 2013, and 2025. title: Modeling Phototaxis and Planktonic Cell Behavior in Phototrophic Biofilms
abstract: We propose a continuous multidimensional multispecies model of planktonic cell invasion in phototrophic biofilms that incorporates phototaxis as a key mechanism driving directed movement along light gradients. The biofilm is modeled as a homogeneous, viscous, incompressible fluid, with the velocity field governed by a Darcy-type law. The phototactic behavior of planktonic cells is integrated in the model by considering a reaction-advection-diffusion equation including a diffusive and tactic flux with a volume-filling term. title: Ecosystem management analysis study in tourist villages
abstract: Background: Arborek Island (8.2 ha), within Raja Ampat's Dampier Strait Marine Protected Area, is a global hub for community-based marine ecotourism and rich biodiversity. Surging tourism imposes acute socio-ecological pressures on fragile habitats and threatened megafauna (Mobula alfredi, Chelonia mydas), exposing vulnerabilities inherent to small-island systems. Methods: This study develops an empirical spatial-ecological and polycentric governance framework, combining multi-criteria GIS overlay (1:25,000) of infrastructure and statutory forest designations with a micro-spatial threat matrix
journal: Journal of Marine Problems and Threats.

title: Reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals: mechanisms, adaptations and evolutionary implications
abstract: Marine mammals inhabit thermally challenging environments in which maintaining internal body temperature is essential for survival, metabolic function, and reproductive success. Unlike terrestrial mammals, many marine male species lack external reproductive structures (e.g. scrotum), raising questions about how reproductive temperatures are regulated in the absence of conventional cooling mechanisms. This review synthesizes current knowledge of reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals, with a focus on cetaceans and pinnipeds, and highlights key anatomical and physiological adaptations.

title: Shell characteristics and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope signatures of Creseis acicula during its 2020 outbreak near Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station
abstract: Abstract China ranks second in the world in terms of nuclear power generation, making significant contributions to China’s green economic and social development. Chinese nuclear power plants are located in coastal areas, which are prone to frequent outbreaks of marine organisms due to inputs from terrestrial sources. These outbreaks have led to shutdowns of varying severity at nuclear power plants. However, there is currently limited research on the processes involved in marine-organism outbreaks. Daya Bay Nuclear Power Station (DBNPS) is the first large-scale commercial nuclear power station

title: Anthropized environments as reservoirs of hidden and exotic diversity in marine annelids: sicilian ports as a case study
abstract: Marine annelids are key components of benthic ecosystems, yet their diversity remains unevenly documented, particularly in anthropized habitats. In Sicily (Mediterranean Sea), significant knowledge gaps persist regarding port benthic communities and their role in the spread of non-indigenous species (NIS). This study provides the first characterization of polychaete assemblages in Sicilian ports in over three decades, with a specific focus on biodiversity patterns and NIS occurrence. title: The Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting Tool: A Software Application for 2‐Dimensional Raman Image Peak‐Fitting and Visualization
abstract: ABSTRACT We present the Carbonate Raman Processing and Plotting tool (CaRPP), designed to perform peak‐fitting and visualization on two‐dimensional Raman maps of calcium carbonate specimens. The CaRPP software enhances transparency and image‐processing capabilities specific to carbonates compared to existing alternatives. Although designed for visualizing peak width and wave number spatial patterns in the shells and skeletons of marine calcifying organisms, CaRPP has potential to be used for Raman spectra peak‐fitting and plotting on a wider range of sample types.

title: Bathymetric structuring of scavenging amphipods in two sub-Arctic fjords
abstract: Abstract The removal of carcasses and consequently recycling of organic matter from food falls depends on a variety of benthic scavenging species in marine ecosystems. Amphipods, more specifically lysianassids, are among the most important scavengers in the deep sea and coastal habitats. Arctic coastal waters were found to have a highly diverse amphipod community, while very little is known about the lysianassid distribution and species composition in sub-Arctic ecosystems. title: Environmental Communication and Multi-Stakeholder Collaboration for Sustainable Fisheries Livelihoods and Coastal Resource Governance on Labengki Island, Indonesia
abstract: The goal of this study was to analyze multi-stakeholder collaboration in environmental communication in developing sustainable marine tourism in Labengki Island, North Konawe Regency, as a means of supporting coastal fisheries livelihoods and improving the social economy of Labengki Island’s small islands. A qualitative exploratory approach was used, with a case study design. Thematic analysis was conducted in NVivo using software, whilst Actor-Network Analysis (ANA) — an approach adapted from Actor-Network Theory (ANT) — was used to map relationships between human and non-human actors. title: Determination of seasonal groundwater recharge potential in the coastal mining town of Jose Panganiban, Philippines
abstract: Coastal groundwater resources are highly vulnerable to the combined risks of heavy metal contamination and saltwater intrusion where artisanal small-scale gold mining is active. This study used a GIS-based analysis to identify susceptible coastal aquifers in the municipality of Jose Panganiban, Philippines, by examining the reduction in groundwater potential coincident with the seasonal oscillation of precipitation, the main driver of recharge. abstract: What are geospatial dashboards, and how can they support planning and Planning Decision Support Systems (PDSS) addressing Climate Change (CC)? Starting from the literature, the paper analyses dashboards and their indicators as used in planning, proposing criteria for an integrated, dynamic, and operational PDSS for diverse plan recipients at local and global scales. title: Salinity challenges and community adaptation: insights from coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Rising sea levels and increasing cyclone intensity are exacerbating salinity problems in coastal regions globally, threatening freshwater availability and public health. To address gaps in understanding community adaptation, we employed a multi-faceted approach comprising meta-analysis, water testing, surveys, focus group discussions (FGDs) and key informant interviews (KIIs) to: ( i ) examine rainwater harvesting trends, ( ii ) assess stored rainwater quality, and ( iii ) investigate community practices, perceptions, and health outcomes in coastal Bangladesh. title: Visualizing the Nuclear: Visibility and Invisibility in U.S. Photographic Representations from the Pacific
abstract: This article examines the visual culture of U.S. nuclear imperialism in the Pacific through an analysis of several widely circulated photographs: two images of atomic testing at Bikini Atoll published in Life magazine in 1946, and a photograph of the nuclear-powered USS Enterprise produced during Operation Sea Orbit in 1964. Drawing on theories of coloniality, whiteness, and militourism, this article traces the shift from the hypervisibility of the atomic explosion to the increasing invisibility of nuclear power within Cold War visual discourse. title: Spatial Variability and Long‐Term Trends in Winter Phytoplankton of the Warming Eastern Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Mediterranean Sea (EMS) is among the fastest‐warming ocean regions, but the impacts of this warming on phytoplankton are unclear. Here, wintertime field observations were conducted across the EMS. These observations showed that small photosynthetic eukaryotes (<20 μm) dominated phytoplankton communities, collectively accounting for >60% of total chlorophyll a (Chl‐a) despite severe nitrate‐ and phosphate‐depleted conditions. title: New records of the rare deep-sea snailfish Acantholiparis opercularis (Cottoidei: Liparidae) in the western North Pacific, with notes on the morphology and distribution of the species
abstract: An unusual snailfish with spines on its head was sampled by the SokhoBio expedition in the southern Sea of Okhotsk at a depth of 3305 m. We identified it as Acantholiparis opercularis Gilbert et Burke, 1912, a rare deep-sea fish described from the Avacha Gulf (southeast of Kamchatka) and the Shumagin Islands (Aleutians) and known from several additional records in the North Pacific (Bering Sea, Oregon, Northern California). title: Lithochloron , a new genus of green algae residing in coral skeleton (Cladophorales, Chlorophyta)
abstract: Coral skeletons host diverse microbial communities, including endolithic green algae that contribute to holobiont functioning. The siphonous green alga Ostreobium (Bryopsidales) is arguably the best-known coral endolith, but recent environmental sequencing has indicated that other lineages of green algae may also inhabit the coral skeleton, including members of the Cladophorales. Here, we characterize a new endolithic green alga isolated from a Porites coral skeleton collected from Heron Island on the southern Great Barrier Reef. title: Sensing a Changing Tide: Community‐Based Monitoring and Collaborative Governance in Mexico’s Small‐Scale Fisheries
abstract: This article examines how small-scale fishing cooperatives on Mexico’s northern Pacific coast integrate technologies into community-based marine governance. Drawing on ethnographic research with cooperatives in Baja California Sur, it asks how oceanographic sensors are used, adapted, and made meaningful in citizen science and co-constructed governance practices, and what that reveals about empowerment and blue justice in coastal communities. title: Climate change and biological traits: interglacial stability and higher glacial functional diversity in Late Quaternary molluscan assemblages of the Adriatic Sea (Italy)
abstract: Abstract Studies on the effects of long-term climate change on marine communities are crucial to our understanding of ecosystem resilience. The Late Quaternary fossil record, dominated by extant taxa, provides a valuable archive of past biotic responses to major climate fluctuations. While most studies on faunal turnover so far have focused on taxonomic identity, trait-based approaches are becoming increasingly common as they provide a stronger link to ecosystem functioning. title: Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. ( Prorocentrales, Dinophyceae ): A new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the open tropical Pacific Ocean
abstract: SUMMARY While phytoplankton from the coasts of temperate seas has received considerable attention, phytoplankton from the open tropical ocean, especially the smallest fraction, remains understudied. Here, we describe a new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the tropical Pacific Ocean. Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. is slightly oval in thecal view, measuring 6–9 μm long and 5–8 μm deep. title: A review on visualization of flexible VOC sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are ubiquitously present in the natural environment and are produced by human activities, serving as key indicators of the chemical state of substances. The integration of flexible sensors and visualization technologies offers novel solutions for on-site, in-situ, and real-time VOC detection. title: Small‐Scale Topographic Variability Shapes Molecular Diversity of Organic Matter in Coastal Dune Soils
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a crucial role in carbon and nutrient cycling across terrestrial, aquatic, and marine ecosystems. Most terrestrial OM originates from litter and soils, where it is mobilized by percolating rainwater before entering the groundwater. Consequently, groundwater OM composition can be influenced by soil processes such as organic matter processing above the groundwater surface. abstract: Abstract In a rapidly changing Arctic, the Kongsfjorden marine ecosystem was investigated to explore its community composition and structural dynamics using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Samples were collected with metaprobes , passive eDNA samplers deployed within fish traps in the coastal zone and towed along a transect in the mid-fjord zone. title: Multi-scale environmental influence on the spatial and bathymetric distribution of the solitary ascidian Halocynthia papillosa (Linneaus, 1767) in the Ligurian Sea (NW Mediterranean)
abstract: Halocynthia papillosa is one of the most common ascidians inhabiting coralligenous and sciaphilic benthic communities on Mediterranean rocky bottoms. Despite its ecological relevance, its broad-scale distribution patterns and environmental drivers remain poorly understood. This study investigates the spatial and bathymetric distribution of H. papillosa along the Ligurian coast (NW Mediterranean Sea) using standardized ROV video surveys conducted between 2015 and 2025 in 37 sites located at 40–100 m depth. title: Profile-wide desalinization is associated with increased deep-soil microbial biomass and reduced iron-bound carbon in coastal wetland restoration
abstract: Tillage- and mulching-based interventions are increasingly used to control invasive plants and modify soil hydro-salinity, but their effects on subsoil carbon (C) stabilization are poorly quantified. We conducted an 18-month field experiment in a Spartina alterniflora–invaded estuarine wetland to compare plastic mulching (PM) and deep tillage (DT) and to resolve microbial–mineral controls on C across the 0–100 cm profile. title: Population structure and gene flow in the endangered Caribbean reef-building coral, Acropora palmata
abstract: Abstract Populations of the Caribbean reef-building coral, Acropora palmata , have declined sharply since their genetic structure was first characterized in the early 2000s. Previous analyses comprehensively sampled coral colonies across the Caribbean and western North Atlantic but genomic resolution was limited by the number of loci assayed. These analyses indicated extensive asexual reproduction via fragmentation, high outcrossing at the genet level, and an east–west population split. title: Volcanic stratigraphy offshore East Montserrat: Selective preservation and subaqueous remobilisation in marine records
abstract: Abstract In tectonically active regions, volcanic eruptions generate large volumes of material that are transported offshore through processes such as pyroclastic density currents, turbidity currents, and secondary sediment remobilisation. These deposits form key stratigraphic markers for reconstructing eruptive histories, yet their preservation, correlation with onshore events, and modification by mass wasting remain insufficiently understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental DNA (eDNA) transforms marine ecological research through non‐invasive assessment of ecosystem structure with higher taxonomic resolution. This study explores the potential of eDNA metabarcoding to enhance fisheries advisories through food web reconstruction, bridging ecological insights with ecosystem‐based fisheries management. This review elucidates the concepts of eDNA and explores its applications in food web studies and Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) dynamics. title: Public support for establishing marine protected areas: an Italian case study
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are management tools aimed at protecting and restoring marine ecosystems and promoting the sustainability of social-ecological systems. Their success, however, depends on stakeholders’ relationships with marine resources and on the quality of the governance processes through which MPAs are designed, calling for research on stakeholders’ perceptions of MPAs long before they are established. title: Evolution of freshwater reproduction in a marine fish: Evidence from genetics and otolith microchemistry
abstract: The evolution of distinct reproductive strategies within the same species can offer unique insights into adaptive divergence. Since the discovery of European flounder (Platichthys flesus) in the freshwater environment of the isolated Lake Pulmanki in the 1970s, the evolutionary origin and reproductive strategy of this euryhaline fish has remained a mystery. abstract: One of categorization method for granitic rock is by their tectonic setting which can be analyzed by plotting their trace element value in discrimination diagram. Discrimination diagrams proposed by Pearce et al., particularly Rb vs (Y+Nb) and Rb vs (Yb+Ta) diagram, have been widely used by igneous geochemists. abstract: In the deep ocean, hydrothermal vents sustain remarkable animal-microbial symbioses, in which bacteria colonizing animal external or internal tissues use reduced chemicals from venting fluids to perform chemosynthesis and nourish their host. Hydrothermal vents also occasionally occur within the photic zone, but the prevalence of photosynthesis within these settings is considered to override the development of chemosymbiotic interactions; animal-microbial associations such as those observed at deep-sea vents have rarely been recorded at shallow vents. Reef-associated fishes of the Indo–West Pacific provide an ideal framework to investigate these dynamics, yet many taxa remain poorly resolved due to morphological conservatism and cryptic diversity. abstract: Evaluating spatiotemporal dynamics is essential to measure and monitor environmental sustainability in coastal zones under rapid urban expansion. Future scenarios of the earth’s surface can be estimated from identified changes in remote sensing. The objectives of this study were to evaluate changes in the land surface temperature (LST), estimated with Landsat 8 images of the Brazilian coastal municipality of Arraial do Cabo on two summer dates—2014 and 2017—and to project a scenario for 2030. abstract: Eco-engineering practices are increasingly implemented in urbanised marine coastal zones to enhance local marine biodiversity, as part of biodiversity offsetting efforts in areas impacted by human activities. Broad-scale, long-term monitoring studies remain scarce in this field yet are essential for robustly assessing the ecological value of these compensation initiatives. abstract: Extreme weather can disrupt traditional fishing activities and increase safety risks, particularly when local weather information is difficult to access before departure. This study develops a web-based extreme weather monitoring and early warning system for traditional fishermen using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with a DHT22 sensor, rain sensor, and anemometer to acquire temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind-speed data at ten-second intervals. abstract: This study investigates, in a two-dimensional wave flume, how idealized reef-flat roughness and reef-flat length affect the transformation of solitary-wave-induced bores. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems in the Niger Delta constitute the largest mangrove forest in Africa and provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon sequestration, coastal protection, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood support for coastal communities. abstract: Conventional vibration sensors are unsuitable for long-term distributed monitoring in ship engine rooms because of high humidity, salt fog, electromagnetic interference, confined space, limited low-frequency performance and dependence on external power supplies. This paper proposes a self-powered marine triboelectric vibration sensor based on spring steel sheets. title: Delta morphology reveals timings of early ocean regression and hydrologic shift on ancient Mars
abstract: Abstract Mars’ ancient hydrologic history remains a subject of debate, with competing interpretations suggesting either a large ocean or scattered lacustrine environments. Here, we show that delta morphology on Mars records a shift between these hydrologic regimes. Through controlled tank experiments, we identify two distinct delta types: “lobe-extruding deltas” formed during water-level falls and “stepped fan-deltas” formed during rising water levels. abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. title: Material-dependent physiological and biochemical responses of marine microalga Tisochrysis sp. to three model nanoplastics
abstract: The physiological responses of microalgae to nanoplastics remain poorly understood, as research has focused almost exclusively on polystyrene nanospheres, limiting insight into the impacts of other polymers at the nanoscale. To address this knowledge gap, this study evaluated laboratory-generated nanoplastics (<200 nm) from polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and residual photopolymerisable 3D resin (PU/PA), and their effects on the physiology of Tisochrysis sp. over a 10-day exposure at 5μg/mL. title: Near real-time heatmap visualization of roadway activity using distributed acoustic sensing
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a promising technology for traffic monitoring. When applied to fiber optic cables near roadways, DAS captures vibrations along the fiber, enabling continuous, distributed sensing of roadway activity. When measurements are collected over long distances of fiber, DAS produces large amounts of spatiotemporal data, where visual analytics can provide a useful means of transforming that data into interpretable information for further analysis. title: Hydrometeorological and hydrogeological trends and drought dynamics in a cold-humid, coastal region
abstract: Quantifying groundwater response to droughts remains challenging, as aquifers typically respond to meteorological conditions with delays, and long-term groundwater records remain limited. This study investigated statistical relationships among meteorological, hydrogeological, and hydrological datasets in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. title: Design and Implementation of a Centralized Vessel Monitoring System Using API Harmonization
abstract: Vessel tracking is critical for ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of the maritime industry. However, the reliance on tracking devices from disparate commercial vendors (e.g., Vendor A, Vendor B, and G-Track) introduces severe data fragmentation, forcing operators to navigate multiple proprietary dashboards. Furthermore, custom-built Internet of Things (IoT) tracking devices lack interoperability with these existing commercial platforms. title: Dynamic‐Coupling Axial Chloride on Dual‐Heteroatom Sites for Highly Anti‐Chloride Oxygen Reduction in Seawater
abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) offers a sustainable and cost‐effective route for energy conversion while alleviating freshwater scarcity, but suffers from chloride (Cl − ) poisoning and corrosion of metal active sites. Herein, we present a dynamic axial Cl coordination strategy to mitigate this issue, realized by precisely engineered O‐bridged dual‐heteroatom catalysts (FeMn DHACs) for ultrahigh electrochemical ORR activity in seawater. title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. title: Local Environmental Habitat Templates and Hydroperiod Contingency Jointly Shape Benthic Macroinvertebrate Dynamics in Tropical Choked Coastal Lagoons
abstract: Abstract Coastal lagoons are highly dynamic transitional ecosystems in which benthic macroinvertebrate communities are shaped by spatial and temporal environmental filters. However, the relative importance of lagoon-specific conditions versus temporal variation remains poorly resolved, particularly in the tropics. Here, we investigated benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages in three neighboring choked coastal lagoons in southeastern Brazil over 23 consecutive months. title: Optimising renewable hydrogen hub locations: A GIS-based spatio-temporal integration framework
abstract: This paper presents a Geographic Information System (GIS)-integrated spatio-temporal optimisation framework for the design of renewable hydrogen hubs. This framework embeds high-resolution spatial datasets directly into an hourly Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to co-optimise the siting, sizing, and hourly operation of system components, thereby minimising the Levelised Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH 2 ). Early‐formed asteroids, driven by the decay of 26 Al, may have also experienced such magma ocean processes. Estimation of Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) over the Hiramandalam Reservoir Catchment Using GIS
abstract: Reliable estimation of the Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) and the resulting Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) is essential for fixing the design flood of high-hazard hydraulic structures such as spillways and flood-control dams. This paper presents a GIS-based estimation of one-day PMP and the corresponding PMF for the catchment of the Hiramandalam Reservoir, located in Hiramandalam mandal of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh. title: Leveraging GIS-based multi-criteria analysis for flood-prone area detection in Nsanje District, Malawi
abstract: Flooding remains one of the most severe and recurrent natural hazards in sub-Saharan Africa, posing persistent threats to rural livelihoods, infrastructure, and environmental stability. In Malawi, the Lower Shire River Valley, particularly Nsanje district, is highly vulnerable to recurrent flooding due to climatic variability, land-use change, and geomorphological characteristics. Despite the growing availability of geospatial data, localized flood vulnerability assessments remain limited, constraining effective disaster preparedness and land-use planning. title: Depth-dependent signatures of dissolved organic matter in the stratified Saguenay Fjord: insights from optical and molecular analyses
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) governs key carbon-cycling processes within coastal and estuarine environments, yet its transport and characteristics are not fully understood. In this study, we investigated depth-dependent patterns of DOM in the Saguenay Fjord (Quebec, Canada), a deep sill-bounded and stratified fjord that receives freshwater inputs from the Saguenay River and saline water intrusions from the St. Lawrence Estuary. title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. title: Post-disturbance temperate reef states influence fish contributions to nature and people
abstract: Abstract Background Climate-driven habitat reorganization is reshaping the capacity of marine ecosystems to sustain biodiversity and human well-being, with implications for SDG 14 (Life Below Water) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger). Yet, it remains unclear to what extent post-disturbance reef fish communities continue to support ecological functioning and human nutrition, particularly in temperate kelp forest ecosystems. title: Underwater hybrid ESD versus conventional ESD for colorectal laterally spreading tumors: a retrospective study
abstract: Background and aims Conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection (C-ESD) is standard for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) but is time-consuming. Underwater hybrid ESD (U-Hybrid ESD) is an emerging technique. We compared the efficacy and safety of U-Hybrid ESD versus C-ESD for colorectal LSTs. Methods This exploratory, single-center retrospective study included 300 patients with LSTs ≥20 mm (U-Hybrid ESD, n = 150; C-ESD, n = 150). title: Field sampling guidelines for sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) research in lacustrine and coastal systems: from field collection to laboratory subsampling
abstract: Abstract Sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) has emerged as a powerful proxy for reconstructing past biodiversity and environmental change in lacustrine and coastal systems, yet standardized field guidance remains limited, particularly for researchers working in tropical and coastal depositional environments. Here, we present a practical sampling framework covering the key field protocols of sedaDNA research, from field collection to laboratory subsampling, with emphasis on contamination control at each step. title: Artificial light at night causes unequal and species-specific shifts in infection risk by a generalist marine parasite
abstract: Abstract Light pollution, in the form of artificial light at night (ALAN), changes the normal physiology and behaviour of animals, leading to alterations in interspecific interactions. Parasitism is likely to be impacted, ranging from altered parasite proliferation and transmission to altered host exposure or susceptibility to infection. How these individual-level effects translate to higher level impacts remains poorly understood. title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
abstract: Abstract The spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). title: Ecotoxicological evaluation of veterinary pesticides in marine environments: Oxidative stress and neurotoxicity of Dinotefuran and Pyriproxyfen in Mytilus galloprovincialis
abstract: This study evaluates the ecotoxicological impact of the neonicotinoid Dinotefuran and the insect growth regulator Pyriproxyfen on the marine mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis . Adult specimens were exposed for 14 days to nominal concentrations of each pesticide (0.1 μg/L and 0.05 μg/L) and their mixture. While individual exposures triggered compensatory antioxidant responses (SOD and GPx), the mixture caused a collapse of these defenses, leading to severe lipid peroxidation (MDA) and protein carbonylation (PC) in the gills and digestive gland. title: Durability of a cement-free ultra-high performance geopolymer concrete: A laboratory comparison with Portland-cement UHPC validated by real marine exposure
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive durability comparison of a 100% cement-free ultra-high performance geopolymer concrete (GEO), based on ground granulated blast-furnace slag and silica fume, against a Portland cement-based ultra-high performance concrete reference of equivalent strength class (REF). title: Colombiains A–C, Three New Alkaloids From the Soft Coral‐Derived Fungus Cladosporium colombiae CSGL 10M10
abstract: Three new alkaloids, colombiains A-C (1-3), together with 8 known ones (4-11), were isolated from the soft coral-derived fungus Cladosporium colombiae CSGL 10M10. Their structures were elucidated by spectroscopic interpretation, electronic circular dichroism (ECD), and single-crystal X-ray crystallographic methods. title: Delineation of Groundwater Potential Zones in Nangarhar Province, Using RS, GIS, and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP)
abstract: Groundwater is the main sources of water supply in Afghanistan, especially that areas where access to surface water is hard and difficult. Nangarhar Province has significant surface and groundwater resources and depend extensively on these resources for domestic and agricultural usage, including orange orchards, vegetable cultivation & sugarcanes production. Therefore, detecting areas with suitable groundwater potential is essential for sustainable SGRM (groundwater resource management) and well siting. title: Allocate optimal locations for EVCSs in major saudi cities using GIS-based AHP approach
abstract: Reducing the usage of fossil fuels is a widely acknowledged concern because of their diminishing supply and the negative environmental effects of transportation. Thus, electrical energy will surely come first when considering alternative energy sources. However, to achieve that process, electric vehicles (EVs) should be preferred over fuel cars. title: GIS-based multi-hazard exposure and financial consequence assessment of PV power plants in Thailand
abstract: Solar energy is one of Thailand’s fastest-growing renewable sources, yet its infrastructure may be exposed to natural hazards, particularly flooding. This study develops an integrated GIS-based framework to assess mapped multi-hazard exposure and financial consequences for 484 PV power plant records representing 2,833.16 MWp, using annual flood footprints from 2011–2023, landslide-susceptibility maps, and seismic-intensity maps. title: A community-informed, multilayered vegetative bioshield for climate-related coastal erosion on Sonadia Island, Bangladesh
abstract: Sonadia Island is an ecologically important barrier island on the southeastern coast of Bangladesh, where shoreline erosion, saline intrusion, cyclone exposure, and habitat degradation threaten both biodiversity and local livelihoods. This exploratory mixed-methods study assessed community perceptions of existing Jhaw plantations, documented selected dune and vegetation characteristics, and developed a site-specific conceptual bioshield for pilot testing. title: Open-Source GIS Applications for Flood and Landslide Assessment: Comparative Cases from Poland and Malaysia
abstract: Research on natural disasters requires analytical procedures that are rapid, reproducible, and based on sound scientific principles. Such procedures should also be accessible to institutions responsible for environmental monitoring, land-use planning, and disaster risk reduction. This study evaluated the practical use of publicly available geospatial data and open-source GIS tools for the preliminary assessment of two contrasting natural hazards: the September 2024 flood in Lower Silesia, Poland, with particular focus on the urban floodplain of Wrocław, and the December 2022 landslide in Batan

title: GIS-Based Flood Risk Assessment in the Johor River Basin Using AHP and Weighted Overlay
abstract: Flood-risk studies in Malaysia have often concentrated on hydrological hazard, although the consequences of flooding also depend on where people and assets are located and how well communities can cope. This study develops a basin-wide flood-risk index for the Johor River Basin by integrating hazard, exposure and vulnerability within a geographic information system-based multi-criteria decision analysis. title: Vertical collision risk of Red-crowned Cranes at coastal onshore wind farms in eastern China
abstract: Background With the continued expansion of coastal wind farms toward wetland edges, understanding the mechanisms that drive collision risk for large waterbirds around wind turbines is becoming increasingly important. Methods Based on satellite tracking data from seven Red-crowned Cranes ( Grus japonensis ) in the coastal area of Yancheng, Jiangsu Province, and the geometric parameters of the wind turbine rotor-swept zone (RSZ), we developed a coupling framework linking crane flight heights with the vertical position of the RSZ. title: Georeferencing Historical Zoning Maps and Their Comparison with Current Zoning: GIS-Based Study of Japanese Regional Cities
abstract: Japan’s land-use zoning system, established with the 1919 City Building Act, has fundamentally shaped long-term urban spatial structures. This study clarifies the evolution of Japanese zoning by georeferencing historical maps and comparing them with contemporary GIS data for 11 regional cities. We introduced the Historical Zoning Consistency Index (HZCI) to quantify spatial continuity. abstract: ABSTRACT Crown ether‐regulated metal halides feature programmable host‐guest coordination and structurally defined emissive centers, making them promising for multifunctional scintillation applications. title: Two Littoral Species of Dicranomyia (Idioglochina) (Diptera: Limoniidae) from Japan: a New Species and Transfer of D. monostromia with Notes on Ecology
abstract: The marine-associated crane fly subgenus Idioglochina Alexander, 1921 of the genus Dicranomyia Stephens, 1829 comprises coastal species whose immature stages are associated with shoreline habitats, but its diversity and ecology in Japan remain insufficiently documented. title: Graphene-oxide-templated P/S-codoped hard carbon with a coral-like layered architecture for pseudocapacitance-boosted sodium storage
abstract: Facing lithium resource and cost bottlenecks, low-cost and abundant sodium-ion batteries provide an attractive complement for grid storage. However, graphite anodes cannot accommodate rapid Na⁺ insertion because of their narrow interlayer spacing. Here, inspired by the layered architecture of coral polyps, we construct a flex–hard carbon architecture consisting of an outer phenolic-resin-derived hard carbon layer and an inner graphene oxide (GO)-derived carbon framework. title: GIS-Based Modelling for Evaluating Soil Erosion Patterns in Ravine-Affected Regions of the Yamuna River, India
abstract: Soil erosion poses a significant environmental challenge, particularly in ravine-affected areas where high-intensity rainfall leads to substantial soil loss, resulting in declining soil fertility and the conversion of productive agricultural land into wasteland. The present study focuses on estimating the rate of soil erosion in one of the severely ravine-affected lands along the Yamuna River and examines changes in soil erosion rates over the years. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) Model was employed using various soil erosion estimation parameters in the ArcGIS 10.5 platform.

title: Residential heating emissions tool in the Climate Action Navigator: High-resolution estimation based on open data
abstract: Reducing CO 2 emissions from residential space heating is critical to achieve carbon neutrality, particularly in urban areas. However, effective climate action is often hindered by the lack of precise location-specific emissions data. This study introduces the first web tool for estimating direct (i.e., scope 1) carbon dioxide emissions resulting from space heating of residential buildings at a sub-city scale (100-m resolution). title: Multiple viewpoint visualization of small scale flow phenomena: application to cavitation on an ultrasonic horn tip
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional (3D) characterization of transient multiphase structures remains a persistent challenge, particularly in cavitating flows where vapor–gas interfaces evolve rapidly and exhibit pronounced 3D effects. This work presents a multiple viewpoint imaging system that delivers full 360° coverage of small scale multiphase phenomena using 30 synchronously triggered cameras and microsecond high power illumination. abstract: Nigeria's mining sector was once a major driver of national economic growth during the 1960s and 1970s, but its prominence declined sharply following the rise of the crude oil industry, leaving it with a marginal GDP share of just 0.17% between 2018 and 2022. Reports from the Development Agenda for Western Nigeria Commission highlight that the country's Southwestern states possess rich mineral reserves such as gold, tin, zircon, rutile, feldspar, and quartz giving the region strong potential to emerge as a global mining hub. abstract: The co-occurrence of nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics in marine environments poses complex threats to primary producers, yet the multi-level mechanisms of their combined toxicity remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically investigated the physiological, biochemical, and transcriptomic responses of the marine cyanobacterium Synechococcus sp. title: Spatial variability and multivariate analysis of natural radioactivity in monazite-bearing coastal soils of Odisha, India
abstract: Abstract This study investigates spatial variability in radionuclide distribution and radiological characteristics of coastal soils from Ganjam and Puri, Odisha, India. title: Pollution duration drives divergent pathways of antibiotic and metal resistance gene dissemination in coastal mangrove sediments
abstract: Coastal mangrove sediments are critical reservoirs of antibiotic and heavy metal resistance genes (ARGs/HMRGs). Yet, how pollution history shapes their dissemination remains unclear. We elucidated this by comparing sedimentary resistomes across three distinct ecosystems: a pristine site (BH), a site under mid-term copper stress (BHCu), and a chronically multi-polluted site (FT). title: A Baseline Study of Historical Population Parameters and Recovery Projections for Southern Black Drum Pogonias courbina (Teleostei) After Fishery Collapse in Southern Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term fishery‐dependent datasets for threatened marine fishes are exceptionally rare, yet critical for reconstructing pre‐collapse population states. We analyzed an extensive archive of biological and fishery records for Pogonias courbina collected in southern Brazil during the 1970s–early 1980s, when the stock remained still abundant. title: Spatiotemporal Patterns of Gars in Two Subtropical Estuaries
abstract: Abstract Characterizing drivers of estuarine fish assemblages provides valuable insights into estuarine ecology and how each species may react to stressors such as climate change and anthropogenic disturbances. Although they are known to inhabit estuaries, gars are managed as freshwater species and little is known about their movements, reproduction, or other ecological requirements. abstract: Groundwater resource protection is a worldwide issue because groundwater plays a crucial role in meeting water supply demands for both natural ecosystems and human activities. Effective groundwater management and protection therefore require appropriate approaches for assessing contamination risks and identifying areas that are particularly vulnerable to pollution. In this study, a GIS-based DRASTIC model was applied to assess groundwater vulnerability in Lai City, southern Chad. abstract: Bacteria emit volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that can be targeted for disease detection. Biological olfactory systems have keen senses of smell, can detect VOCs at low concentrations, and are naturally adapted to classifying mixtures of VOCs as odors. Here, we employed locust (Schistocerca americana) olfactory neural circuitry to differentiate biofilm and planktonic cultures of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus using their odors. Their broad‐spectrum adhesive behavior has inspired the development of many underwater adhesive and coating strategies based on catecholamine polymers (such as polydopamine); however, their complex coating processes and underlying molecular mechanisms (aggregation, deposition, and polymerization) are still not fully understood. abstract: Abstract Understanding which animal produces a sound is essential for animal communication studies and for estimating cue rates for passive acoustic monitoring. In marine environments, biologging tags are used to study vocal behaviour, but efficient underwater sound transmission makes it challenging to identify whether the call is produced by the tagged (focal) animal. abstract: Microplastic pollution has emerged as a critical environmental issue globally, particularly in aquatic ecosystems impacted by industrial and urban activities. This study investigated the distribution of microplastics (MPs), polymer composition, and co-occurring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the Okulu Aleto River, Nigeria. abstract: Frost increases thermal resistance and air-side pressure drop, causes frequent defrosting, and thereby deteriorates overall system efficiency. title: Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Microplastics in Water and Surface Sediments Along the Jawi River–Kakap Estuary, West Kalimantan, Indonesia
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous contaminants in river-estuary systems but their distribution in the water column vs surface sediments in tropical regions is still poorly understood. The present study aims to investigate the spatial and temporal distribution of MPs abundance and properties in water and surface sediments at the Jawi River–Kakap Estuary, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. title: Maritime pine afforestation drives coastal dune habitat contraction and threatens the rare shrub Corema album in NW Spain
abstract: Abstract Afforestation is a widespread driver of land-use change and biodiversity loss, particularly in open habitats such as sand dune systems. Coastal dunes are among the most vulnerable ecosystems, facing multiple pressures including afforestation. Rare specialist species inhabiting these habitats, such as the endemic Iberian shrub Corema album , are especially susceptible to habitat alteration. title: Waste heat recovery from power plants for solar desalination: a mechanical power engineering approach
abstract: Abstract This study presents a thermal design of solar stills by utilizing waste heat from thermal power plant cooling water. The main objective is to enhance energy recovery with solar still technology and minimize mechanical energy consumption. This paper introduces an innovation approach to desalinate the seawater by the free energy from the cooling water of power plants. title: Physiological and transcriptomic responses of Mallotus paniculatus to sustained drought stress: Implications for tropical coastal shelter forest restoration
abstract: Drought constrains seedling establishment and ecological restoration in tropical coastal forests, where native pioneer species are needed to diversify vulnerable shelterbelt plantations. Mallotus paniculatus is a common pioneer tree with broad environmental adaptability, but its drought-response mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated physiological measurements, full-length and short-read transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and qRT-PCR to characterize the responses of M. paniculatus seedlings to sustained drought stress. abstract: Archaeologists have used obsidian artifact tracing to address a variety of issues related to the interaction of prehistoric groups. This study focuses on an area in southwestern Arizona and northwestern Sonora, Mexico where several prehistoric groups overlapped and exploited well documented obsidian sources. Our study includes more than 900 obsidian artifacts from over 300 sites and use of GIS analysis to examine source distributions and regional patterning.
