abstract: Watershed degradation from human encroachment is a worldwide phenomenon and a keystone driver of erosion, transport and deposition of sediment material into downstream lakes and other water bodies. Despite global recognition of the growing scale of these linkages, comprehensive evaluation and ranking of the range of specific parameters associated catchment destruction and subsequent sediment movement, or those contributing to its mitigation, has rarely been undertaken. abstract: In Yellow Sea green tides (YSGTs), the macroalga Ulva prolifera exhibits negligible competitive superiority in the attached growth stage but rapidly outcompetes co-occurring Blidingia sp. after shifting to floating lifestyles. While the physiological basis of this transition remains unclear. title: Coupled salinity, nutrient, and trace-element patterns in arid agricultural soils of hail, Saudi Arabia: an integrated laboratory–GIS screening assessment
abstract: Introduction Arid agricultural soils are dynamic systems in which groundwater irrigation, intense evaporation, limited natural leaching, and heterogeneous parent materials jointly regulate salinity, nutrient accumulation, and potentially contaminating element mobility. abstract: The long–short wave interaction (LSWI) system governs the resonant energy exchange between a rapidly oscillating short-wave envelope and a slowly varying long-wave mean field, a coupling that arises in stratified ocean flows, internal wave dynamics, nonlinear optics, and plasma physics and that single-component nonlinear Schrödinger models cannot capture. title: How Well Can the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) Satellite Mission Observe Irrigation Canals?
abstract: Abstract The capability of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite for observing irrigation canals has remained relatively unexplored. Here, we assess SWOT observability of irrigation canal networks across 22 Asian countries using a new confidence level (CL) metric. Validation against in situ gauge observations showed that higher CL corresponds to significantly lower water‐level retrieval error. abstract: Access to potable water in oil-producing communities of the Niger Delta remains constrained by decades of hydrocarbon exploration and inadequate environmental management. title: Natural sinkholes of Abruzzo (central Italy): expansion of ISPRA National Database and susceptibility analysis
abstract: The term sinkhole refers to sudden ground subsidence caused by natural or anthropogenic factors and represents a locally significant geological hazard. abstract: ABSTRACT The early evolutionary history of modern domestic horses ( Equus caballus / Equus ferus caballus ), known as the DOM2 lineage, is well documented due to numerous archaeological and ancient DNA (aDNA) studies. abstract: Abstract Ecotypic divergence in Atlantic cod ( Gadus morhua ) is well established for adult fish, but the extent to which juveniles differ is still poorly understood. abstract: Benthic organisms have relatively limited mobility and long life cycles, enabling them to comprehensively reflect long-term changes in water quality, sediment conditions, and hydrological conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Marine mammal strandings are common occurrences that attract public and scientific interest. Stranding data can provide important information for rarely sighted species, but while regional and national stranding databases do exist in some areas, cross‐database communication and data sharing are limited. abstract: ABSTRACT Balaenopterid whales are major consumers in pelagic ecosystems and play a fundamental role in marine food webs. abstract: Hurricane Threats and Impacts (HTI) graphics communicate the spatial extent and severity of tropical cyclone hazards but provide limited information about when hazards will arrive, creating challenges for time-sensitive protective decision-making. abstract: Robust wideband beamforming is critical for passive acoustic sensing systems operating in challenging underwater environments characterized by impulsive noise, interference, and array uncertainties. Conventional robust wideband beamforming methods are generally developed under the Gaussian noise assumption and rely on second-order sample covariance matrix estimation. abstract: The origin and evolution of fluids in subduction zones are still poorly understood, largely because of the complex interactions between deep lithospheric fluids and meteoric water in the shallow geothermal systems. title: Sex-dependent behavioural responses of Palaemon varians to submarine power cable electromagnetic fields
abstract: The expansion of submarine power cables (SPCs) associated with offshore renewable energy is increasing the prevalence of electromagnetic fields (EMFs) in coastal environments. These fields fall within the sensory detection range of many crustaceans, however behavioural consequences, particularly in smaller decapods, remain poorly investigated. abstract: Introduction Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose significant threats to aquatic ecosystems, fisheries, and public health worldwide. abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms are recalcitrant to conventional antibiotic therapy due to their extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, in which Psl polysaccharide serves as the primary structural scaffold. PslG glycoside hydrolase can degrade Psl and trigger biofilm dispersal, yet the dynamic glycan release profile and metabolic consequences remain poorly characterized. abstract: Communities’ dependence on aquaculture ponds as their main source of livelihood has resulted in the extensive conversion of mangroves, which then becomes a serious concern for the sustainability of coastal areas in Indramayu Regency, West Java. The economic advantages of aquaculture should be in line with the ecological role of mangroves in achieving sustainable silvofishery management. abstract: Petal color fading in cut flowers of the herbaceous peony 'Coral Sunset' coincides with flower senescence, yet the underlying physiological and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we integrated physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolomic data to elucidate how 2 h pulse treatments with nanosilver (NS, an ethylene action inhibitor) and ethephon (CEPA, an ethylene-releasing agent) influence petal color fading in 'Coral Sunset' peonies. title: TOS²CA: The Thematic Observation Search, Segmentation, Collation and Analysis System
abstract: Background Thematic Observation Search, Segmentation, Collation and Analysis (TOS 2 CA) is an end-to-end system that allows the user to define, collect, and visualize data relevant to naturally occurring phenomena that can be used for current and future Earth science missions and research. Methods TOS 2 CA is a cloud-native, Python-based software library that allows users to define physical phenomena using a conditional threshold to identify occurrences of them in a dataset, tracking them spatially and temporally, and generating a series of masks for the user. title: Spatiotemporal and demographic patterns in commercial catches of tope (Galeorhinus galeus) and spurdog (Squalus acanthias)
abstract: Tope ( Galeorhinus galeus ) and spurdog ( Squalus acanthias ) have been historically overexploited by fisheries, leading to global population declines. Despite both species having well-documented migration patterns and being known to aggregate by sex and life-stage, interactions with commercial fisheries in the Northeast Atlantic have not been assessed in relation to seasonality, sex ratio and/or life-stage. abstract: Swordfish (Xiphias gladius) is managed in the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea as three major stocks, although their correspondence with underlying genomic population structure remains uncertain. abstract: ABSTRACT Ecosystem response to forest management and disturbance is governed by many factors and their interactions. This has historically made it difficult for practitioners to reach consensus on ideal management prescriptions and restoration activities. Forest management to decrease wildfire susceptibility and improve water supply is often informed by estimates of live fuel moisture (LFM). abstract: Satisfaction with the urban environment is among the crucial elements of the quality of urban life. This study examines the results of the most recent wave of the Eurobarometer survey (year 2023), covering 83 European cities, to explore which city characteristics are associated with higher and lower perceived quality of different urban environment areas - air quality, noise levels, green spaces and city cleanliness. abstract: Invertebrate Systematics learning requires physical specimens, as digital media often fail to capture complete morphological traits. Addressing this limitation, this study aims to explore and characterize Bivalve and Gastropod shells from the Gadon coast to evaluate their feasibility as dry learning specimens. abstract: In recent years, offshore wind energy systems (OWES) have risen to prominence as a compelling avenue for capitalizing on the unfailing and consistent wind resources of the open sea, chiefly to supply electricity to coastal regions. Even so, wind intermittency complicates OWES control, reducing energy extraction when generator control proves ineffective. abstract: Vibrio europaeus is an emerging bacterial pathogen responsible for recurrent mass mortality outbreaks in shellfish aquaculture, yet the environmental mechanisms regulating its virulence remain poorly understood. abstract: Peri-urban coastal areas such as Timbulsloko Village, Demak Regency, face increasing development pressure and chronic inundation as a slow-onset hazard that affects residents, public assets, and local micro-enterprises. This study aims to reveal the spatial distribution and vulnerability of public assets and local economic infrastructure to inundation, as well as the forms of adaptive resilience demonstrated by micro-enterprises in responding to changing environmental conditions. title: Moored observations of the deep western boundary current east of the Gagua Ridge in the Northwestern Pacific
abstract: Abstract The deep western boundary current (DWBC) of the Pacific serves as a lower limb of the meridional overturning circulation that has been identified as a key component of the global climate system. title: Mapping potential global change impacts on biodiversity important areas of the contiguous US
abstract: Global trends illustrate unprecedented declines in biodiversity. The main threats driving these trends include climate change, land- and sea-use change, pollution, over-exploitation, and invasive species. Strategic allocation of conservation resources is critical to address the drivers of biodiversity loss and safeguard biodiversity and its benefits to people. abstract: This work presents the preliminary design of a floating dry dock with a rated lifting capacity of 10,000~t, intended to operate in the Bay of Cartagena, Colombia. title: Sabkha systems of the United Arab Emirates as integrated carbonate–evaporite laboratories: facies architecture, brine evolution, critical-element potential, and geoheritage significance
abstract: Sabkha systems of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) represent one of the world’s most extensively documented modern carbonate–evaporite settings, yet their multidisciplinary significance has not previously been synthesized within a unified process-based framework. This review integrates sedimentological architecture, hydrogeochemical dynamics, geomicrobiological mediation, radiogeochemical behaviour, and resource-oriented implications across coastal and inland sabkha domains. title: Photochemical production of ammonium from dissolved organic nitrogen in arctic surface waters
abstract: In sunlit freshwaters, dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) can be degraded photochemically to ammonium (NH4+; photo-production of NH4+). While this NH4+ could be an important source of N to primary and secondary producers, there are too few studies to assess its relative importance in sunlit freshwaters. This study quantified rates and controls of photo-production of NH4+ in ten stream and lake waters in the Alaskan Arctic. abstract: Carbon stock assessment is a critical component of climate change mitigation, particularly in coastal areas experiencing rapid land-use change. This study aims to estimate aboveground carbon stocks, potential CO₂ emissions, and the economic value of carbon across various land use and land cover (LULC) types in Sungai Kakap District, Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. abstract: Introduction. The study aimed to identify spatial differences in the concentrations of Zn, Cd, and Pb in soils of the northern, northeastern, and western industrial belts of Ust-Kamenogorsk. Soil samples were collected in accordance with the sanitary protection zones of industrial enterprises and the prevailing wind directions. abstract: ABSTRACT The large yellow croaker has experienced significant declines in wild stocks, while its populations have been replenished through diverse aquaculture systems, making it currently the most cultivated marine fish in China. The large yellow croaker farming industry has suffered greatly from bacterial and viral diseases. Given the economic importance of this species, extensive studies have been conducted on its genome and immune responses. abstract: This study evaluates the application of remote sensing and GIS techniques for mapping geothermal potential areas in the central-western Taiz, Yemen. The objective is to identify prospective areas for hydrothermal water exploration. Geothermal potential mapping was based on nine factors derived from remote sensing, geological, and geophysical datasets. abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) require three‐dimensional (3D) path planning in environments where computational efficiency is as critical as solution quality. abstract: Archaeological research in the western Pacific has documented a range of terrestrial fauna that may have been the target of Lapita-era foraging. How can our knowledge of extinct and extant fauna aid in understanding prey ranking and targeting by foragers in the early years of island colonization? This study employs the Prey Choice model and biological data related to foraging (i.e., ease of mass capture, locomotor skills, hazards, processing requirements, and caloric yield) to identify the ranking of potential foraging targets in Lapita-era Fiji. title: One-step MCDA-CRISPR/Cas12b platform for point-of-care testing of Shewanella algae
abstract: Shewanella algae (S. algae) is an emerging marine zoonotic pathogen capable of causing various infections with a high mortality rate. Existing detection methods for S. algae tend to be nonspecific, complicated, and time-consuming. abstract: Microbial communities are integral to recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS), yet differences between planktonic and carrier-associated communities in early Litopenaeus vannamei culture remain poorly characterised. abstract: This study aims to design and develop an Arduino Mega 2560-based Integrated Ship Water Ballast System to improve the monitoring and control of ballast water distribution on a ship prototype. The system integrates A02YYUW ultrasonic sensors to measure water levels in four ballast tanks, an MPU6050 sensor to detect pitch and roll angles, relay modules to control eight ballast pumps, and a web dashboard for real-time monitoring. abstract: Reconstructing Holocene surface-water hydrography in the North Atlantic is complicated by the different seasonal and ecological sensitivities of commonly used biological proxies. To address this, we introduce the Coccolithophore Hydrography Index (CHI), a new coccolith assemblage-based environmental proxy. abstract: The study of geologic relics is gaining particular relevance today, as geological objects are a kind of natural archives that contain reliable information about the geological history and development of a territory. abstract: Bureaucratic reform is a strategic agenda for realizing effective, transparent, accountable, and responsive governance to global dynamics. Increasing demands for quality public services, digital transformation, and strengthening institutional capacity have driven the development of research on bureaucratic reform in various countries. title: Incorporating landscape context into species distribution models improves predictions for migratory shorebirds
abstract: Migratory shorebirds are declining worldwide due to coastal habitat loss, making the identification of important habitats a conservation priority. While species distribution models are widely used to map potential habitats, they typically rely on environmental conditions measured at individual locations and underuse the surrounding landscape context. abstract: The study examined impact of perennial pluvial flooding on the architectural quality and performance of residential buildings in selected Areas of Port Harcourt Metropolis. Resilience Theory guided the theoretical framework of this study. The methodology integrates both primary and secondary data sources. With a population of 1,416, a sample frame of 708, and a sample size of 512 determined using the Taro Yamane method, the study employed field observations, surveys, and statistical analysis, including descriptive statistics. abstract: This study investigates the crustal architecture and tectonomagmatic evolution of the central Chilean Andes (32-34° S) through new U-Pb zircon geochronology. abstract: Abstract Advances in genomics have revealed a diversity of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (phylum Nucleocytoviricota) that infect eukaryotes, but their ecology beyond the oceans remains poorly understood. We recover 208 Nucleocytoviricota genomes, including 205 putative new species and 33 novel virus-host linkages by sampling 87 lakes spanning 30° of latitude from southern Italy to northern Norway. abstract: Mangroves are key coastal ecosystems increasingly exposed to potentially toxic elements (PTEs), yet the processes controlling their distribution among soil and plant compartments remain incompletely understood. This exploratory study evaluated the compartmentalization and mobility of PTEs within a mangrove soil–plant system from southeastern Brazil using a combined approach based on sequential translocation factors (TFs) and soil-to-leaf transfer factors (SLTFs). abstract: Picophytoplankton are a group of photosynthetic, unicellular organisms, making them key primary producers in aquatic ecosystems. These cells numerically dominate in oceans and lakes where picophytoplankton communities contain phenotypic subpopulations that correspond to biogeographic patterns. In rivers, however, such community dynamics are less studied. abstract: Abstract Background Forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) provides vital investigative leads by predicting externally visible characteristics (EVCs). abstract: Barrier islands are at the forefront of climate-driven changes, with their resiliency threatened by rapid fluctuations in the physical drivers that shape them. Quantifying magnitudes and directions of storm-driven sediment fluxes and rates and modes of sediment recovery is essential for predicting barrier island trajectories. Enhalus acoroides , a dominant large tropical seagrass, has experienced marked reductions in distribution and abundance, yet information on its population genetic structure remains limited. abstract: The reported construction-material factory linked to Russian investment near Bali's Tahura Ngurah Rai highlights a recurring difficulty in environmental governance: the coexistence of land certificates, business registrations, spatial restrictions and conservation boundaries. This article examines the legal consequences of that overlap through normative legal research using statutory, conceptual and documentary case approaches. title: Building on sand: state capacity, livelihoods, and the limits of environmental governance in Cabo Verde
abstract: Cabo Verde has built an extensive environmental policy framework, ratifying major multilateral agreements and enacting decree-laws that formally regulate the exploitation of natural resources. Yet on Santiago Island, small-scale illegal extraction of development minerals by low-income households continues to cause severe degradation of beaches, watersheds and hillsides. title: Spatializing Simdogihaeng travelogue (1906): place recognition and heritage authorization on Ganghwa Island
abstract: In the early 20th century, Go Jae-hyung authored Simdogihaeng, a travelogue focusing on Ganghwa Island. This study explores the narratives in Simdogihaeng, leveraging theories of cognition and literature as its theoretical foundation. It defines “recognition” in narrative contexts through the lens of epistemology. This approach provides a solid foundation for understanding the intricacies of narrative construction and interpretation in literature. title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
abstract: Abstract Urban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. title: Brief communication: Limitations of medical X-ray computed tomography for estimating ice content in permafrost samples
abstract: X-ray Computed tomography (CT) is increasingly used to estimate ice contents in permafrost samples. In this study, CT-derived estimates of volumetric ice content obtained from medical CT scans were compared with laboratory measurements for 261 samples from northern Canada (Nunavut and Yukon). The results shows that medical CT systematically underestimates ice content in sediment-rich and organic-poor samples, and overestimated it in ice-rich, organic-rich samples. title: STRENGTHENING PEDIATRIC EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS IN REMOTE AND EMERGING TOURISM DESTINATIONS UNDER SAUDI VISION 2030
abstract: Saudi Arabia's rapid development of remote coastal, desert and heritage tourism destinations create a distinctive pediatric emergency preparedness challenge. Children differ from adults in airway anatomy, physiology, medication dosing, equipment needs, communication and psychosocial response; low-frequency, high-acuity events can therefore expose serious capability gaps in isolated facilities. title: Spatial–temporal distribution characteristics and influencing factors of immovable cultural heritage in Jiangxi Province, China
abstract: Immovable cultural heritage (IMCH) constitutes a vital material record of human civilization and represents a precious asset shared by all humanity. This study integrates Geographic Information System (GIS) spatial analysis and the Geodetector model, taking 1,032 IMCH sites in Jiangxi Province as the research object, to systematically investigate their spatiotemporal distribution characteristics and driving factors, and on this basis proposes strategies for their conservation and sustainable development. title: Successful Hemostasis With Direct Clipping Using a Tapered‐Tip Hood and Slim Endoscope for Colonic Diverticular Bleeding Refractory to Endoscopic Band Ligation: A Case Report
abstract: Endoscopic band ligation (EBL) is performed for hemostasis in patients with colonic diverticular bleeding (CDB) due to its low rebleeding rate. However, suction and ligation are not successful in some cases. We describe the case of a 93-year-old woman with CDB in whom EBL failed. Because of tissue rigidity, the sigmoid diverticulum could not be adequately suctioned into the ligation device, which resulted in band detachment and subsequent rebleeding. title: From dental adhesives to injectable hemostats: a scoping review of antimicrobial biomaterials for oral soft-tissue bleeding
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of acute oral hemorrhage in emergency settings is frequently complicated by saliva, high vascularity, and microbial presence. This scoping review maps the emerging field of multifunctional, dental-inspired biomaterials. The objective is to synthesize evidence on injectable materials providing rapid hemostasis and antimicrobial protection, while acknowledging the current transition from laboratory models to clinical applications. title: Archaeological micromorphology in Latin America: an overview
abstract: Micromorphology helps to reveal fundamental aspects of archaeological sites and landscapes that are invisible to the naked eye. Apart from discerning human contributions from patterns of natural sediment/soil formation, deposition, and alteration, this technique, coupled with others, has been able to showcase specific human activities hidden in the archaeological record. Over the last couple of decades, micromorphology has slowly entered the realm of archaeological techniques in Latin America and neighboring regions. title: New Research at Monte Negro, Oaxaca
abstract: Abstract Between 1937 and 1940, a team of Mexican archaeologists led by Alfonso Caso excavated at Monte Negro, a defensible mountaintop settlement in western Oaxaca. Their foundational insights into the Late Formative period (ca. 300–100 BC) were later augmented by surveys and excavations in other valleys of western Oaxaca, which revealed the emergence of contemporaneous hilltop centers. Archaeological research at Monte Negro resumed in the early 2000s with total station mapping and intensive surface collections, followed in 2023–2024 by the first excavations outside of the monumental core. title: Effects of calcareous fine contents on the dynamic behavior of calcareous sand
abstract: To investigate the influence of calcareous fine contents ( FC ) on the dynamic behavior of calcareous sand, a series of undrained cyclic triaxial tests was performed on calcareous sand-fine mixtures with relative densities ( D r ) of 40% and 80%, incorporating FC values of 0%, 10%, 40%, 70%, and 100%. title: Building adaptive capacity of US Gulf Coast city practitioners to extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract Building city practitioners’ capacity to prepare for and respond to climate change-driven events can increase coastal cities’ resilience. We conducted a first-of-its-kind mixed methods research project from 2021 to 2023 with 46 US Gulf Coast small and midsize cities to measure the effectiveness of an adaptive capacity-building intervention: a stormwater planning tool called FloodWise Communities (FWC) deployed through the engagement between researchers and practitioners in each city. City practitioners were surveyed pre- and post-intervention between September 2021 and December 2022.

abstract: This study aimed to develop and evaluate contextually integrated Augmented Reality (AR) flashcards about mangrove ecosystems to enhance scientific literacy in biology education, addressing the critical gap between abstract classroom instruction and complex field ecology. Using a Research and Development design with the ADDIE framework and a quasi-experimental study with a control group (94 experimental students, 100 control students) in five coastal high schools. title: Rising Connectivity, Shifting Hubs: The Evolving Network and Governance Challenges of Global Wild‐Sourced Trade
abstract: ABSTRACT Global wild‐sourced wildlife trade is structured not only by the intensity and composition of traded species, but also by the routes, hubs, and redistribution pathways that connect countries/territories into an intricate network. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of trade networks over time is essential for identifying emerging governance challenges and conservation priorities. title: A novel bacterial symbiont in the seaweed Gracilaria tenuistipitata and its promising anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative potential in relation to special secreted metabolites
abstract: Marine macroalgae host compositionally complex microbiomes that constitute an evolutionarily refined, yet largely unexplored source of structurally diverse natural products. Thus, the bioactivities of the algae may be related to those of their associated microorganisms. Here we describe the discovery of strain S.100, an endophytic bacterium isolated from the red alga Gracilaria tenuistipitata and displaying remarkable anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities, through a primary screening on ethyl acetate (EtAc), chloroform and n-hexane extracts of its culture. title: Bioinformatics pipelines for Metagenomics: A review of data processing and functional annotation approaches
abstract: The diverse environment from soil and air to marine ecosystems and the human gut and hidden places on the earth is a treasure island of metagenomes of microbial consortia. Metagenomics, with the capability of culture-independent characterization of microbial communities can help in understanding the complexity of microbial populations. abstract: Geospatial analyses are becoming fundamentally important on a global scale for the sake of sustainability. abstract: Traditional early medieval historiography frequently treats the early Saxons as a homogeneous, migrating ethnic entity. This paper explores this paradigm by conducting an exploratory quantitative textual and spatial analysis of early medieval identity construction, focusing on the maritime networks of the North Sea and the territorial river systems of the Rhine-Meuse delta in Northwest Europe. title: Spatial Analysis of Atmospheric Pollutants in An-Najaf Governorate Based on Sentinel-5 Satellite Observations
abstract: Sentinel-5P satellite imagery, in combination with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), was utilized to analyze the spatial distribution of the atmospheric pollutant gases—ozone (O₃), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), and carbon monoxide (CO)—across An-Najaf Governorate in central Iraq. The study aimed to assess patterns of pollutant concentration and identify the anthropogenic and environmental factors influencing their distribution. title: Ecosystem engineers and functional dominance: when species loss matters for ecosystem function
abstract: Understanding when and why species loss affects community function in natural communities remains an open question in ecology. Recent cross‐system analyses have shown that functional dominance is associated with whether species loss matters: in communities dominated by few high‐performing species, lost species contribute little to function. But the question is what generates functional dominance in the first place. Here we examine whether an ecosystem engineer can generate it. title: Extensive horizontal gene transfer drives microbial adaptation and diversification in Kermadec Trench hadal microbiomes
abstract: Hadal trenches, plunging beyond six kilometers depth, harbor a dynamic yet enigmatic microbial biosphere. From ~10 km depth Kermadec Trench sediments, we integrated metagenomics, in situ metatranscriptomics, and phylogenetics to reconstruct 300 prokaryotic species and 186,496 viral populations. title: An updated census of southern elephant seals Mirounga leonina at South Georgia using satellite imagery
abstract: Historically, South Georgia supported the largest breeding population of southern elephant seals Mirounga leonina globally. Yet since 1995, this population has remained largely unassessed and was presumed to be stable. Here, we provide an updated assessment of this sub-Antarctic population and demonstrate the application of sub-meter resolution satellite imagery as a valuable approach for censusing an extensive, remote, and challenging breeding population. abstract: Backgroud Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) has become a predominant nosocomial pathogen worldwide, with biofilm formation and quorum sensing (QS) primarily responsible for its high antimicrobial tolerance and clinical refractory infections. Targeting bacterial virulence rather than conventional bactericidal strategies represents a promising alternative to combat multidrug-resistant CRAB. abstract: This thesis sought to determine to what extent photogrammetry can reduce the time and resources required for property assessment when parcels are affected by expropriations linked to infrastructure projects taking the district of Ventanilla during 2025 as the case study. The work followed an applied approach with a quasi experimental design combining drone flights GIS based geoprocessing and document review. abstract: Abstract Digital traces from social media increasingly shape how tourist preferences are observed and interpreted, yet attraction-related attention is often treated as a single aggregate indicator, with limited consideration of where this attention comes from and how attractions are discursively framed. title: A study on the spatial characteristics and influencing factors of traditional villages in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Abstract As key repositories of regional cultural heritage and important carriers of rural revitalization, traditional villages require scientific spatial planning and adaptive conservation. This study examines 4736 traditional villages across 11 provincial-level jurisdictions in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), using 10 km × 10 km geographic grids and integrating GIS spatial analysis, the Geodetector model and the MGWR model to unpack their spatial distribution patterns and driving determinants. abstract: ABSTRACT Many engineering courses are still organized according to a predominantly deductive and content‐oriented approach: theoretical foundations are introduced first, while authentic disciplinary activity is often postponed to later stages of the curriculum. This contribution argues that such an approach is insufficient for sustainable competence development in mechanics education. abstract: ABSTRACT To investigate oral health in the fragmented human remains from the Punic necropolis of Monte Luna, Sardinia, and evaluate what dental pathologies reveal about lifeways and diet. Human remains from 227 individuals recovered from 70 tombs were analyzed, including 21 females, 16 males (> 15 years), and 59 non‐adults (1–15 years). The sample comprised 2362 teeth. title: Land Use/ Land Cover Dynamics and the Decline of Grazing Resources in Dauchi Grazing Reserve, Adamawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change is a major driver of rangeland degradation, threatening grazing resources and pastoral livelihoods in the Guinea and Sudan savanna ecosystems of northeastern Nigeria. This study evaluates the impact of LULC change on grazing resources in Dauchi Grazing Reserve, Song LGA, Adamawa State, Nigeria, using multi-temporal satellite imagery covering forty years. Satellite data were processed and classified using supervised classification techniques within a Geographic Information System (GIS) and remote sensing framework. title: Design and hardware performance of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system with local data storage infrastructure
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of a LoRa-based vehicle tracking system, emphasizing its hardware architecture and field performance. The system uses custom-built end nodes based on Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 (V3) boards (an ESP32-S3 microcontroller with an integrated Semtech SX1262 transceiver) and u-blox NEO-6 M GPS modules, which transmit position data to a centrally located LoRa receiver node. title: Semi-automatic identification of river terraces in steep mountainous regions of Nepal
abstract: This study identifies river terraces in steep mountainous terrain using a semi-automatic approach for the Tamor River Basin in eastern Nepal. River terraces play a critical role in irrigation, soil conservation, and sustainable agriculture in Nepal’s hill regions, yet their watershed-scale mapping remains limited due to the labor-intensive nature of conventional field-based methods. To address this gap, the study integrates remote sensing, GIS, and machine learning within a cloud-based environment to efficiently delineate terrace landforms and evaluate their suitability for irrigation planning

title: The endless invasions: Spatiotemporal patterns of non-native insects in China
abstract: Biological invasions have been defined as one striking indicator of the Anthropocene epoch, with more species being translocated beyond their native range by human activities. The inventory of non-native species in a region provides basic information for further exploration of biological invasions. We compiled a checklist of non-native insects in China and then analyzed their diversity at species level and invasion patterns. abstract: Hypersaline brines (salinity >10 wt%) generated by the water, energy, and agricultural sectors present a significant challenge for sustainable wastewater management. Although solar-driven interfacial evaporation offers an energy-efficient route for brine treatment and zero-liquid-discharge operation, persistent salt accumulation hinders long-term performance and operational stability. abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive aquaculture practices heavily reliant on conventional energy sources have contributed significantly to environmental degradation, primarily through greenhouse gas emissions. abstract: Informal patron-client arrangements in capture fisheries can combine vessel finance, employment, social assistance, and market control, creating both protection and dependency. This study examined how boat owner-crew labor relations are reproduced and how a feasible transformation could be designed at Tenau Coastal Fishing Port and Oeba Fish Landing Base, Kupang City, Indonesia. abstract: This study explains the living conditions of the coastal Bajo tribe in Muna Regency, Indonesia, and examines their potential for improving housing quality through a community-led self-help approach. Adopting a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, fieldwork was conducted across three purposively selected vulnerable settlements: Tapitapi, Lagasa, and Pasikuta villages (N = 259). abstract: Abstract Lithium is a critical mineral for advancing greener technologies. Extraction of lithium ions (Li⁺) from sea salt, minerals, and waste is important, but has been hindered by the lack of extraction methods that offer both high selectivity and strong lithium affinity. Here, we report a dioxaborole-linked, head-to-tail assembled macrocycle – termed borphyrin – featuring a rigid cavity with a 16-crown-4-like configuration. title: ASSESSMENT OF HEAVY METAL AND ARSENIC CONTAMINATION IN THE WATER AND SEDIMENTS OF LAKE BEYŞEHIR, KONYA
abstract: Beyşehir Lake, located within the provinces of Konya and Isparta, is Turkey’s third-largest lake and the country’s largest freshwater resource. Increasing industrialization, agricultural activities, and untreated wastewater discharges within the basin have raised concerns regarding heavy metal and metalloid contamination, particularly due to the growing number of firearms manufacturing facilities in the region. title: Ultrasound diagnostics of superficial (subcutaneous) dirofilariasis
abstract: A clinical observation of superficial dirofilariasis in a 38-year-old man with a subcutaneous formation of the anterior abdominal wall is presented, demonstrating the critical role of ultrasound in the diagnosis of parasitic infections in the context of increasing morbidity. The key diagnostic feature was the visualization of mobile tubular structures during long-term ultrasound scanning, which allowed us to suspect a parasitic nature of the lesion before surgical intervention. abstract: When discussed together, menstrual and socioenvironmental health often focus on questions of hygiene and risk management, centering the materialities, distribution, and disposal of menstrual products. The toxicity of disposable menstrual products has long been a matter of concern, with growing public attention to endocrine disruptors (EDs) accompanying the expansion of a marketplace for “eco-friendly” options. abstract: Fluvial sediment transport plays a key role in geomorphological and hydrological processes, influencing river morphology, watershed and coastal sediment balances, and the environmental response to climatic and anthropogenic changes. title: Organic acid-associated antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of Lactobacillus rhamnosus ATCC 7469 against Acinetobacter baumannii and Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Considering the relevance of biofilms in bacterial resistance and the need for innovative therapies against pathogenic microorganisms, alternative strategies using probiotics as antimicrobial agents have emerged. This study aimed to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of the cell-free supernatant (CFS) of Lactobacillus rhamnosus ATCC 7469 against biofilm-forming strains of Acinetobacter baumannii and Staphylococcus aureus. title: Urban flood risk and the structural importance of cities in a spatial interaction network: evidence from the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Urban agglomeration-scale flood risk assessments commonly treat cities as independent spatial units, overlooking structural dependencies created by administrative adjacency and upstream–downstream hydrological connectivity. Using the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration (YRDUA) as the study area, we assessed flood risk from 1990 to 2020, constructed a flood risk spatial interaction network, and developed a staged XGBoost framework comprising baseline, network, and interaction models. title: Low-cost Efficient Wireless Intelligent Sensors (LEWIS) IoT-Based Rainfall Monitoring
abstract: Rainfall measurement with high spatial and temporal resolution is critical for flood forecasting, drought mitigation, and disaster preparedness. Rainfall patterns are highly variable, both geographically and over time. This variability presents a significant challenge for monitoring, as rain gauges can accurately capture temporal patterns only at a single location. Furthermore, the high cost of commercial instruments restricts their widespread deployment, and rain gauge networks often fail to adequately capture the spatial heterogeneity of precipitation patterns. title: Constructing the Enemy: ‘Us-vs-Them’ discourse in Farage, Le Pen, and Abascal
abstract: This article investigates the discursive construction of ideological antagonism in the speeches of Nigel Farage (UK), Marine Le Pen (France), and Santiago Abascal (Spain), focusing on how each leader produces and legitimizes polarized “us-versus-them” frameworks. Drawing from Critical Discourse Analysis (van Dijk, 1998; Wodak, 2015), the study examines a small corpus of high-stakes public speeches during electoral or national moments in which the “enemy” is explicitly named–be it immigrants, elites, supranational institutions, or political rivals. title: Genetic Classification of Crude Oils from Cretaceous Reservoirs in the Ratawi Oil Field, South of Iraq: Molecular Evidence for Multiple Source Facies
abstract: The current study evaluated the genetic characterization and differentiation of oil families in the units of the Yamama, Nahr Umr, and Mishrif reservoirs of the Ratawi oil field, south of Iraq. The combination of bulk properties, stable carbon isotopes, and molecular biomarkers reveals a distinct pattern of hydrocarbon generation, migration, and accumulation, influenced by salt-induced tectonics in the studyarea. title: Influence of phengite and water on partial melting of basaltic rocks in Earth’s early crust: an experimental study
abstract: Tonalite–trondhjemite–granodiorite (TTG) suites dominate the Archean continental crust and are widely interpreted as products of partial melting of basaltic sources under granulite to eclogite facies conditions. However, their coexistence with potassium-rich, peraluminous granites remains unresolved. In the Barberton Greenstone Belt, Ca-poor, potassic granitoids occur as pebbles and felsic volcanic rocks that are older than or coeval with TTGs, raising questions about their petrogenetic link. title: Floristic Diversity, Habitat Preference, and Ecological Distribution of Zingiberaceae Species in Different Regions of West Bengal
abstract: The Zingiberaceae, a family of aromatic, rhizomatous herbs with its principal centre of diversity in tropical and subtropical Asia, is well represented in the state of West Bengal, which spans an unusually steep environmental gradient from the humid Eastern Himalayan foothills to the saline Sundarbans delta within a comparatively small area. title: Holistic Cyclone Preparedness in a River Nomadic Community: A Study on Manta Community, Bauphal Upazila, Bangladesh
abstract: Cyclones remain a serious threat to Bangladesh's coastal communities. However, their impacts are not felt equally across all geographical locations and sociodemographic groups. The community of Bauphal, Patuakhali, is especially vulnerable because its livelihoods are tied to rivers, boats, fishing, and seasonal mobility rather than fixed land-based settlement. Our current study assists cyclone preparedness among the manta community. A cross-sectional survey of samples selected via the purposive sampling technique. title: Comparison of the YOLO11n model on embedded platforms Orange Pi5 and Raspberry Pi4B
abstract: Context and relevance. Modern trends in technology development are moving towards the transfer of computing from cloud platforms to embedded devices. In this regard, there is a growing need to determine the optimal stack of hardware and software technologies for solving computer vision problems. Goal. Determine the optimal hardware configuration for real-time computer vision tasks based on the criteria of bandwidth, latency, accuracy, and ease of integration. Methods and materials. title: Multi-Source Transfer Weighted Learning with Random Forest for Cross-Project Software Defect Prediction
abstract: Accurate software defect prediction is essential for identifying fault-prone modules early and reducing software testing and maintenance costs. However, Within-Project Defect Prediction (WPDP) models may perform poorly when the target project has limited labeled defect data. Cross-Project Defect Prediction (CPDP) addresses this limitation by transferring knowledge from other projects, but heterogeneous feature distributions, source–target mismatch, and negative transfer remain significant challenges. title: Direct, but not indirect, predation‐risk cues deter larval settlement in a scyphozoan jellyfish
abstract: Settlement represents a key transition from dispersal to recruitment, during which predation can strongly influence population dynamics through both consumptive and non-consumptive effects. Predation generates chemical cues that convey information about the presence of predators, attacks on prey, ingestion of prey and post-attack conditions. title: The Role of Geographical Indications in Sustainable Coffee Tourism in Forest Areas: Lessons from Lemukih Coffee
abstract: Geographical Indications (GIs) protect distinctive local products while supporting community development and sustainable tourism. However, their effectiveness depends on regional government capacity to integrate product protection, economic development, environmental conservation, and tourism. This study examines the potential of Lemukih Robusta Coffee as a regional flagship product, evaluates the effectiveness of the Buleleng Regency Government’s policies in managing and protecting its GI in areas adjacent to forests, and explores how GI protection can support sustainable coffee tourism. title: Integrating spatial econometrics and remote sensing for pixel-level wind energy corridor identification: evidence from West Bengal, India
abstract: This study integrates remote sensing and spatial econometric techniques to identify pixel-level wind energy corridors in West Bengal, India. Weibull scale (A) and shape (K) parameter rasters at 100 m resolution were combined with Dynamic World land-cover data to evaluate how landscape characteristics influence wind resource potential. District-level zonal statistics were analysed using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Spatial Autoregressive (SAR), Spatial Error Model (SEM), and Spatial Durbin Model (SDM). title: Actinomycin Analogs From Streptomyces polyantibioticus S4D258: Structural Elucidation and Antiproliferative Activity Against Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
abstract: ABSTRACT Fifteen new actinomycin analogs were obtained from the marine‐derived Streptomyces polyantibioticus S4D258. title: The Mediating Role of Spatial Skills in Learning Kinematic Graphics Assisted by Vector Animation Videos
abstract: Kinematic graph interpretation is a basic physics competency that often challenges students because of abstract vector representations and weak geometric transformation skills. This study analyzes the influence of vector animation videos on kinematic graph learning, with spatial skills as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was applied to 60 Grade X students of SMAS Ta’miriyah Surabaya. title: Drought vulnerability assessment and its severe impact on crop production and livelihood of people: An empirical modelling of northern Ghana
abstract: Climate change is intensifying drought vulnerability in northern Ghana, posing serious risks to crop production, food security, and rural livelihoods in semi-arid regions. This study develops an empirical modelling framework to assess drought vulnerability and impacts at three temporal horizons, 2026–2050, 2051–2075, and 2076–2100, under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. title: Telling life stories through algorithms embedded in compositional processes
abstract: Abstract In this article, I examine how I embed algorithms in instrumental and electroacoustic compositional practices to organise numerical data drawn from extra-musical environmental and cosmological contexts within musical materials and structures. I explore such material-semiotic exchanges between music and surrounding environments to sonically reconfigure the matter of the life stories suggested by Ursula Le Guin, stories that challenge anthropocentric narratives. title: Aramid inserts to reduce shear fracture in GFRP composite materials for aeronautical and naval use
abstract: Delamination is a critical failure mode in glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) laminates used in artisanal boatbuilding, particularly under dynamic loading associated with slamming phenomena. This study evaluates the effectiveness of interlaminar aramid fiber stitching as a reinforcement technique to improve the interlaminar shear strength and damage tolerance of GFRP laminates manufactured using traditional hand lay-up processes. title: Y la historia no termina. Temporalidades vegetales y Reverberaciones
abstract: This article proposes vegetal reproduction and photographic reproduction as analytical models for accounting for the ways in which the past survives in the present. These models propose non-linear temporalities, defined by latency, germination, and fragmentary reproduction that destabilize narratives of closure and progress. title: Hydrophobic Silica Double-Silane Coating on Steel Surfaces for Enhanced Corrosion Resistance
abstract: Hydrophobic silica double-silane coatings offer unique properties for infrastructure development and serve as a promising alternative for protecting steel from corrosion. This research developed a hydrophobic coating of silica-methyltrimethoxysilane/hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (SiO2–MTMS/HDTMS) to enhance the corrosion resistance of steel. Various concentrations of SiO2–MTMS and HDTMS were tested to determine the optimal composition based on the water contact angle (WCA), which indicates the surface’s hydrophobicity. title: Magnitude and frequency of hurricane experiences shape community preparedness in distinct ways
abstract: Prior hazard experiences can shape how communities prepare for future climate-related risks. Here, we examine this relationship by linking census block group-level wind and rainfall exposures from eleven storms affecting Louisiana during 2017–2021 with mobility-derived preparedness measures during Hurricane Ida (2021). title: Evaluating groundwater potential zones using AHP and geospatial techniques: A case study of Chuadanga Sadar in Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater is a vital natural resource that varies in quality and quantity across Bangladesh. Growing populations and expanding urban areas put significant pressure on groundwater supplies, diminishing both their quality and availability. Groundwater supplies are under a lot of strain due to growing metropolitan areas and populations, which lowers their availability and quality. title: Method‐dependent differences in zooplankton abundance and size metrics: Microscopy vs. ZooScan
abstract: Abstract Image‐based approaches such as ZooScan are increasingly used for high‐throughput zooplankton monitoring. However, quantitative evaluations of methodological differences relative to conventional microscopy remain limited. In this study, zooplankton abundance and size‐based metrics obtained from microscopy and ZooScan image analysis were compared using identical subsamples from 35 net‐collected samples collected between 2022 and 2023. title: Integrative transcriptomic and lipidomic analysis of the effects of Eucommia ulmoides on growth performance and lipid metabolism in Larimichthys crocea
abstract: Introduction Larimichthys crocea is an economically important marine aquaculture species, and improving growth performance while maintaining lipid metabolic homeostasis is important for its sustainable production. This study investigated the effects of dietary Eucommia ulmoides supplementation on growth performance and lipid metabolism in L. crocea and explored the underlying molecular basis using integrated transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses. title: Climate change and the potential global distribution of Agrobacterium tumefaciens: a MaxEnt modeling approach for current and future climate scenarios
abstract: Climate change is fundamentally altering the geographic ranges of plant-pathogenic microorganisms, with profound implications for global food security and agricultural sustainability. Agrobacterium tumefaciens , the gram-negative soil bacterium responsible for crown gall disease in over 140 genera of dicotyledonous plants, is among the most economically significant phytopathogens worldwide, yet its macroecological distribution under current and projected future climates has never been rigorously characterised. title: Universal single-copy genes and 16S rDNA present incongruent evolutionary histories in Vibrio
abstract: A common technique for the study of the diversity and evolution of microbial communities is 16S rDNA sequencing. However, high sequence identity and variable copy number constrain the application of 16S rDNA in differentiation of closely related taxa and estimation of species relative abundance in environmental samples. A promising alternative is the use of universal single-copy genes as phylogenetic markers. title: MerR-type regulator ZccR links zinc homeostasis to biofilm formation and interspecies competition in Streptococcus mutans
abstract: Objectives Zinc is widely present in the oral microenvironment and can influence the growth of oral bacteria. ZccR is a MerR-type transcriptional regulator that controls zinc efflux in Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ), but its role in biofilm virulence and interspecies competition with oral commensals remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of ZccR in the formation of single-species biofilms of S. mutans and dual-species biofilms with oral commensal streptococci, and its underlying regulatory mechanisms. title: Clinical and epidemiological profile of hospitalized patients with leptospirosis: a cross-sectional study in Durán, Ecuador, 2023
abstract: Introduction Leptospirosis is a globally distributed zoonosis, particularly prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions, with epidemic potential during the rainy season. It is caused by pathogenic Leptospira species and produces a wide clinical spectrum, ranging from mild febrile illness to severe, life-threatening disease. Objective To describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized patients with serologically supported leptospirosis in Durán, Guayas province, Ecuador. title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. title: Applications of Kumar Malik Method to $(3+1)$-Dimensional Wazwaz–Kaur Boussinesq Equation
abstract: The Wazwaz–Kaur equation is a significant nonlinear partial differential equation. This equation is used to describe nonlinear wave propagation in fields including fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and other areas of mathematical physics. In this study, we investigate analytical solutions of the $(3+1)$-dimensional Wazwaz–Kaur Boussinesq Equation (WKBE). title: Empirically informed AHP-FR modeling for multi-hazard susceptibility mapping in a mountainous transport corridors
abstract: Abstract Mountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. However, most susceptibility assessments for high-mountain corridors still focus on single hazards or rely heavily on expert-based weighting, which can introduce subjectivity into spatial decision-making. title: Commonly co-occurring stressors in industrialized estuaries disrupt larval development in blue mussels
abstract: Recent, substantial declines in blue mussel ( Mytilus edulis ) beds in northern European estuaries signal an urgent need to unravel how chronic contaminant exposure, climate-driven warming and salinity shifts jointly affect the development and survival of vulnerable early life stages. Here, we investigated the interactive effects of a representative, environmentally relevant pollutant mixture, water temperature and salinity on mussel embryo-larval development. title: A River Wave framework to unify river ecosystem concepts and predict ecological change
abstract: Abstract The River Wave Concept is a theoretical interpretation of river ecosystem processes that links flow to multiple river ecosystem concepts and contextualizes how a river functions with or without anthropogenic impacts. Here we propose a framework that can map the River Wave Concept to ecosystem concepts and wave metrics using widely available flow data from gauging station networks. title: Assessing the evolutionary trajectory of arbuscular mycorrhizal conserved genes in seagrasses and aquatic close relatives
abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) form beneficial associations with plants, and are thought to have been critical to the adaptation of the ancestor of terrestrial plants during the transition onto land. However, the ability of AMF to associate with aquatic plants is unclear. To address this, we used 65 publicly available genomes and transcriptomes (25 freshwater, 23 terrestrial and 17 marine plants) to interrogate the genomic potential to form AMF associations in aquatic plant lineages in the order Alismatales. abstract: This study examines the integration of concept mapping and authentic assessment in pre-service elementary science education using a four-phase professional development model. An embedded mixed-method design was employed, involving 82 seventh-semester students in a primary school teacher education program at a state university in Indonesia. Quantitative data were collected through pre-tests, post-tests, and concept map analysis, while qualitative data were obtained from questionnaires, interviews, and reflections. title: Dynamic CO 2 evasion and colloidal control of trace metals in the Lower Lena River
abstract: Large Arctic rivers integrate carbon and element fluxes across vast permafrost-dominated landscapes, yet the lower reaches of these systems remain poorly constrained in terms of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and solute distributions. title: Engineering high-barrier biopolymer films derived from Sargassum via dual-alginate blending
abstract: The development of high-performance biopolymer films with tunable structure and property relationships remains a key challenge in sustainable materials science. Sargassum , an abundant brown macroalgal biomass inundating coastal zones, presents severe ecological, environmental, and economic challenges while offering a promising yet underutilized source of alginate for advanced material applications. title: Roblox-Based Immersive Learning for Environmental Literacy in Online Science Education
abstract: Environmental literacy requires learning environments that enable students to explore complex ecosystem interactions and evaluate the consequences of environmental decisions, yet conventional online science learning often provides limited opportunities for such experiences. This study developed and evaluated a Roblox-based immersive learning system designed to support environmental literacy, particularly in the context of peatland conservation. title: Phylogeny of Mastigitae sheds light on a hundred‐million‐year‐long morphological stasis of the extant genus Clidicus Laporte (Coleoptera: Staphylinidae: Scydmaeninae)
abstract: Mastigitae comprise 15 genera, of which seven are extinct, and species of two extant genera are also documented as fossils. The rich fossil record makes Mastigitae exceptional among Staphylinidae. Based on results of phylogenetic analyses comprising 33 extant species, 10 dated fossils and ~300 adult morphological characters, including structures visualized by synchrotron microtomography in mid-Cretaceous and Eocene specimens, we attempt to resolve the phylogeny of Mastigitae. title: Predicting the Relationship Between the Spatial Organization of Animal Farms and Water Quality in the Maumee River Watershed
abstract: Animal agriculture in the United States (US) continues to industrialize and expand, transforming agricultural landscapes and raising water quality concerns, particularly in northwest Ohio. While animal feeding operations (AFOs) tend to cluster spatially, a phenomenon linked to increased nutrient loading nationwide, there is a critical need to evaluate how AFO clustering influences water quality at regional watershed scales. title: Automated morphometric modelling of an endangered freshwater cetacean from unscaled UAV imagery using an internal scaling framework
abstract: With the rapid advancement of drone technology, aerial photogrammetry has been increasingly applied to morphometric research, particularly for endangered species, owing to its fully non-invasive nature. Photogrammetry-derived morphometric models (e.g., three-dimensional reconstructions) provide critical insights into individual health conditions and population demographic characteristics. abstract: This study aims to analyze the development, trends, and patterns of research related to the Halal Assurance System (SJH) in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Southeast Asian region using a bibliometric approach. A total of 101 articles indexed in Scopus for the period 2010–2023 were collected through the Publish or Perish application, then analyzed and mapped using VOSviewer software. abstract: This study presents an inaugural analysis of rock-forming mineral chemistry within andesites from the Polovinkinskaya Depression, situated at the junction of the Tynda and Nimnyr terranes in the central Aldan- Stanovoy Shield. Utilizing microprobe data processed through MagMin PT, WinPyrox, and COMAGMAT, we evaluated the systematics, thermodynamic crystallization conditions, and potential metallogenic significance of these rocks. abstract: Natural products, including isolated compounds, complex extracts, traditional medicinal preparations and marine, microbial, fungal and animal-derived materials, remain important sources of therapeutic agents and pharmacological discovery. abstract: Abstract Background Floods and landslides frequently affect the same catchment systems, yet they are usually assessed in isolation, which limits the ability of local authorities to identify areas exposed to their combined spatial influence. An integrated multi-hazard assessment is therefore needed to provide a more comprehensive understanding of spatial hazard susceptibility. abstract: Developing contextual digital teaching materials that integrate local wisdom is essential to support mathematics learning in primary schools. This study aimed to develop and validate MODULOKA, an e-module based on Jepara's local wisdom, focusing on fractions for fourth-grade students. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE model, limited to the analysis, design, and development stages. title: Nightjars trade off cruising speed efficiency for hovering capabilities and link upstroke thrust production with restricted wing folding
abstract: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus) is a long-distance migrant that also uses slow, hovering, flight as part of its feeding ecology. This reflects complex tradeoffs in aerodynamic mechanisms and makes studies of their flight performance, in relation to their wing shape, particularly interesting. Here we reveal, using wake visualization and aerodynamic measurements of nightjars flying in a wind tunnel, a unique double tip vortex phenomenon at cruising speeds. abstract: For the first time, the fluorescence of the hydrothermal vent communities of the Lucky Strike vent field (1700m depth on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge) was visualised using a non-invasive illumination method featuring a royal blue excitation light and a yellow barrier filter. Dominant fauna at the active vents consisted of Bathymodiolus azoricus mussels whose shells fluoresced and alvinocaridid shrimp with fluorescent spots on the carapax. abstract: The freight and logistics sector is experiencing significant growth in Lubumbashi, with an increase in imports from China and other countries. The agency Sky Nine Cargo, specialized in freight transport and consolidation, faces a recurring problem: many clients do not collect their packages within the allotted 14-day period, resulting in an accumulation of goods, higher storage costs, tied-up capital, and slower inventory turnover. Despite their ecological importance, they are among the region's most threatened ecosystems, particularly around Lima, where informal urbanisation and climate change drive their degradation. abstract: Microplastics are an emerging environmental problem with profound impacts on global biodiversity, as evidenced mostly in marine systems. However, the impacts of microplastics on the hotspot of biodiversity - soil - remain largely unexplored. Studies examining the influence of microplastics on a broader range of soil biodiversity, including trophic interactions between organisms, such as bacteria and nematodes, are rare. abstract: Petroleum-based plastics are widely used in packaging, but their extensive use and poor biodegradability contribute significantly to persistent plastic waste and environmental pollution. abstract: Abstract Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) remains a major health challenge, and although fucoxanthin (Fx) shows therapeutic potential, its poor stability and low bioavailability limit clinical application. In this study, a novel delivery system for Fx, a marine-derived xanthophyll carotenoid with anti-obesity, anti-diabetic, and hepatoprotective properties, was developed by encapsulating it within coaxial electrospun nanofibers. title: Migration of the common noctule Nyctalus noctula (Chiroptera: Vespertilionidae) on the Curonian Spit (Kaliningrad Province, Russia)
abstract: We analyzed capture data for the common noctule Nyctalus noctula (Schreber, 1774) on the Curonian Spit using a unique 53-year trapping dataset (1973–2025) from the Fringilla field station (Zoological Institute RAS). Over the 53-year period, the average peak of the spring passage occurs on May 17, and the autumn peak on August 31. This study aimed to identify long-term phenological shifts in passage timing. abstract: Marine corrosion of mild steel (MS) demands protection that is both durable and sustainable. We prepared an epoxy (EP) coating that carries a plant-derived inhibitor from Lemna minor (LM) by loading the extract into diatomaceous earth (DE) to form a DE@LM reservoir. abstract: Integrating proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems (PEMFCSs) with batteries can reduce aircraft emissions, but degradation must be addressed during design and operation. This study proposes a degradation-aware co-design framework determining the beginning-of-life PEMFCS rating to meet an end-of-life (EoL) power target, accounting for stack degradation, altitude-induced losses, and balance-of-plant (BoP) parasitic consumption. abstract: Rural-theme painting is an important visual art form that carries regional cultural memory and constructs local cultural identity. Current creation is troubled by the superficial selection of symbols, the convergence of regional characteristics, the disconnection between symbols and painting language, and the lack of a verifiable method. abstract: Post-mining areas affected by historical shallow mining are often exposed to sinkhole hazards associated with abandoned underground workings. abstract: Soil salinization and phosphorus (P) deficiency often co-occur in coastal saline–alkali soils, severely limiting crop productivity. Streams with lotic waters are often characterised by a mixture of herbaceous to shrubby vegetation, while more lentic waters and less rocky parts of a river are mostly dominated by gallery forests or tall reed vegetation. abstract: This paper presents a ride-comfort strategy for non-stationary road excitations. Because real road inputs are transient, accurate identification of their frequency, amplitude, and damping components is essential for subsequent comfort assessment. abstract: As the population of persons living with HIV (PLWH) ages, the Peruvian National HIV, STI and Hepatitis Program (NHSTIHP) faces the question of how best to provide care for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among PLWH. abstract: Interferon (IFN)-stimulated genes (ISGs) 56 is a prominent antiviral agent and negative regulator of the IFN signaling pathway that specifically binds and discriminates viral RNAs in mammals. abstract: ABSTRACT Cave beetles are an excellent group for studying evolutionary history and speciation within cave habitats. abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastic pollution is a ubiquitous ecological stressor, with particles and nanoplastics detected across aquatic, terrestrial, atmospheric, and biological systems. title: The Intertidal Hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, Maine
abstract: We examined the intertidal hydroids of Mount Desert Rock, ME, a remote island in the Gulf of Maine. Our study was conducted concurrently with a long-term ecological survey. We collected 20 specimens of hydroids in June through August 2023 and identified these specimens using a combination of morphological keys and DNA barcoding with the 16S rRNA gene. We recorded 13 species representing 6 families and 12 genera. Our investigation reveals a diverse group of species not reflected in modern ecological surveys and represents the first inventory of hydroid species for this island.

abstract: To clarify the mechanism by which reservoir thermal stratification influences the succession of zooplankton functional groups, this paper systematically reviews the national and international research progress and future development trends concerning both reservoir thermal stratification and zooplankton functional groups. title: Pb and Cd Accumulation of Avicennia marina Leaves and Roots in the Angke Kapuk Mangrove Protected Forest, Jakarta, Indonesia
abstract: The Angke Kapuk Mangrove Protection Forest (AKMPF) in Jakarta is an urban mangrove area affected by ongoing human-caused pollution. There is little information on how much Pb and Cd accumulate in Avicennia marina tissue, the dominant species there. This study measures Pb and Cd concentrations in the leaves and roots of Avicennia marina and examines whether distance from the shoreline affects metal accumulation. Sampling was conducted from June to August 2022 using three transect plots (20 × 140 m) in two distance zones: within 100 meters of the shoreline and beyond 100 meters of the shoreline.

title: From local hubs to regional impact: harnessing the social and solidarity economy in small-scale fisheries
abstract: Abstract The global 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development calls for more equitable and sustainable pathways by integrating traditional communities into development efforts. Despite these ambitions, challenges persist, as many initiatives, including Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) businesses, often operate in regional silos with broader transformative potential. Small-scale fisheries (SSF), particularly in the Global South, remain as one of the most affected sectors by economic imbalances and social injustices. title: Mangrove spatiotemporal changes in four areas with restoration projects in Southern Mozambique from 2009 to 2025
abstract: Mozambique contains approximately 300,000 ha of mangrove forests distributed along its northern, central, and southern coastline. Significant losses of this ecosystem have been reported over time. For instance, between 2008 and 2015, approximately 5,900 ha were lost in the provinces of Inhambane, Gaza, and Maputo. Climate change, urbanization, and socioeconomic development have been identified as factors directly associated with mangrove degradation. institutions: Centro de Ciências do Mar do Algarve

title: High Strength Steel Fatigue Crack Growth Database for Offshore Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT High strength steels can reduce costs and carbon emissions in offshore renewable energy, but their effect on structural integrity remains unclear. In welded structures, such as support structures for offshore wind and tidal turbines, fatigue life is dominated by crack growth from flaws at weld toes. Although some fatigue crack growth data for modern high strength steels exist, they are sparse compared to the widely used S355 grade. title: Chain architecture-dependent liquid-like PDMS interfaces for multifunctional antifouling surfaces
abstract: In this work, liquid-like PDMS interfaces with systematically tailored chain architectures were developed to investigate how grafted polymer topology and molecular weight regulate interfacial organization and antifouling performance. By varying chain length, grafting topology, and substrate geometry, we establish correlations among molecular architecture, interfacial homogeneity, surface mobility, and fouling resistance. title: First genomic analysis of Platycopioida and phylogenomics across six copepod orders
abstract: Recent advances in bioinformatics have significantly expanded our understanding of the genetic properties of organisms and have provided valuable insights into their phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary histories. However, molecular phylogenetic studies of the class Copepoda remain limited, and the focus has been mainly on the major taxa, namely Calanoida, Cyclopoida, Harpacticoida and Siphonostomatoida. title: Eleven tenets for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia
abstract: Research Infrastructures are increasingly central to scientific discovery, innovation and evidence-informed policy, but their management requires the integration of many dimensions that are often treated separately. This paper proposes an eleven-tenet framework for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia, extending existing tenet-based approaches by adding the explicit dimension of enabling scientific excellence. title: An historic fishery collapse driven by socioeconomic and environmental factors
abstract: Abstract In the Late Middle Ages, the western Baltic herring fishery played a central role in Europe. Salted herring was the basis for welfare and political power. We make use of a 450-year time series of Baltic herring catches (1200–1650), to identify which factors drove the herring catch dynamics during different phases of our time series. By the year 1570, the fishery suddenly collapsed, causing large-scale dislocations in trade, with major social and political consequences. institutions: German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research

title: The influence of climate change on temporal shifts in food systems and diets in Kiribati: a scoping review
abstract: Background Kiribati has undergone substantial changes in its food systems and diets, transitioning from traditional to contemporary diets that rely heavily on imported foods. This shift has been shaped by interconnected social, economic, and climate-related drivers, including the progression from traditional food sources to retail markets, food aid, colonialism, global trade, open-market policies, and climate-extreme events. title: Solid waste management practices in riparian communities are a key driver of microplastic concentrations in the Mekong River, Cambodia
abstract: Rivers are major conduits of plastic pollution, however the role of community level waste collection on riverine microplastic concentrations remains poorly understood. We investigated seasonal patterns and drivers of microplastic pollution along the Lower Mekong River, Cambodia, with a focus on riparian waste collection services. Surface water samples were collected during dry and wet seasons using a pump and filter method (100 µm minimum aperture), and more than 15,000 particles were chemically identified using Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).
