title: Exploring household livelihood resilience and natural resource dependence in urban-oriented resettlement in rural China
abstract: Urban-oriented resettlement is a key policy instrument for alleviating resource-driven livelihood constraints and fostering rural transformation and sustainable development in ecologically fragile regions. However, relocation not only changes residential locations but also alters households’ access to natural resources, livelihood capital structure, social networks, and livelihood strategy choices, leading to heterogeneous post-resettlement livelihood outcomes. title: A single domain intrabody biases the follicle-stimulating hormone receptor subcellular trafficking
abstract: Abstract Variable fragments from camelid heavy-chain only antibodies (VHH) can stabilize active conformations of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), enabling 3D structural characterization and supporting detailed structure–activity studies by linking receptor conformational states to downstream signaling. title: Flow Tree: a model for navigator dynamics and environmental complexity
abstract: Navigation is a dynamic process, involving learning new environments and manoeuvring through them. Individuals differ widely in their abilities and strategies. Prior research often uses static measures, such as total distance travelled or location tallies, which overlook the variability and asymmetry in how trajectories unfold. To address this, we introduce the Flow Tree, a novel data structure that encodes how trajectories evolve relative to each other through time and space. title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN
abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. title: A first, provisional, annotated checklist of the microlepidoptera of Albania (Insecta: Lepidoptera)
abstract: All available published data on the microlepidoptera fauna of Albania are collated and combined with the results of modern sampling to form the first known checklist of Albanian microlepidoptera. Published data are minimal as a consequence of the political history of the country; these historic reports are supplemented by active sampling during the present millennium. In total we record 1266 species across 46 families. Of these, a total of 932 species (72%) are recorded in the present millennium and are considered to be currently resident. title: IOT-driven multimodal deep visual analytics for air pollution forecasting in firework industrial regions
abstract: The increasing atmospheric burden associated with firework manufacturing requires intelligent environmental monitoring frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous pollution indicators. This study presents an IoT-driven multimodal surveillance architecture designed for industrial air quality assessment in Sivakasi. The framework integrates environmental sensors with camera-based visual analytics to improve Air Quality Index forecasting under dynamic industrial conditions. title: Effects of compound microbial fertilizer combined with potassium fulvic acid on soil physicochemical properties, microbial community structure, and cotton productivity in saline-alkali soil
abstract: To explore the effects of compound microbial fertilizer (containing Lactobacillus acidophilus and Corynebacterium glutamicum ) combined with potassium fulvic acid on cotton growth and soil ecology in Xinjiang saline-alkali soil, a two-year field experiment with seven treatments was conducted in a randomized block design. We analyzed cotton emergence rate, yield components, rhizosphere soil physicochemical properties (pH, water-soluble salts, major ions), and soil microbial community structure using high-throughput sequencing. title: Spatiotemporal wildfire occurrence, burn severity and early post-fire vegetation recovery in a tropical Andean landscape: Quilanga, southern Ecuador
abstract: Wildfires are recurrent environmental hazards in tropical Andean landscapes, where limited spatial records can constrain prevention, impact assessment, and post-fire management. This study presents an integrated assessment to characterize wildfire occurrence, burn severity, and early vegetation-greenness recovery in Quilanga, southern Ecuador. Official wildfire records from 2010-2025 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Mann-Kendall tests, Sen’s slopes, and multiscale kernel density estimation. title: Public support for novel carbon removal hinges on procedural and distributive fairness
abstract: Abstract Alongside the need for rapid emissions reductions, removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere is emerging as a central pillar of global climate policy. Scaling up carbon removal raises pressing questions about how this can be done in an equitable and socially legitimate manner. title: Macroinvertebrate communities respond to spatial patterns of water quality and habitat within mining-influenced headwater streams of central Appalachia
abstract: Surface coal mining in central Appalachia (USA) often results in salinization of headwater streams, with documented loss of several macroinvertebrate taxa and changes in community metrics across streams that vary in specific conductance (SC). However, the extent to which this salinization alters within-stream patterns in water chemistry and macroinvertebrate communities in these headwater streams is largely unknown. title: The Role of Simulation Technology in Enhancing Port Crane Operator Competence and Safety
abstract: Global maritime trade increasingly depends on efficient and safe port operations, where crane operators play a vital role in container handling. Although traditional training methods are effective, they require considerable time and may involve operational risks. Simulation-based training offers a risk-free, cost-effective, and performance-oriented alternative. This study evaluated the effectiveness of simulator training for ship-to-shore (STS) and rubber-tyred gantry (RTG) crane operators by examining error types, training periods, and changes in operator performance. title: From Normalization to Geopolitical Stress Test: The Abraham Accords After Five Years
abstract: This article examines the Abraham Accords (AA) 5 years after their signing, reconceptualizing them as a stress-tested security framework rather than a linear normalization project. Drawing on regional security developments—including the Hamas–Israel war, Houthi maritime attacks, the collapse of the Assad regime, and Iran–Israel confrontations—the article evaluates how conflict both constrains and reinforces normalization. title: The Preparation of Novel Fluorenes Inspired by Hipposudoric Acid
abstract: ABSTRACT The growing challenge of antimicrobial resistance has intensified the need for new antimicrobial therapeutics. Hipposudoric acid and norhipposudoric acid, pigments isolated from the skin secretions of Hippopotamus amphibius , are predicted to exhibit antimicrobial activity, but are limited by intrinsic chemical instability and synthetically demanding access. title: Unlocking microbial dark matter: A biotechnology framework for replenishing the antibiotic pipeline
abstract: The antibiotic pipeline is in crisis, even though microbial natural products account for most approved antibacterial drugs and retain vast, untapped biosynthetic potential. Genuinely new scaffolds are rare because discovery remains constrained to a narrow set of cultivable taxa and expressed biosynthetic gene clusters, while most microbial chemistry persists as "dark matter" in uncultured organisms and silent clusters. abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of dietary carbon‐to‐nitrogen (C/N) conditions, generated by combining Dunaliella salina with sugar beet raffinate, on the growth, survival, reproductive performance, biochemical composition, fatty‐acid profile, digestive enzyme activity, microbial community, and biomass production of Artemia parthenogenitica cultured in biofloc systems. title: Bioremediation of environmental media contaminated with emerging organic contaminants: biodegradation pathways, by-products, indicators, and end-points
abstract: Abstract Due to their widespread production and subsequent release into the environment and their associated ecological and public health risks, emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) continue to attract global research and societal focus. Bioremediation is ecofriendly and sustainable compared to chemical and physical methods; thus, it has been extensively reported in literature. title: Enabling Smart Home Sustainability with LoRaWAN: A Review of Energy and Water Sensing Technologies and Applications
abstract: LoRaWAN is cost-efficient, provides long-range communication, and has low power consumption, making it an appropriate communication technology for the IoT-based energy and water sensing system. This review presents recent developments in LoRaWAN for domestic energy monitoring, water sensing, and integrated smart-home resource management. title: Advancing benthic diatom-based freshwater health assessment in China: from an index application to an integrated assessment framework
abstract: Abstract Benthic diatoms are widely used as bioindicators in freshwater assessment, and diatom-based biomonitoring tools have been applied in China for several decades. However, existing knowledge in China remains fragmented across Chinese and English literature, geographical regions, ecosystem types, and methodological traditions. abstract: The valorization of seafood by-products is often framed as a technical opportunity, yet adoption in practice depends on whether small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can embed new systems in their operational, economic, spatial, and regulatory realities. Drawing on survey-based evidence from Greek fisheries and seafood enterprises, the analysis identifies key operational and economic constraints and translates them into a configurational model of adoption credibility for blue SMEs. abstract: This study estimates condominium rental price differentials from online listings across Thailand’s three major tourist cities, using Bangkok as the benchmark for Phuket and Pattaya while controlling for observable unit characteristics. Intercity differentials are measured with a hedonic regression in which the dependent variable is the natural logarithm of monthly rent (in Thai baht). title: A convolution–attention network predicts boiler slagging and warns of waterwall overheating from the furnace temperature field
abstract: Abstract Slagging and wall-temperature overheating rank among the costliest threats to safe and economical coal-fired boiler operation, yet plants still diagnose them separately although both grow out of the same non-uniform furnace temperature field. abstract: ABSTRACT Topographic change detection is widely applied in fields such as geological hazard early warning, environmental monitoring, and geographic process analysis. abstract: Soil-transmitted helminths (STHs) pose significant challenges to public health in endemic areas, necessitating reliable methods for their detection. Shotgun metagenomics enables simultaneous detection of STHs and microbes in a sample without prior knowledge of what is present. title: Depth-stratified boreal peatland microbiomes reveal recurring community organization and methane-cycling potential
abstract: Microbial communities in peatlands vary with depth, but most studies have been limited in spatial extent or replication, constraining assessment of general community patterns. We characterized microbial community structure and metabolic potential across replicated depth profiles in seven boreal peatlands in Sweden. Combining 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics, we identified recurring vertical stratification across sites. abstract: Finding the appropriate supplier is becoming increasingly difficult because of the complexity in evaluation criteria. Clustering algorithms and metaheuristic algorithms continue to face challenges while dealing with large data because of their inconsistent convergence, inconsistent balance between exploration and exploitation, and scalability problem. abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are chronic, complex wounds that pose a significant global health care burden, particularly for individuals with poor control of their glycemic index. The current study sheds light on the prevalence of polymicrobial infections that are mostly brought on by drug-resistant bacterial strains by investigating the microbial diversity within DFUs. title: Women in Portuguese industrial microbiology: a fifty-year perspective on progress and persistent barriers
abstract: Industrial microbiology sits at the heart of food safety, fermentation technology, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance, and sustainable biotechnology, yet leadership in the field remains disproportionately male. Only 26% of full professors in Europe are women, despite women making up the majority of life-science graduates. Portugal offers a particularly telling paradox. abstract: This study examines how service quality based on the SERVQUAL model dimensions (Tangibles, Reliability, Responsiveness, Assurance, and Empathy) affects customer satisfaction and customer loyalty in the hotel industry. abstract: Climate change is reducing the stability of crop production through more frequent drought, heat, salinity and combined stresses, while rising atmospheric carbon dioxide threatens the nutritional quality of staple crops. Plant biostimulants, defined by their capacity to improve nutrient use efficiency, abiotic stress tolerance, quality traits or nutrient availability independently of their nutrient content, are increasingly promoted as adaptation tools. abstract: Solar power is a rapidly growing renewable energy source that converts sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic (PV) cells. abstract: The rapid growth of food waste valorization within the framework of circular food systems has opened up new possibilities for the sustainable recovery of resources, but also poses unclear and less explored biological threats. Food waste streams provide dynamic habitats for a wide range of microbial communities that comprise foodborne pathogens, spoilage organisms, toxin producing fungi, viruses, parasites, and anti microbial resistant (AMR) bacteria. abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial cultivation remains essential for understanding the physiology, ecology, and biotechnological potential of environmental microbes, yet conventional plate-based methods (CPM) recover only a minute fraction of the environmental microbiome. abstract: Extreme rainfall modeling is crucial for flood-risk assessment, drainage design, and urban planning in tropical monsoon regions. UV-C irradiation may provide a supplementary non-chemical approach for reducing bacterial contamination on tableware; however, the effect of different exposure durations under standardized conditions requires further evaluation. abstract: Cloud screening algorithms have always been a critical component of Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) aerosol optical depth (AOD) Level 1.5 and 2.0 product. The initial cloud screening algorithm in the Version 1 and 2 database was semi-automatic and required involvement of a human analyst to finalize the results. title: Uncertain consequences of releasing game‐farm mallards: further insights and implications
abstract: Abstract Mallards ( Anas platyrhynchos ) have been domesticated and released in Europe and North America for centuries to supplement hunter harvest and in attempts to increase populations. They have interbred with wild mallards, most notably in the Atlantic Flyway of North America. Published research indicates that >90% of mallards harvested in the Atlantic Flyway are hybrids, and the species has formed a hybrid swarm of wild‐strain and game‐farm (GF) birds. abstract: Abstract The class Thermoleophilia represents a deep‐branching lineage within the phylum Actinomycetota , and yet, its taxonomic diversity remains incompletely resolved due to the limited availability of cultured representatives and uneven integration of genome‐resolved diversity. Here, we performed an integrative phylogenomic and taxonomic analysis of Thermoleophilia using three newly generated genomes derived from desert soils in Xinjiang, China, including two cultured isolate genomes and one metagenome‐assembled genome (MAG), together with publicly available MAGs. title: Floods Early Warning Messages in a Rural Province in South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Floods remain among the most frequent and damaging natural hazards globally, with effective flood early warning messages (FEWMs) playing a critical role in reducing disaster risk and enhancing community preparedness. Despite advances in early warning systems, many rural communities in developing countries continue to experience challenges in accessing, understanding, and responding to warning information. abstract: The discrepancy between sustainability claims and actual practices in tourism and hospitality has brought forth the "greenwashing" phenomenon. This conceptual study analyzes the multi-dimensional effects of greenwashing perceptions on consumer trust through legitimacy theory, signaling theory, and attribution theory. abstract: African leafy vegetables are important sources of dietary nutrients, including amino acids, but agronomic factors can influence their nutritional composition. abstract: This study examines the effects of edible gelatin films enriched with citrus fruit peel extracts (grapefruit, orange, and lemon) at concentrations of 1%, 2%, and 4% on the quality and shelf life of chicken burgers during frozen storage at - 18 °C, over 147 days. Significantly, the duration of shelf life was increased by inhibiting two factors, microbial and oxidation, in chicken burgers by using enriched gelatin films. abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is one of the World Health Organization's (WHO) priority pathogens requiring urgent intervention because of its remarkable ability to develop antimicrobial resistance. The rapid emergence and global dissemination of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa have made the treatment of these infections increasingly challenging, posing a major threat to public health worldwide. abstract: Abstract Gearbox fault detection under practical operating conditions is challenged by scarce fault labels, heterogeneous sensor measurements, and condition-dependent anomaly patterns. abstract: ABSTRACT Chitosan is a natural polymer found in many products, including food preservatives, packaging, health supplements, and medical items. Traditionally, strong acids and bases are used to remove proteins, minerals, and acetyl groups, but this can harm the polymer and create hazardous waste. abstract: Abstract The Kharita Formation represents one of the principal Lower Cretaceous clastic reservoirs in the Shushan Basin, Western Desert, Egypt. title: Remediation of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)- Contaminated Environments: Emerging Nanomaterials, Electrochemical, and Biological Strategies
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a large class of synthetic chemicals widely used for their hydrophobic and lipophobic properties in industrial and consumer products. However, their extreme persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity have led to significant environmental and human health concerns. Conventional treatment methods are often inadequate for PFAS removal due to the stability of the carbon-fluorine bond. title: Violent & Valiant: Comparing the Portrayals of Vikings in the Medieval, Romantic, and Modern / Postmodern Eras through Analyses of Visual Media
abstract: Vikings have been represented in many different ways throughout history. By analyzing visual media about Vikings from different time periods, one can understand how they were portrayed while also learning about the different places and historical contexts in which the representations occur. Vikings have been represented both brutally and idealistically, but those representations have never been consistent. title: Morocco's grand strategy: Pillars and limitations
abstract: The Grand Strategy aims to align a state’s means and resources with its strategic priorities in pursuit of national interests, while taking into account internal and external constraints. For Morocco, the Grand Strategy provides a key framework for achieving national interests and redefining the country’s position within the international community. The New Development Model constitutes the backbone of this Grand Strategy and serves as the roadmap to be followed, although it is not the only component. abstract: The Free Nutritional Meals (MBG) program is one of the Indonesian government's largest post-2024 social interventions and positions schools as a crucial arena for fulfilling the right to food and developing human capital. This article evaluates the MBG program for students in its second year of implementation by developing an integrative framework linking state responsibility, the social investment paradigm, implementation theory, William Dunn's policy evaluation criteria, and the Context–Input–Process–Product (CIPP) model. abstract: Depending on their application, chemicals may enter the environment and exert harmful effects on organisms, necessitating environmental hazard assessment (EHA) as part of most approval processes. While the NOS3 rs1799983 variant is known to impair endothelial function, data regarding its genotypic and allelic frequency and association with hypertension in Indonesian rural populations remains limited. abstract: Global warming poses a significant threat to rear-edge populations owing to their geographically marginal distributions. Understanding the historical dynamics and future trajectories of these populations is crucial for developing effective conservation strategies, yet they remain poorly understood. abstract: Mechanical characterisation of soft materials is challenging, with significant measurement variability observed across techniques and laboratories. This study introduced a robust indentation methodology to achieve traceable capabilities and high operational reproducibility by standardising the experimental setup and mathematical analysis. abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial neurological disability, and effective strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are limited. Dihydromyricetin (DHM) has shown neuroprotective properties in experimental neurological disorders, but its effects and associated molecular mechanisms in CIRI remain incompletely understood. This study therefore evaluated the protective effects of DHM pretreatment and examined the signaling events associated with these effects in experimental CIRI. abstract: Benzophenones (BPs) are widely utilized across various industrial sectors, leading to environmental contamination and bioaccumulation in living organisms, where they act as endocrine disruptors. Despite their ubiquity, data regarding BP exposure in livestock remain remarkably scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the concentrations of selected BPs (BP-1, BP-2, BP-3, and BP-8) in raw sheep wool. abstract: We develop a multi-regional computable general equilibrium (CGE) modeling approach to assess both direct and cascading supply-chain effects of complex seaport disruptions across U.S. regions and sectors. abstract: Afghanistan became one of the principal arenas in which great power rivalry, regional intervention, and internal political fragmentation intersected during the Cold War. This study analyses the political transformation of Afghanistan from the Soviet invasion of December 1979 to the Taliban’s capture of Kabul in September 1996 within its historical context. abstract: Abstract Alpine plant communities are structured by fine–scale interactions among soil properties, topography and microclimatic conditions, but these gradients are difficult to monitor consistently across space and time. abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is an important foodborne pathogen that causes human gastroenteritis worldwide through the secretion of staphylococcal enterotoxins in food. Consumption of contaminated raw food or cooked food handled by S. aureus carriers is the primary cause of staphylococcal food poisoning. abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). abstract: Abstract Biological interactions involving host-associated fungi are driven by chemistry shaped over evolutionary time. For antagonistic fungi, specialization often involves acquiring genes for novel secretions—including proteins and specialized metabolites—that mediate nutrient acquisition and host defense interactions. title: Corruption and sustainability in shipping: empirical evidence of institutional quality, environmental governance, and maritime connectivity
abstract: The sustainability of international shipping involves not only emissions reduction and energy efficiency, but also institutional quality, transparency, and policy enforcement. This study examines the relationship between corruption perceptions and environmental governance to highlight the institutional conditions required for sustainable development in shipping. abstract: ABSTRACT The apparel and footwear (A&F) industry accounts for up to 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions, much of it arising from supplier activities. abstract: Accurate estimation of tree biomass is essential for tropical forest management, climate change mitigation, and REDD+ monitoring. abstract: Shrimp aquaculture is a crucial sector in global seafood production, yet environmental stressors adversely affect shrimp metabolism and immunity. abstract: Abstract Mutations in Rab7a GTPase (RAB7A) cause the development of hereditary peripheral axonal neuropathy, referred to as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease 2B (CMT2B). abstract: Social media play an important role in how populist radical right (PRR) leaders communicate with supporters and present themselves to the public. Previous research has examined how political leaders’ self-presentation varies by gender and by platform, but we know less about how these two factors interact. abstract: ABSTRACT COVID‐19 and geopolitical tensions have compelled global firms to diversify parts of their operations to other countries. Although India looks primed to gain from this ‘China+1’, the authors' research, including interviews with 50 executives, officials and experts across India, America, Europe and Singapore, paints a more cautious picture. abstract: Maintaining pH homoeostasis is essential for neuronal excitability and for regulating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). title: Accuracy assessment of terrestrial laser scanning for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height, crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass
abstract: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) provides dense three-dimensional observations of forest structure and has the potential to complement or replace labor-intensive conventional measurements for selected tree attributes. This study establishes an accuracy-assessment framework for estimating tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), crown dimensions, and aboveground biomass (AGB) from TLS point clouds. title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the Endangered scaly-sided merganser Mergus squamatus with insight into its demographic history
abstract: The scaly-sided merganser, Mergus squamatus, is an Endangered piscivorous duck which has been declining since the late 1900s due to habitat loss, over-hunting, and climate change. Despite being a species of global conservation concern and subject to ex- and in-situ conservation efforts, genomic research has been limited, hindering our understanding of its population genetic status and evolutionary history. abstract: A profound paradox characterizes the contemporary international system; unprecedented digital connectivity coincides with a deepening crisis of trust, creating what this paper terms a “digital abyss” for traditional diplomacy. This paper examines how populist politics and disinformation use language through framing and delegitimization to challenge traditional diplomacy and principles of statecraft. abstract: This study examined the association between coping skills and stress management techniques as relative determinants of job performance among business education instructors at South West Nigerian Colleges of Education. The study used a descriptive survey research design and was based on the transactional model of stress and coping (Lazarus & Folkman, 1984). abstract: Abstract This study evaluates wood‐derived cellulose nanocrystals (WCNCs), produced via non‐conventional processes, as nano‐reinforcement in normal‐strength concrete with a fixed mixed design. title: Analysing user-generated overtourism posts on social media: a content analysis
abstract: Overtourism is an increasing concern for destinations seeking to accommodate visitor growth while protecting residents’ quality of life and long-term sustainability. Yet, how overtourism is represented through user-generated social media content remains underexplored. Drawing on destination image theory, this study analyses 600 Instagram posts tagged #overtourism to examine the visual themes, attraction types, sentiment, and thematic framing associated with overtourism. abstract: Abstract Collagen and its derivatives stand out as valuable biomaterials for applications in foods, cosmetics, healthcare products, medical equipment, and drug delivery carriers due to their high biocompatibility, biodegradability, and lack of toxicity and immunogenicity. However, the problem of microbial contamination in collagen is too important to ignore, which limits its further application in various fields. title: Wounded from Within: Trauma and the Body in Yesika Salgado’s and Rigoberto González’s Latinx Life Writings
abstract: Abstract This essay develops the conceptual framework of the wound as both a critical and interpretive method for reading the life writings of Salvadoran American poet Yesika Salgado and queer Chicano author Rigoberto González. Drawing on insights from trauma studies, somatic theory, and Latinx literary and cultural criticism, I examine how their works register the biological and internalized reverberations of historical, intergenerational, and intersectional trauma. abstract: The growing prevalence of antibiotic resistance and biofilm-forming dental pathogens necessitates the development of alternative antimicrobial strategies. Staphylococcus epidermidis is an opportunistic pathogen associated with dental biofilms, oral microbial colonization, and implant-related infections, contributing to persistent infections and treatment challenges. abstract: Abstract Acoustic sensors and microphone array technologies are widely used in industrial condition monitoring and fault diagnosis, and their reliability directly affects monitoring stability and equipment safety. However, existing acoustic sensor fault diagnosis methods under complex operating conditions still face limitations, including insufficient feature representation, reliance on handcrafted features, high computational cost, and difficulty in real-time deployment. title: Temperature–based quantitative detection of micro–internal leakage in heat–cycle isolation valves of nuclear power plants
abstract: The internal leakage of heat-cycle isolation valves in nuclear power plants impairs plant economics and may trigger environmental contamination or safety issues due to medium release. Non-destructive, on-line and quantitative detection methods are therefore urgently required. Among existing techniques, the temperature method is the most promising for quantitative on-line leakage detection of high-temperature valves; however, the coupled multi-physics nature of micro-leakage and their invisibility make both identification and quantification challenging. abstract: Currently, climate change and the dwindling availability of water resources necessitate sustainable water management strategies in arid and semi-arid agriculture. title: Seismic and Surge-Induced Responses of Large-Diameter Buried Gas Pipeline Bends in Marshy Soil: A Multi-Hazard Framework
abstract: Large-diameter buried gas pipelines traversing marshy or potentially liquefiable soils may be exposed simultaneously to transient internal surge pressure, seismic ground motion and reduced soil restraint. Pipeline bends are particularly vulnerable because changes in direction generate local thrust, bending and non-uniform soil–pipe interaction. title: The 1956 Suez crisis: Britain’s relative decline and the geoeconomics of British power
abstract: The Suez Crisis of 1956 is conventionally seen as a turning point in Britain’s decline as a world power. This article argues instead that the Suez Crisis exposed the consequences of a much longer process of relative economic decline. By 1956, slower productivity growth and declining international competitiveness had weakened Britain’s economic position, while the need to defend sterling left it increasingly dependent on American financial support. abstract: Zebu cattle (Bos indicus) represent a critical livestock resource in the arid and semi-arid regions, known for their disease resistance, heat tolerance and physiological hardiness. Despite their agricultural importance, the precise matrilineal evolutionary history, genetic diversity and demographic trajectory remain incompletely resolved within the broader context of South Asian cattle domestication. abstract: Preserving Indigenous Peoples’ values, rights, and sovereignty within food composition programmes is both an ethical obligation and a scientific necessity. This paper argues that embedding Indigenous Peoples’ knowledge, spirituality, and governance principles across the stages of a food composition programme—designing, sampling, compilation, dissemination and use—ensures ethical research, protects cultural heritage, and prevents exploitation. abstract: In vitro dissolution testing is central to pharmaceutical development, yet it is increasingly challenged by poorly soluble drugs, which account for over 40% of marketed products and up to 90% of new chemical entities, for which dissolution often limits absorption. abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease, with rising incidence driven by climate change, rapid urbanization, and increased international travel. Although early warning systems (EWSs) have shown promising predictive performance in endemic settings, limited evidence on implementation barriers from local end users hinders their integration into routine proactive vector control. title: From phenomenon to mechanism in the circadian clock of Synechococcus elongatus
abstract: Creative and collaborative research in the early 21st century revealed the mechanistic secrets of the cyanobacterial circadian clock, a nanomachine whose function can be studied in vitro. The structural dynamics of the Synechococcus elongatus circadian oscillator, comprising KaiA, KaiB, and KaiC, establish a near 24 h cycle of activity of the global transcription regulator RpaA by rhythmically changing the interaction platform of kinases that control RpaA phosphorylation.

abstract: The model organism Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 is routinely employed in biophotoelectrochemical systems for the study of extracellular electron transport and the production of solar electricity, chemicals and fuels. abstract: Maritime Internet of Things (IoT) deployments increasingly rely on the space-air-ground-sea integrated network (SAGSIN) to connect underwater sensors with terrestrial and space backbones. abstract: The thermal emission spectra of terrestrial exoplanets provide a window into their surface compositions and corresponding geological processes. Close-in, rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs are ideal targets for these studies, as observations have shown that most have little to no atmosphere. LHS 3844 b is an ultra-short period super-Earth orbiting a nearby M dwarf, and is the most favorable target that does not have a dayside magma ocean. title: What Do City Codes Say About Climate Risk?
abstract: Climate change is intensifying natural hazards, and preparing cities for them falls primarily to local governments. Yet what municipal codes say about hazards, and whether their requirements match each city's risk profile, has not been measured. I analyze 3.6 million sentences from 204 U.S. cities' municipal codes and compare each city's hazard text to its actual risk from FEMA's National Risk Index. I document four patterns. abstract: IoT terminals served by LEO satellite constellations transmit data to passing satellites in discrete uplink windows. That data is delivered to buyers only when the satellite reaches a ground station. This store-and-forward structure makes the achievable price a discontinuous function of the delivery completeness threshold (a phenomenon we call a pricing cliff) and creates a geographic pricing asymmetry between polar and equatorial terminals that depends on constellation size. abstract: The 1-ton prototype detector for Jinping neutrino experiment (JNE-1ton) has completed its hardware upgrade and has been successfully operated in both water and liquid-scintillator modes at CJPL-I, which is situated under a 2400-m rock overburden. abstract: Long-running LLM agents compress past interactions into persistent memories that may be reused as premises for later tasks. This creates a distinct derivation problem: whether the memory actually follows from what the interaction history supports. abstract: Skills equip LLM agents with professional knowledge and guidance to complete long-horizon and complex tasks. Although skills have been widely adopted in recent agent paradigms and harnesses, how to synthesize reliable training data and how to train agents for skill use remain underexplored. In this work, we propose SkillGym, an automatic pipeline to build verifiable environments, collect trajectories, and train skill-use agents. abstract: The inclusion of isospin-breaking corrections arising from electromagnetic interactions and the up-down quark mass difference is becoming increasingly important in lattice QCD calculations, as the precision of observables is at or approaching the percent level. abstract: This paper studies constraint certification in synchronous distributed model predictive control (DMPC) when neighboring predictions change between sampling instants. title: DISCERN: Can AI Agents Work Like Scientists and Guide Discovery?
abstract: Reliable automated research requires agents to vet data, verify analyses, and generate hypotheses grounded in trustworthy evidence, potentially reducing routine scientific workload while allowing scientists to focus on interpretation and discovery. Existing benchmarks often only assess analytical task completion or hypothesis generation separately rather than testing whether reliable evidence supports valid and novel claims. title: Scanless quantum Fourier-transform mid-infrared spectroscopy for solids and surface analysis
abstract: Quantum infrared (IR) spectroscopy is a novel technique based on nonlinear interferometry and quantum sensing with undetected photons. title: Your Benchmark Is Not Saturated: Reviving Multiple-Choice Evaluation with Answer Pooling
abstract: Multiple-choice benchmarks are cheap to grade and are running out of room, and the standard remedy, writing harder items, is slow and repeated for every benchmark. abstract: As large language models (LLMs) advance, AI agents are increasingly deployed in open-world environments to tackle complex sequential tasks (e.g., document processing, cross-application collaboration), relying heavily on actions ranging from GUI operations to semantic APIs. title: Precise Stellar Age Constraints and Habitable Zone Evolution in Exoplanet Systems
abstract: Abstract Accurate stellar ages are fundamental to interpreting the evolutionary histories of habitable zone (HZ) planets. Because stellar luminosity evolves over time, HZ boundaries migrate outward, meaning that present-day HZ planets may have experienced different irradiation environments earlier in their evolution. abstract: We test whether collisions involving Titan can eject enough water-rich material onto sufficiently distant Saturn-bound orbits to form Iapetus, while also accounting for Titan's orbital eccentricity. abstract: Abstract Burst oscillations observed during thermonuclear X-ray bursts arise from asymmetric brightness patterns on the neutron star surface and provide a direct probe of the neutron star spin frequency. abstract: Passive-wheeled terrestrial-aerial bimodal vehicles (TABVs) combine aerial mobility with energy-efficient ground locomotion. title: Controls of Tectonic, Sedimentary and Paleoenvironmental Factors on Source Rock Formation of the Lower Wenchang Formation, Pearl River Mouth Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT The Kaiping–Baiyun Western Sag in the Pearl River Mouth Basin is a key area for deepwater petroleum exploration in China. However, due to complex tectonic changes and limited well coverage, the differential formation mechanisms and multi‐scale controlling factors of source rocks in rift basins remain unclarified. This study investigates the tectonic, sedimentary and paleoenvironmental controls on source rock formation through well‐seismic calibration, organic geochemical analysis and paleoenvironmental reconstruction. title: U-Net-based time-series mapping of tidal flat areas and carbon sink variations under fluctuating tidal levels
abstract: Tidal flats are crucial for carbon storage but are threatened by human activities. Satellite remote sensing data and deep learning methods help extrapolate field-based carbon measurements to broader spatial and temporal scales. However, inconsistent tidal heights during satellite image acquisition can bias carbon sink estimates. This study employed a U-Net model to map tidal flat areas and estimate their organic carbon sequestration rates from 2016 to 2024 in Seocheon, South Korea. title: Dual northward overseas radiation from Japanese islands shaped the phylogeography of North-East Asian tree frog
abstract: The tree frog Dryophytes japonicus has a broad geographic distribution in northeastern Asia, comprising two major genetically divergent clades whose geographic boundary is located within the Japanese mainland. However, the evolutionary and adaptive mechanisms underlying this wide overseas distribution remain unclear. To uncover the phylogeographic history of the species, we conducted comprehensive genetic and reproductive analyses. title: Analysis of the Implication of Climate Change Policies on Urban Planning and Development in Calabar Metropolis
abstract: All aspects of Nigeria’s development are vulnerable to climate-related stressors. Its natural capital (including land, forests, landscapes, water, and fisheries) and physical capital (including cities, infrastructure, and other kinds of produced capital), as well as its human capital, are highly susceptible to the impact of climate change. Nigeria’s economy and other sectors of development are equally very vulnerable to climate change. title: Structural evolution, block differentiation, and driving factors of the spatial network of fishery economic resilience in China
abstract: China’s fisheries economy has long faced multiple external shocks, and enhancing its resilience is crucial to achieving sustainable development. Based on panel data from 27 provincial-level administrative regions in China from 2013 to 2023 (Tibet, Qinghai, Gansu, and Ningxia were excluded due to missing data), this paper constructs a fishery economic resilience (FER) evaluation system, and comprehensively employs the entropy-weight TOPSIS method, the modified gravity model, social network analysis, and QAP regression to examine the structural evolution and driving factors of the resilience spa

title: Mapping and dynamic monitoring of desertification on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau using surface Albedo and Solar-Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence
abstract: Desertification poses a significant threat to humanity's long-term survival and sustainable development. In this study, four types of 2D desertification assessment models were created by integrating surface albedo with four vegetation-related indicators: NDVI, MSAVI, EVI, and solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF). A comprehensive analysis of the spatiotemporal variations in desertification on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) from 2001 to 2020 was then conducted. title: Addressing InSAR long wavelength errors enhances the reliability of GNSS and InSAR combined 3D deformation estimation: methodology and application to the 2011 Tohoku-Oki earthquake
abstract: Summary Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) deformation measurements are susceptible to long wavelength errors, yet existing geometric and strain models for estimating three-dimensional (3D) deformation from combined Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and InSAR observations do not explicitly account for these errors. Neglecting long wavelength errors can substantially bias 3D deformation estimates for large earthquakes. title: Dynamic assessment model for lifting stability of oversized loads
abstract: This paper establishes a dynamic model for suspension systems used in lifting oversized loads, aiming to investigate the dynamic behavior of slings and the suspended cargo and to provide quantitative guidance for safe operations. The numerical solution employs an implicit finite difference algorithm to solve the system equations, with particular consideration of bending stiffness to address the critical low-tension problem. title: Modeling nutrient dynamics in an urban stormwater wetland and a wet pond using EFDC
abstract: Stormwater wetlands and wet ponds are widely used urban stormwater management systems for nutrient mitigation, yet the hydrodynamic and biogeochemical processes governing their nutrient dynamics remain insufficiently understood. This study developed a three-dimensional Environmental Fluid Dynamics Code (EFDC) model to investigate nutrient transport and transformation processes in a stormwater wetland and a wet pond in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, using two years of field observations for calibration and validation. The model broadly captured temporal nutrient variations and system-scale concentra

title: Determination of Earth's Static Gravity Field Using Quantum Gravity Satellites at Very Low Earth Orbit
abstract: Abstract Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellite platforms and quantum‐optical sensing technologies may provide new observation approaches for improving Earth's static gravity field models. This study conceptually assesses their potential contribution through a two‐tier closed‐loop simulation framework. title: Metal‐Organic Frameworks for Precise Separation of Radionuclides: Our Journey and Perspective
abstract: Comprehensive Summary The efficient separation of radionuclides is essential for sustainable nuclear energy and nuclear environmental safety. Conventional adsorbents exhibit limited selectivity and removal efficiency due to the lack of specific recognition sites for target radionuclides. Over the past decade, our group has developed a series of metal‐organic framework (MOF)‐based adsorbents based on the principle of “precise recognition of radionuclides”. title: An unknown scale: Radiocarbon and stable isotope analysis of keratinous pangolin scales
abstract: Abstract At least eight species of pangolins, or “scaley anteaters,” are extant today. All are classified as vulnerable, endangered or critically endangered, with the most significant threat coming from the illegal trade in pangolin scales. Radiocarbon analysis is now frequently used help monitor and understand the illegal trade of ivory and rhino horn, and to understand the biology and ecology of certain species. title: Tree-ring-anchored analog reconstruction of daily climate distributions from instrumental data with Bayesian distributional regression: Application to the European Alps
abstract: Daily to seasonal weather information remains rare in Quaternary science, because proxy archives typically resolve only seasonal or annual means. Yet climate is felt at daily timescales, through frost, snowfall, wind and precipitation. Here a framework of Bayesian Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape is presented that anchors a modern day-of-year marginal climatology to a proxy-reconstructed seasonal mean, two millennia into the past. title: A multi-channel information fusion with adaptive weighting network for cross-domain fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: Abstract In complex industrial environments, single monitoring signals, limited labeled data, and varying operating conditions often lead to low accuracy and poor generalization in cross-domain fault diagnosis of rotating machinery. To address these issues, a multi-channel information fusion with adaptive weighting network (MIFAWN) is proposed in this paper. title: International Case Studies of Acid Mine Drainage: Environmental Impacts, Treatment Performance, and Transferable Lessons for Global Mine-Water Management — A Critical Review (2020–2026)
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD), acid rock drainage (ARD), and related acidic or metalliferous mine waters remain among the most persistent liabilities of sulfide-bearing mining because oxidation, hydrologic transport, secondary-mineral reactions, and legacy infrastructure can sustain contaminant release for decades after extraction ceases. journal: Journal International Review of Research Studies

title: Fabrication and characterisation of biomimetic porous materials using diffusion-generated images and additive manufacturing
abstract: Biological porous materials exhibit complex architectures that are challenging to design using conventional modelling approaches. This study presents a reproducible workflow that integrates prompt-driven diffusion image generation with additive manufacturing to fabricate biomimetic porous polymer structures. A general pre-trained diffusion model was used to generate two-dimensional image slices imitating natural porous materials, while a fine-tuned model conditioned on X-ray microtomography data was employed to generate hybrid-like morphologies. title: Image-based roughness estimation for patinated bronze surfaces: a practical multivariate algorithm applied to benchtop and portable microscopy
abstract: Surface texture is a key functional property of metallic substrates and surface treatments. In industrial metrology, surface roughness is traditionally characterized by contact methods, such as stylus profilometry, standardized by ISO 4287. However, in cultural heritage applications, direct contact measurements may be unsuitable for delicate and heterogeneous surfaces, while non-contact optical profilometry is often not readily available for routine investigations. title: AI-AUGMENTED VIRTUAL-REAL INTEGRATED SIMULATION AND CONTROL SYSTEM FOR INDUSTRIAL ROBOTIC MANIPULATORS

title: Indoor extension of an inverse acoustic SPL model: a direct-reverberant field correction for multi-pattern construction noise
abstract: Construction-noise propagation models are typically formulated and validated outdoors, under free-field (FF) conditions, and for a single temporal noise pattern (most often impulsive pile-driving noise). Neither assumption holds for construction and renovation work carried out inside occupied buildings, where reflected sound energy accumulates in the enclosed volume and the operating equipment may be steady, fluctuating, intermittent, or impulsive. title: Single-Particle Microplastics Analysis via Laser-Assisted MicroPyrolysis Flowing Atmospheric-Pressure Afterglow Mass Spectrometry Imaging
abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as ubiquitous contaminants in the environment. Thus, novel MP characterization techniques are in urgent demand to achieve the necessary environmental monitoring, as well as studying the impact of MPs on human health. Herein, laser-assisted micropyrolysis flowing atmospheric pressure afterglow high-resolution mass spectrometry (LAMP FAPA MS) is developed toward direct imaging of single-particle MPs collected on filters. title: Architectural Reflections of Society: Examining Socio-Economic and Demographic Influences on Rivers State Government House Designs
abstract: Architecture has long been regarded as a powerful medium through which societies express their values, priorities, and historical narratives. This study examined the architectural design of the Rivers State Government House, exploring how socio-economic and demographic factors influence its structure and symbolism. The analysis revealed that Statehouse architecture in Nigeria is shaped by a blend of colonial legacies, modernist principles, regional diversity, and governance ideologies. journal: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Cartographic Analysis of the Spatial Changes in the Tourist Resort of Saly (Senegal) Between 1988 and 2024
abstract: The creation of the seaside resort of Saly in Senegal in 1984 marked the beginning of a transition from a village to an urban center. However, the development of a designated area is often marked by a context of urban transformation and expansion, giving rise to various territorial and societal challenges. Hence, the objective of this study is to assess the spatial dynamics of the Saly tourist resort between 1988 and 2024. title: Predicting meteorological-disaster-induced damage to melon crops in Taiwan by using decision-tree-based algorithms
abstract: Agrometeorological disasters pose substantial risks to melon ( Cucumis melo L.) production. This study developed interpretable decision-tree-based models to predict both the occurrence and severity of crop damage caused by typhoon-induced rainfall (TIR), non-typhoon-induced rainfall (NTIR), and cold events—the primary hazards affecting melon cultivation in Taiwan. Classification and regression tree (CART) and M5′ regression tree models were used to predict damage occurrence and damage percentage, respectively, based on county-level disaster records (2003–2022) and meteorological data. title: Multi-GNSS clock combination for PPP with an epoch-wise clock alignment and variance component estimation
abstract: Abstract Applications of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for positioning, navigation, and timing rely on precise orbit and satellite clock corrections provided by multiple Analysis Centers (ACs) of the International GNSS Service (IGS). To address modeling errors and data gaps inherent to individual ACs, the GNSS community develops and refines procedures for receiving a single, robust combined product. title: Morphological analysis of Lautaro volcano, Austral Volcanic Zone of the Andes: Insights into the evolution of an active volcano in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field
abstract: The Lautaro volcano is the northernmost and highest volcanic center of the Austral Volcanic Zone (AVZ) of the Andes. It is in the northwestern part of the plateau of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field along the northern continuity of the Pío XI chain. The volcano is almost entirely ice-covered, nourishes numerous large outlet glaciers, and has been the object of only very limited field-based geological studies. title: Vehicle-bridge coupled dynamic response of cable-stayed bridges under heavy-cargo transportation loads
abstract: The burgeoning market for heavy-cargo transportation poses an increasing challenge to the normal use of highway bridges. This study investigates the vehicle-bridge coupled dynamic response of a twin-tower three-span cable-stayed bridge under the load of heavy-cargo transportation by employing the holistic solution method and the direct integration method. The influence of vehicle load and speed on the dynamic response of the bridge when heavy-cargo transportation vehicles pass through cable-stayed bridges is discussed. title: A socio-environmental analysis of households’ livelihood vulnerability to agricultural drought in Kwara State, Nigeria
abstract: Agricultural drought has significant consequences on agriculture, water resources and the livelihoods of rural communities. This study examined the key socioeconomic and environmental factors that influence drought risk and resilience and assessed how exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity interact to shape rural households' livelihood vulnerability, using the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change vulnerability framework. title: A method for characterising fire events in high fire frequency landscapes: case study application to North Kimberley fire regimes, Western Australia
abstract: Background Identifying fire events provides insights into fire size distribution, the timing of significant fire events, their behaviour and ignition causes. However, this can be challenging when using temporally coarse datasets across high-fire-frequency savanna landscapes. Aims Develop and validate a fire event delineation (FED) methodology. title: The insurance of climate-related physical risks: challenges and opportunities for actuaries
abstract: Abstract We examine the key challenges associated with insuring climate-related risks in the context of a changing climate. Adopting a balance-sheet perspective on insurance company management, we analyze the concept of insurability and how it may be reshaped by climate change. Focussing on non-life perils, we further explore the roles of regulation, risk prevention and mitigation in addressing these issues, and discuss a range of potential solutions – and limitations – that emerge. title: Analysis of Depth and Magnitude Heterogeneity in Cluster-Based Segmentation of Andaman and Nicobar Earthquake Data
abstract: The dimension of space (depth from ground) and magnitude of each earthquake play a crucial role in explaining its characteristics. Our study examines seismic characteristics in the Andaman and Nicobar region using power spectral density (PSD) analysis and probability density function (PDF). The dataset is segmented into clusters using the K-means clustering algorithm, determined through the silhouette score method. title: Robust, Breathable and Stretchable Liquid Metal Composite Nanofibre for Physiological Electrical Signal Monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive elastic composite materials possess great application potential in the field of bioelectronic devices due to their excellent stretchability and electrical conductivity. However, conventional electronic skins hardly integrate the core characteristics of human natural skin simultaneously, including air permeability, water resistance, and high mechanical strength. In this work, a flexible and stretchable electronic skin is fabricated by combining liquid metal and electrospinning technology. title: Tourism, digital finance, and urban concentration in shaping regional economic growth in China
abstract: International tourism plays an important role in promoting economic growth in developing economies, particularly when supported by digital infrastructure and urban development. Following the rapid expansion of China’s tourism industry since 2000 and the parallel rise of digital finance, understanding the dynamics of tourism-led growth has become increasingly important for achieving balanced regional development. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of ecosystem health in the Poyang lake region under compound pressures
abstract: Abstract Revealing the mechanisms underlying ecosystem health evolution in large river-connected lakes under intensive human activities is essential for adaptive management. However, existing studies primarily focus on ecological state changes or individual driving factors, with limited attention to the continuous process linking engineering disturbance, ecological response, and societal feedback. title: Utilizing Geographic Information Systems Techniques to Study Solar Radiation Variations in Iraq for the Period (2008-2022)
abstract: Calculating net solar radiation (Rn) is of great importance in various fields, including agriculture, the environment, and industry. Several methods are used to calculate Rn, including the direct method (composite net solar radiation (CNR4)) and the indirect method using several empirical equations that depend primarily on temperature and astronomical location. The primary objective of this research is to calculate and evaluate changes in net solar radiation values for Iraq during the period 2008-2022, using several variables such as (Rnl, Rns, Rso, Rs, Ra, and ea). title: Spatiotemporal assessment of drought in the Rajshahi Division of Bangladesh using Google earth engine cloud platform
abstract: Northwestern Bangladesh, particularly the Rajshahi Division, faces increasing vulnerability to multi-type droughts, resulting in food and water scarcity. A study utilizing Google Earth Engine conducted a spatiotemporal drought analysis of this critical region from 1989-2023 using Landsat imagery and other datasets. journal: Sustainable Geosciences People Planet and Prosperity

title: Integrated analysis of nuclear safety, security and physical protection systems: A comparative evaluation of nuclear terrorism risks
abstract: This study examines nuclear safety and nuclear security within an integrated framework, systematically analysing the functional distinctions and common denominators of these fields. The design processes of physical protection systems (PPS), layered defence architecture, domestically developed analytical software tools and risk assessment models are evaluated through a literature synthesis methodology. title: Spectral sensitivity-adversarial MixUp approach for the remaining useful life prediction of bearings across operating conditions with limited data
abstract: Abstract An accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings is crucial in industrial systems. However, the scarcity of labeled degradation data and heterogeneity of data distributions are known to lower the prediction accuracy and generalization capability of model. To address these issues, a spectral sensitivity-adversarial MixUp method is proposed for predicting the RUL of rolling bearings under different operating conditions with limited data. title: Self‐Healing Pd(II) Cage Metallogels for Iodine Capture in Water and Heterogeneous Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive multifunctional systems that integrate responsiveness, environmental remediation, and catalysis within a single platform remain exceptionally rare. Herein, two carbazole‐derived metal‐organic cages (MOCs) were constructed through coordination‐driven self‐assembly and subsequently transformed into fibrous metallogels ( MOC1G and MOC2G ) in mixed DMSO/H 2 O media through cooperative π−π stacking and dynamic supramolecular interactions. title: Modeling the impact of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation on the dynamics of dengue outbreaks in Argentina between 2018 and 2024
abstract: Background Dengue fever has become an epidemiological concern worldwide, with 531,617 cases reported in Argentina during the 2023–2024 season. The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon has been linked to changes in dengue dynamics. This study assessed the relationships among ENSO, local climatic variables, and dengue outbreaks in Argentina from 2018 to 2024. title: Edge fuzzy digital image restoration algorithm based on virtual reality
abstract: Image blurring can greatly reduce the usefulness of images and affect their practical application effects. To effectively restore edge blurred digital images, virtual reality technology is combined with edge filtering to design an image restoration algorithm. The study first uses virtual reality technology to roughly restore blurred images. Then, a tripartite image restoration algorithm is constructed using edge filtering and anti non-blind convolution based on rough restoration. title: Eccentric Compression Behavior of Geopolymer Concrete-Filled Stainless Steel and Carbon Steel Tube Stub Columns
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation of the structural performance of circular geopolymer concrete-filled stainless steel and carbon steel tube stub columns subjected to combined compression and bending. A total of eight stub columns were tested under eccentric compression, consisting of four geopolymer concrete-filled stainless steel (GCFSST) specimens and four geopolymer concrete-filled carbon steel tube (GCFST) specimens. title: Protecting Ports using Range-Free Triangulated Sensor Networks: A Case Study
abstract: Range-free wireless sensor networks rely on sensors that detect only the bearing of an incoming signal, so that localizing a transmitter requires simultaneous detection by at least three sensors, a condition known as triangulated coverage. This paper extends a previously developed geospatial computational framework with a formal treatment of sensor activation and applies it to the protection of the port of Thessaloniki, Greece. title: The nuclear-climate nexus for net-zero pathways: Opportunities, challenges, and policy directions: A review
abstract: Rapid decarbonization is now a central sustainability challenge because electricity demand is rising while climate risks are increasingly affecting energy infrastructure. Although solar, wind, storage, efficiency and electrification remain essential for net-zero pathways, many power systems also require firm low-carbon resources, resilient infrastructure and governance arrangements that can sustain reliable energy services under extreme weather, geopolitical disruption and growing industrial demand. title: Blue-Green-Grey Infrastructure for Urban Carbon Reduction and Heat Resilience: A Review of Mechanisms, Methods, and Assessment Challenges
abstract: Urban blue-green-grey infrastructure (BGGI) is increasingly discussed as a strategy for reducing carbon emissions and improving heat resilience, but evidence on its mechanisms and assessment methods remains fragmented. This review synthesizes BGGI studies retrieved from Web of Science and ScienceDirect, focusing on carbon reduction pathways, analytical approaches and unresolved assessment challenges. title: Iran’s nuclear retrenchment, 1977–1980: the unravelling of US-Iran nuclear cooperation
abstract: In August 1978, as protests swept Iran, a quieter crisis unfolded within Prime Minister Jamshid Amuzegar’s government. A high-level commission recommended suspending Iran’s nuclear programme, then among the most ambitious in the developing world. This article argues that Iran’s nuclear retrenchment began not with the 1979 revolution but months earlier, driven by fiscal crisis, the erosion of institutional autonomy at the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, and the withdrawal of Western suppliers during the final years of the Pahlavi monarchy. title: Compound drought–heat wave hazards are concentrated in US regions with multiple social vulnerabilities and agricultural dependence
abstract: Compound drought and heat wave (CDHW) events are becoming more frequent and intense across the contiguous United States, increasing risks to human health, ecosystems, agriculture, and energy production systems. However, their distribution across socioeconomically vulnerable communities remains largely unexplored at the national scale. In this study, we develop a CDHW metric by integrating weekly US Drought Monitor classifications with daily temperature extremes from 2000-2021, allowing consistent mapping of CDHW occurrences along county-level socioeconomic conditions. title: Rethinking transmission line health indices under rising lightning activity
abstract: Health and condition indices (HI and CI), based primarily on physical inspections, are fundamental in asset management but show severe limitations in regions with high lightning activity. In a 230 kV transmission line (TL) in Colombia, failure rates vastly exceeded design Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) despite assets being classified in "good condition", evidencing the inadequacy of static evaluations. title: Multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak based on groove structural unit
abstract: This paper presents a multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak (AMCC) composed of groove-structured units. These structural units function as multi-frequency metasurfaces and operate effectively at both the fundamental and harmonic frequencies. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed AMCC can effectively cloak a triangular object, with a broad operational bandwidth ranging from 3110 to 3750 Hz near the fundamental frequency. title: Paying Attention to the Earth: The Development of Ecological Poetics in Jorie Graham's Materialism
abstract: The article examines Jorie Graham’s 1993 collection, Materialism, as a pivotal transitional moment in the development of her ecopoetics. It argues that the collection marks a discernible shift from the central experiences of virtuality and alienation characterised in Region of Unlikeness (1991) towards a decisive and sustained engagement with physical matter. title: Reusing Chemically Recycled Cross-Linked Matrix from Succinic Acid–Epoxidized Linseed Oil
abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of thermoset resin circularity, the solvolyzed products from biobased succinic acid/epoxidized linseed oil (ELO) cross-linked resin were valorized into new starting materials for the preparation of recycled cross-linked systems. First, the recycled product was characterized by using spectroscopy and chromatography techniques (FT-IR and LC-MS), providing insights into their molecular composition. title: Improving the accuracy of distributed cooperative positioning at urban intersections based on mathematical analysis and robust filtering
abstract: To improve the cooperative positioning accuracy of urban intersections under conditions of global positioning system signal blockage and complex traffic flow, this paper proposes a cooperative positioning model that integrates a mathematical analytical Gaussian belief propagation robust filtering algorithm with a spatial attention mechanism. A hardware verification platform integrating roadside sensing units, connected test vehicles, and 5G-vehicle-to-everything communication is constructed to achieve distributed cooperative positioning analysis of urban intersections. title: Assessment of intraspecific skull variation in the Campanian baenid turtle Plesiobaena antiqua
abstract: Baenids are freshwater paracryptodiran turtles with a fossil record ranging from the Early Cretaceous to the Eocene. The baenid Plesiobaena antiqua is the most common turtle in the Campanian (Late Cretaceous) Dinosaur Park Formation in Canada, but the apparent intraspecific variation remains poorly understood. We apply micro-computed tomography scanning technology (μCT scanning) and bone-by-bone segmentation to a sample of four crania and three mandibles representing different size classes. The available material allows us to rigorously document variation to the skull, of which most can be att

title: Assessing Climatic Vulnerability for Yellow-eyed Pigeon (Columba eversmanni) in India's Arid Region
abstract: Columba eversmanni, commonly known as the Yellow-eyed Pigeon, is a species with a limit-ed geographical distribution. It breeds in Central Asia and it moves toward South Asia during winters. The species faces significant threats from human activities and climate change. In this study, we used the MaxEnt model to assess the current and potential future distri-bution of the species based on climatic variables across its non-breeding range in the arid region of Rajasthan, India. We modelled the current climatic niche and predicted future cli-matic suitability for the year 2100 under four greenhou

title: Using spatiotemporal fusion algorithms to fill in potentially absent landsat images for estimating forest aboveground biomass
abstract: Forest aboveground biomass (AGB) estimation is important for forest resource monitoring and carbon stock assessment, but cloud contamination often limits the availability of optical imagery. To address cloud-related gaps in optical imagery, this study developed a forest AGB estimation framework that couples a comparative evaluation of spatiotemporal fusion algorithms with multi-source feature integration. Specifically, STARFM, ESTARFM, and FSDAF were compared to reconstruct cloud-contaminated Landsat imagery using Landsat–MODIS data. Optical features from fused images were combined with SAR, t

title: An open-access workflow combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks to assess air quality mortality
abstract: Surface-level air pollution is a major source of human mortality worldwide, and future emissions projections and resulting climate change are expected to alter concentrations of pollutants such as ozone and particulate matter. Estimating the health burden of these changes requires combining climate model projections with epidemiological frameworks, such as those developed in the Global Burden of Disease (GBD). However, significant barriers hinder this integration. Climate model outputs differ from health metrics in spatial resolution, temporal aggregation, and pollutant metrics. For example, G

title: Automatic evergreen forest mapping based on Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 and existing broad-category land cover product within Google Earth Engine
abstract: Evergreen forests retain green foliage throughout the year and exhibit distinct phenological and biophysical characteristics. However, although many regional and global land cover products are available at 30 m resolution, most adopt coarse classification schemes and do not explicitly distinguish evergreen forests from other forest types. This study proposes a novel Automatic Evergreen Forest Mapping (AEFM) framework to generate annual evergreen forest maps at the city scale using dense Harmonised Landsat Sentinel-2 time-series data on the Google Earth Engine platform. The framework employs an

title: Advances in Municipal Solid Waste Management in Nigeria: A Review
abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) are unwanted or undesirable products obtained from food-scraps, papers, plastics, electronic waste, metals, glass and other used materials from our day to day domestic, institutional and industrial activities which are discharged into the environment. However, as the global production of MSW increases due to increase in population, economic and industrial advancement and urbanization in Nigeria, MSW has become a global concern due to its persistence in the environment, causing various issues like climatic change, global warming and contamination of soil, air and wat
journal: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF PURE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY

title: Shaded fuel breaks support diverse bee communities in fire-prone managed conifer forests
abstract: Fuels management is critical for wildfire mitigation, yet our understanding of how this practice influences forest insect pollinators is limited. In this study, we evaluated bee communities in shaded fuel breaks (n = 27) and untreated reference sites (n = 9) on private conifer forests of northern California during 2023-2024. Across both years we captured 17,124 bees comprising 5 families, 33 genera, and 188 species. We found bee abundance was 3.2× greater in shaded fuel breaks relative to reference sites, whereas fuel breaks only averaged 2.4% more species than reference sites. Using Hill numb
institutions: National Council for Air and Stream Improvement

title: Liberation-controlled beneficiation of Moroccan andalusite ore through particle size optimization and integrated gravity–magnetic separation
abstract: The beneficiation efficiency of andalusite ores is strongly governed by particle size because of its effect on mineral liberation and separation selectivity. In this study, the effect of particle size on the upgrading performance of an andalusite ore from the Moroccan Sidi Bou-Othmane deposit was investigated using shaking table gravity concentration followed by dry high-intensity magnetic separation.
