abstract: The LUX--ZEPLIN (LZ) Collaboration has reported a nuclear-recoil candidate at $248\pm23~({\rm stat})\pm23~({\rm sys})~{\rm keV}$ in an extended high-energy search window. abstract: We analyze the effect of axion contribution on the mass, radius and dimensionless deformability of a neutron star (NS) at finite temperature. abstract: We present a multiwavelength analysis of the star $ρ$ Oph C, covering X-ray, optical, near-infrared, and radio observations to test for the presence of interferometrically-detected cool star companions. The X-ray observations from Chandra, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR show flare-like events lasting minutes or days in time and spectral properties consistent with those of cooler stars instead of the primary magnetic B star. title: Physalia: Redistribution-Resistant Content Protection for Decentralized Storage
abstract: In decentralized storage systems, access control is often implemented by encrypting the data before upload and sharing the decryption key with authorized parties. A leaked key, however, makes the data publicly accessible, which lowers the barrier to content piracy below that of traditional systems, where piracy requires redistributing the full data. We present Physalia, an end-to-end access-control system for decentralized storage that secret-shares the data itself, instead of just the key, across multiple servers. title: EP-Mem: Elastic Privacy Memory for Social Relationship-Aware LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents face critical privacy risks when acting as delegates in human-agent-human communication. To prevent such breaches, agents must understand users' social relationships and adhere to context-dependent social information disclosure boundaries. Current studies on agent memory privacy focus on instantaneous interactions, leaving the long-term relational disclosure problem unexplored. title: TOI-6981 b: a transiting sub-Neptune at the water ice line
abstract: We present TOI-6981 b, a cold (Teq= 170.0 +/-4.5 K, assuming an Earth-like albedo) sub-Neptune (Rb=2.40+/-0.10 R_oplus) on a 60.8 day orbit around around its M4-type host star (R*=0.304 +/- 0.012 R_odot, M*=0.296 +/- 0.026 M_odot, Teff = 3215+/-58K), part of the SPECULOOS TEMPOS program. We validate the planetary nature of TOI-6981 b using ground-based follow-up photometry, statistical validation and high-resolution spectroscopy. title: ENVIDDA: Environmental data discovery and access framework
abstract: The relevance of environmental data as a major category of geospatial information is evident, as demonstrated by the continuously growing volume of data produced by observation and modeling systems. Ensuring compliance with the FAIR principles in environmental data discovery and access infrastructures requires not only the registration of rich metadata, but also the systematic documentation of contextual and provenance information, together with the adoption of standard protocols and data formats. title: The TIB Terminology Service and Its Terminology Collection for the Earth System Sciences
abstract: Advancing Earth System Sciences (ESS) depends on our ability to integrate highly diverse data from a range of disciplines, including geographical information sciences, palaeontology, marine science, biodiversity research, atmospheric sciences and biology. A major scientific obstacle to this integration is semantic heterogeneity: different disciplines use different methods and terms to describe data, resulting in fragmented vocabularies. We address this challenge by providing the ESS terminology collection, which is a source of state-of-the-art terminologies for this scientific community. This

title: Africa’s first permanent Ocean Observatory: powering science, defending nature, and shaping policy for ocean governance and the blue economy
abstract: Sustained, high-resolution ocean observation is essential for understanding how marine ecosystems respond to climate variability, human pressure, and conservation action. Yet long-term observing platforms remain scarce across the Global South, limiting the capacity to detect environmental change, evaluate management interventions, and support evidence-based ocean governance. To help address this gap, we established Africa’s first permanent, multi-ecosystem Ocean Observatory in Mozambique’s Bazaruto Archipelago, operated by the Bazaruto Center for Scientific Studies (BCSS) and Kisawa Sanctuary
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture Forestry and Fisheries

abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ), a major cause of bovine mastitis, represents a significant challenge for the dairy industry due to its economic and zoonotic importance. title: Connecting international ocean, climate and biodiversity governance to protect deep-sea life
abstract: Deep-ocean biodiversity plays a fundamental role in the global carbon cycle and Earth’s climate system. Despite this critical function, international biodiversity and climate change governance frameworks have rarely considered deep-sea life to any considerable extent historically. abstract: This study assessed fisherfolk perceptions of coastal resource importance, the perceived condition of resources in Mati’s coastal barangays, differences in views across demographic profiles, existing management practices, and implications for the Coastal Resource Management Program (CRMP). A descriptive research design was used, with data collected from November 2003 to January 2004 from 358 respondents across 16 coastal barangays. abstract: This qualitative study examines how international student-teacher interns enact day-to-day pedagogy during cross-border practicum placements under the SEA-Teacher Project of SEAMEO. Data were collected from eight interns representing higher education institutions in the Philippines (n = 4), Indonesia (n = 2), and Thailand (n = 2) and analysed using a narrative-informed thematic approach to capture both lived experience accounts and cross-case pedagogical patterns. abstract: La disponibilidad de datos abiertos demográficos en los portales autonómicos españoles presenta diferencias territoriales que dificultan identificar si los catálogos más amplios ofrecen también una mayor cobertura de esta categoría. abstract: In the Persian-Arabian Gulf, conservation is uniquely complicated by transboundary ecosystems, migratory species, and anthropogenic pressures in the world’s hottest sea. abstract: Abstract The presence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants in the environment enables their dissemination and transfer from and into human microbiomes. Environmental surveillance is a recognized cornerstone for evaluating, understanding, and mitigating emergence and exposure to resistant pathogens. title: Cyber-Physical Testing of Wind-Assisted Ships: Recent Developments and Open Data Set for the SOBC-1 Bulk Carrier
abstract: Abstract This paper presents recent improvements in the cyber-physical test method for wind-assisted ships at SINTEF Ocean. In particular, a dynamic lifting line method, that interacts in real-time with the physical ship model, enables now modelling transient aerodynamic effects, sail-hull interaction, and sail-sail interactions. title: The Role of Segoro Lestari Conservation in Community Empowerment and Sea Turtle Conservation on Serang Beach, East Java
abstract: Sea turtles play a vital ecological role in maintaining the balance of marine ecosystems; however, their populations continue to decline due to egg collection, poaching, habitat degradation, and natural threats. Community-based conservation has emerged as an effective approach to addressing these challenges while simultaneously empowering local communities. abstract: Understanding population structure is critical for effective fisheries management in species with complex life histories and variable recruitment. Southern flounder (Paralichthys lethostigma) is a valuable flatfish species with declining populations in the Southeast United States. Improved management may depend on a better understanding of fine-scale and temporal population genetic structure in this region; however, such structure remains poorly characterized. title: Blue Economy and Climate Change in Nigeria: Unlocking the Role of Coastal Ecosystems in Carbon Sequestration and Livelihoods
abstract: Coastal vegetated ecosystems particularly mangroves, seagrasses, and intertidal wetlands are widely recognized as “blue carbon” systems due to their ability to sequester and store large volumes of carbon in biomass and sediments while providing vital ecosystem services that support coastal livelihoods and resilience. abstract: This paper presents a reduced–order mathematical model and an energy–optimal neuro–fuzzy control method for a cylindrical autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). abstract: Osmomixotrophic use of dissolved organic compounds may be more widespread than previously recognized, but research seems so far isolated and mostly focusing on single phytoplankton groups or strains. Here we combined data from 24 marine and 22 freshwater strains to analyse their ability to use dissolved organic compounds. abstract: Offshore wind farms (OWF) have become a vital renewable energy source and represent a promising sector for electricity generation in Brazil. title: Social Engineering and Agrarian Empowerment among Coconut Farming Communities in Coastal Sumatra
abstract: The main economic support for the coconut sector on the coast of Sumatra is challenged by low productivity and weak institutions and dependence on middlemen. This study aims to analyse the potential of social engineering based on community empowerment and the sociological factors that influence the sustainability of coconut farming in Indragiri Hilir, Asahan, Sabang and Aceh Besar. abstract: Global change is threatening the microbial consortia that sustain the services and functions of blue carbon ecosystems (BCEs), but little is known about how the composition and functioning of these consortia will respond to ecological and anthropogenic stressors. abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to address the pressing need for harmonised life cycle assessment (LCA) practices in the food sector by developing methods that enable comparable, accessible, acceptable, and applicable environmental footprint assessments of food products. abstract: Trigonometric functions are fundamental in mathematics, with significant theoretical and practical applications. Despite this importance, many secondary school students in rural South Africa struggle to expand their knowledge beyond basic techniques. abstract: A key challenge in developing fiber–wireless (FiWi) access networks is determining the optimal positions of optical network units (ONUs) to maximize network performance and minimize development costs. abstract: This paper presents the development and experimental validation of a roll-motion oscillating-body wave energy converter (OB-WEC) with passive frequency tuning via gate-valve-controlled internal sloshing. title: The role of intermediary actors in driving just adaptation
abstract: Abstract Just adaptation refers to the process of adapting to climate change in ways that are fair, equitable, and inclusive, especially for those most vulnerable to its impacts. However, there are significant challenges in realizing justice principles across different scales of adaptation. Drawing on consultations with 22 climate adaptation stakeholders in Kenya, we argue for the important role of intermediary actors in addressing these challenges.

abstract: Natural fibre-reinforced biocomposites are increasingly recognised as promising alternatives for reducing the high carbon footprint of the construction sector; however, the environmental implications of transcontinental supply chains remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of a sisal yarn-reinforced polylactic acid biocomposite plate manufactured in Denmark using sisal fibres cultivated and spun in Tanzania. title: Revisiting Animal Reservoirs of Hantavirus and Other Zoonotic Viruses Associated with Cruise Travel: Impact and Prevention
abstract: The sustained growth of international maritime tourism and the expansion of the cruise industry have increased the importance of emerging zoonotic diseases as a significant challenge to global public health. Cruise ships constitute complex epidemiological settings characterized by high population density, rapid international mobility, and constant interaction between humans, animals, and coastal environments, factors that favor the introduction and spread of emerging infectious agents. abstract: The article analyses natural and anthropogenic changes in the morphology of Cenozoic sedimentary sections on the right bank of the Kyiv Reservoir (Vyshgorod district, Kyiv region). The work aims to investigate the directional transformations and dynamics of the strato-type section of the Cenozoic on the right bank of the Kyiv Reservoir. abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a practical, standardized ophthalmic examination protocol for teleost fish using captive rockfish (Family Sebastidae) as a pilot population. METHODS: One hundred twenty-seven captive rockfish housed at Hatfield Marine Science Center and 11 newly acquired rockfish at the Oregon Coast Aquarium, representing 9 Sebastes and 1 Sebastolobus species. title: Organizational justice: a multidimensional analysis of military students’ perceptions
abstract: This study examines perceptions of organizational justice, namely distributive, procedural, and interactional justice, among military students enrolled in a Romanian military educational institution. Using survey data collected from 245 cadets, the analysis combines descriptive statistics, psychometric validation, non-parametric group comparisons, and regression modeling to investigate the multidimensional structure of organizational fairness perceptions. title: La confrontación entre el ordenamiento federativo y el ordenamiento estatal. A propósito del caso Dani Olmo
abstract: This article examines the conflict between federative and state legal systems through the case of Dani Olmo, whose registration was denied due to a breach of Financial Fair Play regulations. The study assesses the reasonableness of such denial under the principle of proportionality, weighing the balance between competition stability and the fundamental rights of professional footballers, particularly the right to work. The conclusion is that the registration ban fails the proportionality test.

title: LHR-YOLO: A SAR small-target ship detection method based on improved YOLO11
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) ship target detection holds significant application value in maritime traffic monitoring and marine environmental monitoring. However, due to challenges such as small ship targets, complex marine backgrounds, and speckle noise interference, existing methods still suffer from insufficient accuracy in small-target detection scenarios. To address this issue, this paper proposes a high-resolution detection algorithm named LHR-YOLO, based on YOLO11. abstract: Objective: To explore the privatisation of ports. This article makes the general case in favour of privatisation, vis-à-vis government ownership is a strong one: efficiency, lower costs, greater flexibility. We apply it to the special case of ocean ports to the same end. If we want more effective harbours, we should move in the direction of privatisation. We understand this opening as occurring at the intersection of, on one hand, the agency of women demanding fair recognition for their work and seeking to occupy a position previously denied to them. title: The role of wildlife in the epidemiology of Toxoplasma gondii: Surveillance and Public Health Implications
abstract: Introduction: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed zoonotic parasite capable of infecting numerous species of warm-blooded animals. Wildlife plays an important role in its ecology and epidemiology by participating in transmission cycles and reflecting environmental contamination. In Spain, evidence of infection in wildlife has increased, although it remains heterogeneous and poorly integrated into coordinated surveillance systems. title: Water, ritual, and the spectral urban commons
abstract: This article theorises the spectral urban commons through Participatory Action Research with Afro-Indigenous and Afrodescendant groups in the Costa Chica of Guerrero, Mexico. It locates the urban in these small coastal municipalities in an uneven regional process through which roads, pipes, administrative concentration, development promises and extractive projects reorganise water, territory and collective life. abstract: The literary motif of a tempest experienced at sea has permeated Western literature since antiquity, with Horace’s Ode I.14, Shakespeare’s The Tempest, and Joseph Conrad’s Typhoon and Other Stories constituting major literary examples. abstract: Cross-border renewable energy powered desalination offers a potential response to water scarcity in conflict-affected regions, but its implementation is constrained by interconnected technical, political, institutional, environmental, financial, and social challenges. This study identifies and prioritizes the critical success factors affecting such projects using the Analytic Hierarchy Process. abstract: BACKGROUND: Neglected tropical diseases are often co-endemic in affected areas but how they interact is less clear, especially in the case of Hansen's Disease (HD), commonly referred to as leprosy. Prior studies have demonstrated associations between helminths and HD and tuberculosis, but our understanding of the epidemiology of these infections is limited. Our goal was to assess the prevalence and potential associations of Mycobacterium leprae infection and parasitic infections in a sample of community members in a highly endemic area for HD in Minas Gerais, Brazil. abstract: Understanding the richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in aquatic ecosystems is important because these zoonotic nematodes circulate through complex food webs involving invertebrates, fish, birds, and occasionally humans. This study investigated the species richness and distribution of Contracaecum spp. in Iranian waters through a literature review combined with morphological and molecular characterisation of adult specimens collected from piscivorous birds. abstract: ABSTRACT Sirenians are a lineage of herbivorous marine mammals morphologically specialized for exploiting aquatic vegetation in shallow‐water habitats. In manatees ( Trichechus ), continuous horizontal tooth replacement may represent a solution for mitigating heavy dental wear incurred by a diet of abrasive plant material. title: Generative AI and digital productivity: Transitions, institutional misalignment, and human role redefinition
abstract: Generative AI is widely framed as a productivity tool. This framing understates its significance: when a technology lowers the cost of a fundamental input to the point of abundance, it disrupts not only the tools of an activity but the evaluation systems and professional cultures built around prior cost structures. abstract: This study analyzes the impact of population growth on the availability of socio-community infrastructure in the central district of Grand-Popo, Benin. It is based on a review of existing literature and a field survey of 227 households in the Onkuihoué, Houssoukouè, and Ewe-Condji neighborhoods. title: Malay Manuscripts as Cultural Memory: Islamic Knowledge Transmission in the Malay-Indonesian World
abstract: This article examines Malay manuscripts as media of cultural memory in the transmission of Islamic knowledge in the Malay-Indonesian world. Rather than treating manuscripts only as philological sources, material objects, or historical documents, it asks how material form, textual patterning, and social use jointly stabilize knowledge across generations. abstract: Global climate change is reshaping the schedules and routes of migratory birds, which can disrupt annual cycles, ecological interactions and the fitness trade‐offs of migrating or staying resident. In particular, climate change has led to advances in arrival at the breeding grounds and to shifts in the timing of post‐breeding migration, whereby both later and earlier departures have been reported. title: Multifaceted dynamics in variety and seed choices: the case of pumpkin farmers in northern Vietnam
abstract: Abstract Smallholder farmers’ crop variety and seed choices shape agro-biodiversity and livelihood sustainability. However, existing studies often overlook the dynamic, context-specific nature of these choices. We explored how introductions of hybrid pumpkin affected farmers’ pumpkin variety choices, seed sourcing, and seed management strategies across spatial and temporal contexts. title: Environmental Degradation and Tyre Waste Management Challenges in Nigerian Cities
abstract: The rapid pace of urbanization and vehicular growth in Nigerian cities has resulted in a substantial surge in end-of-life tyres (ELTs), many of which are indiscriminately discarded in open spaces, drainage channels, and public environments. These ELTs constitute a mounting environmental hazard, contributing significantly to soil, air, and water contamination, while also posing risks to public health and urban infrastructure. Although environmental protection frameworks exist in Nigeria, there remains a notable absence of targeted policies specifically addressing the management of scrap tyres.

This study aims to analyze the application of AUPB in improving the quality of public services in Bengkulu City, identify its influence mechanisms, and formulate strengthening implementation. abstract: AI platforms, while offering many positive applications, also present new risks to society, including the facilitation of trade in threatened and illegal wildlife. Although these platforms employ safeguards to block harmful or criminal requests, studies show such protections are imperfect and can be easily bypassed. abstract: This paper studies the dilemma and optimisation ideas of liability division in international cargo multimodal transport. It will not provide new empirical data but will collect existing legal and policy research on multimodal liability systems to clarify how uniform, network and modified systems distribute responsibility, and where practical and doctrinal gaps exist. abstract: Bangladesh confronts an acute and multi-dimensional tension between formal commitments to clean energy transformation and the entrenched structural realities of a fossil-fuel-dependent economy. This paper offers a theoretically grounded and empirically situated analysis of Bangladesh's just energy transition (JET) deficit, conceptualizing the gap between the state's declared ambition of 100% renewable energy by 2050 and an energy system in which fossil fuels account for over 85% of electricity generation and renewables contribute less than 3% of total supply. title: Revealing the unequal availability and socioeconomic factors of health facilities based on taxi trajectory data and geospatial analysis
abstract: As China’s economy grows, healthcare equity concerns intensify. Historically, healthcare resource allocation often mismatches cities’ economic status, and their spatial distribution remains uneven. This study examines healthcare disparities at a grid level using a two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) that accounts for distance decay. It utilizes big data and API technology to develop a more accurate distance decay function based on travel data, obtaining results that reflect the healthcare fairness. title: Los Resabios del Positivismo en el Siglo XXI
abstract: Legal positivism has stood as one of the most robust doctrines over the past few centuries; however, since the mid-twentieth century, the world has witnessed multiple phenomena whose theoretical treatment requires analysis from the perspective of legal philosophy. The rise of constitutionalism is one of the factors that has triggered a crisis in positivism, given that the Constitution is an instrument directed at society that enshrines the popular will. This study proposes an intelligent optimization framework based on the Queen Honey Bee Migration (QHBM) algorithm to improve wind power generation performance. abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of multiple YOLO model generations, namely YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLOv11, and YOLO26, for Indonesian banknote detection under real-world conditions. abstract: Background: Digital media increasingly mediate how publics encounter, interpret, and participate in cultural heritage, yet wider circulation does not necessarily produce deeper understanding or more equitable participation. abstract: Objective: Climate change is no longer just a future problem, it's a current issue that affects how we govern, our rights, how we spend public money, and who is responsible for what. abstract: Abstract Environmental genomics has transformed our view of the microbial world, yet progress remains largely prokaryote-centric. abstract: Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requires action at all levels, from local to global, through synergy among all societal actors. Norway shares responsibility for SDG-based sustainable development with local authorities (municipalities and counties). The Planning and Building Act’s purpose clause stipulates that it shall promote sustainable development for the benefit of individuals, society and future generations. title: Quantifying ecosystem degradation via energetic deficits
abstract: Abstract Ecosystem degradation is accelerating, posing critical threats to both biodiversity and human economies. A central challenge is to quantify degradation relative to a reference baseline in a way that supports restoration planning and resource allocation. Here, we address this challenge by examining the energetics of population dynamics, where energy inputs, such as sunlight, are transformed into embodied energy in the form of biomass. title: Environmental Jurisprudence in Anthropocene: Evaluation of Law in Addressing Impact of Environment Degradation on Economically Disadvantaged Communities
abstract: The Anthropocene represents a period in which human activities have become a major force influencing the Earth’s ecological systems. Environmental degradation arising from climate change, pollution, deforestation, biodiversity loss and resource depletion does not affect all sections of society equally. Economically disadvantaged communities, including rural, tribal, forest-dependent, agricultural and fishing communities, often experience greater environmental burdens because of their dependence on natural resources and their limited capacity to adapt or to obtain effective remedies. abstract: Endophytic fungi are prolific sources of bioactive natural products, but many biosynthetic gene clusters remain silent under laboratory conditions. title: Suitable habitats redistribution for the European pond turtle (Emys orbicularis) lineages under future climate change
abstract: Emys orbicularis is a freshwater ectotherm turtle sensitive to climatic variation and landscape quality. Because this species is structured into several evolutionary lineages with distinct biogeographic histories, modelling it as a single unit may obscure lineage-specific responses to climate change. Here, we assessed how future climate change may reshape the distribution of its main European lineages by integrating lineage-level, dispersal limitation, and landscape quality into ensemble ecological niche models. abstract: With the tremendous growth of cloud computing, cyber threat intelligence systems, and compressed big-data storage, efficient and secure compressed pattern-matching techniques are in high demand. title: Snake diversity based on rescue records in urban Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
abstract: We documented the snakes of Jaipur City, Rajasthan, India, using rescue records generated through a structured volunteer network, comprising primary data collected between January 2024 and October 2025, supplemented by historical records. A total of 787 primary rescue events along with past records (before January 2024), yielded records of 21 snake species across six families, including three venomous and 18 non-venomous taxa. Rescue records were dominated by Naja naja (65.4% of all rescues), while other frequently recorded species included Platyceps ventromaculatus and Spalerosophis atriceps.

abstract: The bioactivity of seaweeds is garnering increasing attention, highlighting the potential of seaweed-infused beverages as sustainable functional foods.However, research in this area remains limited and often lacks an integrated consideration of functional efficacy, sensory acceptance, and safety.In this review, we conducted a bibliometric analysis of global research trends in seaweed-based beverages using Scopus-indexed literature published between 2005 and 2025.Performance analysis was conducted using the Biblioshiny interface, while co-authorship mapping and keyword co-occurrence analyses we

title: Beyond the catch: examining the gendered and migrant workforce in Scotland’s post-harvest fishery
abstract: Abstract Research on the fishing industry typically centres the male-dominated catching sector, neglecting the post-harvest fishery historically sustained by fishermen’s wives. This study explores social change and migration in Scotland’s fish-processing sector, in Northeast Scotland, where non-UK workers comprised up to 70% of the processing workforce in 2019, the highest regional proportion in the UK (Seafish 2019). title: Operationalizing Smart Specialization in Emerging Economies: A Quintuple Helix Framework for Smart Tourism and Regional Innovation in Vlora, Albania
abstract: China’s community and neighborhood governance has become increasingly multi-actor, yet the literature remains fragmented across residents’ committees, homeowner self-governance, social organizations, crisis response, and participatory regeneration. This systematic critical review synthesizes 62 English-language studies published from 2018 to 2025. abstract: MAUSAM is officially published by India Meteorological Department. It has a huge scope in the field of meteorology, hydrology and geophysics. title: The Poster Child of Climate Change? The Changing Iconography of the Arctic Polar Bear
abstract: ABSTRACT Informed by scholarship on climate change and polar bears, this paper analyses alternatives to images of polar bears stranded on ice floes. The empirical frame of reference is recent prize‐winning images and photo essays in popular media, drawn from a selection of news reports on targeted websites. The aim is not to produce a comprehensive data set of polar bear images, but to ask what messages about climate change impacts these images can help to convey. abstract: Purpose: This study examines how education policy implementation capacity contributes to public value creation in education. It further investigates the mediating role of purposeful use of performance information and examines whether political salience of education policy changes the relationships between implementation capacity, algorithmic performance management, and public value creation. abstract: Abstract Numerical simulations are performed for hypervelocity water entry of spherical projectiles, validated against experimental data. The scaling of principal phenomena is investigated using time histories of the pressure at the stagnation point, the axial portion of the shock wave, and the radial portion of the shock wave. title: Stress and growth biomarkers in adult rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) reared in a novel photo-electrocatalytic recirculating aquaculture system
abstract: Introduction The present study is part of the PRIMA Fish-PhotoCAT project, which aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a smart purification system for improving water quality, fish production, and environmental sustainability in aquaculture. The system employs an innovative TiO 2 -based photo-electrocatalytic (PEC) filter that combines the photocatalytic properties of TiO 2 with the biocidal effect of UV radiation to remove nitrogen compounds from rearing water. title: Direct 3D extreme rainfall risk mapping from urban aerial LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Flooding is one of the most frequent and damaging natural hazards, increasingly intensified by rapid urbanization and extreme precipitation events. Accurate modelling of water accumulation and runoff in dense urban environments remains challenging due to complex geometries and the limitations of conventional surface-based representations. Most approaches require extensive LiDAR preprocessing before hydrological analysis. title: The Precautionary Paradox in Environmental Disputes: Navigating Uncertainty and Legal Authority in International Investment Law
abstract: Abstract This article examines how investor–state dispute settlement (ISDS) tribunals engage with the precautionary principle (PP) when environmental measures are challenged in the face of scientific uncertainty over ecological harm. An analysis of awards identifies three recurrent treatments: (i) strong risk prevention, (ii) flexible risk management, and (iii) nominal acknowledgement. abstract: Abstract Microbial ammonia oxidation, the first and rate-limiting step of nitrification, plays a central role in soil nitrogen cycling. It is most relevant in agricultural soils as nitrifiers compete with crops for ammonia-based fertilizers. Therefore, synthetic nitrification inhibitors are widely used alongside fertilizers to reduce the activities of dominant drivers of this process, i.e., ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and bacteria (AOB). abstract: Species-level identification of representatives of the genus Candida in complex biological samples of natural, agrobiological and technological origin is necessary for the accurate analysis of mixed microbial communities, the control of microbial contamination and the assessment of potential sources of fungal pathogen dissemination. abstract: This paper analyses the European Commission’s first informal opinion on a sustainability agreement between competing port terminal operators, representing a landmark case aimed at reconciling decarbonisation objectives with European competition law. Our study focuses on a specific project involving APM Terminals and its competitors in jointly purchasing and standardising electrical container handling equipment. title: Flash floods in traditionally less flood prone areas of southeastern Bangladesh
abstract: The growing threat of climate-driven urban flash floods signifies the need for rapid damage assessment tools. Understanding the impacts of sudden floods on populations and croplands in historically less flood-prone regions is essential for effective risk management. This study highlights the significant impact of the flood event that began on August 20, 2024, affecting three southeastern districts of Bangladesh Noakhali, Feni, and Cumilla that had experienced minimal flooding in the past three decades. abstract: This study aims to map the intellectual structure and development of research on the implementation of the rule of law through order and security, with particular attention to its relevance to the Philippine governance context. A qualitative descriptive bibliometric approach was employed to examine scholarly publications retrieved from Dimensions AI, Google Scholar, and selected secondary sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology enables efficient thermal management through high solar reflectance and thermal emission within the atmospheric infrared window. However, conventional radiative coolers predominantly exhibit white or silver appearances due to stringent solar reflectance requirements, thereby limiting their aesthetic appeal. abstract: Abstract This article investigates the world of the late Seleucid Empire on the eve of Roman control of the Eastern Mediterranean. title: Digital Colonialism and the Reproduction of Hegemony in Africa: A Postcolonial Approach
abstract: This article presents a critical analysis of contemporary manifestations of digital colonialism in Africa, focusing on how global technology powers reproduce traditional patterns of domination through modern digital infrastructures and platforms. Drawing on a postcolonial analytical framework, the authors examine how data extraction, technological dependency, and regulatory asymmetries reinforce new forms of digital hegemony across the continent. abstract: The Niger Delta presents a uniquely challenging emergency logistics environment characterized by extensive creek systems, seasonal inundation of road networks, and dispersed communities accessible only by water or air, yet emergency response operations in the region rely predominantly on road transport, with minimal integration of inland waterway and aviation modalities. title: Challenges and Opportunities for Sustainable Water Resources Management in Nigeria: A Review
abstract: Water resource management in Nigeria is a complex issue shaped by its diverse geography, climate variability, and rapid population growth. Despite substantial water resources, the country faces significant challenges in ensuring reliable access to clean and safe water. This paper examines the current status of water resources in Nigeria, highlighting issues such as uneven distribution, infrastructure deficiencies, pollution, and the impacts of climate change. abstract: Physiological biologging is a flourishing field enabling researchers to answer fundamental questions about animal behaviour and physiology in their natural environment. As biologging devices are further miniaturised their use on small species (< 1.5 kg) is increasing-making this a pivotal time to review how this technology is being used, and what technological limitations and practices users must be aware of, to answer questions in small animals. abstract: Problem, research strategy, and findings Metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs) have rarely taken on equity or housing agendas in the United States; rather, structural and political conditions have allowed for regional governance to be characterized by interjurisdictional competition or center on economic development goals. abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. abstract: The development of efficient and durable non‐noble metal electrocatalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a critical challenge due to the sluggish four‐electron kinetics and the reliance on scarce iridium/ruthenium‐based materials. abstract: Introduction Traditional dress constitutes an important medium through which cultural meanings, social identities, and collective memory become materially and visually communicable. This study examines cultural codes in Kazakh and Nogai traditional dress through a qualitative, comparative, and interpretive approach, focusing on how clothing communicated gender, social status, ritual transition, and collective belonging within historically situated cultural contexts. title: Global patterns of genetic diversity and evolution in chikungunya virus E2 glycoprotein
abstract: The E2 glycoprotein of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mediates host-cell attachment and entry and contains key antigenic determinants targeted by host immune responses. Variation in E2 can influence host interaction, immune recognition, lineage diversification, and epidemic fitness, it represents a biologically relevant target for assessing evolutionary pressures and epidemic dynamics. abstract: ABSTRACT Rates of evolutionary change vary by gene. While some broad gene categories are highly conserved with little divergence over time, others undergo continuous selection pressure and are highly divergent among populations or species. abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. title: Valuing and Protecting Inland Fisheries and Biodiversity for Livelihoods and Nutrition
abstract: Inland fisheries provide livelihood, nutritional, and leisure opportunities to people around the world; associated biodiversity and functioning freshwater ecosystems are necessary for sustainable inland fisheries. These connections and contributions, however, have largely been overlooked or under-appreciated by national and international development and conservation communities. abstract: A quantitative calibration strategy is proposed for the non-destructive determination of calcium (Ca) in historical parchment by X-Ray fluorescence (XRF). abstract: Abstract John Broome and Duncan Foley argue that future generations should shoulder the full burden of climate mitigation. title: Prediction of Potentially Suitable Areas of Hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) in Romania Based on Bioclimatic Variables
abstract: The hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) is widespread throughout Europe, except in the northeastern parts. Due to its exceptional nutritional profile and associated health benefits, it’s recognised as a premier nut crop, ranking fifth among nut crops, based on total harvested area. abstract: This article theorizes a singular form of temporal and historical immanence—or poetic historicity—manifest in the Church of St. Dimitrios Loumbardiaris, designed by Dimitris Pikionis (1887–1968) as part of the landscape setting of the Acropolis and Philopappou Hill in Athens (1951–1957). title: Post-2020 conservation priorities are threatened by global mining
abstract: Abstract The United Nations has committed to halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030. Despite this commitment, mining remains a major driver of biodiversity decline, particularly in conservation priority zones (CPZs) and areas with high species extinction risk. Regardless of growing awareness, the full extent of current and future mining threats to biodiversity remains inadequately quantified, limiting effective global conservation strategies. abstract: To address image quality degradation, difficulty in recognizing small defect targets, difficulty in quantifying external-damage risks, and limited computing resources of embedded devices in edge inspection of the power Internet of Things (Power IoT), this paper proposes an image enhancement and lightweight object detection model for power safety perception, named EEL-YOLO. abstract: As an archipelagic nation, Indonesia's maritime connectivity is a constitutional mandate for social justice. abstract: ABSTRACT Due to the low damping characteristics of thin plate structures, harmful vibrations can easily occur under external excitation, potentially leading to fatigue failure and a reduced service life. A single dynamic vibration absorber (DVA) is often insufficient to effectively suppress the multimodal vibrations of the plate. abstract: This article develops and presents the Resilient Mercantile Hub, a conceptual architectural design framework for sustainable waterfront regeneration in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, synthesising historical building condition data, community survey findings (n = 364), and semi-structured interview testimony from informal traders and built-environment professionals into a coherent, three-zone spatial and governance model. title: Overcoming urban climate injustice: synthesising global pathways and principles
abstract: Urban communities continue to face unequal exposure to climate impacts and exclusionary governance; however, cities are increasingly deploying joint mitigation and adaptation interventions. This paper presents a rapid review of global case studies to map promising pathways for achieving urban climate justice. Interrogating evidence, we find that the core pillars of justice—distributive, procedural, and recognitional—are being engaged with in climate action. abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a guided inquiry-based Cell Biology practicum guide integrated with Maluku local wisdom and to examine students’ responses to the developed product. title: Land Triadic Nexus: A conceptual framework for land governance through the strategic adaptive alignment of land use, rights, and values
abstract: Land governance persistently fails to achieve its stated objectives, producing unintended outcomes, coordination failures, and inequality. This paper argues that a major reason is the treatment of land use, land rights, and land value as parallel administrative domains rather than as mutually constitutive components of one recursive governance structure. The Land Triadic Nexus, developed here, explains governance outcomes as a function of the degree of alignment among these three domains. title: THE MANUSCRIPT COLLECTION OF LEIMONOS MONASTERY HISTORICAL VALUE PRESERVATION AND DIGITAL PROMOTION
abstract: This article examines the manuscript collection of the Holy Monastery of Leimonos on Lesbos as a complex body of material evidence preserving aspects of Byzantine and post-Byzantine literature, Orthodox worship, education and local history. It considers the historical formation of the collection, its religious, palaeographical, codicological and artistic significance, and the contribution of digitisation to research and protection. abstract: The dominant frame for current Information System research on environmental sustainability (usually termed as "Green IS") is still based on Western, anthropocentric, techno-bureaucratic which mirrors in corporate metrics, carbon footprint accounting, and compliance-driven enterprise architectures. Such top-down design slogans have little immediate scope for entering into an organic, bottom-up behavioural change paradigm of community groups, especially outside the Western dominions. title: Social context information and acoustic convergence in elephant vocal choruses
abstract: Abstract Elephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. title: A major monastic centre? Rethinking Lismore’s place in the ecclesiastical landscapes of early medieval Britain
abstract: Until recent decades, the monastery of Lios Mòr (Lismore) in Argyll, Scotland, established by Saint Mo Luóc in the sixth century, was attested only via historical references and local traditions. Community-led investigations have now revealed an early medieval cemetery, sophisticated craftworking of international importance and early structures around the island’s parish church. title: METimE: A maximum entropy framework with data-derived micro-scale dynamics
abstract: The Maximum Entropy Theory of Ecology (METE) derives probability distributions for micro-scale variables, such as species abundances and metabolic rates, solely from macro-scale observables like total abundance and species richness. While METE performs well in systems with relatively constant macro-scale observables, its predictive accuracy declines in disturbed or rapidly changing systems due to its inherently static approach. title: A phosphoproteome atlas of human cell lines reveals the landscape of kinase activity
abstract: Protein phosphorylation orchestrates cellular signaling and controls most biological processes, with its dysregulation driving diseases, notably cancer. Comprehensive, high-throughput phosphoproteomics remains limited by detection sensitivity, data completeness and computational bottlenecks, especially in low-input settings. Here we present a comprehensive empirical human phosphoproteome resource, regrouping over 200,000 class I phosphosites across 33 diverse human cell lines. We demonstrate that this spectral library dramatically improves single-shot phosphoproteomics with 30-fold faster data

title: Sustainability and Willingness to Pay: A Review of Approaches in Urban Mobility and Climate Change Resilience
abstract: Willingness to pay (WTP) is widely used to inform sustainability-related policy and investment decisions, yet its application remains fragmented across research domains. In urban mobility, WTP is typically employed to value service quality improvements, technological adoption, and efficiency gains, while climate change resilience research primarily frames WTP around risk reduction, loss avoidance, and adaptation measures. title: Between Revelation and Digitality: A Gadamerian Qur’anic Hermeneutics of Prophet Jonah and the #KaburAjaDulu Phenomenon
abstract: The emergence of the hashtag #KaburAjaDulu on various social media platforms represents a manifestation of psychosocial distress, structural criticism and the younger generation’s urge to escape the economic pressures and public policies perceived as failing to prioritise their interests. This qualitative, literature-based study aims to contextualise the Qur’anic narrative of the story of Prophet Jonah in Surah al-Anbiya’, verse 37, using Hans-Georg Gadamer’s hermeneutic framework. title: Household and community drivers of Aedes aegypti infestation in tropical cities: Guiding community-led interventions
abstract: Disadvantaged communities characterised by poor sanitation conditions, overcrowding, and limited vector control are highly susceptible to Aedes aegypti proliferation and arboviral disease transmission. Effective mosquito vector control requires a detailed understanding of Ae. aegypti oviposition preferences and spatial distribution within such urban environments. title: Curating the Polycrisis: Affective Assemblages, the Interactive Synopticon, and Trans-Corporeal Narratives in the Anthropocene
abstract: Humanity currently navigates an era defined by the Anthropocene and the “polycrisis”—a complex, destabilizing web of interconnected ecological, social, and political emergencies. Concurrently, our primary mode of processing, debating, and governing these existential threats is mediated through the algorithmic infrastructure of digital platforms. This said, this paper synthesizes five distinct but deeply interconnected domains of contemporary scholarship to propose a novel theoretical framework: Digital Anthropocene Studies. title: Governing urban floods in an emerging capital region: a social-ecological-technological systems policy analysis of Samarinda City, Indonesia
abstract: Urban flood governance in Samarinda is entering a new regional context. The establishment of Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) and the emerging IKN–Samarinda–Balikpapan urban ecosystem are accelerating spatial, infrastructural, and institutional interdependence across East Kalimantan. This transition increases the importance of ensuring that Samarinda's flood policies are not only technically effective but also socially inclusive and ecologically grounded. title: Plant- and algae-derived bioactive compounds as agricultural bioinputs: a global bibliometric and semantic analysis (2020–2025)
abstract: Plant- and algae-derived bioactive compounds have emerged as promising alternatives for sustainable agriculture due to their multifunctional roles as biostimulants, biopesticides, biofertilizers and crop-protection agents. Despite growing scientific interest in these natural products, research remains fragmented across several disciplines, which makes major trends and emerging themes difficult to identify. title: Measuring Market Accessibility of Insular Areas based on Network Distance and Shipment Cost
abstract: In this paper, we calculate the two-sided (consumer and producer) market accessibility of the Greek islands, based on different measures of transport cost, namely, the actual network distance and the freight shipment cost from/to mainland regions and between them. For this purpose, we employ a unique micro-dataset of 1,026,469 shipments for the year 2021 originated from the platform of Islands’ Transport Equivalent for firms. title: Nature-based solutions in built environment education for developing sustainability competencies through bibliometric and systematic analysis
abstract: Abstract Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognized for their potential to address complex urban sustainability challenges; however, their integration into higher education curricula within built environment disciplines remains fragmented. This study examines how NbS contribute to the development of professional sustainability competencies and identifies pedagogical strategies most effective for embedding NbS in built environment education. title: Governance, dependency, and performance in nuclear megaprojects: A strategic analysis of the Akkuyu NPP
abstract: This study examines the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) as a strategic governance system within Türkiye’s long-term energy transition. While existing research has primarily focused on the technical, environmental, and economic aspects of nuclear energy, limited attention has been given to the governance mechanisms that shape high-risk megaprojects. title: Global Harmonization of Life Cycle Assessments for Small- and Medium-Scale Wastewater Treatment
abstract: Abstract Wastewater management (WWM) is vital for protecting human health and the environment, yet conventional centralized systems are resource-intensive and unsuited to growing urban pressure. Small and medium WWMs offer a potentially more sustainable alternative, but the lack of standardized life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches limits robust comparison and informed decision-making. In this study, we conduct a global harmonization of life cycle assessments of small- and medium-scale systems across 96 LCAs and 9 treatment technologies. title: Effects of Renewable Energy Adoption on Public Health Outcomes in Nigeria's South-South Region
abstract: The worldwide transition to renewable energy is crucial for tackling environmental deterioration, climate change, and health issues related to reliance on fossil fuels. This research focused on the influence of renewable energy on public health and examined perceptions, possibilities, and obstacles concerning the energy shift in Nigeria's South-South area. A mixed-methods approach was employed, involving 400 questionnaire participants and 60 interviewees chosen from six states in the region. title: An Ecocritical Perspective on the Poems “Darg‘a” and “Tabiat Xato Ketdi” by the Uzbek Poet Tursunoy Sodiqova
abstract: The relationship between human beings and nature has been interpreted in various ways throughout history, and the meanings attributed to the natural environment have evolved in response to social, cultural, and economic transformations. Literature, as a reflection of human experiences and perceptions, has consistently incorporated natural elements and, particularly in the modern era, has developed new perspectives in response to growing environmental concerns. abstract: Objective: This study aims to determine the adequacy of overhead shading shading elements in the urban landscape of these heavily used public open green spaces in Baku and to develop recommendations for identified deficiencies.Materials and Methods: Park Boulevard, Merkezi park, Gençlik park and Kış Park constitute the main material of this study. abstract: This study aims to analyze research topic trends and citation characteristics in undergraduate theses of students in the Department of Library and Islamic Information Science at UIN Datokarama Palu from 2021 to 2024. A quantitative approach with bibliometric analysis was employed to examine 55 undergraduate theses obtained from the library collection and institutional repository. title: The role of traditional leadership in environmental governance in Africa: Lessons from indigenous institutions
abstract: Traditional indigenous governance systems have long played a key role in conserving Africa’s natural assets. This study examines the role of traditional leadership in fostering responsible environmental management across selected indigenous communities in Africa. Employing a qualitative approach that integrates oral interviews, archival materials, and secondary sources, empirical evidence was gathered from the Yoruba in Nigeria; the Mijikenda and Kikuyu in Kenya; the Zulu in South Africa; the Chagga and Maasai in Tanzania; the Lozi in Zambia; and selected communities in Botswana. title: Remote estimation of plastic distribution in California agriculture using Sentinel-2 imagery: a case study
abstract: Global application of agricultural plastic mulch is increasing. While these films offer benefits for crop production, they also are a large source of plastic waste and pollution in both terrestrial and aquatic systems. The current scale of global mulch application and its deleterious impacts are unclear. Current estimates of agricultural plastic use remain limited by field-specific growing patterns and data limitations. title: Hay Fever Symptom Burden From Grass Pollen: Implications for Public Health Warning Thresholds
abstract: Abstract This study quantifies the lagged association between grass pollen exposure and the onset of allergic rhinitis (AR) symptoms, including differences between asthmatic and non‐asthmatic subgroups. Data included 114,834 self‐reported AR symptoms collected from 25,194 uniquely identified users of a smartphone application. Reports were gathered prospectively for seven consecutive grass pollen seasons (2017–2023) in Melbourne. We adjusted for meteorological, air quality, and other time‐varying covariates. title: Still seeking permission to narrate: On international law and the question of Palestine
abstract: Abstract At the foundation of knowledge production is the question of who exactly is doing the producing, on what basis, when, where and for whom? Are all views equal? Whose views are or ought to be included? And with what implications? In this 2025 LJIL Lecture, Professor Ardi Imseis meditates on these and other related questions through the prism of one of the most pressing international legal and moral issues of our time: Palestine.

title: Cell-type composition, cognitive performance, and neuropathologic correlates in aging and dementia
abstract: Alzheimer's disease and related dementias are increasingly understood as multicellular disorders in which neurons, glia, and vascular-associated cells may contribute differently to cognitive status and neuropathologic burden. This manuscript summarizes figure-level findings from a postmortem aging and dementia dataset that measured cortical cell-type proportions and tested their associations with dementia diagnosis, cognitive scores, time from last assessment, and common neuropathologies. title: Global Research Trends and Empirical Evidence on Physician Response Time and Family Psychological Outcomes in Emergency Departments: A Bibliometric Study
abstract: Physician response time is a key performance indicator in Emergency Departments (ED), influencing service efficiency and quality of care. Although research has expanded, the literature remains fragmented, limiting a comprehensive understanding of global research trends and thematic development. This study aims to analyse global research trends, scientific contributions, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution related to physician response time in ED using a bibliometric approach. journal: Contagion Scientific Periodical Journal of Public Health and Coastal Health

title: A Satellite-Based Framework for Flood Mapping: Enhancing Explainability Through Multispectral Indices and SHAP Analysis
abstract: While machine learning (ML) models have shown considerable promise for modelling complex environmental phenomena such as floods, their adoption in flood mapping is often constrained by limited interpretability. This study develops an integrated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-enhanced framework for satellite-based flood extent mapping using multispectral and topographic variables. title: Evaluation of seismological evidence for decadal changes in Earth’s lowermost mantle and outer core
abstract: Abstract Recent reports of decadal-scale structural changes in the lowermost mantle and transport of strong heterogeneity in the outer core may offer important insights into core-mantle structure and dynamics. These reports are derived from waveform comparisons of earthquake pairs or repeating earthquakes, particularly using differential travel-time measurements made with cross-correlation techniques. title: On Prizes
abstract: ABSTRACT This article discusses prize‐creation and prize‐allocation. Such activities may seem morally neutral, or perhaps even beneficial. A central thesis of this article is that such practices have significant moral implications and should be brought under the remit of moral reasoning. I suggest that in many cases, the harmful effects of prizes are overlooked, and that they stand in need of scrutiny, revision, and possibly abolition. title: Impact of Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant Effluent on Wupa River as a Source for Consumption in Zhidu Settlement
abstract: The qualities of the treated effluent of the Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant located in a rural community of the Federal Capital Territory (Abuja-Nigeria) were assessed over two seasons (wet and dry). This study evaluated the Wupa Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) with acceptable local (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency –NESREA) and international (World Health Organization-WHO) standards and the effect on the receiving surface water (Wupa River) sources around Zhidu Settlement in Abuja. title: EvoPatch-IoT: Evolution-Aware Cross-Architecture Vulnerability Retrieval and Patch-State Profiling for BusyBox-Based IoT Firmware
abstract: BusyBox is widely reused in Linux-based Internet-of-Things (IoT) firmware, but stripped symbols, heterogeneous instruction sets, uncertain component versions, and selective patch backports make N-day vulnerability localization difficult. We propose EvoPatch-IoT, an evolution-aware retrieval framework whose novelty lies not in another standalone encoder, but in coupling target-local geometric localization, architecture-normalized anonymous multi-view evidence, and a version-causal historical prototype memory for reference-guided retrieval. title: An AI-Powered, Multilingual Pedagogical Support Framework for Integrated Science Teacher Education in Resource-Constrained Nigerian Contexts
abstract: Integrated Science teacher education is central to developing scientifically literate learners capable of understanding and applying concepts across biology, chemistry, physics, and environmental science. However, teacher education programmes in many Nigerian contexts face persistent challenges, including limited instructional resources, inadequate pedagogical support, linguistic diversity, and uneven access to digital technologies. title: De la certeza a la probabilidad: debilitamiento epistémico del adverbio 'seguramente' en la diacronía del español
abstract: The diachronic evolution of the adverb seguramente (‘surely’) reveals a shift from its original use as a manner adverb –expressing physical or psychological security– to modal meanings conveying first certainty and later high probability. Drawing on a corpus of more than 2,000 occurrences extracted from CORDE and CREA, this study examines the interaction between several linguistic parameters –including adverbial type, syntactic distribution, degree of integration, and verbal tense, mood, and semantics– in the semantic evolution of seguramente. title: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights’ Advisory Opinion on the Climate Emergency: Implications for Canada
abstract: Abstract This article analyzes the Inter-American Court of Human Rights’ 2025 advisory opinion on the climate emergency from the perspective of its implications for Canada. The authors identify key legal developments: “climate emergency” as a decisive interpretive element; the peremptory ( jus cogens ) obligation not to generate irreversible harm to the common planetary ecosystem; a new right to a healthy climate; and states’ “enhanced” due diligence obligation. title: Multi-facility GNSS antenna calibration
abstract: Abstract Accurate antenna calibrations are a cornerstone of high-quality global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) positioning, time and frequency transfer, precise orbits, and troposphere estimates. The international GNSS service (IGS) antenna committee maintains antenna phase center corrections in the ANTEX file relying on five calibration facilities. abstract: Namibia is emerging as a pioneer in Africa's green transition, leveraging its abundant renewable resources to pursue a development pathway that integrates green economy management, sustainable development, and technological transformation. This abstract examines Namibia's strategic approach, which is anchored in the Long-Term Low-Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) and the sixth National Development Plan (NDP6). abstract: Poaching for bushmeat is a rising problem for wildlife conservation, yet standard surveys often understate its true drivers because respondents conceal illegal behavior. We surveyed 219 households living near the Kafue National Park in the Central province of Zambia, and applied a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with a split-sample design: half the respondents answered direct questions; the remainder used an indirect questioning format that masks individual answers. title: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON PHOTOAGING - CONCEPTUAL UNDERSTANDING AND REJUVENATING SOLUTIONS
abstract: Photoaging is a major contributor to premature skin aging and results from the cumulative effects of ultraviolet (UV) radiation on cutaneous structures. It presents clinically with wrinkles, laxity, dyspigmentation, dryness, and vascular changes, and histologically with collagen degeneration, elastosis, epidermal irregularity, and chronic inflammation. title: A Human Rights Analysis of the Legal Framework Governing Communication Surveillance and the Right to Privacy in Tanzania
abstract: The increasing adoption of digital communication technologies has enhanced States' ability to monitor communications for national security, crime prevention, and law enforcement. While such surveillance may serve legitimate public interests, it poses significant privacy risks if surveillance powers are broadly defined or poorly regulated. This article critically analyses Tanzania's legal framework for communication surveillance, evaluating whether it adequately protects the right to privacy. title: TLCG-VMD: A two-layer coupled graph-constrained variational mode decomposition framework for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Variational mode decomposition has been widely used for vibration signal analysis due to its clear variational formulation and non-recursive decomposition mechanism. However, most existing variational mode decomposition–based methods mainly improve parameter optimization, initialization, or target-mode selection within a single-layer framework. title: Policy narratives and digital compliance: comparative governance during COVID-19 in Indonesia, Japan, and China
abstract: Why do governments using broadly comparable digital governance technologies during the COVID-19 pandemic exhibit markedly different levels of observable digital compliance? Institutional capacity, technological capability, and regime characteristics help account for this variation, but they do not fully explain why similar interventions generated different trajectories as implementation unfolded. title: Gadaa as a Model of Democratic System: The Peaceful Transfer of Power (Alangee) of Tulama Oromo
abstract: The Gadaa system of the Oromo people represents one of the world's most enduring and sophisticated indigenous democratic governance systems. This article examines the recent peaceful transfer of the Alangee (ceremonial baton of authority) from the 70th Gadaa leader, Abbaa Gadaa Goobana Hoolaa (Gadaa Meelbaa cycle), to the 71st Abbaa Gadaa of the Tulama Oromo, Geetuu Taliilaa (Gadaa Muudanaa cycle), which occurred at the sacred site of Ardaa Jilaa Dhaka Koraatti in June 2026. abstract: Sporotrichosis, a subcutaneous mycosis caused by Sporothrix spp., has emerged as a major zoonotic disease in Brazil, primarily driven by Sporothrix brasiliensis. The southern state of Rio Grande do Sul exhibits distinctive ecological and climatic conditions that may shape the persistence and distribution of this pathogen in this region. This study conducted molecular and epidemiological surveillance of feline and canine sporotrichosis in southern Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. title: CRISPR-Cas immune repertoires as an ecological record of bacterial interactions with mobile genetic elements in the human gut
abstract: Bacteria in the human gut influence host physiology and disease risk, but their ecology is strongly shaped by mobile genetic elements (MGEs) such as phages and plasmids. title: Significance of Environmental Justice for Human Dignity: A Nexus between Right to life and Right to Environment
abstract: The impact of environmental pollution, climate change, and loss of biodiversity poses a direct threat to the existence of human beings. This article examines the development and interaction of these two fields through references to legal instruments, constitutional provisions, and cases that support a sustainable environment for human rights. It posits that environmental rights should no longer be seen as secondary or optional, but as core, justiciable elements of contemporary human rights systems. title: Integrating CLAHE and H-MHI with CNN for prompt recognition in children with a diagnosis of autism
abstract: Individualized therapeutic prompts such as physical, gestural, or verbal cues are necessary to enable children diagnosed with autism to become independent in daily activities. However, the automated detection of the prompts in naturalistic conditions is difficult. The solutions currently proposed also have difficulty with unstructured video data obtained from real-world therapeutic settings with different camera angles, uneven lighting, and random movement of children. title: Value chain dynamics, opportunities, and constraints shaping Baru (Dipteryx alata Vog.) commercialisation in the Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Abstract The nut of the Baru tree ( Dipteryx alata Vogel), native to Brazil’s Cerrado, has gained attention for its strong nutritional profile and growing market potential. At the same time, the Cerrado faces increasing deforestation driven by agricultural expansion. In this context, Baru is considered a promising sustainable land-use option within forest-based bioeconomy strategies. This study examines the Baru value chain in a key commercialisation hub, focusing on actor interactions, financial dynamics, institutional conditions, and major constraints. title: Impact of piece-wise linear receiver clock modeling on sub-daily PPP coordinates for highly stable IGS H-maser stations
abstract: Abstract Modeling highly stable GNSS receiver clocks helps to increase the stability of correlated parameters, especially the station height. The use of a piece-wise linear receiver clock model, which is a common method for clock parametrization in Very Long Baseline Interferometry, has not yet been extensively investigated for GNSS. In this work, we examine piece-wise linear receiver clock modeling for GNSS. Based on a one-month series of kinematic Precise Point Positioning analyses for 56 highly stable hydrogen maser stations, the effects of piece-wise linear clock modeling are demonstrated.

title: Cross-regional emission reduction based on government-enterprise-public collaboration in the construction industry
abstract: Excessive carbon emissions are recognized as a significant contributor to climate change and environmental degradation. Achieving carbon neutrality has become an imperative for sustainable development. This study examined carbon emission reduction mechanisms in the construction industry, focusing on collaborative efforts among key stakeholders to achieve balance, coordination, and sustainability in carbon emission control. title: A Qualitative Case Study of Overtourism vs. Regenerative Tourism in Bali, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: The booming tourism in Bali has further fuelled the debate on overtourism, destruction of the environment, commercialisation of cultures, and the rising pressure on available resources that require destination management strategies beyond traditional sustainability planning. This study seeks to critically address governance, community engagement, and environmental management practices as a way of transitioning overtourism into regenerative tourism in Bali. title: Autopoiesis and the Limits of Closure in International Law: Interpretation, Social Practice, and the Temporal Life of Legal Meaning
abstract: This article re-examines the claim that international law is an autopoietic legal system. Autopoiesis remains attractive because it explains how a legal order may preserve a distinct identity through self-reference, recursive norm production, and operational closure in the absence of a central legislator, compulsory jurisdiction, or unified enforcement. title: Stars, stories, and STEM: indigenous-led science communication as a catalyst for transforming Australia's National Science Week
abstract: Indigenous storytelling is both cultural heritage and a powerful mode of science communication. This article examines how Storywork rooted in relationships, Country, and community authority can convey scientific knowledge alongside Western approaches. Drawing on Australian National Science Week case studies, this article shows how Indigenous-led storytelling fosters accessible, engaging STEM learning for diverse audiences, bridges knowledge systems, and strengthens relational understanding. title: Slavery and slave-raiding in Africa in the nineteenth century
abstract: Aim: The General Assembly of the United Nations on 25 March 2026 adopted a resolution declaring “the transatlantic slave trade the gravest crime against humanity”. Leaving the political rhetoric of “the gravest crime” to one side, I note that the history of slaving and slave-hunting in Africa was completely neglected, as was the Islamic involvement in the African slave trade and slave employment (and the role of Western traders in the Islamic slave trade as well.). title: From Show Programs to Linked Data
abstract: Many heritage institutions hold extensive collections of show programs. Too numerous to be cataloged individually, they remain difficult to access and are still largely undigitized. This paper presents a workflow for transforming such documents into structured, interoperable data by combining vision-language models (VLMs), a custom extension of the Linked Art ontology for the performing arts, and different approaches for automatic semantic data annotation. title: Fine Brown Carbon Aerosol Emitted by Wood Pyrolysis - New Harmful Tracers and Cytotoxicity in Human Lung Cells
abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) is a major global source of light-absorbing organic aerosols, the so-called atmospheric brown carbon (BrC), which negatively affects human health. However, the interplay between the molecular composition and toxicity of BB emissions remains ambiguous. In this study, cytotoxicity analyses and molecular-level characterization of fine BrC generated by wood pyrolysis at 350 °C, representative of smoldering combustion during vegetation fires, were performed. abstract: Background . The growing availability of large prokaryotic genomic datasets presents an opportunity to discover new metabolic pathways and enzymatic reactions useful for industrial or synthetic biological applications. Efforts to identify new enzyme functions in this vast number of sequences cannot be achieved without bioinformatics tools and the development of new strategies. abstract: Abstract Background Little is known about the relationship between weight gain during treatment and the subsequent risk of cardiovascular and metabolic (cardiometabolic) diseases. We assessed the relationship between changes in body mass index (BMI) during TB treatment with prevalence of post-TB metabolic syndrome, a strong predictor of cardiometabolic diseases. title: An interdisciplinary perspective on the interpretation of legal‐scientific concepts in rights‐of‐nature initiatives
abstract: Abstract Despite an ever‐growing body of environmental laws, biodiversity loss and climate breakdown persist globally. This has prompted debate over whether existing legal regimes can be strengthened sufficiently to address these crises, or whether more transformative legal approaches are needed The concept of rights of nature , which is gaining traction worldwide, represents one such transformative approach by recognising ecosystems as rights‐bearing entities. title: That’s not what a uterus looks like: representations of female reproductive anatomy produced by Adobe Stock creators and the generative AI tools they use
abstract: The production of medical illustrations has traditionally required professional skills in illustration, knowledge of human anatomy, and access to reference material such as cadavers, specimens, or surgical photos. The ability of generative AI tools to rapidly produce visually compelling illustrations introduces new issues in trustworthiness of medical illustrations. We collected representations of the female reproductive system on the Adobe Stock platform that had been created with generative AI. title: Women and Management of Oil-Related Conflict in Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta States: from 2013-2023
abstract: The study was focused on women and management of Oil-Related Conflict in Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta States; from 2013-2023. This was because the series of conflicts associated with oil are pervasive major societal issues in the Niger Delta area. title: The age-dependent relationship between childcare attendance and children's daily napping frequency
abstract: BACKGROUND: The majority of children in developed economies attend childcare services during the first five years of life-a period coinciding with their developmental transition from regular napping to consolidated nighttime sleep. Whether childcare attendance affects this transition is not well understood. Previous studies have relied primarily on cross-sectional designs or widely spaced longitudinal observations, limiting their ability to distinguish childcare effects from differences between children and families. abstract: Abstract Phylogenetic studies of insular radiations have traditionally relied on mitochondrial DNA, yet the increasing availability of genomic datasets has revealed numerous cases of phylogenetic discordance between mitochondrial and nuclear markers across animal taxa. The present study focuses on the Aegean Dailognatha, a group of six predominantly insular darkling beetle species.
