title: Trade-off Analysis of Reliability and Energy Efficiency in SPA and MSA LDPC Decoding Algorithms for Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes provide strong error-correction capability for wireless communication systems, but their iterative decoding process introduces computational and energy costs that are particularly important in energy-constrained Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This study comparatively evaluates the Sum-Product Algorithm (SPA) and the Min-Sum Algorithm (MSA) for LDPC decoding, with emphasis on the trade-off between communication reliability and estimated decoding energy. title: The Body as a Bridge Between Earth and Mars: Tai Chi Culture and the Human Art of Space Adaptation
abstract: Long-duration spaceflight raises a human question as well as an engineering one: how can crews maintain physical coordination, emotional steadiness, and supportive relationships when familiar conditions change? This conceptual article introduces the Cosmo-Embodied Adaptation Framework, a research map for connecting Tai Chi (Taijiquan, 太极拳) cultural practices with specific questions about space adaptation. title: Dilemmas of engagement: local government officials’ perspectives on roles and responsibilities in climate change adaptation in rural and remote Nordic municipalities
abstract: As climate change impacts intensify across the Nordic countries, calls for deeper and more sustained citizen engagement in adaptation efforts have become increasingly prominent in both national and local policy agendas. This shift has spurred growing scholarly interest in how citizen responsibilisation is reshaping the roles and responsibilities of local government officials. While existing research has predominantly focused on urban contexts, this article examines local government officials in remote rural municipalities in Denmark and Norway. title: Carbon credits as market-based mechanisms for climate mitigation: Opportunities, challenges and future perspectives
abstract: Carbon credits are a promising market-based tool for combating climate change, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation, three of the most pressing environmental problems currently facing the global environment. Carbon credit schemes have stimulated investments in renewable energy, forestry, sustainable agriculture, soil carbon management and decreased emissions by putting a monetary value on greater carbon sequestration and reduced emissions. title: Gut microbiota of dung beetles shows taxonomic turnover but relative functional stability
abstract: The dung beetle gut microbiota is essential for host health and plays a key role in regulating the biochemical processes underpinning grassland ecosystem functioning. Understanding how its taxonomic and functional composition varies across species may help predict the ecological consequences of changes in dung beetle communities driven by shifts in pastoral practices. Elucidating the mechanisms of microbial acquisition and potential transmission is also crucial. title: Business roles in 1.5 °C transitions: a stakeholder-informed scenario analysis
abstract: Limiting global warming to 1.5 °C requires profound transformations of production and consumption systems, yet the role of businesses in enabling such transitions remains insufficiently addressed in scenario-based sustainability research. Existing scenarios often conceptualize firms as implementers of mitigation measures rather than governance actors shaped by policy, institutions, and societal expectations. title: Persistent spatial hotspots and socioeconomic inequalities of snakebite envenoming in Peru: A nationwide spatiotemporal analysis, 2010–2025
abstract: BACKGROUND: Snakebite envenoming remains a major neglected tropical disease worldwide, disproportionately affecting rural and socioeconomically vulnerable populations in tropical and subtropical regions. In Peru, snakebite burden is strongly concentrated in Amazonian territories, yet nationwide evidence on its long-term spatial dynamics and socioeconomic determinants remains limited. abstract: As batteries are widely used in port operation vehicles, cargo handling equipment, and fixed energy storage systems, ports need to establish reliable mechanisms for battery recycling and disposal. This study develops a Stackelberg model led by a battery system integrator, with an authorized recovery service provider and a representative green-port operator. abstract: BACKGROUND: Peatland rewetting is a cost-effective strategy for climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation, yet its potential to alter mosquito species composition and abundance carries implications for public and veterinary health. Anopheles algeriensis and Anopheles claviger s.s. are broadly distributed across European wetlands, including peatlands, but despite their vector potential, their specific ecological niches and responses to rewetting remain poorly understood. title: Remote Sensing–Driven Drought Assessment Using Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) Derived from Landsat 8 Imagery
abstract: Drought, a persistent state of water scarcity, is a critical challenge for agriculture and resource management. This study examines drought variability in Lamongan Regency from 2021 to 2023 using the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) derived from Landsat 8 imagery, integrating Land Surface Temperature (LST) and NDVI to classify conditions from wet to dry. title: Why Sand Mining Governance Remains Challenging in the Lower Mekong Basin: The Need for an Integrated Driver‐to‐Management Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT Sand mining is widely recognized as one of the most significant threats to river health in the Lower Mekong Basin, where intensive extraction interacts with sediment starvation, hydropower development, climate variability, and delta subsidence to produce complex, transboundary environmental impacts. abstract: Abstract Determining earthquake magnitude and location through fast, automated methods is fundamental for seismic monitoring. Recent studies have shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) can operate as pattern‐recognition systems capable of handling novel domains and purely numerical tasks. Here, we assess the utility of LLMs for earthquake characterization and propose a novel approach based on a small LLM called TinyLlama. abstract: Abstract Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is critical for achieving global sustainability, yet translating international commitments into actionable local policies remains challenging, not least because interdependent goals require coherent implementation. This article examines how external pressure, local capacity, and local demand condition coherent SDG localization at the level of discourse, norms, and institutions. title: Mapping the exposome of Zimbabwean preschool-aged children using a novel peptide microarray approach
abstract: Immune responses vary substantially between individuals and populations, reflecting differences in genetics, environment, and cumulative antigenic exposures. title: Changes in Patient Safety Culture in Pharmacists after Training and Application of the Model in Pharmacy Referral Program: A Pre-Post Quasi-Experimental Study
abstract: Patient safety culture in community pharmacies requires adequate knowledge, operational tools, and continuous organizational learning. This study assessed changes in pharmacists’ knowledge and patient safety culture following training and two months of model implementation. abstract: The increasing number of Indonesian citizens (WNI) departing the country by providing false information (misrepresentation) has become a challenge in the implementation of immigration supervision, particularly in preventing trafficking in persons (TIP) and the non-procedural placement of Indonesian migrant workers (PMI). title: From Reactivity to Proactivity: The Use of Behavioural Data in Life and Health Insurance
abstract: Abstract Traditional life and health insurance compensates after the fact, acting reactively in response to adverse events. Today, the rise of digital technologies enables insurers to intervene proactively, monitoring policyholders’ behaviour and incentivizing lifestyle changes intended to reduce risks before they materialize. title: Commercial Floriculture in Kerala, India: Major Cut Flowers, Production, Marketing and Business Prospects
abstract: Commercial floriculture in Kerala must reconcile the biological suitability of tropical ornamentals with the exacting requirements of a perishable, quality-differentiated market. This critical narrative review examines the principal cut-flower groups relevant to the state, their production systems, postharvest constraints, marketing arrangements and business prospects. abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient recognition accuracy and lack of explanation in the diagnosis process of behavioral indicators of potential learning disabilities, an intelligent diagnosis model integrating knowledge map and long-term and short-term memory network is constructed. abstract: Sleep disruption increases with age and is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, integrative analyses of human and mouse transcriptomic and proteomic datasets identify proteostasis pathways whose aging trajectories align with responses to chronic sleep disruption across tissues, cell types, and molecular layers. abstract: Extrusion-based additive manufacturing, such as fused filament fabrication and direct ink writing, is valued for its versatility and material compatibility. Nozzle geometry governs material flow, bead morphology, dimensional accuracy, and mechanical performance. abstract: Objectives This study investigated the effects of a nanocomposite comprising N-acyl -homoserine lactonase Est816 and silver nanoparticles (Ag-Est816) on the microbial community of an enriched in vitro biofilm model derived from supragingival plaque of children with early childhood caries (ECC). abstract: The study correlates with several UN Sustainable Development Goals, namely: Good Health and Well-being (focusing on students’ mental health), Quality Education (highlighting the impact of trauma on the learning process and the creation of a safe educational environment), and Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions (outlining ways to overcome the consequences of war for the stable development of society). abstract: The democratic health and pupils' involvement are positively related. abstract: Abstract The annual festival of Shāh-e Sarāb has been a major Hazara pilgrimage in Waras district of Afghanistan’s Bamiyan Province on the fourteenth day of Jawzā/Khordād (June 4). Drawing on published accounts, virtual ethnography, remote interviews, and satellite imagery, this article describes the shrine and the principal ritual components of the celebration in arguing that Shāh-e Sarāb represents a “Shi’i-ized” continuation of Khordādgān, the ancient Iranian month/day festival of the Zoroastrian goddess Khordād. title: Technical progress, democratic deficits: Communication and socio-environmental conflicts in wind energy expansion in Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil
abstract: In the context of global decarbonization imperatives, renewable energy expansion drives the energy transition while intensifying local socio-environmental conflicts. Although environmental and economic impacts of wind energy are widely researched, the role of democratic communication in legitimizing this transition remains underexplored. title: Evaluation of Comprehension and Views on Green Cities and Sustainable Urban Environment: A Developmental Perspective
abstract: Green cities and the sustainable urban environment have gained popularity worldwide, both in literature and in practice. It is, however, indicative that, it is still unpopular among Nigerians. abstract: Organic coconut sugar exports depend on claims about origin and process that buyers cannot verify directly, so exporting firms are increasingly required to make their information verifiable. Previous studies have examined traceability systems and business ethics separately and have rarely tested how transparency reaches performance, which constitutes the research gap of this study. abstract: The use of near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy for material classification in recycling facilities has become increasingly prominent due to its rapid, accurate and non-destructive capabilities. However, the high cost of commercial NIR spectrometers – driven largely by their wide spectral range and high resolution – limits widespread adoption, particularly in the smaller-scale decentralized waste segregation stations. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Feminists for Life's (FFL) rhetoric and activism on US college campuses in the 1990s as a case study into the complexities of organizing against abortion in a historical context whereby few supports existed for young pregnant women. title: Evaluating the Use of Blockchain Technology in Enhancing Transparency and Security in Supply Chain Management
abstract: Blockchain technology is revolutionising UK supply chain management by improving security and transparency. This study examines how blockchain mitigates fraud, improves traceability, and optimises operational efficiency through Everledger, IBM Food Trust, Maersk TradeLens, and Walmart UK case studies. abstract: This study examines Piil Pesenggiri as the basic framework of education based on local wisdom and its role in promoting cultural identity and social cohesion among the people of Lampung Pepadun. title: Laying the Groundwork for Moveable Heritage Disaster Risk Management: A Database-Driven Evacuation Tool at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale
abstract: This paper presents a case study conducted at the Musée d’Archéologie Nationale (National Archaeology Museum) in France, to develop a dedicated database application to safeguard its moveable heritage from risks, as a foundational component of the museum’s wider Disaster Risk Management (DRM) strategy. It responds to calls from both national and international cultural organisations to implement DRM strategies within cultural heritage institutions, emphasising the importance of preparedness in an era marked by increasing frequency and intensity of natural and anthropogenic disasters worldwide. title: Operationalizing the CBDR-RC principle in the WHO Pandemic Agreement: from environmental law to pandemic governance
abstract: Introduction The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, represents a major step toward strengthening global pandemic governance after COVID-19. However, the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) was not incorporated into the legally binding provisions of the Agreement, leaving unresolved questions regarding how equity-based obligations should be implemented in future pandemic preparedness and response. title: Assessment of Oil Spillage and Its Control in the Oil and Gas Industry in Nigeria
abstract: This project set out to examine the compensation of oil spill victims in the Nigerian oil industry. The compensation of these victims has become clumsy and dark in the wake of oil bunkering, pipeline vandalism, sabotage, since in the past, oil spill was as a result of the activities of the oil companies or operators. abstract: Background Feedlot nutrition is formulated to maximize growth rate and feed efficiency for high-quality meat production; however, high-grain diets can disrupt rumen function and cause digestive disorders, the inclusion of non-nutritive feed additives helps counter these effects, thereby enhancing growth performance and overall feed efficiency. abstract: Abstract This survey paper opens a Special Issue of ZDM – Mathematics Education on “Enhancing data literacy for citizenship: Innovative approaches in data science and statistics education.” In this paper we aim to conceptualize ‘data literacy for citizenship’ (DataLitCit), going beyond prior conceptualizations of statistical and data literacies. title: Creating Safe Schools: School Leadership and Teachers’ Perceptions of Child Safety and Well-Being
abstract: This study examines the role of school leadership in promoting child safety and well-being in a public basic education school in Dumaguete City, Philippines. Anchored in an integrated leadership–school climate–child safety and well-being framework, it adopts a quantitative, descriptive-correlational, cross-sectional design. A structured questionnaire is intended for 79 teachers from a population of 98 to assess school leadership practices and teachers’ perceptions of child safety and well-being. abstract: Abstract Background The field of interventional bronchoscopy (IB) has experienced rapid advancements over the past two decades, evolving from a predominantly diagnostic modality into a highly technological specialty encompassing use of endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS), electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB), robotic-assisted bronchoscopy (RAB), transbronchial cryobiopsy, airway stenting, and image-guided interventions. title: A bibliometric analytics study of hybrid choice modeling evolution and decision-making trends from 2010 to 2026
abstract: Over the past 15 years, Hybrid choice modeling (HCM), also known as the integrated choice and latent variable (ICLV) approach, has become an increasingly important extension of discrete choice modeling. Despite the rapid growth in HCM publications, the structural and temporal evolution of this research field has not yet been systematically examined. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the HCM literature from 2010 to 2026. abstract: The Ketungau Basin in West Kalimantan is classified as an unexplored basin, although geological, seismic, and non-seismic data are available for petroleum system evaluation. This study evaluates the geochemical characteristics and source rock potential of the Ketungau and Kantu Formations using Total Organic Carbon (TOC) and Rock-Eval Pyrolysis. title: Public-Private Collaboration and Spaces for Innovation: The Evolution of the Digital District of the Valencian Community and its Precursors (1982-2024)
abstract: This article analyses the implementation of innovation policies in Alicante (Spain) between 1982 and 2024, exploring public-private collaboration in the Digital District of the Valencian Community (DDCV) and its predecessors: the Innovation Triangle and Ciudad de la Luz. Drawing on qualitative methods and primary business sources, it reconstructs the historical trajectory of these initiatives and assesses the impact of political cycles on their continuity. title: A DEMATEL-TOPSIS control model for enhancing rock mass rating reliability in weak rock conditions
abstract: Purpose. This study aims to improve the reliability of the classical Rock Mass Rating system by introducing a control-based DEMATEL-TOPSIS framework that explicitly incorporates parameter interactions and reduces classification uncertainty near boundary conditions. Methods. Parameter ratings were represented using triangular fuzzy numbers to model evaluation uncertainty, DEMATEL was applied to quantify interrelationships among classification criteria, and TOPSIS was used to determine the most representative rock mass class. title: Rethinking Carbon Taxation as Strategic Management: Insights from Mintzberg’s Ten Schools
abstract: This study evaluates carbon tax policies from the perspective of strategic management, employing Mintzberg’s ten schools of thought as the analytical framework. These schools-comprising both prescriptive approaches (design, planning, and positioning) and descriptive perspectives (entrepreneurial, cognitive, learning, power, cultural, environmental, and configuration)-offer a multidimensional understanding of how carbon taxation strategies are conceived, implemented, and adapted over time. title: Insights and opportunities from materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions in the U.S.
abstract: Materials chemistry research at primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs) in the United States is often characterized by the constraints faculty face: limited instrumentation, smaller research groups, heavier teaching loads, and rapid student turnover. This Perspective argues that PUI materials chemistry research is better understood not as a diminished form of research university science, but as a distinct and productive research mode with its own logic and strengths. title: Impact of Funding Constraints on Rural Development Project Implementation in Owo Local Government Council, Ondo State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the impact of funding constraints on rural development project implementation in Owo Local Government Council, Ondo State, Nigeria. The research was driven by concerns over persistent project delays, abandonment, and poor-quality outcomes resulting from inadequate and irregular funding. The study adopted a quantitative research design and used data collected from 237 respondents selected from the Owo Local Government workforce. title: False kings and imagined protestants: why schismogenesis does not explain variation in inequality among Indigenous societies of the Pacific Coast
abstract: Indigenous societies along the temperate Pacific coast of North America embody diverse cultural institutions. This variation is conventionally classified into two distinct cultural areas: the Northwest Coast (NWC) and California (CAL). Discussion of the environmental, material, social, and ideological variation in these societies has a long and continuing history in anthropology. abstract: Abstract Integration of Internet of Things (IoT) and Edge Computing (EC) presents significant challenges, particularly in guaranteeing secure communication amid IoT devices and cloud systems formerly to data aggregation. Existing aggregation schemes often compromise on cost-effectiveness while struggling to preserve data integrity and confidentiality in face of emerging quantum computing threats. title: Beyond participation: procedural justice, relational legitimacy, and sustained engagement in evaluating the effectiveness of DDR programs
abstract: Evaluation of disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration (DDR) programs tends to focus on weapons collection, demobilization of combatants, reduction of violence, and participation in programs. These measures provide less insight into why people remain engaged in peacebuilding implementations after the programs have concluded. abstract: The provision of safe, high-quality drinking water is becoming increasingly important due to the growing anthropogenic pressure on water resources, the deterioration of environmental conditions, and stricter requirements for the sanitary and hygienic characteristics of water. Drinking water quality is one of the key factors determining public health, ecosystem stability, and regional environmental safety. title: His life is his message
abstract: Abstract This tribute about William (Bill) Labov is focused on his work on AAVE (African American Vernacular English), establishing his career-long commitment to social and educational justice for the Black community. The title (“His Life is His Message”) are the words of Mahatma Gandhi and reflects Bill’s work and spirit—his words, his principles, and the motivation he instilled in others to act with authenticity and integrity. title: Beyond “Chimerica”: U.S.–China strategic competition and African agency in a disordered world
abstract: The intensification of strategic competition between the United States and China has become one of the defining dynamics of 21st-century international relations, reshaping patterns of global governance, economic interdependence and geopolitical alignment. While existing scholarship has largely examined this rivalry through the lens of great-power competition, Africa is frequently portrayed as a passive arena in which external actors pursue competing interests. title: A Design of Relief Logistics System by Axioms
abstract: Aim: This study scientifically addresses aid logistics operations, a subfield related to disaster management. It aims to conduct a design study that will guide those in authority. The study is in line with the classical logistics flow, with a value-oriented lean perspective, and eliminates processes that are not beneficial to disaster victims and include waste. abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) ha dejado de ser una promesa para convertirse en una realidad que empieza a transformar la consulta pediátrica, impulsada por el acceso a grandes bases de datos y por la digitalización de la asistencia, especialmente a través de la historia clínica electrónica y la creciente interoperabilidad. title: A circular approach to reduce, recover and recycle graphene-based printed electronics
abstract: Abstract The shift towards renewable materials and circular processes is crucial for sustainable printed electronics. Conventional conductive inks rely on petrochemical-based solvents and synthetic binders that hinder recyclability and recovery of high-value materials. Here, we report a recyclable graphene ink formulated with a bio-renewable terpene solvent and cellulose-based binder for electrochemical sensing applications. abstract: This study aims to reconstruct the paradigm of wasathiyah (moderate) character education based on Islamic humanism at the Al-Asror Islamic Boarding School in Semarang. It employs a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and the analysis of relevant documents. title: Designing curriculum at the intersection of language, culture, and coloniality: reflections from primary French textbooks in Mauritius
abstract: Curriculum development, specifically textbook conception, in postcolonial contexts like Mauritius is neither a neutral nor a primarily technical undertaking; it remains a deeply situated process shaped by linguistic and cultural diversity, tacit colonial language hierarchies, and underlying ethnic tensions. This paper explores these dynamics as they manifested during the conception of Grades 5 and 6 Primary French textbooks within the Nine Year Continuous Basic Education reform. abstract: Agritourism is increasingly positioned as a practical route to encourage more responsible environmental behaviour by bringing tourists into direct contact with farms, local landscapes, and everyday sustainability practices. Building on established measurement work on key pro-environmental constructs, this paper takes a narrower and more applied step by testing whether gender, age, and income meaningfully differentiate tourists’ environmental awareness, concern, values, knowledge, attitudes, and pro-environmental behaviour in agritourism settings. title: Global Research Trends in Centella asiatica for Cosmetic and Skin-Related Applications: A Bibliometric Analysis: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Centella asiatica (L.) Urb. has attracted considerable scientific interest because of its effects on wound repair, inflammation, antioxidant activity, collagen formation, scar formation, skin barrier function, and skin aging. In the current study, a bibliometric mapping approach was applied to investigate global research activity on C. asiatica in cosmetic and skin-related applications. abstract: The plant genus Riccia L. comprises a highly diverse group of complex thalloid liverworts and accounts for a substantial share of bryophyte diversity. However, the literature indicates that Riccia liverworts are widely distributed but little is known about Riccia species from semi-arid environments of western India. title: The Effect Of Price, Packaging, And Product Quality On The Purchase Decision Of Msme Products (Case Study Of Palm Souvenir Shops In Lubuklinggau City)
abstract: MSME souvenir products are one of the local business sectors that help support regional economic growth by offering products that represent the unique characteristics of an area and are often purchased as gifts or souvenirs. To remain competitive and continue growing, MSME businesses need to understand consumer needs and preferences. Therefore, identifying the factors that influence purchasing decisions is important for improving business performance and competitiveness. title: Metabolomics and network pharmacology of Ethiopian antidiabetic medicinal plants: A comprehensive framework for mechanistic elucidation and drug discovery
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) affects approximately 537 million adults worldwide, and this number is expected to increase to 783 million by 2045, highlighting the urgent need for effective and affordable therapeutic strategies. In Ethiopia, where nearly 80% of the population depends on traditional medicine for primary healthcare, more than 30 medicinal plant species have demonstrated antidiabetic activity in experimental studies. title: Work Stress in Chinese Hospitals: Evidence Across Doctors, Nurses, and Administrative Staff with Regional Patterns and International Comparisons
abstract: Work stress among doctors, nurses, and administrative staff is an important hospital-management concern because it is associated with workforce stability, service quality, and patient safety. This structured narrative review synthesizes 20 core sources published between 2000 and August 2026, including empirical studies, reviews, and three foundational theoretical articles. title: Algorithmic Silences: Postcolonial Blind Spots in Dutch AI Media Discourse
abstract: The Kingdom of the Netherlands comprises four countries: the Netherlands, Aruba, Curaçao, and Sint Maarten, as well as three public entities located on the islands of Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, and Saba. All these regions are former Dutch colonies and are located in the Global South. News coverage from former colonisers toward their former colonies is shaped by historical frameworks, political interests, evolving global power dynamics, and unequal news creation. title: Bridging the gap between damaged infrastructures and disaster mortality
abstract: Abstract Driven by the lack of global empirical data, there is limited research that analyzed the relationship between infrastructure damage and disaster impact. In this research, we addressed this gap by scraping 79 Post Disaster Needs Assessment reports to collect disaster specific infrastructure damage data for 79 disaster events of this century. title: Brief communication: InSAR Svalbard Ground Motion Service – observing surface displacements in the High Arctic
abstract: The InSAR Svalbard Ground Motion Service (GMS) provides open-access surface displacement maps and time series in the Svalbard archipelago, derived from Sentinel-1 Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR). The service provides seasonal products capturing short-term 2016–2024 displacements and interannual products documenting long-term 2018–2024 velocity trends. title: Comparative environmental and economic assessment of biogas and biodiesel production from palm oil mill effluent (POME)
abstract: Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME) is one of the major by-products of the palm oil industry and represents a promising feedstock for renewable energy production through biogas and biodiesel pathways. This study comparatively evaluated the environmental, energy, and economic performance of biogas and biodiesel production from POME using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), energy performance analysis, and a preliminary economic assessment. title: Distinct Environmental DNA States Reveal Biodiversity and Transport Patterns Across Alpine Watersheds
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) exists in three states: membrane-bound, adsorbed and dissolved. These states differ in persistence and degradation, strongly influencing the interpretation of eDNA data. Despite this, they have rarely been separated and analyzed independently from environmental samples. title: Integrative analysis of immune-cell eQTLs and Mendelian randomization identifies genetically supported genes associated with breast cancer susceptibility
abstract: Breast cancer susceptibility loci identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have revealed extensive genetic contribution to disease risk, yet the genes and immune regulatory mechanisms underlying these associations remain largely unresolved. Here, we integrated immune-cell-specific cis-eQTL data with breast cancer GWAS using a two-sample Mendelian randomization framework. title: Climate‐Driven Shifts in Flowering Phenology of Wild Tropical Plants Uncovered by Century‐Long Herbarium and Photographic Records
abstract: Research on phenological responses to climate change has primarily focused on temperate regions, while tropical species remain critically understudied due to a historical scarcity of long-term monitoring data in these areas. We utilized digitized herbarium specimens and photographs to analyze century-long shifts (1921-2020) in the flowering phenology of 56 native plant species on Hainan Island, China. title: Strengthening evidence on migrant workers’ health in Nepal
abstract: Abstract Thousands of Nepalese labour migrants have died abroad in past decades, and morbidity is also high. The high volume of data collected through pre-departure health screening, unfortunately, remains largely unused. Making better use of health data, including by trusted public health researchers, could help develop health interventions for migrant workers.

title: CMIP6 data usage: lessons learned from more than 200 million downloads
abstract: Earth system simulations from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are considered the gold standard in terms of representation of the Earth's climate system, its past and present states, and possible future evolution. As CMIP moves into its seventh phase, the increasing complexity of Earth system models (ESMs) means that there is a greater need for infrastructure resources to store, distribute and utilize CMIP simulations. abstract: This paper examines inflation dynamics in Türkiye within a state-dependent Phillips curve framework by jointly considering domestic and external factors. Using monthly data for the period 2005–2025, conditional relationships across different forecast horizons are estimated through the local projections (LPs) method. title: Why should fisheries professionals care about instream flow and water level conservation?
abstract: Abstract Conservation of instream flows and water levels (instream flows) are vital to sustaining healthy aquatic, riparian, and terrestrial ecosystems. Natural instream flow regimes provide habitat and life history cues, sustain ecological communities, influence water temperatures and other water quality attributes, and affect geomorphic processes. title: Digital Transformation and Agricultural Supply Chain Resilience: The Mediating Role of Sustainable Consumption and Production
abstract: Digital transformation has emerged as a critical driver of agricultural supply chain resilience, yet the mechanisms through which technology investment translates into resilience outcomes remain inadequately understood. Addressing this gap, this study examines the mediating role of sustainable consumption and production in this relationship. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the SDG12 framework, an integrated model is developed and tested using survey data from 423 agricultural enterprises across six provinces in China. title: Teacher Retention in Remote Areas: The Role of Leadership, Intrinsic Motivation and Organizational Support
abstract: Teacher retention is a critical issue in educational management, particularly in remote areas such as East Java. This study analyzes the association between principal leadership style, intrinsic motivation, and organizational support with teacher retention. Data were collected from 206 teachers using the PLS-SEM approach. abstract: Rural human-settlement systems in cold regions mediate the interaction between climatic stress, population restructuring and unequal access to housing and public services, yet the relevant evidence remains divided among building science, spatial analysis and governance research. This review synthesizes 196 studies retained through a PRISMA-informed search and screening process. abstract: Abstract China's recent shareholding cooperative (SC) reform heralds a shift from expropriation‐led rural change to a post‐expropriation regime in which the countryside is reconstituted through circulation, capitalization, and new forms of collective governance. title: Geological hydrogen storage in South Asian sedimentary basins thermodynamic considerations, geotechnical challenges, and energy perspectives
abstract: Geological hydrogen storage (GHS) is a critical technology for enabling large-scale, low-carbon energy systems in South Asia within the water–energy–carbon nexus. abstract: The main purpose of this study was to examine the effect of stakeholder engagement on the performance of the Sustainable Agricultural Intensification and Food Security Project (SAIP II) in Rwamagana District. Specifically, the study examined stakeholder engagement in planning, project implementation, and monitoring and evaluation. abstract: Climate change has become a major threat to environmental sustainability and food security in Nigeria, particularly among rural communities that rely heavily on agriculture for their livelihoods. Increasing incidences of drought, flooding, desertification, land degradation, and erratic rainfall have significantly reduced agricultural productivity and intensified food insecurity. abstract: Abstract The neo-Brandeisian anti-monopoly movement that emerged in the United States following the 2008 financial crisis provides a new perspective on anti-monopoly thought, politics, and practice in the less recent past. The “home protection” crusade led by renowned temperance activist Frances Willard is a case in point. title: Community Empowerment Through Health Education on Rational Antibiotic Use in Sempu, Banyuwangi
abstract: Unsupervised antibiotic use remains a public health concern and may contribute to antimicrobial resistance, inappropriate medication use, and antibiotic-related renal impairment. Limited knowledge regarding antibiotic indications, acquisition, dosage, and resistance highlights the need for targeted community education. This community service activity aimed to improve residents’ knowledge, perceptions, and behavioral intentions regarding rational antibiotic use in RT 02, RW 04, Sempu, Banyuwangi Regency. title: Beyond taxonomic richness: Network topology and functional gene abundance reveal tillage and nitrogen as physiological and topological filters across heterogeneous corn agroecosystems
abstract: Soil microbial communities underpin key ecosystem functions, yet their responses to agricultural intensification remain difficult to predict across heterogeneous landscapes. This study evaluated the impact of nitrogen (N) fertilization rates (0–200 kg N/ha) and tillage intensity (conventional ploughing, reduced tillage, direct drilling) on bacterial diversity, functional potential, and co-occurrence networks across 84 corn fields in southern Québec, Canada. abstract: The Nigerian print media industry is currently grappling with an "economics of decline" and digital disruption, resulting in high mortality rates for legacy publications. abstract: Increasing drought frequency and intensity across East Africa are altering ecological conditions and intensifying interactions between pastoral communities and large carnivores, posing significant challenges for biodiversity conservation and pastoral livelihoods. abstract: El emprendimiento en el ámbito universitario constituye una alternativa vinculada con la formación profesional, el desarrollo de competencias y las transformaciones del entorno socioeconómico. abstract: Automatic voltage regulator (AVR) systems require fast, accurate, and robust voltage regulation under parameter variations, external disturbances, measurement noise, and actuator limitations. abstract: Objective: To evaluate the effect of video- plus brochure-assisted education versus brochure-only education on pain, anxiety, and vital signs in patients undergoing chest tube insertion. abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of legal incentives on the performance of startups in Algeria, focusing on the incentives provided for under Investment Law No. 18-22 and Public Procurement Law No. 12-23. title: Towards Vision‐Language Geo‐Foundation Models: A Survey
abstract: ABSTRACT Vision‐Language Foundation Models (VLFMs) have made remarkable progress on various multimodal tasks, such as image captioning, image–text retrieval, visual question answering, and visual grounding. However, most methods rely on training with general image datasets, and the lack of geospatial data leads to poor performance on earth observation. abstract: Abstract The maritime shipping industry is responsible for approximately 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions. As a result, it faces growing regulatory and environmental pressure to shift towards cleaner alternative fuels. Green hydrogen, produced from renewable sources, is the possible alternative to change the maritime industry, as it represents a zero-emission alternative. abstract: The property position of Galo women in West Siang District cannot be determined merely by asking whether women are socially described as heirs or whether daughters receive property in practice. abstract: Climate change acts as a risk multiplier, increasing disaster hazards worldwide. This study assesses the regional decarbonization of Russia’s Housing and Communal Services (HCS) sector through the lens of disaster risk reduction (DRR), using the IPCC AR6 hazard-exposure-vulnerability framework. abstract: This study examines how the textual tourist gaze is expressed in online reviews of Jiangnan classical gardens through ABSA-inspired dominant-aspect classification and review-level sentiment analysis of 30,478 reviews from 28 sites. abstract: Abstract Accurate and timely assessment of soil tillage practices is crucial for monitoring sustainability in agriculture. To achieve more site-specific discrimination, it is necessary to understand the spectral and temporal properties of tillage practices across seasons. This study presents developments in tillage-practice discrimination by comparing two high-resolution remote sensing datasets, PlanetScope and Sentinel-2, to characterise and discriminate fields under intensive tillage (IT) and conservation tillage (CT) in the winter and spring seasons. abstract: Hong Kong, recognized as a preeminent international insurance hub, is experiencing a significant transformation in its traditional insurance landscape, primarily driven by the rise of Insurtech startups, including fully virtual insurers. abstract: Across Europe, economically and demographically declining regions offer limited educational and occupational opportunities for young people. These opportunities are often restricted further for those in vulnerable life situations, as vulnerabilities are connected to and impacted by limited resources and capacities. While many young Europeans move from declining to more thriving regions in search of better educational and labour market opportunities, some choose—or are forced by their circumstances—to stay. abstract: AFLIBER v.2 provides an updated synthesis of vascular plant distributions in the Iberian Peninsula and the Balearic Islands, a major Mediterranean biodiversity hotspot. abstract: The five Regional Internet Registries (RIRs) provide the critical function of IP address resource delegation and registration. abstract: Voice provides a natural and immediate interface for AI agents. abstract: Communities exhibiting cyclic (i.e., ``winnerless'') competition occur throughout nature. These systems can exhibit qualitatively different long-term behavior depending on the strength of inter-species competition and a specific property of the number of interacting species: parity. abstract: The aeroelastic instability known as vortex induced vibrations (VIV) has its origin in the coupling of bluff body shedding and the structure dynamics, and can have adverse effects on several industrial fields. abstract: Today's Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) are too small and too noisy to solve large combinatorial optimization problems directly, so practical hybrid solvers split a problem into pieces and iterate a decompose-solve-aggregate loop over whatever backends are available: classical heuristics, simulators, emulators, or a QPU. abstract: Multi-party interaction is a central setting for human communication and a necessary target for human-agent interaction systems that must participate in group conversation. abstract: A minimal perfect hash function (or MPHF) maps a set of \(n\) keys to \([n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) without collisions. abstract: The sooner we receive information, and the more accurate it is, the better planning decisions we can make. Every day, prediction markets let anyone bet on tomorrow's high temperature in cities around the world, creating a market-implied forecast built on dispersed information. We use the past five years of market data from the Kalshi exchange for seven American cities to extract, hour by hour, the market-implied forecast. title: Centroid Angle Estimation of Multiple Scatterers Using Monopulse Radar with Frequency Diversity
abstract: The monopulse technique determines the angle of a target by comparing signals from two narrow beams, yielding a precise angular estimate with low complexity. However, it struggles to resolve multiple closely spaced scatterers within the same resolution cell. Existing methods for estimating multiple scatterer angles involve complex signal processing and system modifications. title: Properties of biodiversity indices that incorporate future extinction risk
abstract: The loss of biodiversity due to the likely widespread extinction of species in the near future is a focus of current concern in conservation biology. One approach to measure the impact of this extinction is based on the predicted loss of phylogenetic diversity. These predictions have become a focus of the Zoological Society of London's 'EDGE2' program for quantifying biodiversity loss and involves considering the HED (heightened evolutionary distinctiveness) and HEDGE (heightened evolutionary distinctiveness and globally endangered) indices which are based on phylogenetic diversity on a tree.

abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in marine environments must navigate rugged bathymetry, ocean-current disturbances, sudden obstacles, and limited perception. abstract: In response to the unprecedented environmental pressures on the Arctic marine cryosphere, sea ice geoengineering (SIGE) has recently emerged as a potential strategy to restore the Arctic marine environment. The restoration of the environment has been affirmed by international courts as part of states’ due diligence obligations or as a form of reparation deriving from state responsibility. Yet, technological interventions in the Arctic marine cryosphere can be perceived as efforts to expand exploitative uses of ocean spaces, which could result in profound socio-ecological consequences. title: Drag-reduction mechanisms in autonomous underwater vehicle formations: Physical analysis and physics-guided surrogate optimization
abstract: The hydrodynamic interaction between closely spaced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in formation produces strongly nonlinear drag responses. In the present configuration space, two dominant pressure-related mechanisms are identified: stern pressure recovery at the leader and bow low-pressure immersion at the follower. abstract: The paper proposes a cost-effective solution for simultaneously determining the coordinates for a group of inexpensive autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). It is assumed that each AUV lacks expensive precision time system and absolute velocity log. The presented method for providing navigation support for a group of AUVs is based on the use of a short-baseline acoustic navigation system (SB ANS). abstract: This study develops a free-surface-constrained hydrodynamic modelling and control simulation framework for an underactuated Autonomous Underwater Vehicle manoeuvring near the water surface. title: A lag-compensated kinematic integration network for short-horizon AUV trajectory prediction under degraded navigation observations
abstract: Reliable short-horizon trajectory prediction for autonomous underwater vehicles is difficult during Doppler velocity log (DVL) outages because the latest reliable navigation state becomes stale relative to the current vehicle state. This paper presents a lag-compensated kinematic integration network (LC-KIN) that treats this staleness as a displacement of the prediction boundary. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles operating in confined environments such as shipwreck interiors, underwater archaeological sites, and aquaculture structures must coordinate both position and orientation to safely navigate narrow passages. Existing path planning methods model the vehicle as a point mass or a sphere, neglecting the rotational degrees of freedom critical to such tasks. title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. abstract: Underwater vectored thruster is an important development direction for the propulsion system of autonomous underwater vehicles. However, conventional vectored thruster systems generally consist of multiple actuators and complex transmission structures, which results in large system mass, accumulation of errors and poor dynamic performance. abstract: Biomimetic underwater vehicles (BUVs) are an evolving class of autonomous underwater systems that mimic the locomotion mechanisms of aquatic animals to achieve high maneuverability, low acoustic signature, and energy-efficient propulsion. However, their motion control remains challenging due to highly nonlinear dynamics, strong fluid–structure interactions, and tight coupling between propulsion and vehicle motion. abstract: The limited endurance of autonomous underwater vehicles has motivated the development of in situ wave energy harvesting. This paper proposes a novel wave-powered multi-joint submersible robot that integrates articulated joints with buoyancy bladders, pectoral fins, suction attachment, and retractable propellers. abstract: Planktonic foraminiferal assemblages preserved in deep-sea sediments provide valuable information on assemblage composition, diversity, and upper-ocean habitat structure. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles require the integration of inertial, velocity, optical, and acoustic measurements for reliable underwater navigation where GPS signals are unavailable or intermittent. During a mission, the utility of these modalities may vary due to changes in environmental visibility, Doppler velocity log tracking, acoustic geometries, or available infrastructure. abstract: Near-surface operations conducted by underwater vehicles (UVs) feature strong nonlinear disturbances and speed-dependent control effectiveness, which make depth and heading regulation challenging under strict state and actuator limits. title: Summertime Aerosol Composition in Southern Greenlandic Fjords: Impacts of Sources and New Particle Formation Events
abstract: Abstract Arctic fjord systems are a dynamic interface between ocean, ice, and land, with high summertime biological activity. abstract: Hybrid underwater robotic vehicles integrate features typically found in separate classes of vehicles: autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), amphibious robots, and cross-medium robotic vehicles. abstract: The deployment of multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) for large-scale oceanic search and mapping missions is frequently constrained by inefficient task assignment and strict collision avoidance protocols. Traditional deconfliction methods block adjacent operational regions, significantly reducing the feasible search area and delaying the exploration of high-priority zones. Action-conditioned dynamics learning for model predictive control of flexible fish locomotion
abstract: Closed-loop navigation of an autonomous flexible fish requires rapid prediction of the trajectory evolution induced by body-wave commands. However, evaluating candidate command sequences one by one with high-fidelity flow simulations would incur prohibitive computational cost. To address this challenge, this work proposes an action-conditioned fish–fluid dynamics learning framework for predictive planning of flexible-fish locomotion. The framework uses disagreement-driven active sampling to selectively enrich the trajectory database in regions where the latent dynamics remain highly uncertain.

title: Launch and recovery systems for autonomous underwater vehicles on unmanned boats
abstract: The article examines the design and operating principle Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS) for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) based on unmanned boats (UBs) of various purposes. Some of the patented technical solutions of the IPMT FEB RAS in this field are described. The results of experimental studies of the operational characteristics of the LARS for a small-sized AUV based on the UB are presented.

title: In situ assessment of a single underwater acoustic vector sensor for direction-of-arrival estimation over multiple ranges
abstract: Underwater acoustic vector sensors (AVSs) are widely used for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in underwater surveillance and marine bioacoustics applications. Compared with conventional hydrophone arrays, a single compact AVS offers greater flexibility and simpler deployment while enabling DOA estimation using the acoustic active-intensity method (AIM). abstract: The aim of this study is to examine how residents’ perceptions of cruise tourism in a spatially constrained heritage city are structured across multiple domains and which perceptual dimensions most strongly affect support for further cruise tourism growth. abstract: The taxonomic history of the pagurid hermit crab Ostraconotus spatulipes A. abstract: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) maintained its clove monopoly in the Maluku Islands through Hongi Tochten, a series of naval expeditions traditionally interpreted as instruments of military coercion and commercial control. title: Extreme challenges in the coldest continent: 10 years of Antarctic adventure sport tourism (2014–2024), participation trends and qualitative risk analysis
abstract: Abstract Adventure tourism in Antarctica has expanded significantly over the past couple of decades and has brought along new challenges for managing human and environmental safety in one of the world’s most remote regions. This study provides a retrospective qualitative analysis of participation in and associated risks with adventure sport tourism activities conducted between 2014 and 2024, using data obtained from the International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators (IAATO). abstract: Lakes are large natural sources of methane (CH4), a potent greenhouse gas, resulting from the net balance of inputs from anaerobic and oxic methane production (OMP) and removal by methane oxidation (MOX). Here we investigate spatial patterns and causes of MOX variability in 79 African lakes. MOX is highest in the most productive lakes presumably due to methanotrophs attached to phytoplankton, as well as in lakes draining the wetlands of the Congo basin presumably due to inputs of methanotrophs from flooded forest soils. MOX represents the largest sink of dissolved CH4 in the mixed layer (>70%)

title: South Atlantic range extensions of the caridean shrimps Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 (Alpheidae) and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930) (Palaemonidae), identified using an integrative taxonomic approach
abstract: We report range extensions for two species of caridean shrimp, Synalpheus pandionis Coutière, 1909 and Periclimenaeus perlatus (Boone, 1930), from the continental shelf off Bahia, Brazil. These records represent the southernmost occurrences for both species in the south-western Atlantic. Synalpheus pandionis was found associated with the sponge Mycale ( Zygomycale ) angulosa (Duchassaing & Michelotti, 1864), while P. perlatus was found associated with the sponge Aplysina fistularis (Pallas, 1766). title: High-Altitude Exposure: Effects on Cognitive Performance, Neurovascular Mechanisms, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: Abstract Travel to and work at high altitudes expose individuals to hypobaric hypoxia; however, its effects on neural activity and function remain insufficiently understood. Here, we present findings from a longitudinal panel study incorporating oxygen supplementation tests in individuals who traveled from low altitude (Beijing, ∼50 meters above sea level (m.a.s.l.)) to high altitude (Xizang, 3600–5000 m.a.s.l.) and subsequently returned to low altitude. title: Mercury in Fish from Guanabara Bay, Southeast Brazil: Tissue-Specific Accumulation and Human Health Risks
abstract: Abstract Guanabara Bay is Brazil’s second-largest bay and has a long history of intense industrial and domestic pollution. Some local communities rely on fish as a primary protein source, justifying an assessment of mercury (Hg) contamination. This study determined total mercury (THg) concentrations in nine fish species and evaluated the toxicological risks associated with human consumption. One hundred specimens were analyzed, and samples of muscle, liver, and gills were collected. Hyperbaric medicine in Latin America did not emerge from a single institution or a single pioneering individual. Rather, it evolved through diverse national experiences that were shaped by geography, maritime traditions, military and civilian medicine, engineering, scientific curiosity, and the dedication of countless, often silent, professionals. title: Acoustic emission monitoring of infrastructure using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) techniques - possibilities, limitations, and optimization
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) testing is an established method for structural health monitoring and damage detection in engineering structures. Conventional AE systems are based on piezoelectric sensors that are applied at discrete locations, requiring extensive cabling and offering limited spatial coverage. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) provides an alternative approach as a fiber-optic measurement technique, in which a single optical fiber cable serves as a continuous, spatially distributed sensor. In this work, both methods are systematically compared with respect to their detection capability
institutions: Fraunhofer Institute for Ceramic Technologies and Systems

title: An annotated district-wise account of Odonata (Dragonflies and Damselflies) from Uttarakhand, India
abstract: This study presents a list of 135 odonate species recorded from Uttarakhand, based on an extensive and critical review of published literature. Notes on the present status of some recorded taxa are included. The documented diversity includes 15 families and 73 genera, comprising 84 species of Anisoptera and 51 species of Zygoptera. Among the districts, Dehradun has the highest recorded species richness, followed by Nainital and Pauri Garhwal. Five species recorded are endemic to India. abstract: Abstract The “Collaborative Gas Hydrate R&D Project in Alaska,” led by the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC), the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and the U.S. Geological Survey, aims to examine and assess gas hydrate reservoir systems, their production behavior, potential environmental impacts, and extraction methodologies. The existing oil and gas infrastructure on the Alaska North Slope (ANS) has enabled long-term field studies and helped pave the way for evaluating Alaska’s gas hydrate production characteristics. title: A New Record of Dirivultus spinigulatus (Copepoda: Dirivultidae) from Japan Associated with a Siboglinid Tubeworm
abstract: The siphonostomatoid copepod Dirivultus spinigulatus Humes, 1999 (Dirivultidae) was originally described as an associate of the siboglinid tubeworm Paraescarpia echinospica Southward, Schulze, and Tunnicliffe, 2002 from the Edison Seamount hydrothermal vent in Papua New Guinea. Here, we report a new record and range extension of this copepod from the Off Toi cold seep in Suruga Bay, Japan where it was also found on P. echinospica. title: Carbon intensity compliance of a crude oil tanker: A five-year voyage-level analysis
abstract: The Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) of ships is evaluated annually; however, this aggregated calculation may conceal substantial variation in carbon intensity across different voyage types. To investigate how voyage parameters affect CII outcomes, this study presents a five-year (2020–2024) voyage-level empirical analysis of a Suezmax crude oil tanker. The findings indicate that laden voyages with high waiting time (>40% of voyage days) exhibit the poorest CII performance, averaging 4.84 gCO₂/dwt·nm, well above the 2024 required threshold of 3.30 gCO₂/dwt · nm. title: The anatomy and taxonomy of selected Neogastropoda (Gastropoda) of phylogenetic importance
abstract: Recently the phylogeny of the order Neogastropoda based on exon-capture [Fedosov et al., 2026], has confirmed the monophyly of the group and achieved high resolution for many deep nodes. Thorough examination of the sequenced species frequently revealed novel and distinctive morphological characters, and in several cases highlighted unresolved taxonomic issues. Some sequenced species proved to be new to science, while others required reassessment of their generic or familial placement in light of the phylogenetic results. The anatomy of the anterior foregut of Enigmavasidae is described herein

title: Structural attributes of dominant seagrass species modulate invertebrate assemblages within the Shark Bay world Heritage Area
abstract: Abstract The structural complexity of seagrass meadows plays a central role in shaping the diversity and composition of associated invertebrate assemblages. In the Shark Bay World Heritage Area of Western Australia, the dominant species Amphibolis antarctica and Posidonia australis differ markedly in their above- and below-ground morphology, yet the invertebrate assemblages they support remain poorly characterised. institutions: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions

title: Displacement and the Reshaping of Indigenous Livelihoods: A Review of the Literature on Mumbai’s Koli and Agri Communities
abstract: The Koli and Agri communities have occupied a visibly glaring space in the landscape of Mumbai since time immemorial.They have made their presence felt not only demographically, but also culturally and politically.However, despite being the city's age-old inhabitants and landowners, both communities have been pushed to the margins for various reasons.From facing a serious bout of identity crisis to being introduced to other religions, the Koli and Agri communities are plagued with a whole host of problems.As a permanent solution to these problems and also for a sense of security, the two commu

title: Dorsal-Fin Musculoskeletal System of Oarfishes (Regalecidae): Fin Rays as Rotating Elements in an Undulatory System
abstract: In addition to lateral undulation, oarfishes (Regalecus spp.) swim by passing unidirectional or counter-propagating waves along the elongated dorsal fin. Such ribbon-finned swimming evolved independently in several groups of teleosts, such as the gymnotiform knifefishes, which have an elongated anal fin. Studies of ribbon-finned swimming in knifefishes led to an interest in the biomimetic potential of this type of propulsion. title: Fletcheria gen. nov. (Ralfsiales, Phaeophyceae): A new crustose brown algal genus clarifying evolutionary relationships of Ralfsia pacifica
abstract: The genus Ralfsia was historically broadly circumscribed but has recently undergone significant taxonomic revision. Based on molecular data, a restricted Ralfsia sensu stricto was delineated that had many species reassigned to new genera and families. The current work builds on that work by resolving the phylogenetic position, defining the morphological features, and establishing the biogeographic distribution of Ralfsia pacifica-a crustose brown alga widely distributed along the eastern Pacific coastline. institutions: Universidad Autónoma de la Ciudad de México
Universidad Católica de la Santísima Concepción

title: First record of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg (Bacillariophyta) from Uganda and South Africa
abstract: African records of Terpsinoë musica Ehrenberg are scarce and mainly restricted to North and West Africa, with previous East African reports limited to Ethiopia and fossil material from Kenya. Here, we extend the geographic distribution of this species in Africa by including two new observations in East and Southern Africa: the first observation of the species in Uganda (East Africa) was in the guts of Oreochromis leucostictus collected from Lake George. title: Scientific Research as Geopolitical Practice: Innovation, Diplomacy, Subversion
abstract: This article examines scientific research as a geopolitical practice. Drawing from IR literature on innovation in geopolitics, scholarship on science diplomacy and hybrid warfare theory, the article suggests that scientific research is best understood as a practice that simultaneously aims at furthering the national interest and at tackling global challenges through diplomatic means. Crucially, moreover, it also contends that uncertainty over which of these aims is primary is what affords scientific research its geopolitical edge. title: Heavy metals in raw cow, goat and sheep milk: Associated dietary exposure and human health risk assessment in eastern Algeria
abstract: In recent years, the presence of heavy metals in milk has emerged as an important public health issue, owing to their potential detrimental effects on milk quality.The present study aimed to assess the occurrence and levels of heavy metals in raw cow, goat, and sheep milk obtained from eastern Algeria.Sixty milk samples were analysed for Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni and Fe using atomic absorption spectrometry.Results demonstrated that Fe (5.49 ± 21.93) was the dominant metal in cow milk, followed by Cu (0.86 ± 0.02) and Cr (0.56 ± 0.05).In goat milk, Fe (9.77 ± 0.69) and Cu (2.79 ± 0.04) were highest, while

title: ‘My Single True Activity’: Sinéad Morrissey’s Found Architecture and Self-Conscious Ecopoetics
abstract: In this article, I will closely read Northern Irish poet Sinéad Morrissey’s more recent work to articulate a ‘found architectural’ mode of poetic attention. Her intricately formal poetry explores its own potential as an ecopoesis or ‘housebuilding’, self-consciously addressing climate catastrophe in ironising domestic registers and typographies. I argue that poems like ‘Found Architecture’, ‘Meteor Shower’ and ‘The Italian Chapel’ foreground the limits and complications of human-made artifice in the context of the overwhelming threat of environmental collapse. title: Challenges of the assessment of nature conservation value of aquatic habitats using microalgae
abstract: Abstract The increasing focus on ecosystem restoration in European environmental policy highlights the need for reliable methods to quantify the nature conservation value (NCV) of aquatic habitats. Current Water Framework Directive (WFD) metrics assess ecological quality mainly through the phytoplankton community composition and abundance. However, these approaches do not reflect properly the real conservation value of the habitats, because they overlook the contribution of rare and unique algal species. title: Deconvolving the depleted mantle: boron systematics from MORB glasses at a ridge–transform intersection
abstract: Boron concentrations and isotopic compositions were determined in basaltic glasses from the Eastern Romanche Ridge Transform Intersection along the Equatorial Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a tectonically and thermally complex ridge–transform setting characterised by reduced magma supply and consequently limited melt homogenisation. title: Aligning risk frameworks with fieldwork realities: extending Rasmussen’s model to scientific research settings
abstract: Scientific fieldwork is an essential component of research across many academic disciplines. Fieldwork entails numerous risks, ranging from interpersonal to environmental risks, and can often result in physical and mental injury or illness. Despite these potential harms, standardized frameworks for understanding, managing, and responding to incidents in fieldwork remain underdeveloped. A limited understanding of incident causation in fieldwork contexts compounds this gap. title: Science as added value? Tourists’ perceptions of science-tourism practices in Antarctic deep-field tourism and implications for ambassadorship
abstract: This paper investigates the role of science-tourism practices in shaping tourists’ perceptions and ethical positioning within Antarctic deep-field tourism. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in East Antarctica and semi-structured interviews, the study examines how operators’ support for science influences tourists’ pre-trip decision-making, perceptions of legitimacy, and environmental responsibility. title: Association between parasitic load and the chemical composition of muscle tissue in Pacific halibut (Hippoglossus stenolepis) from the waters of Eastern Kamchatka
abstract: Based on the parasitological and chemical analysis of Pacific halibut (Hippoglossus stenolepis) caught in Pacific waters off eastern Kamchatka in March–April 2022, infection with trematodes, nematodes, and acanthocephalans was recorded, with the highest prevalence for Hemiurus levinseni (83.3%) and Derogenes varicus (79.2%). Total parasite load ranged from 3 to 116 specimens per fish. No helminth larvae were found in the muscle tissue. abstract: The Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping for Seafarers (STCW) Convention establishes statutory requirements for seafarers’ practical proficiency in maritime English, which is directly related to navigation safety and international shipping operations. However, current maritime English instruction in higher vocational colleges focuses more on theoretical knowledge, such as vocabulary and grammar, while neglecting practical onboard applications, leading to a disconnect between students’ examination performance and actual job requirements. abstract: Context Tree hollows are essential habitat resources used by fauna in woody ecosystems globally. In addition to extensive historical and ongoing clearing, human use of woodlands has left remnants with structurally modified tree assemblages, including reductions in large hollow-bearing trees. Aims We aimed to assess tree hollow resources for dependent, arboreal vertebrates in fragmented, peri-urban woodlands. title: Ontogenetic shift to more efficient locomotor morphology coincides with migration in anadromous alewife, Alosa pseudoharengus (Wilson, 1811) (Clupeomorpha; Alosidae)
abstract: Anadromous fishes experience different locomotory demands throughout their life cycle. We evaluated how functional locomotory traits change over ontogeny in anadromous Alosa pseudoharengus (Alewife). We found that as juveniles, a period in which predator avoidance, food acquisition and manoeuvring in complex environments are critical to survival, Alewife have traits conducive to higher turning performance. title: First confirmed record of Centrophorus uyato (Rafinesque, 1810) in Irish waters: integration of morphological traits and DNA barcoding
abstract: Abstract We report the occurrence of a mature male Centrophorus uyato (Squaliformes: Centrophoridae) from the Porcupine Bank off western Ireland. A single specimen with a total length of 853 mm was caught by bottom trawl in 2023 at a depth of 660 m. The specimen was identified morphologically and confirmed by molecular taxonomy using DNA barcoding. The morphometric data obtained are consistent with previous descriptions of the species. title: Sustainable art practice and involvement of social community base project.
abstract: Indian knowledge system associated with the traditional methodology aesthetic philosophy and cultural heritage.And this study explores sustainable art practices within the Indian art field through a practicebased research methodology.The primary objective is to examine art projects, case study and the creative processes, as well as their ecological and social impacts on society.It is imperative to acknowledge the environmental crisis of the current century and to adapt our ecological framework to safeguard the future.This research focuses on the work of artists engaged in sustainable art pract

title: Discovery of the type material of Polynoe fasciculosa (Annelida, Polychaeta, Polynoidae)
abstract: Émile Blanchard described 3 polynoid species from Chile: Polynoe chilensis, P. fasciculosa, and P. virens. The type material of P. chilensis was found in the Muséum National d’Histoire Naturelle, Paris, but the 2 other species were regarded as indeterminable, and without type specimens. title: Results of two-year observations of snow evaporation and sublimation in the area of the “Ice Base Cape Baranova” Research Station (Severnaya Zemlya archipelago)
abstract: Instrumental data on sublimation from the snow cover surface in the high-latitude Arctic remain scarce. Existing estimates indicate a wide range of sublimation losses, varying from 10 to 90 % of the total cold-season precipitation depending on local climatic and landscape conditions. The paper presents the results of two-year (2024–2025) instrumental observations of sublimation from the snow cover in the high-latitude Arctic, specifically in the area of the research station “Ice Base Cape Baranova” (Severnaya Zemlya archipelago). title: Surfacing the Need for Groundwater Ecological Research in Polar Regions
abstract: Out of all raw natural resources, groundwater is among the most exploited by humans.We have entered an era of global water bankruptcy, with many regions consuming water resources beyond their capacity for natural renewal.As groundwater extraction escalates, we are not only depleting the vastest global unfrozen freshwater reservoir but also compromising the integrity of groundwater (and groundwater-dependent) ecosystems and aggravating climate change-related effects such as salinization and desertification.Aiming to widen our understanding on the role of groundwaters within the global water cyc

title: Morphological Bionics and Functional Integration Technologies for Bio-inspired Robots
abstract: Probing tasks in complex and unknown working environments are placing increasingly demanding requirements on robots in terms of terrain adaptability and locomotion agility. Against this background, conventional rigid robots have shown obvious shortcomings, while bio-inspired robots—developed on the basis of biological body shapes and motion mechanisms—have gradually become one of the most compelling research directions in robotics. title: A high-throughput method for quantifying degradation in maritime PEM fuel cells using a multichannel potentiostat
abstract: The durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells under maritime conditions is influenced by the vessel's operational profile, for example idling and intermittent shutdowns. To investigate this, we introduce a high-throughput accelerated stress test (AST) methodology using a multichannel potentiostat to simultaneously analyze up to eight membrane electrode assemblies. Voltage hold ASTs identified 0.825 V as a practical upper limit for idling voltage, above which Pt oxidation and dissolution significantly accelerate electrochemical surface area (ECSA) loss. title: “They can smell the ‘short-termness’ on you”. Student learning and sense of belonging in the Arctic
abstract: BACKGROUND: Student well-being is recognized as central to academic success, yet little is known about how extreme, isolated learning environments may shape this relationship. PURPOSE: To explore student's and staff's perception of student well-being and learning at the University Centre in Svalbard (UNIS), focusing on the Arctic context. METHODS: We used a qualitative, exploratory design, conducting semi structured interviews and focus groups with students and staff at UNIS. title: A tengeralattjárók fejlődésének története
abstract: A tengeralattjárók fejlődése a haditechnika egyik legizgalmasabb és legdinamikusabb területe, amely a kezdeti, egyszerű víz alatti járművektől a modern, nukleáris meghajtású, nagy hatótávolságú tengeralattjárókig terjed. A cikk – nagy vonalakban - áttekinti a technológiai innovációk és a stratégiai alkalmazások fejlődését, valamint a tengeralattjárók szerepét a hadviselés és a tengerészeti biztonság területén.

title: Pérez de Ribas’ Historia (1645) and the Protohistoric Period in Sonora and Southern Arizona
abstract: The protohistoric period along the Arizona-Sonora borderlands is an important yet poorly understood period. Historical sources, particularly Perez de Ribas’ Historia (1645), are discussed along with archaeological data that point to a late prehistoric expansion of the Opata into O'odham lands. Evidence of warfare and invasion is presented that may help explain the appearance of forts and defensive retreats, Sobaipuri origins, and Eudeve/Teguima linguistics.

title: CARACTERISATION HYDROGEOCHIMIQUE DES EAUX DES FORMATIONS KARSTIQUES AU SUD DE MBANZA-NGUNGU, REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO
abstract: This study characterizes waters associated with the karst formations of southern Mbanza-Ngungu, within the Kwilu watershed, Kongo Central Province (DR Congo). It aims to determine the lithological, structural and anthropogenic controls governing the mineralization of groundwater and surface water. The methodological approach integrates field observations, petrographic and mineralogical investigations, physicochemical measurements, major-ion hydrochemistry, saturation indices, Principal Component Analysis and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis.
