title: The nature of science in Finnish primary school textbooks
abstract: Recent international assessments indicate a decline in Finnish students’ interest and performance in science, emphasising the need for more relevant and motivating science education. Including the nature of science (NOS) into teaching offers an approach to address this issue as NOS instruction has been shown to enhance students’ interest in science, challenge stereotypical images of scientists, and promote a more realistic understanding of scientific practices and processes. This study examines the extent to which NOS is represented in primary school textbooks and workbooks used in environment

title: Strategy and Contradiction: Towards a Theory of Strategic Judgement
abstract: Strategy is commonly concerned with relating political purposes to the means available for their achievement. This article asks a prior question: what conditions make strategic judgement necessary in the first place? It argues that strategic problems arise from the contradictory character of political life, in which competing purposes cannot be permanently reconciled, and every decision alters the circumstances confronting those that follow. Strategy therefore requires practical judgement rather than the application of predetermined solutions. Drawing upon Clausewitz and examining deterrence,

title: Outpacing: A Grand Strategy for Avoiding the Carthaginian Error
abstract: This article warns Western democracies against committing the Carthaginian error, that is, not taking a strategic rival seriously. It argues strategic rivals should be dealt with through a grand strategy of Outpacing, the aim of which is to establish a lead over them severe enough to cause their political and economic collapse, or their forfeiture of the competition.

title: The Fortified Disposition, Part I: Strategic Complexes, Historical Attenuation, and the Return of the Guarded City
abstract: Fortification is better understood as a movement-slowing strategic complex than as a wall that either holds or fails. This paper traces the long attenuation of that disposition in the West, then shows how scarce manpower, costly platforms and persistent surveillance are bringing it back—first of all in the guarded, closable city assembled through dual-use fabric, regulation and urban air defence.

title: The Golden Dome, Missile Defenses and Deterrence
abstract: This article examines the Trump administration proposal for a Golden Dome missile defense system in terms of its implications for technology, strategy and U.S. national security policy. It also considers whether the proposed missile defense system, once having been deployed, will support deterrence as we now understand it, or require a rethinking of past assumptions about nuclear-strategic stability.

title: Research on Tourism Environmental Economy of Hainan Free Trade Port: Evolution Context, Hotspot Review and Frontier Prospect
abstract: As the highest form of opening-up in the global contemporary economy, the free trade port undertakes the strategic function of promoting institutional reform and high-quality regional development through opening-up. As the core experimental field of China’s open economic system with Chinese characteristics, Hainan Free Trade Port (Hainan FTP) deeply integrates tourism, ecological environment and economic development in its construction process, forming a unique research field of tourism environmental economy. title: Oligocene radiolarian fossil assemblage preserved within goethite concretions from the Nishinoomote Formation, Kumage Group distributed in Tanegashima Island, Kagoshima, SW Japan
abstract: 種子島中部の西海岸に分布する熊毛層群西之表層から産出した，コンクリーションの鉱物組成と内部に保存される放散虫化石群集を検討した．コンクリーションは，ゲーサイト及び石英で構成される緻密な外殻と，石英や斜長石といった母岩と同様の鉱物で構成される内部から構成される．本コンクリーション（ゲーサイトコンクリーション）の内部から放散虫化石が産出し，前期漸新世後期（放散虫化石帯RP20c帯下部〜RP21a帯中部）の年代を示した．本コンクリーションを含む層準付近の岩相も考慮すると，種子島北部に分布する西之表層とほぼ同時期の地層が種子島中部にも分布していることが判明した．本研究で検討したコンクリーションに類似した鉄酸化物の殻で覆われているコンクリーションは世界中で産出が報告されている．今後，より多くの微化石情報を得るための手段として，特に海成層に産出するこれらのコンクリーションの活用が期待される．
journal: The Journal of the Geological Society of Japan

title: Heteroptera (Insecta, Hemiptera) fauna of Eritrea
abstract: The suborder Heteroptera, commonly known as “true bugs,” represents the largest group within hemi-metabolous insects, comprising over 45,000 species. Eritrea, characterised by a Hot Semi-Arid to Hot Desert Climate, is notable for its four regional centres of vegetation endemism and approximately 430 woody plant species. This study aims to review and update the list of Heteroptera fauna recorded in Eritrea, based on existing historical literature. A total of 136 published works, spanning from 1870 to 2025, were reviewed. In total, 384 species across 236 genera and 40 families have been document

title: Iron Age Trade in Bronze Age Scarabs at el-Ahwat, Israel
abstract: A newly discovered scarab from the 2024 excavation season at el-Ahwat features a well-known depiction of an Egyptian king on a chariot – a hallmark of Ramesside royal iconography. Similar scarabs from the Southern Levant are known from Late Bronze Age funerary contexts, but the el-Ahwat scarab was found in a secure Iron Age IB context, at a site that was not settled during the previous Late Bronze period. title: Trigonometrical Juridism in British India: Unificatory Images and Jurisdictional Rationality
abstract: Abstract This article engages with two aspects of how cartography enabled law and jurisdictional ordering in a specific historical context. First, by interrogating the ways in which the great trigonometrical surveys of the British colonial enterprise and the Atlas of India entrenched “India” as a distinct, coherent, and contiguous geographical entity, this article will demonstrate how an epistemology rooted in a civilising impulse produced the perception of India as a thoroughly refined British legal territory. title: Opegaster plateen n. sp. (Digenea: Opecoelidae) from the giant mudskipper Periophthalmus schlosseri (Pallas, 1770) (Perciformes: Gobiidae) from Thailand
abstract: Abstract Mudskippers (Oxudercinae) are amphibious gobioid fishes inhabiting intertidal and mangrove ecosystems throughout the Indo–West Pacific region. Despite their ecological importance, information on their helminth fauna remains scarce. During a survey of parasites infecting the giant mudskipper, Periophthalmodon schlosseri (Pallas, 1770), in Chumphon Province, Thailand, specimens of an undescribed species of Opegaster Ozaki, 1925 (Opecoelidae) were recovered from the intestine. The species is described herein as Opegaster plateen n. sp. on the basis of morphological and molecular evidence

title: Archipelagic memories at Lau King Howe Hospital Memorial Museum
abstract: Colonial pasts, geopolitical differences, and plural social constructions of Malaya/post-independence Malaysia contributed to and were reflected in hospital design. Sarawak in East Malaysia, on Borneo Island, saw developments that paralleled those in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur. How did the multi-ethnic complexity of the patient demographic impact post-independence medical institutions? Situating this research in the region’s medical developments, this article explores hospital museums as repositories for institutional memories. journal: Interstices Journal of Architecture and Related Arts

title: Violating the Sacred Order: Sin, Punishment, and Ecological Consciousness in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
abstract: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner by Samuel Taylor Coleridge explores themes of sin, guilt, retribution, and salvation. According to the research, the Mariner’s killing of the Albatross violates the sacred bond among humans, nature, and the divine and is a moral transgression. The study examines how Coleridge portrays punishment as a psychological and spiritual process rather than a consequence, drawing on the poem’s symbolism, supernatural imagery, and religious themes. The Mariner's pain, loneliness, incapacity to pray, and recounting of his tale serve as phases of moral development and repent

title: Churns and Churning as a Solution for Preserving Excess Milk Yields and Surplus as Dairy Products: A Case Study from the Late Chalcolithic of the Southern Levant
abstract: Abstract The first clear evidence of advanced dairy production in the Southern Levant emerges during the Late Chalcolithic period. This shift is marked by the widespread discovery of clay churns across diverse geographic regions, alongside herd management practices and organic residue analyses that point to a dairy-oriented economy. A comprehensive study of Late Chalcolithic churns suggests that, alongside increased reliance on herds for milk production, churning became significant. We argue that this technological innovation arose from the need to process larger quantities of milk for growing

title: An integrated AHP-DEMATEL-QFD-FBS framework for designing an in-carriage intelligent delivery cart for China’s high-speed rail
abstract: To address the problem that manual delivery services cannot adequately meet the needs of complex service scenarios in crowded high-speed rail cars in China, this study proposes an integrated design framework for in-carriage intelligent delivery carts. User needs were collected through questionnaire surveys, semi-structured interviews, and behavioral observation, and a need indicator system for high-speed rail in-carriage delivery services was constructed. AHP was used to calculate the initial weights of need indicators, and DEMATEL was applied to revise the interrelationships among indicators.
institutions: North China Institute of Aerospace Engineering

title: Life cycle assessment of diesel, e-diesel, and hydrotreated vegetable oil for passenger cars
abstract: Biofuels and electrofuels (e-fuels) are among the proposed options allowing the continued sale of new internal combustion engine light-duty vehicles beyond 2035. However, their environmental performance is still predominantly assessed through climate change indicators, overlooking potential burden shifting towards other impact categories. title: The impact of behavioural activity on the EEG power spectrum, its source localisation, and global functional connectivity in rats Behavioural modulation of rat EEG dynamics
abstract: The behavioural activity of freely moving animals is a confounding factor that affects the recording, analysis, and final results of animal EEG experiments. Along with the lack of standardisation in animal in vivo electrophysiology experiments, this could lead to huge inconsistencies, especially in the analysis of centrally acting drugs. Therefore, the main aim of this paper is to investigate the effects of behavioural activity versus inactivity on the multichannel EEG in freely moving rats. title: Sacred waters, gendered labour and survival: Ngamee women in the floating village of Loktak Lake
abstract: Loktak Lake in Manipur is more than an ecological resource — it is a deeply storied landscape embedded with material, cultural, and spiritual significance. Central to its ecological uniqueness is the phumdi , a floating biomass that supports both human habitation and rich biodiversity. However, state-led interventions like the construction of the Ithai Barrage in 1983 and the implementation of the Loktak Lake (Protection) Act, 2006, have disrupted the ecological balance and delegitimised indigenous lifeways by labelling native fisherfolk as ‘occupiers’. abstract: Purpose. This article presents the results of an interdisciplinary study of the materials from Layer 2.1 of Tsagaan-Agui Cave in the Gobi Altai, obtained through stratigraphic, palaeontological, and techno-typological analyses. title: Boycotting racial capitalism
abstract: This article explores how racial capitalism in colonial Ireland was successfully challenged through the world’s first ever boycott. In the political economy of the late nineteenth-century, race and class were mutually constituted. The colonial landholding system of Ireland was a peripheral part of the British Empire. Catholic Irish tenants were cast as an inferior Celtic race in opposition to superior Anglo-Saxon Protestant English landlords. title: ‘ALLOWING THE MOST CAPABLE TO LEAD’: ELITE LEADERSHIP, COMPETENCY, AND CAPACITY IN THE FIFTH-CENTURY ATHENIAN STRATĒGIA
abstract: This paper interrogates the paradox of military leadership in the Athenian democracy within the analytical framework of mass and elite political negotiation. Although the stratēgia (the Athenian generalship) was filled by election rather than by democratic lottery, thereby privileging wealthy, notable citizens as candidates for office, the institution simultaneously incorporated robust democratic oversight and availed the dēmos of benefits that attended the personal networks of the Athenian elite. abstract: Purpose. The aim of the work is to present aspects of semantics associated with sacrifices, identified in the materials of mound 7 of the Sargat culture of the Tartas-2 burial ground (Baraba forest-steppe). The authors’ attention is focused on the design of the ditches, the particularities of the placement of the lintels and the methods of their “closure”, and the localization of sacrifice in the grave structure. title: An end-to-end conversational AI coach for heavy-duty eco-driving: An industrial case study
abstract: Heavy-duty trucks account for a disproportionate share of road-transport emissions, yet the eco-driving coaches deployed in commercial fleets typically deliver generic and opaque feedback. This paper reports an industrial case study, conducted with Volvo Group, of an end-to-end conversational AI coach for heavy-duty eco-driving. Per-segment LightGBM models predict fuel efficiency from vehicle-level telemetry aggregated over weekly to monthly windows for two operational segments, 5XT (50–59 t Gross Combined Weight) and 7XT (70–79 t). title: Historical Turning Point: the Battle of Zigetvar a Turning Point in Ottoman Military and Political History: The Siege of Szigetvar (1566)
abstract: The Siege of Szigetvar in 1566 was the closing move of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's 46-year reign and one of the peak points of the Ottoman Empire's military strategies towards Western Europe in the 16th century. Historians examine the military, logistical, socio-economic, and political dimensions of the campaign with an interdisciplinary approach. This study provides a multifaceted investigation of the Siege of Szigetvár, comparing the defensive strategy of the fortress commander Nikola Šubić Zrinski with the siege, fortification, and artillery techniques of the Ottoman army. title: Work Stress, Coping Strategies, and Job Satisfaction Among Food Service Workers in Bohol: A Descriptive-Correlational Study
abstract: Work stress is a significant occupational concern in the food service industry, with documented links to burnout, emotional labor, reduced service quality, and turnover intentions. This study examined the relationships among perceived work stress, coping strategies, and job satisfaction among food service workers in Bohol, Philippines, and explored which stressor domains – particularly social support – are more salient in this context. title: The Mosses of Mount Muruk Mio and Bukit Rimau in Sipitang District of Sabah, Malaysian Borneo
abstract: This study presents the results of bryological surveys conducted in 2003 and 2012 on Mount Muruk Mio and Bukit Rimau in Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo, with a focus on assessing species richness and composition of mosses. A total of 142 taxa in 70 genera and 31 families of mosses were collected, representing 18% of the mosses reported for Borneo and 21% for Sabah.The families with the highest number of taxa were Dicranaceae, Sematophyllaceae, Leucobryaceae, and Pylaisiadelphaceae. title: Bodies of knowledge: experience, commodification and labour in the imperial wildlife trade
abstract: The production of zoological knowledge in the late nineteenth century and the early twentieth was closely tied to the supply of animal bodies to institutions like zoological gardens and university departments, sustained by a growing wildlife trade. This trade, however, used, developed and altered independent forms of knowledge that relied heavily on skills and competencies formed through experience and familiarization. title: Un oracional del siglo xv en aljamía hebraicoaragonesa: textos y vocabulario
abstract: The following pages present the transcription of a small corpus of texts in Hebrew-Aragonese aljamía, datable to the last third of the fifteenth century. These texts appear to have originally formed part of a prayer book intended for women. An appended vocabulary is included as an accompanying resource.

title: Mitigating the human link in emerging reptile fungal pathogen transmission
abstract: Handling wild reptiles is common among amateur herpetology enthusiasts, professional researchers, social media influencers, and photographers. However, the potential for these interactions to spread diseases that threaten wild reptiles remains underappreciated. With the rise in such interactions due to today's socially connected landscape and the offering of an increased number of wildlife-focused ecotourism trips, the possibility of increased spread of human-vector-mediated reptile diseases is substantial. title: Proposal for defining the severity of environmental hypoxia
abstract: Every day, millions of people are exposed to environmental hypoxia, primarily due to living at or travelling to high altitudes for reasons such as work, tourism, business, or sports, e.g., mountaineering. Furthermore, hypoxic exposure at low altitudes (e.g., in hypoxia rooms or tents) is increasingly being used to pre-acclimatize individuals to high altitudes for activities such as athletic training, trekking and high-altitude climbing, as well as for preventive and therapeutic purposes. title: The ceramic complex of Solkhat as a source on the history of everyday life of the Golden Horde population of Crimea
abstract: Purpose of this study: To systematize and analyze specialized artifacts that can serve as a source for understanding the daily life of the Golden Horde population of Crimea. Research Materials: Specialized ceramic items are the primary source for studying the daily life of the Golden Horde population of Crimea. Golden Horde-era ceramic items discovered in Stary Krym can be used to date archaeological sites, complexes, and cultural layers, both at the settlement itself and at other contemporaneous sites in Crimea along with other regions of the Golden Horde if similar items have been discovered

title: Sociodemographic Analysis of the Art District in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico
abstract: This study presents a socioeconomic and demographic analysis of the Art District in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico, examining its role as a contributor to local economic and cultural development within the creative industries. Through the assessment of demographic variables and economic indicators, the principal enterprises and stakeholders of the district are identified, highlighting their role as a local economic engine. title: annotated checklist of the herpetofauna of Krka National Park, Croatia
abstract: Krka National Park in Šibenik-Knin, central Croatia, supports a unique assemblage of herpetofauna owing to its location in the transitional zone between the continental and Mediterranean biomes. We undertook eight seasons of targeted and incidental recording of amphibians and reptiles, as well as a review of available records of herpetofauna from the park and its surrounds. title: Mapping Russia with Korean Eyes: The Aguk Yeojido Revisited
abstract: Aguk Yeojido 俄國輿地圖 (“Map of Russia”) is a rare late-nineteenth-century Korean manuscript of considerable significance for understanding border interactions among Russia, Korea, and China, as well as the early history of Korean settlement in the Russian Far East. Produced at a time when the Joseon court sought alternatives to Chinese suzerainty, Japanese expansion, and Western pressure, the map reveals Korea’s strategic engagement with shifting imperial frontiers. title: Mineralogy of gold-telluride-sulfide ores of the Kokkiya deposit, Kazakhstan
abstract: Purpose. To establish the mineral-formforming sequence and clarify the features of gold-telluride-sulfide mineralization at the Kokkiya deposit based on the study of mineral assemblages, typomorphic characteristics of ore minerals, modes of occurrence of native gold and tellurides, and their spatial and paragenetic relationships. title: Women in Geosciences: an overview
abstract: This article examines the evolving role of women geoscientists, highlighting both progress and persistent inequalities that continue to shape this discipline. Although women now account for approximately 40% of researchers worldwide, their representation in Geosciences remains uneven, particularly in senior academic, leadership and decision-making positions. Data from the United States, Europe and at country level consistently reveal a pronounced “leaky pipeline,” whereby female representation declines progressively beyond the PhD stage, often falling below 20% among full professors. title: Multilevel risks and war related crisis severity shape tourist psychological distress and responses to crisis management
abstract: War-related crises exacerbate fear, insecurity, risk, and emotional tension. In light of these conditions, we propose and test a novel framework applying stress mindset theory to a war-crisis setting. Specifically, we investigate the effects of multilevel risks (personal, travel, and destination) on tourists’ psychological distress and subsequent emotional exhaustion. Furthermore, we examine the effects of emotional exhaustion on travel withdrawal intentions and travel choice satisfaction, while evaluating the moderating boundary effects of perceived crisis severity and crisis management. title: Auto‐Tuning Weights Model Predictive Control for Three‐State Switching Cell Boost Converters
abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents an improved robust model predictive control (MPC) for DC‐DC boost converters operating under polytopic uncertainty. The proposed controller guarantees constraint satisfaction for voltage, current, and duty cycle bounds while ensuring asymptotic stability through a common quadratic Lyapunov function. To circumvent the computational complexity of online optimization, the control law is synthesized offline via semidefinite programming (SDP) using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), yielding a static state‐feedback gain. title: DISTURBING THE HEARTH: ARISTARCHUS’ HELIOCENTRIC UNIVERSE AS COURT PARRHÊSIA
abstract: Abstract Aristarchus of Samos’ heliocentric model of the universe has usually been treated by modern scholars as an astronomical controversy somehow removed from the ideological concerns of the Ptolemaic court in which it was produced. This traditional approach has not fully accounted for the contemporary reception of the astronomer’s work, which included accusations of disruption, and even impiety, by scholarly rivals. title: One new obligate commensal species of Coenaletes (Collembola, Coenaletidae) from the hermit crab Coenobita compressus (Crustacea, Coenobitidae) from Colombia
abstract: A new species of Coenaletes associated with the hermit crab Coenobita compressus H. Milne-Edwards, 1836, living in shells of Tegula atra Lesson, 1830 (Gastropoda: Tegulidae) on the seashores of Chocó, Colombia, is described and illustrated. The ontogenetic development, including measurements and ventral setation from first instar to adult, is provided. A key for the identification of the three species known in the genus is included.

abstract: "This study analyses gastronomy as a vector of cultural identity and sustainable development in tourist cities through a comparison between Juazeiro do Norte, Brazil, and Santiago de Compostela, Spain. The objective was to examine how residents and tourists perceive local gastronomic spaces across dimensions elated to hospitality, authenticity, affective memory, accessibility, and sustainability. In the course of the study, the structural and technological features of the products were identified, their cultural and historical connections and chronological place were clarified. title: PIRATE FESTIVALS AROUND THE WORLD AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE FOR LOCAL DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The shift of contemporary tourism toward experiential, cultural, and thematic experiences creates new opportunities for destinations seeking differentiation, an extension of the tourism season, and stronger local entrepreneurship. In this context, pirate festivals constitute a distinctive form of event tourism because they combine historical or mythological narratives, harbour landscapes, re-enactments, parades, music, and participatory entertainment. title: Identification and Pathogenicity of Pythium Species Isolated from the Wheat Fields of Eskişehir Province
abstract: Wheat (Triticum spp.) is a staple food for approximately 35% of the world’s population and is cultivated in 102 countries, covering 32% of global arable land. Disease agents are among the factors that decrease wheat yield and quality. Embryo and root infections caused especially by soil-borne pathogens reduce yield by negatively affecting plant growth and tillering. Pythium species are polyphagous pathogens that cause root rot and damping-off diseases on various plants. title: Islands, Power and Conflict: A Classical Geopolitical Reading of the Azorean Civil War (1821–1831) | Ilhas, Poder e Conflito: Uma Leitura Geopolítica Clássica da Guerra Civil Açoriana (1821–1831)

title: Active layer microbial inocula restore missing functions across thawed permafrost soils
abstract: Abstract Microbial dynamics in thawing permafrost induce a climate feedback of uncertain magnitude. Upon thaw, active layer microorganisms may establish in formerly frozen layers and introduce missing functions. Here we test the prevalence of functional limitations and how active layer microorganisms can mitigate these across four widespread permafrost types over 389 days. By restoring functions with a multifunctional microbial community, we demonstrate widespread functional limitations, as increased CO 2 emissions across four permafrost types, and onset N 2 O emissions in two of those. title: Efficient Coverage Path Planning via Gradient-Based Rectangular Segmentation
abstract: Coverage Path Planning (CPP) is the task of finding a route that covers every point in a region or volume (i.e., all reachable cells) while avoiding obstacles. A typical CPP solution proceeds in two main stages: partitioning the environment into subregions, and planning a path within and between these regions. Effective segmentation is critical for smooth and efficient operation. For example, dividing the area into rectangular cells allows a simple back-and-forth (boustrophedon) sweep in each cell, exhaustively covering it without overlap. title: Books on the Road: Experiences of Reading in Robert Lee’s Travel Journal, 1824–1826
abstract: This article considers the reading life of the early-nineteenth-century British traveler and physician, Robert Lee (1793–1877). Drawing on evidence from Lee’s unknown manuscript travel journal penned during his travel to and residence in the Russian Empire in 1824–1826, where he worked as a family physician at Count M. S. Vorontsov’s household, it reconstructs his reading list and discusses the circumstances in which his reading acts took place. title: Uniendo disciplinas. Imagen digital y la narrativa en la intersección del 2D, el CGI, los videojuegos y el cine
abstract: Para comprender las capacidades fluctuantes de la imagen en movimiento, quienes trabajan e investigan en animación deben ser conscientes de las consecuencias que conlleva el continuo histórico desde la animación predigital hasta la animación digital actual. title: First Observation of Wild Double‐Flowered Rhododendron nivale With Stamen Petaloidy and Possible Parallel Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Parallel evolution of similar phenotypes under similar selective pressures is often viewed as evidence for natural selection. However, how often such parallel variation occurs in floral traits, and its underlying mechanisms, remain poorly understood—especially in alpine plants. Here we report the first discovery of wild double‐flowered plants in Rhododendron nivale , a dwarf shrub of the eastern Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau, and the first record of double flowers in subsection Lapponica (small‐leaved, high‐altitude sky‐island shrubs). title: Detrás del telón. El motivo visual de la cortina en el cine de David Lynch (segunda parte)
abstract: En esta segunda parte, el motivo visual de la cortina se expande más allá de su presencia escénica para convertirse en un mecanismo que altera la percepción del espacio y fractura la identidad en el cine de Lynch. Su función opera como un dispositivo liminar que articula refugio, ilusión y tránsito, donde lo inestable se convierte cada vez más en la norma.

title: Parachiloglanis gurungi, a new species of torrent catfish (Teleostei: Sisoridae) from western Bhutan
abstract: A new species of Parachiloglanis is described, based on specimens collected from the Kalikhola stream, a tributary of the Jaldhaka River, Samtse Dzongkhag, Bhutan. Parachiloglanis gurungi, new species, differs from its congeners in having a white bar on anterior flanks on dorsum of the body, white spot at the upper caudal-peduncle base, short and deep caudal peduncle, long predorsum, and differences in vomerine toothplate shape. Phylogenetic analysis of the cytochrome oxidase subunit B (cytb) gene sequences reveal lineage independence, corroborating its distinct status and establishing it as a

title: The Freedom Struggle of the Caucasian Highlanders in the XIX Century and the Influence of Mountain Relief on Military Tactics
abstract: In this work, we consider the resistance of the Caucasian highlanders during the 19th century in relation to the Caucasian War of 1817-1864 (although several Western authors date this period from 1763 to 1864). We compare the two main centers of geopolitical resistance: the organized resistance headed by Imam Shamil in the Northeast Caucasus (Chechnya and Dagestan), and the more scattered but no less consistent resistance of the Circassians (Adygs) in the Northwest Caucasus. In this work, the main emphasis is placed on the relationship between the geography of the Caucasus mountains – gorges,
journal: The Research Journal of Mountains Biodiversity Landscapes and Cultures

title: La tecnología digital en acción para la aventura de Cristóbal Colón
abstract: La personalización del aprendizaje mediante tecnologías digitales ha demostrado ser una estrategia efectiva para mejorar la enseñanza de la historia, específicamente en el estudio de Cristóbal Colón. Este artículo analiza cómo las herramientas digitales personalizadas impactan en la comprensión histórica, la motivación estudiantil y los desafíos de implementación. Se ha empleado una metodología cualitativa basada en el estudio de caso. Para la recopilación de datos, se llevó a cabo un análisis documental, revisando fuentes históricas, registros educativos y estudios previos relacionados con la
journal: Edutec Revista Electrónica de Tecnología Educativa

title: Additions to the flora of Pakistan: three new records in the genera Achillea, Amaranthus and Cicer
abstract: This study is based on field surveys conducted during 2022-2024, during which three vascular plant species were recorded first time for the Flora of Pakistan.The newly recorded species Achillea ptarmica (Asteraceae), Amaranthus polygonoiodes (Amaranthaceae), and Cicer chorassanicum (Fabaceae) are documented here.Achillea ptarmica was collected from Khaplu in Ghanche district of Gilgit-Baltistan and subsequently cultivated in Islamabad for detailed study and identification.Amaranthus polygonoides was collected from the Lower Dir district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Islamabad Capital Territory and C

title: Rediscovery, new records, and conservation assessment of the rare orchids Bletia concolor and B. similis (Orchidaceae) in Michoacán, Mexico
abstract: Background: Bletia comprises 56 species distributed throughout the Americas, with its principal center of diversity in Mexico. Among them are Bletia concolor and B. similis, two rare species for which information on morphology, distribution, and ecology is limited. Neither species had been recorded for the last 13 and 62 years, respectively, since their most recent collections. Questions: How do the new records of Bletia concolor and B. similis contribute to the knowledge of their distribution and to the assessment of their conservation status? Studied species: Bletia concolor and B. similis.
publisher: Sociedad Botánica de México, A. C.

title: Dynamic Impact Response of Composite Aircraft Radomes Subjected to Hailstone Impact: A Computational Study
abstract: Abstract The structural resilience of aircraft is significantly challenged by hailstorms, with the radome serving as a primary point of vulnerability to high-velocity impact. Driven by the requirement for impact-tolerant aerospace structures, this study investigated the dynamic response of fiber-reinforced composite radomes subjected to a single 50.8 mm (2 in.) diameter hailstone impact. Using an SPH–FEM coupled model developed in ANSYS Explicit Dynamics, a quantitative comparative evaluation was performed between glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) and Kevlar fiber-reinforced polymer (KFRP)
journal: International Journal of Aeronautical and Space Sciences

title: The Interdimensional Universe— Part 2: Out-of-Body Journeys, Coordinate Points, and Crucial Observations and Experiments for Scientific Exploration
abstract: This two-part essay addressed a two-part question: “If extraterrestrial life exists, then where are they?” and “Is interdimensional travel possible and, if so, how?” Drawing upon the insights of Jane Roberts’s philosophical psychology, the following thesis is advanced and defended: Alternate life planes and reality systems exist and make contact with the spacetime structure of our own physical universe at coordinate points through which non-human intelligent beings may travel that can be scientifically investigated utilizing both objective instrumentation and subjective tools. title: Battlefield Nuclear Thresholds and the 2025 India–Pakistan War
abstract: Is limited or battlefield nuclear employment re-emerging as a usable instrument of statecraft? This article takes the four-day India–Pakistan confrontation of May 2025 as its empirical anchor for that question. The study is a theory-guided interpretive single-case analysis that draws on official statements and briefings issued by both governments, post-crisis reconstructions by research institutions, and contemporaneous reporting, read against the established scholarly literature on deterrence thresholds. It argues that Pakistan’s investment in tactical nuclear weapons (TNWs) under the doctrin
journal: Journal of political science and international relationship.

title: Guadua londonoae (Poaceae, Bambusoideae), a new bamboo species from the Amazon Basin with remarkably large foliage leaf auricles
abstract: Summary A new species of Guadua (Poaceae, Bambusoideae) from the Amazon Basin is described and illustrated. Guadua londonoae is easily distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of primarily vegetative morphological characters. The most prominent diagnostic feature is the size of the auricles on the foliage leaves, which are on average four times longer than the maximum length previously recorded for any Guadua species. This species occurs in the southern and central Amazon rainforest, distributed mainly along the Madeira and Tapajós River Basins, where it grows alon
institutions: Instituto de Pesquisas Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro

title: Two new threatened Inversodicraea (Podostemaceae) species from waterfalls in Sierra Leone: I. joulei and I. lebbiei
abstract: Summary Two threatened new species of Podostemaceae belonging to the genus Inversodicraea , I. joulei and I. lebbiei , both from the Republic of Sierra Leone, are described and illustrated. A first record in Sierra Leone of the genus Lestestuella is also reported. Inversodicraea is the most species-rich genus of Podostemaceae in Africa and now comprises 38 species. Inversodicraea joulei is recognised because it has a persistent spine distally on the median rib of each fruit valve, and scattered, membranous scale-leaves with broadly rounded apices, while I. lebbiei is distinct in having narrowl
institutions: International Union for Conservation of Nature

title: Unshackled?: China, the ‘unequal treaties’, and the limits of international law, 1919–1929
abstract: Abstract The post-1919 international order extended to China formal sovereign equality while offering few legal means to exercise it. The Sino-Belgian treaty dispute of 1926–29 reveals this: when China abrogated its 1865 treaty with Belgium and Brussels sued at the Permanent Court of International Justice, the institutions that promised peaceful revision could not deliver it without the consent of the powers whose privileges were at stake. The ‘unequal treaties’, a political category coined only in 1923, named the contradiction the order had built in. Four lawyer-diplomats—Wellington Koo, Wang

title: From collective action to collective rescue: rethinking distribution and cooperation in climate governance under common peril
abstract: Distributive conflict is central to climate governance but is often treated as an external obstacle to cooperation. This conceptual paper argues that such conflict is partly generated by the dominance of a Collective Action Problem (CAP) cooperation grammar, which frames climate mitigation as managing a shared resource and makes agreement over individual contributions a precondition for action. Once institutionalized, CAP embeds distributive questions into the authorization of action itself, contributing to delay and deadlock. The paper introduces a Common Rescue (CR) cooperation grammar, illu

title: Seasonal decoupling of climate and human activity on litter and dung decomposition across the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau
abstract: Abstract In grassland ecosystems of the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau, litter and dung decomposition are essential for nutrient cycling and productivity. Using remote sensing data, field observations, and machine learning, we examined spatiotemporal patterns of litter decomposition mass (LDM) and dung decomposition mass (DDM) from 2000 to 2020. Both showed increasing trends: during the growing season (GS), LDM rose from 76.1 to 105.8 kg ha-1 and DDM from 16.9 to 26.6 kg ha-1. During the non-growing season (NGS), LDM increased from 29.0 to 46.6 kg ha-1 and DDM from 1.3 to 4.3 kg ha-1. A consistent sou
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

title: A review of structural design for in-wheel motors in new energy vehicles
abstract: The in-wheel motor (IWM) drive system represents one of the most promising architectures for new energy vehicles (NEVs), offering distinct advantages in drivetrain efficiency, vehicle packaging flexibility, and independent wheel torque control. This review systematically examines the structural design aspects of in-wheel motors, encompassing electromagnetic topologies, mechanical integration, thermal management, and fault-tolerant configurations. Particular emphasis is placed on permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) variants, including surface-mounted, interior, axial-flux, and transverse-

title: THE CYPRUS ISSUE IN THE EUROPEAN UNION’S REPORTS ON TURKEY: APPROACH, DISCOURSE, AND POLICY
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze how the Cyprus issue was addressed in the European Commission’s Regular Reports on Turkey published between 1998 and 2025, the thematic shifts it underwent, and its impact on Turkey-EU relations. The scope of the study includes the decisions of the 1999 Helsinki Summit, the 2004 Annan Plan referendum process, the commitments under the 2005 Additional Protocol, the suspension of eight negotiation chapters in 2006, and the disputes over maritime jurisdiction areas in the Eastern Mediterranean highlighted in recent reports. title: REDEFINING LIMINALITY IN THE READING OF ICELANDIC SAGAS
abstract: Redefining Liminality in the Reading of Icelandic Sagas. This article introduces a revised and expanded definition of the concept of liminality, with the purpose of utilising it as a methodological tool in the study of the corpus of medieval Icelandic sagas. The paper proposes an alternative interpretation of liminality, distinct from that established in foundational works such as those of Arnold van Gennep and Victor Turner. It argues that liminality does not merely constitute an intermediate phase within a ritual system, but may also represent a state of continuous reconfiguration and metamo

title: THE BALKANS AS A HETEROTOPIC SPACE IN HARRY DE WINDT’S THROUGH SAVAGE EUROPE
abstract: In this paper, the depictions of the Balkan Peninsula in Harry de Windt’s 1907 travelogue Through Savage Europe are explored in relation to Michel Foucault’s notion of heterotopia. This concept is brought into connection with Maria Todorova’s notion of Balkanism, as the two can function in complementary ways and elucidate our understanding of the Balkans as imagined by travel writers. We explore how the Balkans are constructed as a special place, a counter-site to Europe. Particular emphasis is placed on the Otherness of the Balkans, as well as their mixed, hybrid nature. journal: Facta Universitatis Series Linguistics and Literature

title: Veins of Influence: Photographic Albums, Curatorial Authority, and Colonial Self-fashioning in Charles Hose’s Sarawak
abstract: Charles Hose (1863–1929) is widely recognised for his contributions to ethnography, natural history and colonial administration in Sarawak during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. While scholarship has focused on his fieldwork and extensive collections, his photographs have largely been treated as individual ethnographic images embedded in texts or dispersed across museum archives, rather than as parts of structured visual artefacts. journal: The Journal of Imperial & Commonwealth History

title: Royal Idealism in the Achaemenid Persian Empire and Its Iconographic Reflections in Anatolia
abstract: The Persians, who established an empire in the mid-sixth century BCE, came to control a vast portion of the ancient world. Centered in Iran, this imperial formation was governed by the Achaemenid dynasty. Although the Achaemenids adhered to Zoroastrian religious traditions, they also incorporated earlier Mesopotamian ideological and political models—particularly those of the Assyrian Empire—into their imperial discourse and legitimizing strategies. In this context, Persian rulers did not hesitate to represent themselves and their political actions in ways reminiscent of Assyrian royal ideology

title: Receptor‐Targeted Niosomal Nanocarriers: Advances, Challenges, and Opportunities in Natural Compound Delivery for Cancer Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Receptor‐induced targeting of a niosomal delivery system may be a good tool for targeted and safe delivery of bioactive natural compounds to the tumor site with reduced systemic toxicity. Natural phytochemicals have strong therapeutic effects; however, their clinical applications are greatly hampered due to poor solubility, rapid metabolism, and low bioavailability. This review systematically reviews the state‐of‐the‐art surface‐engineered niosomes for phytochemical oncology, with a particular focus on ligand‐mediated delivery to overexpressed tumor receptors. title: BEYOND MADNESS: A RE-EVALUATION OF THE STRATEGIC RATIONALE BEHIND THE BYZANTINE–SASANIAN WAR OF 572
abstract: The reign of Emperor Justin II (565–578) is commonly overshadowed by that of Justinian I and is frequently portrayed in traditional historiography as an irrational and hubristic interlude, largely because of the war launched against the Sasanian Empire in 572. This article reconsiders that judgement by reassessing the strategic rationale behind Justin II’s decision and the factors that shaped the war’s trajectory. title: Mejoramiento de la calidad en taza del café a través de modificaciones al proceso de fermentación espontánea
abstract: El café es la segunda bebida más consumida en el mundo, después del agua, y está transitando de un producto comercial a uno de alta calidad. El presente estudio investiga el impacto de la maceración y adición de fuentes de carbono sobre los atributos sensoriales en taza del café, utilizando frutos provenientes de dos altitudes: 650 y 1,200 masl. Se aplicó un diseño en parcelas divididas, donde los tratamientos fueron el proceso de maceración carbónica y los subtratamientos la adición de fuentes de carbono. Los resultados demostraron que un proceso de 12 h de maceración carbónica de los frutos,

title: Reimagining Desire Beyond Gender: Body Politics and Ambiguous Identity in Jeanette Winterson’s Written on the Body
abstract: The paper attempts to examine ambiguity, and bodily existence in Jeanette Winterson’s Written on the Body. At the central core of the narrative exists an unnamed narrator, whose identity is deliberately rendered ambiguous. Due to the ambiguity the gender remains unrevealed. In the novel, Jeanette Winterson has adopted this innovative narrative strategy to challenge conformist expectations about gender identity, sexuality and desire. The present study is situated within the frameworks of queer theory and body politics. The frameworks aid to explore how the novel destabilises fixed binaries and
journal: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research

title: Learning across Borders: Pre-Service Teacher Development through Overseas Classroom Observation across Diverse Asian Contexts
abstract: This study examines the impact of short-term overseas classroom observation experiences on pre-service teachers' professional development in different Asian contexts, using a convergent mixed-methods design. The sample consisted of reflective narratives from 20 pre-service teachers studying at the Faculty of Education, Prince of Songkla University in Thailand. Descriptive statistics, correspondence analysis, and reflexive thematic analysis were applied to identify interconnections among reflection patterns and the underlying themes across destination contexts. journal: International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research

title: The limits of models in the debate on Great Moravian centres
abstract: The paper examines the limits of existing models used to interpret the functioning of Great Moravian centres through the case study of Bojná-Valy in Western Slovakia. While recent debate has been structured around Jiří Macháček’s triad of models (agrarian hinterland, autarky, and local market) critically revised by Michal Hlavica, this study argues that such frameworks are insufficient when applied to non-standard sites. publisher: Institute of Archaeology of the Czech Academy of Sciences

title: A digital specimen of the extinct Imperial Woodpecker: integrating museum scans, historical film and animated feather articulation
abstract: The Imperial Woodpecker ( Campephilus imperialis ), the world’s largest woodpecker species, is presumed extinct following the collapse of old-growth pine forest in its endemic range in the Sierra Madre Occidental, Mexico. Here, we present a detailed, animated 3D reconstruction of an adult female C. imperialis , built from photogrammetric scans of a physical museum study skin and parameterised against historical footage of the species in the wild. title: “ … based on the skewed theory building of the postcolonial movement”: Media conflicts surrounding postcolonial studies and antisemitism in Germany
abstract: The increasing recognition of postcolonial studies gave rise to a revisionist counter-movement on the conservative side in Germany, which went largely unnoticed until 2019. In the course of media conflicts over antisemitism in recent years, however, a majority opinion emerged in the liberal and left-wing camps that fundamentally suspected and criticized postcolonial studies as antisemitic. title: Representations of air tragedy in Chinese press: a corpus-driven critical discourse study
abstract: This article examines discourses surrounding air tragedies, aiming to investigate differences in ideological stances adopted by Chinese journalists toward three social actor groups associated with the crashed China Eastern Boeing 737. By integrating theories and methodologies from corpus linguistics and critical discourse studies, and employing corpus linguistics software, the study reveals that Chinese media constructs a positive representation of the “Our” group (the Chinese government and China Eastern Airlines) while framing the “Others” group (Boeing) negatively. title: Phase composition and microstructural heterogeneity of ancient ceramics from east Kazakhstan: raman spectroscopy, x-ray microtomography and scanning electron microscopy
abstract: This study presents the results of a comprehensive investigation of ceramic fragments from the Shagantogay archaeological site (Makanchi District, Abay region, Republic of Kazakhstan) using modern non-destructive analytical techniques: Raman spectroscopy, X-ray microtomography, and scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). Raman spectroscopy revealed a heterogeneous mineral composition of the ceramics, comprising quartz, anatase, feldspars, and carbonate phases. title: Prince of Crimea: Adil Giray
abstract: Research objectives: This study examines the brief biography of Adil Giray, a Crimean prince who has largely remained in the shadows of historical literature. The present research aims to analyze his life and activities within their historical context and highlight his role in the political, military, and diplomatic dynamics of the era. Research materials: Information on Adil Giray’s life and activities has been compiled through the analysis of documents from various sources. title: Adaptive variable-exponent sliding mode control for energy management of battery-supported hybrid electric vehicle
abstract: This study presents a robust converter-level control framework for a fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) equipped with a multi-source hybrid power system (HPS) comprising a fuel cell (FC), an ultracapacitor (UC), and a lithium-ion battery. The considered powertrain employs a boost converter for the FC and bidirectional converters for the energy storage units and is represented by a fourth-order nonlinear model. title: Altitudinal gradient patterns and community assembly mechanisms of birds in the eastern Kunlun Mountains, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China
abstract: Avian altitudinal distribution on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is shaped by contemporary environmental heterogeneity, history lineage diversification, and high-altitude adaptation. Understanding this pattern is crucial for explaining biodiversity maintenance in the “Third Pole”. However, in extreme arid boundaries with minimal human impact, how the interplay of historical evolutionary constraints and contemporary ecological filters shapes avian communities remains largely unquantified. title: The Volga Bulgars’ Ambush on the Mongols and the Death of Jebe Noyan
abstract: Research objectives: This study seeks to reassess the events that occurred during the return phase of the Dasht-i Kıpchak campaign, led by Jebe Noyan and Subutai Ba’atur, with a particular focus on determining the circumstances of Jebe Noyan’s death. By critically analyzing historical sources, the research aims to reconstruct the sequence of events and evaluate competing hypotheses regarding his fate. title: Teaching Thoughtful Statistical Inference: Stories for the World Beyond p < 0.05
abstract: ABSTRACT Statistical hypothesis tests and p values are poorly understood by many students of statistics. Poor application and misinterpretation of statistical inference procedures are common in published research. Over‐reliance on the “ p < 0.05” threshold to claim “statistical significance” often masks weaknesses in the evaluation of statistical evidence. This state of affairs presents a challenge for statistics education. This article proposes to teach statistical inference in the context of teaching statistical thinking. title: Beyond Turkish representation: The evolution of the function of Janissary music in Europe from military bands to concert halls
abstract: The adoption of Janissary music and instruments into European military bands represents one of the earliest examples of direct musical exchange between the Ottoman Empire and Europe. While previous scholarship has primarily examined the appearance of Turkish elements as markers of exoticism, less attention has been given to their long-term functional transformation within the Western musical tradition. This article investigates how, and through which historical, political, and musical processes Janissary music evolved from an Ottoman military practice into an integral component of the Western

title: Opioid use following spinal cord injury: a qualitative study of the perspectives of healthcare providers and people with lived experience
abstract: Purpose This qualitative study sought to understand opioid use following spinal cord injury (SCI) and identify capacity for improving patient safety from the perspective of people with lived experience and healthcare providers (HCPs).Materials and methods Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 23 participants (14 HCPs; 9 people with SCI) from January to September 2025, using interpretive description. title: Baseline indices of cardiorespiratory fitness for predicting acute mountain sickness: an interpretable four-task ensemble model
abstract: Background Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses formidable challenges for individuals venturing into high-altitude (HA) environments. Early and precise prediction of AMS is crucial for the timely identification of high-risk individuals and the development of effective treatment strategies. We sought to develop and validate an interpretable Acute Mountain Sickness Four-Task Ensemble (AMS-FTE) model for predicting AMS occurrence and severity according to the old and new LLS definitions. title: Inventing an interstice: les Français d’Asie, the canonisation and the location of Franco-Asian culture
abstract: This article focuses on the Belle Époque activities of an understudied literary and artistic grouping, Les Français d’Asie (1909–1914), led by Albert de Pouvourville, and uniting some of the key figures of the cultural and political sphere of that period, including Pierre Loti, Camille de Saint-Saëns, Claude Farrère and Albert Sarraut. Drawing on unpublished archives and period press, the author proposes to retrace the history and workings of Les Français d’Asie as a case study into broader questions surrounding the amalgamated cultural identities and discursive authority over them in the year

title: Master of Light Arkhip Kuindzhi’s Contributions to Luminism, Philosophical Aesthetics, Art Pedagogy, and Regional Cultural Identity
abstract: This study provides a systematic examination of the multifaceted legacy of Russian landscape painter Arkhip Ivanovich Kuindzhi (1842–1910), extending beyond his established contributions to luminist technique to investigate lesser-explored dimensions of his pedagogical practice, interdisciplinary links to music, and long-term cultural influence. title: Work recovery through virtual and real nature experiences: Employee perspectives
abstract: While nature is known to support employee wellbeing, virtual leisure activities can also be utilised for work recovery. The study examines the role of virtual and real nature in employee recovery by using the experience economy framework. In this randomised crossover trial, with a qualitative approach, 57 employees visited real and virtual nature. The virtual visits in different types of nature environments were described as providing escapism, while in real nature, it was more difficult to detach from duties. title: GREEK ATHEISM: A REALITY
abstract: This article is a response to Thomas Harrison’s lively thesis that atheism in ancient Greece is not a historical reality but ‘fundamentally, a scholarly mirage’. Repurposing and updating the arguments from the influential work of Lucien Febvre, The Problem of Unbelief in the Sixteenth Century , Harrison reasons that atheism could not have emerged in the age of Socrates and Plato: all we have from this period are empty accusations of atheism, a religious mentality which was incompatible with total unbelief, and a society in which religion dominated every sphere of personal and public life. title: Does capitalist risk-taking justify profits?
abstract: Abstract The profits collected by owners of companies are commonly taken to be a just and rightful compensation for the economic risks that they take. However, in the last two-and-a-half centuries, the risk-taking that follows with ownership has been drastically reduced as a consequence of legal and organizational changes, including incorporation, limited liability, and diversified investment. Investing money in companies is no longer per se a particularly risky activity. title: Britain’s reaction to the 1857–61 Mexican Civil War
abstract: By focusing on the British response to the 1857–61 Mexican Civil War, this article provides, for the first time, a study of the calls for military action that were made by the diplomats on the ground, Charles Loftus Otway and George Benvenuto Mathew. It highlights how their conflicting views of the liberal and conservative governments evolved as the war unfolded, and it assesses the Foreign Office’s response to their dispatches. journal: Journal of Iberian & Latin American Studies

title: Hacer visible lo implícito: la construcción discursiva del acusado en sentencias sobre chemsex mediante marcos, presuposición e IA generativa
abstract: This study analyses the discursive construction of the defendant in a corpus of twelve criminal court rulings on chemsex (39,856 words) issued by the Provincial Court of Madrid (2023–2025). Using Fillmore's frame semantics and Sbisà's taxonomy of presupposition triggers, two AI systems (Claude and ChatGPT) independently annotated eight frames across three functional levels: criminal act, institutional apparatus, and accused subject. journal: Círculo de lingüística aplicada a la comunicación

title: Feeding power
abstract: Even after 150 years of archaeological research on fortified centres, to which key central functions in early medieval Central Europe are generally attributed, we still do not have a clearer idea of how their populations were supplied with basic goods in practice. This text follows on the discussion opened by Jiří Macháček (2026) for Great Moravian agglomerations. It presents a systematic analysis of possible subsistence strategies, consistently linking them to the social profile of the inhabitants of the centres and to the property regimes that determined the forms of exchange. title: The materiality of postapartheid: post-racial signifiers in Gray Hofmeyr’s Yankee Zulu (1993) and Mad Buddies (2012)
abstract: In 1994, South Africa transitioned from apartheid rule to a post-apartheid democracy, with a constitution in place. Significant scholarship has since covered the many constitutionalised aspects of the period after the end of apartheid: governance, political, social, cultural, and economic, among others. Less discussed is how citizens’ everyday life in this period was not merely about inhabiting a new time, but rather encountered that time as a unique experience, herein termed the postapartheid. title: Four Case Studies in Comparison and Analogy: Political and Religious Culture, Conversion, Genealogy, and Time in Latin Europe and Medieval Japan
abstract: Our article follows two related objectives. We, first, reconsider the relationship between religion and politics by eschewing the uniform modern State–Church model and questioning its Eurocentric tenets. To do so, we focus on the Middle Ages and pair our decentring perspective with a comparison between Latin Europe in the 9th to 13th centuries and medieval Japan from the late Heian period to the Kamakura and early Muromachi eras (10th to 14th centuries). title: Humans are Made of Mud: the Genealogy of Farmland Legal Protection in Religious Traditions
abstract: Abstract: This article delves into the sacred origins of farmland legal protection, aiming to illuminate the profound rituals and beliefs that historically shaped human relationships with land and, more specifically, farmland. This analysis requires a deeper reflection on the interplay between land, religion, agriculture, and societal structures, ultimately contributing to the intricate process through which communities imbue land with meaning and, in so doing, give a value to it. To achieve its aims, the paper’s methodology combines legal research with historical and religious-cognitive appro

title: Inventing the ninja ancestor: Prince Shōtoku and the media circuits of martial tradition
abstract: This article traces the modern invention, transnational circulation, and persistence of the claim that Prince Shōtoku (574–622), the ancient Japanese regent, founded or patronized ninjutsu. While early chronicles portray Shōtoku as a statesman, Buddhist patron, and military leader, little to no premodern evidence connects him to such espionage traditions. abstract: This article is the outcome of the exploratory phase of a research project on collective filmmaking in South Africa that focuses on the lived experience of workers in the audiovisual industry. title: Physics-Guided Spectral Distillation for Underwater Image Enhancement on Resource-Constrained Devices
abstract: Underwater image enhancement is crucial for improving visual perception in marine applications. Existing underwater image enhancement studies mainly focus on enhancement quality and visual fidelity, while rarely considering real-time deployment capability, which is essential for resource-constrained underwater robots. title: Vision-based Underwater Formation Control With Input Saturations via Barrier Lyapunov Functions
abstract: In this work, we propose a communication-free framework for vision-based formation control of fully actuated underwater robots subject to sensing constraints, collision-avoidance requirements, and input saturations. Recentered barrier Lyapunov functions encode sensing and collision-avoidance constraints, while command-filtered backstepping extends the design to the second-order vehicle dynamics. abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) assisting human divers must continuously track not only the diver's 3D position but also their full-body orientation. However, vision-based perception is unreliable underwater, and forward-looking sonar -- despite being widely used -- discards the elevation information needed for orientation estimation, posing a fundamental limitation. abstract: Many spatial (3D) vehicles, including AUVs and fixed-wing aircraft, are effectively nonholonomic and subject to limited actuation, such that continuous time-invariant stabilization is fundamentally obstructed by Brockett's necessary condition. To overcome this obstruction, we exploit the geometric singularity of spherical coordinates to design a backstepping continuous, time-invariant feedback law that exponentially stabilizes a 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated solely by forward surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate. abstract: In this paper, the parameterized complexity of the multiplicative $α$-spanner problem with independent weights and lengths on undirected graphs is considered for the first time. abstract: Green Building Rating Systems (GBRSs) are widely used to promote and guide sustainable development across the built environment. However, a significant gap remains between certification achievement and actual operational performance, limiting the ability of existing GBRSs to support Performance-Based Contracts (PBCs), particularly in the rapidly growing and energy-intensive data centre sector. abstract: Abstract Despite continued warming in the Mediterranean Sea, tropical and sub-tropical hermatypic (i.e., reef-building) zooxanthellate scleractinian corals (henceforth referred to as hermatypic corals) have not returned since their disappearance after the Messinian Salinity Crisis almost 6 Mya ago. abstract: This study examines the local wisdom lexicon related to marine tourism in Manado City through an ecolinguistic approach to explore the traditional ecological knowledge system of coastal communities. Using a descriptive qualitative method involving observation, interviews, and literature study, this research focuses on the inventory of local marine lexicons. abstract: Stamukhas are dangerous ice formations typical of the shallow parts of freezing seas. In conditions of poor visibility, stamukhas pose a threat to shipping, and when they run afloat and drift, they also pose a threat to offshore infrastructure. Regular monitoring of stamukhas and obtaining comprehensive information about their location and size is essential for the safety of maritime operations in the Russian Arctic. abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is a significant threat due to its widespread presence, hidden diffusion through ingestion by organisms, and entry into edible species. abstract: During the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), atmospheric p CO 2 was approximately 90 ppm lower than in the pre-industrial era. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain this difference, including changes in nutrient supply, increased iron input to the ocean, reduced air-sea gas exchange due to changes in sea-ice coverage, and variations in overturning circulation strength driven by differences in wind stress and atmospheric moisture diffusivity. abstract: Members of the insect order Megaloptera (alderflies, fishflies, dobsonflies) are ecologically important freshwater insects and valuable biological indicators in freshwater biomonitoring programs, yet their spatial patterns and vulnerability to climate change in Southeast Asia remain poorly understood. abstract: Ocean transparency refers to the ability of water to transmit light, which directly influences the depth to which sunlight penetrates the water column. This parameter is crucial for marine ecosystems, as it determines the availability of light for photosynthesis, a process vital for phytoplankton, the primary producers of the ocean. abstract: ABSTRACT Thermodynamic constraints and empirical evidence often suggest that fabric‐retentive replacement dolomites are stable carbonate minerals that preserve ancient seawater properties. abstract: Displaced persons, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, are vulnerable to several diseases, including hepatitis B. abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a nutrient-like trace metal whose burial in marine sediments influences both the long-term (10 3 –10 4 yr) oceanic Cd mass balance and the interpretation of Cd-based paleoceanographic records. abstract: Anthropogenic sound has become an increasingly important environmental stressor in marine, estuarine, and freshwater ecosystems. Fishes rely on acoustic information for communication, orientation, habitat selection, predator and prey detection, social interactions, and reproduction. abstract: This article examines Seenu Ramasamy’s Tamil film Neerparavai through an ecocritical framework. Much of the value associated with marine restoration is non-use, non-market benefit values, which require the use of stated preference surveys to uncover. abstract: Abstract Tidal inundation of saltmarshes can mitigate anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions by rapidly accumulating carbon-rich sediment, with the potential to sequester this “blue carbon” for thousands of years. The desire to remove atmospheric carbon, alongside increased flood risk from sea-level rise, is driving scientific and financial interest in restoring low-lying land into saltmarshes. abstract: Urban coastal areas face environmental pressures due to rising sea levels, coastal erosion, and tidal flooding. abstract: Abstract The Late Ordovician Mass Extinction (LOME) comprised two pulses of biodiversity loss under contrasting climatic conditions, yet how these transitions reshaped marine redox conditions remains enigmatic. title: Caste, Memory, and the Afterlives of Bondage: How a Spectral Slave Became a Demigod in Coastal Kerala
abstract: The former colonial port town of Kochi in India is home to memorial sites dedicated to enslaved Africans (Kapiri in Malayalam), called Kapirithara. Unlike memorials to slavery that centre victimhood, these sites venerate the Kapiri as a mighty, cigar-smoking demigod. According to popular lore, when the Portuguese lost the city to the Dutch in 1663, they killed their enslaved and buried their treasure with them, believing they would guard these treasures until the owners returned. This study presents a tide-aware Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for quantifying siltation evolution in the northern sector of Taichung Port, Taiwan, using 276 Sentinel-1 ascending-track VV images acquired from 2015 to 2024. abstract: International marine environmental law increasingly depends on scientific information, but the legal consequences of new monitoring technologies remain underexplored. This article asks when environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring may affect what states knew or ought reasonably to have known about marine biodiversity risks and consequently the application of due-diligence obligations. title: Alleviating over-tourism and advancing sustainable tourism on coral island through virtual reality (VR)
abstract: The main objective of this study is to examine how virtual reality (VR) might help reduce overtourism in places with coral islands. A purposive sampling approach was used to reach people who had previously engaged in or were interested in VR tourism because there was no easily accessible database of VR users. abstract: Seaweeds sustain dense and metabolically distinctive microbial communities whose members produce morphogens, phytohormone analogues, siderophores, vitamins, polysaccharide-degrading enzymes and antimicrobial metabolites. These properties have prompted the proposition that the seaweed-associated microbiome constitutes an underexploited reservoir of biostimulant and biocontrol agents for terrestrial crop production. title: Lascars at war: Maritime labour and the logistics of empire in Amitav Ghosh’s Ibis trilogy
abstract: This article foregrounds lascars, an indispensable yet overlooked category of imperial labour, in its analysis of Amitav Ghosh’s Ibis trilogy: Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, and Flood of Fire. Rather than being identifiable as subaltern heroes or figures of cultural hybridity, lascars are understood as agents who navigate the material conditions of empire and negotiate their status as shipboard, commercial, or martial units of labour discipline. abstract: Marine macroalgae are increasingly valued as a sustainable resource for food, feed, and high-value bioproducts, yet the regulatory frameworks governing their wild harvest and cultivation remain fragmented across the North Atlantic. This study reviews the management and harvesting of marine macroalgae species in Atlantic Canada, Iceland, the Republic of Ireland, France, the United Kingdom, and Norway (45° N–66° 34′ N), drawing on 148 sources, including 34 statutory documents, from a systematic search of peer-reviewed and grey literature. abstract: Abstract: Background: Beachy Head is a high-frequency public coastal location associated with suicidal crisis, suicide attempts, and deaths by suicide in England. Although evidence from frequently used jumping locations supports access restriction and multicomponent prevention, the evidence specific to this site has not been systematically mapped. Aims: To identify and summarize academic, policy, and gray literature addressing suicidal crisis, suicidal behavior, deaths by suicide, and suicide prevention at Beachy Head. title: Documenting the coastal erosion-driven collapse of a Cold War underground monitoring station via laser scanning
abstract: Rapid soft-cliff coastal erosion along the Holderness Coast, United Kingdom, continues to result in the loss of infrastructure, including buildings of local historical interest. The terrestrial laser scans presented in this data note were collected to document the post-failure condition of the Tunstall Royal Observer Corps monitoring post; a Cold War structure progressively exposed by ongoing soft-cliff coastal erosion. The structure was discovered to have collapsed onto the beach by local residents on the morning of 23 January 2026 and was subsequently surveyed by the authors on the same day.

abstract: Abstract The Southern Ocean around Antarctica remains the only large area on the planet populated by almost entirely native and mainly endemic species. Despite being one of the most constant environments for millions of years and still the least human populated, the polar regions are now hotspots of physical climate change, and this is likely to make the shallow waters less inhospitable to invading non-indigenous species (NIS). abstract: The fossil record is inherently incomplete, yet its physical limits remain largely uncharted. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal coverage of the global shallow-marine metazoan fossil record across the Phanerozoic, using a large dataset of georeferenced collections intersected with global geological data. This study aims to examine the community structure of Echinodermata in the waters of Bunaken Island. abstract: Abstract Symbiotic interactions are central to coral ecology, spanning the coral holobiont’s internal microbial partnerships to broader associations with reef fishes and other motile species. Coral-dwelling damselfish live in close association with coral colonies, using their branches as shelter. These associations can influence the coral’s immediate environment through various mechanisms including nutrient inputs, oxygen dynamics, and sediment removal, while fish may also serve as vectors for microorganisms. title: Sonic selves, ancestral archives: Identity, language and cultural memory in amaXhosa sacred practice
abstract: Among the amaXhosa of South Africa’s Eastern Cape, knowledge lives less in texts than in bodies, voices and sacred landscapes. In Hamburg, at the mouth of the Keiskamma River, knowledge of the ocean, river, forest and healing plants is transmitted in isiXhosa through song, carried by elders whose authority rests on accountability to the ancestors rather than institutional credentials. abstract: Abstract Based on the data acquired during the 2024 hydrochemical survey, taking into account previously published and archival material, the evolution of the chemical composition of Lake Karymsky was studied. abstract: Sea turtles are susceptible to opportunistic infections, particularly when debilitated, injured, or exposed to environmental stressors. abstract: The Late Palaeozoic Ice Age (LPIA) represents one of the most significant climatic transitions in Earth's history, characterised by dramatic fluctuations in atmospheric CO 2 , O 2 , and global temperatures. This study investigates the influence of these global climatic shifts and latitudinal gradients on the diversity, complexity, and size of trace fossils during the Carboniferous and Permian periods in continental deposits. title: Rare Earth Elements in Chile: A Critical Review of Primary, Secondary and Marine Resources, Metallurgical Recoverability and Future Supply Chain Opportunities
abstract: The economic value of rare earth elements (REE) is concentrated in Nd, Pr, Dy and Tb. The supply chain for these elements is dominated by a single country, China, which accounts for about 60% of mined production, over 90% of refinement, and nearly 95% of permanent magnet manufacturing. abstract: Shallow nearshore habitats can serve as nursery areas for coastal elasmobranchs but are increasingly exposed to coastal development. abstract: The western Neo-Tethys Austroalpine and Southern Alps sedimentary successions are proven archives of environmental and climatic changes and tectonic activity across the Triassic to Jurassic times. title: The climate-conflict nexus and environmental governance in southern Thailand
abstract: The connection between climate change and peacebuilding is increasingly recognised globally, yet little is known about how these dynamics unfold within contexts of ongoing violent secessionist conflict. This study explores the conflict-peace-climate nexus in the protracted ethno-nationalist conflict in Thailand’s southernmost provinces, drawing on analyses and recommendations from local civil society organisations. abstract: This article examines how the March 2025 conviction of Marine Le Pen for the misuse of European Parliament funds was framed in the French press and how the event became a discursive site for negotiating democratic legitimacy and political enmity. The ruling generated extensive media coverage that combined legal reporting with political interpretation. title: Valuation of Flood Risk in Coastal Housing Markets: Evidence from Tampa Bay
abstract: Florida exhibits growing tension between urban population growth and increasing exposure to coastal flooding risk. More than half of the state’s municipalities are threatened by chronic flooding, and in recent years the insurance market has been characterized by rising premiums and insurer withdrawals. abstract: Abstract Dam regulation of tropical monsoonal rivers enhances seasonal contrasts in the tidal river zone (TRZ) hydrology, altering the delivery of dissolved silicon (DSi) to the coastal ocean. title: Assessment of Beach Plastic Waste Pollution Using the Clean Coast Index: Evidence from Thanh Hoa Province, Viet Nam
abstract: Marine plastic pollution is an increasingly important environmental and socio-economic challenge for coastal provinces of Viet Nam, where tourism, fisheries, river discharge and coastal urbanization interact to shape the accumulation of beach litter. abstract: Tissue samples from European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) naturally infected with Aeromonas veronii biovar veronii were subjected to bacteriological, molecular, pathological, and immunohistochemical analyses. abstract: Abstract Root-associated fungi (RAF) are important for plant performance because they form beneficial, neutral, or pathogenic relationships with their hosts, thus regulating nutrient uptake, stress tolerance, and overall plant fitness. abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health concern, particularly with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), which are associated with limited treatment options and poor clinical outcomes. abstract: Contemporary magical realism can challenge the epistemic boundaries through which modernity defines reality.
