title: Green Computing Infrastructure and the Environmental Governance of Nearby Firms: Evidence from China’s National Green Data Centre Pilot
abstract: Data centres are among the fastest-growing sources of electricity demand, and the policies that govern them are evaluated almost entirely by what happens inside the facility. This study asks whether such a policy also reaches the firms around it. Using 30,547 firm-year observations for 3918 Chinese A-share listed companies in 249 cities between 2010 and 2024, we treat successive designations under China’s National Green Data Center Pilot as a staggered, city-level shock and estimate its effect on how firms govern environmental responsibility. abstract: The threat of climate change to coastal areas' existence encourages efforts to protect the balance of mangrove ecosystems, especially in small island areas. This study was conducted in the Protected Mangrove Forest of Molinese Village, Lainea Subdistrict, South Konawe, Southeast Sulawesi, to describe species composition and mangrove diversity levels. Accurate species-level identification remains challenging because commercial matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) databases have limited species-specific spectral representation of A. schubertii. abstract: The cryosphere plays a crucial role in global climate change. To accurately quantify impacts of typical cryospheric surface types, such as snow, ice, and melt ponds on the radiative processes both in the atmosphere and at the surface, new developments in the radiative transfer modeling are necessary. This paper summarizes recent developments in the coupled atmosphere-snow(water)-ice-water radiative transfer model SCIATRAN, which are essential for cryospheric science applications. title: Evolving motivations for participation in community-based conservation: A relational perspective
abstract: Successful outcomes of community-based conservation, both ecological and social, rely on local actors being motivated to engage at the outset of the programme and to sustain their motivation over time. Using semi-structured interviews, we explore the motivations of 22 community Conservation Officers who have participated in marine turtle conservation in Tanzania for more than two decades. title: El poema incendiado como archivo visual y performance en los años sesenta
abstract: This article analyzes a visual-poetic action carried out by Carmelo Arden Quin and Julien Blaine in the 1960s, based on a photographic image documenting the burning of a poem. Through its circulation in experimental magazines, the image becomes an active archive that reconfigures the memory of a transnational network of marginal aesthetic practices. abstract: Abstract The little tunny ( Euthynnus alletteratus, Scombridae) have great economic importance with a large volume of catches. Recently, both the south-eastern and northern stocks were found to be at high and moderate risk of overfishing, respectively. Here we investigated the stock structure of E. alletteratus and the phylogenetic relationships through a combination of genetic, genomic and growth analysis. title: Allocation and stock status of Kamchatka flounder Atheresthes evermanni off the southern Kuril Island
abstract: According to the industry monitoring system of the Federal Agency for Fishery, an analysis of the Kamchatka flounder Atheresthes evermanni Jordan et Starks, 1904 fishery in the South Kuril zone was conducted. Based on the results of bottom trawl survey in September-October 2025 off the Southern Kuril Islands, as well as archival and literary data, the spatial distribution of the Kamchatka flounder is presented. Information is provided on the size composition of individuals at various depths. An assessment of the biomass is made.

title: Market Access and Adoption of Climate Smart Agriculture: A Systematic Review
abstract: Market access is an important determinant influencing farmers’ adoption decisions by affecting prospective profitability, access to modern inputs, availability of information and extension services, and exposure to production and price risks. This systematic review is a synthesis of the evidence on the relationship between market access and CSA adoption in various agroecological settings. abstract: Floating solar photovoltaic (FSPV) systems have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional land-based photovoltaic (LSPV) systems by reducing land-use constraints and improving electrical performance through the natural cooling effect of water bodies. However, long-term deployment in humid and saline coastal environments may accelerate moisture ingress, salt deposition, and corrosion, reducing system reliability and energy generation. This study demonstrates how hyperspectral observations with exceptionally low radiometric uncertainty, exemplified by the proposed Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial and Helio Studies (TRUTHS)-like configuration, can strengthen these constraints relative to PACE Ocean Color Instrument (OCI)-like configuration. title: The role of host resource dynamics in shaping life-history evolution of pine processionary moths
abstract: Synchronization between larval development and peak resource quality drives life-history evolution in forest defoliators from cold-temperate regions but is less considered in other ecosystems, such as those in the Mediterranean region. Studies on Thaumetopoea pityocampa , the main Mediterranean pine defoliator, which typically develops during winter (winter population [WP]), have mostly focused on climate. title: Evaluation of 18 S rRNA as an endogenous control in OpenArray® plasma RNA qPCR workflows
abstract: Abstract Background Reliable qPCR analysis depends on stable endogenous controls, particularly in high-throughput pre-amplification workflows where technical bias may arise. The suitability of highly abundant 18 S rRNA as a reference gene in multiplex OpenArray ® platforms remains debated. This study evaluated the stability of 18 S rRNA, its impact on co-amplified targets, and comparability between archived and newly manufactured primer pools. abstract: Introduction. The village of Kolvitsa, located on the Kandalaksha coast of the White Sea, is the only Karelian settlement on the Kola Peninsula and, at the same time, the northernmost Karelian locality still in existence. Founded in the late 19th century, it remained for many decades largely outside the scope of scholarly inquiry by ethnographers, historians, and linguists. abstract: Few glacial chronological studies have been conducted in the extremely cold and arid interior of the Tibetan Plateau, limiting a plateau-wide understanding of Quaternary glacial spatiotemporal patterns. abstract: Natural compounds of animal and plant origin play a key role in maintaining human health and preventing diseases. title: Floods as the Dominant Disaster Type in Explaining Disaster Impacts: A Dominance Analysis of Affected Population in Indonesia
abstract: Understanding the types of disasters that contribute most to social impacts is crucial for formulating effective disaster management policies. However, most previous studies assess disaster impacts using a limited regression approach to explain the relative importance of various correlated disaster types. This study aims to identify the dominance hierarchy of various disaster types in explaining variations in the number of affected populations in Indonesia. abstract: This study introduces the new global Mesoscale Eddy Trajectory Atlases, META4.0 available in an AVISO repository at https://doi.org/10.24400/527896/a01-2026.001 (CLS and CNES, 2026). abstract: In this study, a safety classification model based on analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method (FCE) was established to prevent and control the risk of repetitive diving for leisure divers. Sixteen key risk factors were selected by literature analysis and Delphi method, covering four criteria levels: physiological state, diving operation, interval accumulation and environmental equipment, among which the maximum diving depth, underwater residence time and water surface interval time were the core indicators. abstract: In 1822, the American Colonization Society established a settlement on Providence Island, at the mouth of the Mesurado River in present-day Liberia. This settlement, which later became part of Monrovia, marked the beginning of Liberia as a colony for free Black Americans, some of whom were formerly enslaved. abstract: This article reconceptualizes the Aegean maritime disputes as a structural contest over regional hierarchy rather than a purely technical problem of maritime delimitation. Drawing on Power Transition Theory and Multiple Hierarchy Model, it examines how the changing material balance of power between Türkiye and Greece reshapes legal interpretations of maritime jurisdiction within the Aegean regional subsystem. abstract: The sympathetic-adrenomedullary system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis are both activated by acute stress. Although adaptive initially, excessive acute stress causes glucocorticoid overload, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. abstract: Abstract Fossil fuels continue to dominate the global energy supply. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates changing housing provision in rural Nottinghamshire during the 19 th and early 20th centuries using archival material and historical census data. The Manvers estate archives contain valuable information to reconstruct the role of landed estates, land agents and tenant farmers in shaping housing provision and conditions. abstract: Summary The Global Carbon Budget, maintained by the Global Carbon Project, summarizes Earth’s global carbon cycle through four annual time series beginning in 1959: atmospheric CO2 concentrations, anthropogenic CO2 emissions, and CO2 uptake by land and by ocean. We analyze these four time series as a multivariate (cointegrated) system. abstract: High-resolution photogrammetry has become a pivotal tool in palaeontology for scientific documentation, morphometric analysis, and virtual heritage preservation. This study details the photogrammetric workflow implemented to digitise Pleistocene fossil molluscs sampled near Gravina in Puglia (Southern Italy). title: In-situ tracer percolation experiments to quantify the influence of near-surface melting on Svalbard snow signatures
abstract: The Arctic is at the forefront of global warming. More frequent and intense rain-on-snow events during winter are altering the annual snowpack with its environmental proxy records, so that Svalbard glaciers are not only rapidly losing mass but are endangered as climate archives. In this study, we aim to visualise and better quantify the influence of near-surface melt caused by small-scale rain-on-snow events on stable water isotope signatures in seasonal snow in the vicinity of Ny-Ålesund in Svalbard. abstract: This article examines the socio-historical profile of a West Siberian village during the second half of the nineteenth century. The scholarly significance of this study lies in its contribution to social history through an analysis of regional particularities within the Russian Empire's administrative periphery. abstract: Saltwater and industrial contamination is gradually rendering groundwater in coastal India undrinkable, and the impact is most severely felt by the populations who lack access to centralised water treatment facilities. This paper details the design, construction, and initial performance assessment of the Umbrella Desalinator, a portable passive solar still intended to serve precisely these households. abstract: John L. Volk (1901–1984), an architect in Palm Beach, adapted the Bermuda Style in residential designs, between the Great Depression and the beginning of the Second World War. These homes combined the simplicity, austere aesthetic, and functional features of Bermudian homes that were suited to the subtropical climate of Florida. title: The Emergence of Iron Shipbuilding on the River Tyne: A Study of Entrepreneurial Agency
abstract: Abstract From the 1840s, Tyneside emerged as a key center for iron shipbuilding, rivaling Britain’s established hubs. This industrial shift was driven initially not by legacy firms but by migrant entrepreneurs from Aberdeen—John Coutts, Charles Mitchell, and Andrew Leslie. This article investigates the divergent trajectories of these entrepreneurs, asking why two succeeded in establishing sustainable enterprises while the other failed. abstract: Elazığ is a settlement in Anatolia that has retained its importance throughout history due to its natural resources, climate and geographical location, and is also rich in water resources. The district of Maden, situated within this settlement, stands out for its deep-rooted history and cultural riches. This study quantifies and compares cargo-vessel congestion at three major US gateways, Los Angeles/Long Beach, Houston/Galveston, and New York/New Jersey, using open Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the United States Nationwide AIS archive. abstract: In the following paper, the media coverage by the newspapers Clarín, La Nación, Página/12, and various argentine cultural magazines surrounding the figure of bahiense writer Héctor Libertella (1945-2006) is explored in order to analyze the extent to which they contributed to the construction of his authorial image, the dissemination of his achievements and career, and his current positioning and placement within the literary field. title: Más allá del snacking: microinteracciones informativas de comunicadores en formación
abstract: This study examines the factors associated with the frequency of news consumption and small acts of engagement (liking, sharing, commenting, reading in full, and archiving). Drawing on a survey (N=730) of communication students at Jesuit universities in Mexico, the findings show that proactive political practices in the digital sphere catalyze all five micro-interactions, followed by the consumption of both hard and soft news topics, particularly those related to crime and court news. title: Material and environmental performance of breakwaters with varying slopes and concrete armor types
abstract: Global climate change and resource scarcity have intensified the need for sustainable and resilient coastal protection. Breakwaters, which dissipate wave energy and mitigate shoreline erosion, traditionally rely on large natural stones or mass concrete armor units. However, the increasing unavailability of suitably sized natural stones and significant carbon emissions associated with concrete production present critical challenges for sustainable design. title: First finding of Icelandic tephra in Czechia: Vedde Ash identified in palaeolake sediments of Stará Jímka
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report the first documented occurrence of the Icelandic Vedde Ash (VA) in the Bohemian Forest, identified within palaeolake sediments from Stará Jímka, Czechia, representing the first Icelandic tephra layer identified in Czechia. As part of ongoing efforts to close existing tephrochronological gaps in Eastern Central Europe, two parallel lacustrine sediment cores were investigated for the presence of cryptotephra layers. title: Distribution of songbird migrants in autumn in the arid belt of Central Eurasia: West vs. East
abstract: The arid belt of Central Eurasia is a formidable obstacle for annual migratory movements of songbirds. Most birds that breed in the forests of Eurasia and spend their winter in the subtropics and tropics of the Old World have to manage this ecological barrier. Some of them cross it directly, whereas others make detours. abstract: Environmental degradation requires broader forms of social accountability that extend beyond formal regulations. abstract: Abstract This paper examines Fahmīdah Riyāẓ’s collection of Urdu poems titled Tum Kabīr as a (meta-)archive that maps the affective, semiotic, and mnemonic landscapes of her dialogic poetic imagination. Through a sustained exploration of the implications of dialogism, it analyzes the interplay among different voices, texts, languages, and competing parts of the self that animate Riyāẓ’s poetic practice, using subjectivity and linguistic innovation as analytical lenses. title: On the distribution of Jordanita (Roccia) hector (Jordan, 1907) (Lepidoptera: Zygaenidae, Procridinae, Procridini)
abstract: The species Jordanita (Roccia) hector (Jordan, 1907) is known only from the Levant (a subregion of West Asia situated along the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea), an area characterized by high level of endemism. Recently, this species has been reported from Azerbaijan (Buntebarth et al. 2024). Examination of the material cited in aforementioned publication revealed that the record was based on a misidentification of Jordanita (Roccia) paupera (Christoph, 1887). The morphology and biology of J. hector are discussed.

abstract: Background: As part of an ongoing revision of Senecio, it is apparent that Senecio viminalis Bremek. is a distinct species. It was therefore surprising that together with Kleinia longiflora DC., Kleinia scottioides C.Jeffrey and Senecio garcianus Schltr. it has been listed as a synonym of Curio avasimontanus (Dinter) P.V.Heath in some of the world’s main taxonomic databases. Aim & objectives: To clarify the status of the names and synonyms in this species group and to provide a verifiable reference for nomenclature in taxonomic databases. title: ‘To Write Władysław Szpilman’s Odyssey’: The Music of the Warsaw Ghetto in The Death of a City and The Pianist
abstract: Abstract Unbeknownst to most audiences today, the memoirs that form the basis of the film The Pianist (2002) were likely ghostwritten by a non-Jewish music critic, Jerzy Waldorff, who was notorious for his antisemitic and fascist views prior to the war. Drawing on rarely considered archival sources and attending to the original 1946 text of the memoirs, this article contextualizes them within the political climate of early post-war Poland, where they were written and published. title: The Socio-Cultural Basis of Sendang Lamongan Batik: An Integrated Cultural-Historical Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the socio-cultural foundations underlying the emergence and development of Sendang Lamongan Batik across centuries. Employing a qualitative method with an anthropological-historical approach, the study integrates Fernand Braudel's concept of long-term history (longue duree) and Marvin Harris's cultural materialism into a unified analytical framework. Data were collected through direct observation, in-depth interviews with two village heads, three artisans, three entrepreneurs, and two batik traders, and archival documentation. title: Stable isotope analysis of freshwater gastropod carbonates from Swanscombe: Insights into climate stability and seasonality during MIS 11c
abstract: ABSTRACT Stable isotope analyses of freshwater mollusc carbonate can record environmental conditions at the time of mineralisation, yet this technique remains underused in British Middle Pleistocene fluvial sequences, despite the abundance of fossil shell material in these deposits. We present new δ 18 O and δ 13 C measurements from calcitic Bithynia tentaculata opercula and aragonitic Valvata piscinalis shells from fluvial sediments at Swanscombe, in the Lower Thames Valley, correlated with the Hoxnian Interglacial (MIS 11c). title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids in the Prevention of Cardiovascular Diseases: Still Relevant?
abstract: Background: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide, responsible for an estimated 17.9 million deaths annually. Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) - principally eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) derived from marine sources, and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) from plant sources - have been investigated for decades as potential modulators of cardiovascular risk. journal: Journal of Education Health and Sport

title: A Fully Green Process Based on Recycled Primary Zn–C Battery and Natural Lemon Extract for Highly Efficient, Salt Tolerant, and Multi‐Use Desalination
abstract: Solar evaporation for seawater desalination requires solar absorber materials with high solar‐to‐thermal conversion efficiency, good heat retention ability, and salt tolerance. The material purity standards for the stated purpose are not very stringent; hence, recycled materials can potentially address both the issues of affordability and functionality concurrently. title: Cross-Library Audit of DFT Magnetic Moments for Curie-Temperature Ranking: An Empirical Residual-Gating Protocol
abstract: Reliable magnetic-materials screening requires more than a model that performs well within one computational catalogue. We develop and audit a composition-anchored library residual (CALR) protocol for transferring density-functional-theory (DFT) magnetic-moment information across heterogeneous databases. title: PIRATE MUSEUMS AND THEIR CONTRIBUTION TO LOCAL DEVELOPMENT THE CASE OF ALONISSOS
abstract: Cultural heritage is one of the most important resources for differentiating contemporary tourist destinations, particularly in areas seeking to reduce their dependence on the mass-tourism model of ‘sun and sea’. In this context, thematic museums can showcase local history, strengthen cultural identity, and create new visitor experiences. Museums devoted to maritime and pirate heritage are of particular interest because they connect historical interpretation with experiential engagement and destination appeal. title: “A Candle in the Darkness”: On Palestine Uprooted: Nakba Past and Present at the Canadian Museum for Human Rights
abstract: A scholar of Jewish studies, Itay Zutra reviews On Palestine Uprooted: Nakba Past and Present, an exhibit at the Canadian Museum for Human Rights that opened in June 2026 and is expected to run through November 2028. The exhibit, curated by Isabelle Masson, recognizes the historic and ongoing displacement of Palestinians by the Israeli government by including both historic relics from the initial removal of Palestinians in 1948 and contemporary art engaging continued violence there. title: Toponymy and Shifted Identity: A Study of the Language Change in Rejang-Language Village Names
abstract: This study examines the changes in village names from the Rejang language to Indonesian in Kepahiang Regency, Bengkulu, focusing on referential meanings, community perceptions, and the impact on local cultural identity. Using referential meaning analysis and thematic analysis based on interviews with both older and younger generations, the findings show that the language shift alters not only linguistic forms but also the cultural, historical, and spiritual values embedded in the original toponyms. title: Method for estimating 13 C NMR chemical shifts in sp3 hybridized C atoms as a simple NMR teaching strategy
abstract: By observing the chemical shifts of Z / cis and E / trans of small groups such as alkyl (methyl, methylene), and hydroxyl groups, their determination of the configuration can be determined via shielding effect between neighboring groups. Such effect is a shielding relationship between the groups which are close to each other in space. Their proximity in space can be confirmed by correlations in the 1 H – 1 H NOESY NMR (nuclear overhauser effect spectroscopy nuclear magnetic resonance) spectra. title: Climate change exposure and firm value in China: evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation
abstract: This paper examines the relationship between firm-level climate change exposure and firm value in China. Using A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2020 and a disclosure-based measure of perceived climate change exposure, we find a significant negative association between climate change exposure and firm value. Our measure provides incremental explanatory power beyond conventional proxies, including ESG indicators and climate change news risk measures. title: Institutional Development and Political Activities of the Permanent Ottoman Embassy in Madrid (1857–1922)
abstract: Although the Ottoman Empire experienced a chronological delay in transitioning to permanent diplomacy, it established an embassy in Madrid, as it did in various other European cities, to improve its relations with European states and to closely monitor continental politics. This study aims to analyze the activities of the Madrid Embassy, which operated between 1857 and 1922, and its strategic role in nineteenth-century Ottoman diplomacy. abstract: Abstract People living in and around terrestrial and marine protected areas can contribute to protected area law enforcement in different ways. While the involvement of local residents is considered important for bringing benefits to both conservation and people, evaluations of community‐based approaches to protected area law enforcement are limited. We conducted a qualitative evaluation of an intervention that represents a common model for community engagement in protected area law enforcement. abstract: Ògún, Ọba and Ọ̀ràmfẹ̀ festivals are the most elaborately celebrated festivals in Oǹdó Kingdom, for their spiritual and social significance. Some of the dramatic features which make up the festivals are costumes, make-up, and properties. abstract: Bottom sediments of Arctic lakes are widely used as archives of environmental change and indicators of trace element accumulation. However, the interpretation of integrated geochemical pollution indices may be complicated in regions with complex geological settings, where natural lithogenic and post-sedimentary processes significantly influence sediment chemistry. title: The Parish Church of San José in Montealto (1960-68)
abstract: In 1954, the Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela commissioned the young priest José Lamas Pallas to start up the parish church of San José in the Montealto neighborhood of A Coruña, located at the end of the peninsula on which the Tower of Hercules stands. The church was designed by Jacobo Rodríguez-Losada Trúlock, a respected architect who has received little historiographical attention to date. title: Archaeobotanical Data Reveal Divergent Agricultural Strategies in the Uplands and Lowlands of Ancient Iraq
abstract: Agriculture is considered a primary driver for the emergence of some of the world’s earliest large-scale urban societies in ancient Iraq. Plant remains recovered on archaeological sites from the area represent a unique opportunity to explore the evolution of the plant-based economy directly over the longue durée and across different ecological zones. title: ¿Sinónimos o divergentes? Sobre los conceptos “lenguaje no sexista”, “lenguaje inclusivo de género” y “lenguaje inclusivo” en la prensa española
abstract: This study analyses the use of the terms in the Spanish press ‘inclusive language’, ‘gender-inclusive language’ and ‘non-sexist language’, which are often used imprecisely. Inclusive language seeks to include every person or group regardless of their gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, age, etc.; genderinclusive language aims to include include all gender identities, including non-binary ones, whilst non-sexist language focuses on non-discrimination on the grounds of sex. title: The Lake Urmia Disaster – Manmade or Natural
abstract: Was the desiccation of Lake Urmia a natural disaster or a manmade collapse? This paper reverts climatic factors from foregrounds to background but brings forth a range of hidden drivers and diagnostic techniques to unravel the decisive role of the trigger cause: infrastructural encroachments, planning omissions, and governance failures. Applying the SPRC (Source, Pathways, Receptors, Consequences) framework, the analysis reveals how human decisions transformed a vulnerable lake into a wicked problem. title: Multi-wavelength spectral attribution of equivalent black carbon in Medellín, Colombia (2010–2023): Disentangling fossil fuel and biomass burning using the MABI instrument
abstract: Black carbon (BC) remains a critical driver of radiative forcing and urban health degradation, yet its source-specific dynamics in tropical Andean basins are poorly understood. This study provides the first multi-wavelength spectral characterization of equivalent black carbon (eBC) in the Aburrá Valley (Colombia) using the Multi-Wavelength Absorption Black Carbon Instrument (MABI). title: Regional sonic cosmopolitanism: Palestinian musicians and Arab urban music in the Galilee region, 1948–1980
abstract: This article examines how Palestinian wedding musicians in the Galilee region sustained engagement with regional Arab urban music traditions during the decades following the 1948 Nakba. While the events of 1948 shattered the musical infrastructure that had connected Palestinian cities including Haifa to the broader Arab world, cosmopolitan Arab art music continues until today to form part of the everyday sonic lives of Palestinian communities in northern Israel. title: Un documento xudicial inédito: achegamento aos preitos e conflitos no Ribeiro medieval
abstract: This article presents a transcription of an unpublished judicial document from the Archive of Ourense Cathedral concerning the monastery of San Clodio do Ribeiro. The edition includes a brief study of the two manuscripts recording the proceedings and an examination of the dispute between the monastery and Vasco Rodríguez de Espiño, a squire serving the adelantado mayor of the kingdom of Galicia. The litigation, conducted between 1429 and 1434, concerns the possession of property in the parish of Santa María de Beade. title: Petro-structural geology of the Northern Adula Nappe Complex (Central Penninic Alps, Switzerland)
abstract: The Adula Nappe Complex is the largest fragment of Penninic continental crust in the Central Alps, where it deformed alongside the Valais Ocean ophiolites and metasediments. This study presents an integrated structural and petrological analysis of its northern tip, where pre-Alpine eclogites occur within phengite-bearing schists. Field investigations identified five Alpine ductile deformation phases in the phengite-bearing schists. title: Performance Optimization of Stand-Alone Solar PV Systems for Rural Electrification
abstract: Background: Rural electrification remains a major development challenge in Nigeria, particularly in the northern regions where grid extension is economically and technically constrained. Stand-alone solar photovoltaic (PV) systems have emerged as a viable alternative due to their modularity, declining costs, and suitability for decentralized energy access. title: The Use of Suspended Substrate to Facilitate Juvenile Mussel Recruitment in Restored Mussel Reefs
abstract: Mussel reefs have been depleted globally by overfishing and habitat degradation, but the advent of reef restoration has produced promising results in terms of adult mussel survival and biodiversity enhancement. However, an absence of juvenile recruitment into restored mussel reefs is regularly cited as jeopardising their persistence and expansion. title: Overturning urban visuality: knockoff aesthetics and the unruly kings of Hong Kong
abstract: This article examines the aesthetic and political significance of the street writings of Hong Kong’s King of Kowloon (Tsang Tsou-choi) and Plumber King (Yim Chiu-tong) beyond celebratory framings of collective memory. Drawing on archival research and extensive fieldwork-based visual analysis, it develops knockoff aesthetics as a framework for understanding how political force can emerge from urban inscriptions widely received as improper and visually unappealing. title: The Effect of Omega-3 Fatty Acids Supplement on Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: Autism is characterized by impairments in social interaction and communication skills, as well as repetitive behaviors and restricted interests. This review examined the potential effects of omega-3 fatty acid consumption on individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Articles included in the study were searched comprehensively in electronic databases such as PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar. title: GOVERNING INFORMALITY : Eviction, Recognition, and Legal Ambiguity in Kampung Akuarium, Jakarta
abstract: Abstract Informal settlements in Jakarta have long been governed through cycles of tolerance, eviction, and selective recognition. Rather than resulting from the absence of planning, informality is often produced through spatial regulations, legal ambiguity, and political intervention. This article examines Kampung Akuarium, a settlement in North Jakarta, to explore how informality is governed through planning instruments and political change. title: Crop Husbandry After the Assyrian Conquest: The Case Study of Tel Kinrot (Kinneret, Tell el ʿ Orēme )
abstract: In 733/732 BCE, the Neo-Assyrian Empire conquered the Kingdom of Israel in the southern Levant, transforming settlement patterns and local economies. Scholars continue to debate the Assyrian economic agenda: some emphasise neglect, agricultural decline, and tribute extraction, while others argue that the Assyrian administration strategically reorganised agricultural production to meet local administrative and military needs. title: Managing Hydro-dependence and Risk: Hong Kong’s Water Insurance Policy, 1967–1982
abstract: Abstract Using archival and unofficial sources, this article examines how political calculations, economic considerations, local consumption patterns and international dynamics shaped the colonial administration’s water governance strategies in Hong Kong. It focuses on how the 1967 water emergency prompted the colonial government to recalibrate its approach, from a policy of manageable dependency to one of risk aversion. title: La literatura de la España vacía: la despoblación como motor temático en La tierra desnuda de Rafael Navarro de Castro y Lo demás es aire de Juan Gómez Bárcena
abstract: This article examines how contemporary narrative addresses the phenomenon of rural depopulation in Spain, focusing on two paradigmatic novels: La tierra desnuda (2019) by Rafael Navarro de Castro, and Lo demás es aire (2022) by Juan Gómez Bárcena. Within the framework of “rural literatures”—a term preferred over the more contested “neorrural literature”—the notion of a “literature of empty Spain” is proposed, understood as that in which demographic decline functions as a thematic driving force. title: Settler colonial biopolitics at the border: a transnational entanglement of law, medical sciences, and migration control at Ellis Island
abstract: Migration from Europe to the United States in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries is known for its confrontation with racialized and gendered migration control. In line with this, this paper aims to analytically extend the migration control of that period to the biopolitics of settler colonialism. By patchworking transnational archives (in the United States and the Netherlands), it investigates how medical and immigration control infrastructures were established at Ellis Island (US) and how they operated to identify ‘undesirable immigrants’. title: It’s about time: On the uneven temporalities of Turkey’s first mega-dam
abstract: This article examines the Keban Dam (1966–1974), Turkey’s first mega-dam on the Upper Euphrates, as a case study of the uneven temporalities embedded in energy infrastructures. Conceptualising the dam as an infrastructural chronotope, it shows how mega-dams mediate conflicting temporalities linked to Cold War geopolitics, state-led modernisation and global capital. abstract: Cigading 1 Port, operated by PT Krakatau Bandar Samudera, demonstrates good operational service performance; however, the utilization of its storage facilities remains suboptimal, as indicated by the low Shed Occupancy Ratio (SOR) and Yard Occupancy Ratio (YOR). This study aims to analyze the utilization levels of warehouses and storage yards, identify the factors contributing to low utilization, and formulate strategies to improve their utilization. abstract: Abstract Archaeological studies of the transatlantic slave trade in West Africa have traditionally focused on coastal and discrete sites of slavery, leaving interior communities comparatively underexplored. This paper advances methodological frameworks for the archaeology of transatlantic trade that move beyond the search for direct material signatures of enslavement to examine the circulation, appropriation, social valuation, and consumption of imported trade goods, and how they shaped political and economic landscapes in Peki, an Ewe-speaking polity in southeastern Ghana. abstract: ABSTRACT Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is the dominant non‐native fish species in Kenya's inland waters, but its spread reflects a coupled socioecological process rather than a simple biological invasion. This review examines the socio‐economic, governance and ecological drivers of its expansion within a socioecological systems and invasion biology framework, with evidence published between 2000 and 2025. abstract: Precision medicine selects individual treatments from a small toolbox of therapies already available. Personalized drug discovery (PDD) brings this concept one step ahead, developing drugs for individual patient's diseases. abstract: Domoic acid (DA) produced by toxigenic species of the diatom genus Pseudo-nitzschia during harmful algal blooms (HABs) bioaccumulates in filter feeders, bait fish, and commercial seafood products, posing a threat to marine organisms and public health. abstract: Abstract From small molecules and systemic administration to biologics and targeted drug–carrier complexes, the drug delivery field’s “toolbox” of therapeutic materials has skyrocketed in scope and sophistication over the past decade alone. The tunable properties, modularity, and structural control afforded by such materials as lipids, synthetic polymers, peptides, and polysaccharides are highly favorable not only to the design of novel drugs but also drug carriers which help guide and deliver them. abstract: In this study, 8 of the 11 lakes on Valaam Island were surveyed: Leshchevoe, Nikonovskoe, Krestovoe, Sisjarvi, Igumenskoe, Chernoe, Ossievo, and Germanovskoe. Ichthyological fieldwork on lakes Nikonovskoe and Leschevoe in June 2025 was the first effort of this kind for these lakes; additionally, interview data and photographic materials from 2004–2026 were used. abstract: In the twenty-first century, international politics unfolds within a battlespace where narratives, imagery, and algorithmic influence operate alongside conventional instruments of power. As reality itself becomes a strategic target, state and nonstate actors weaponize information to shape perception, legitimacy, and decision-making. abstract: Abstract Precise dating of Carlin-type gold deposits (CTDs) remains challenging owing to the scarcity of suitable, widely distributed minerals for reliable isotopic dating. title: Knowledge Driven Event Extraction from Low Resource Language Content Using Strategic Few-Shot Learning
abstract: Timely extracting structured information from social media during disaster events is critical for effective response and coordination. This work presents a comprehensive pipeline for sub-event information extraction (IE) from Hindi-language tweets and news articles, covering eleven key categories such as casualties, infrastructure damage, relief operations and others. We introduce CrisisIE-Hindi, a benchmark dataset of around 9.6k annotated posts spanning cyclone, earthquake, flood and other disaster events. abstract: Within the meroplankton, the group of fish eggs and larvae is specifically called ichthyoplankton. To increase knowledge about ichthyoplankton in Mochima Bay, bimonthly collections were made from December 2015 to October 2016 at three stations within the bay. abstract: The lungs are one of the target organs affected by scorpion venom. Given the expansion of scorpion distribution ranges and climate change, the likelihood of venomous scorpions appearing in new territories inhabited by humans is increasing. Thus, there is a need for an in-depth morphological study of the delayed outcomes of envenomation by medically significant scorpion species. abstract: Background: Catch per unit effort (CPUE), fishing effort, and production data for Pseudotolithus senegalensis remain limited in Mondoukou, Côte d’Ivoire. abstract: Sustainable agricultural water governance in monsoon-dependent tropical watersheds requires effective socio-institutional mechanisms alongside physical engineering interventions. This study evaluates the role of local institutional capacity building in driving sustainable irrigation management within the Cidanau-Ciujung-Cidurian (CCC) River Basin, Serang Regency, Indonesia. title: Near‐infrared confocal imaging reveals the spatial organisation of far‐red photosynthesis in Shark Bay microbial mats and Halomicronema sp.
abstract: Far-red light (FRL) cyanobacteria occupy spectrally filtered habitats where visible wavelengths are depleted but far-red radiation persists. title: Resilient Civil Infrastructure Design against Earthquake and Flood Risks Under Climate Change
abstract: The civil infrastructure is becoming more and more prone to earthquake and flood hazards whereas climate change is adding another level of uncertainty for infrastructure designs, structural performance, and sustainability. This research work attempts to explore resilient civil infrastructure designs under earthquake and flood hazards and changing climatic conditions, which include topics related to structural vulnerability, multi-hazard assessment, climate adaptation, and sustainable engineering practices. title: Dating of Late Pleistocene sediments along the coast of Brittany (W France) by Optically Stimulated Luminescence, paleoclimate implications and Eemian highstand
abstract: Numerous sedimentary deposits are present along the coast of Brittany (W France). It is assumed that these sequences are related to glacioeustatic variations of the Late Pleistocene, but the scarcity of reliable ages prevent accurate chronological constraints to correlate their deposition with a clearly defined paleoclimate context. title: Trophic reorganization may contribute to shifts in nitrogen transformations following alleviation of saline alkaline stress
abstract: Soil salinization is a widespread form of land degradation, yet how saline-alkaline stress is linked to belowground micro-food webs and shapes nitrogen transformations remains poorly understood. Here we compare natural saline–sodic and reclaimed farmland soils in northeastern China using microscopy and genetic sequencing. Farmland has higher nematode and prokaryote abundances and greater nematode, protist and prokaryote richness, whereas fungal richness is higher in solonetz soils. Nitrogen mineralization rates and nitrification potential are 118.2% and 72.3% higher in farmland, respectively.

abstract: Antecedentes y Objetivos: Silene es uno de los géneros más diversos de Caryophyllaceae. abstract: A study carried out on the dam impacted Dikrong River, which is one of the major tributaries of the Brahmaputra in Arunachal Pradesh, suggests that the river has undergone significant ecological alteration following the commissioning of the Sopo dam in 2018 and increasing anthropogenic pressures. abstract: Abstract Complex systems can experience gradual or sudden changes in their dynamics when a system parameter changes. For real world systems such as animal populations, vegetation fields, and climate systems, it is important to develop analysis tools able to infer that a change of behavior is approaching. title: Behavioral thermoregulation and survival of released Brook Trout following assisted recovery after angling
abstract: Abstract Objective Temperature plays a critical role in postrelease outcomes and survival from catch-and-release recreational angling. During warm periods in lentic systems, the ability of coldwater fish such as Brook Trout Salvelinus fontinalis to avoid warm surface waters or other water column regions that exceed thermal thresholds is essential for postrelease recovery. abstract: Abstract The Breede River in the Western Cape Province is one of South Africa’s major freshwater systems and of high ecological and socio-economic value. Similar to other freshwater systems worldwide, it is threatened by environmental degradation and multiple invasive species. title: Detection of black loss in aquaculture using machine vision
abstract: Black loss (the unaccounted loss of fish in fish farming) is a widespread problem in aquaculture that has economic, reputational and welfare implications. abstract: Introduction Phenotypic plasticity enables organisms to adjust their traits in response to environmental conditions, yet studies of animal coloration, particularly in cephalopods, have largely focused on rapid neural control while overlooking slower changes in the cellular substrate underlying color change. Here, we investigated whether morphological color change contributes to phenotypic plasticity in the bigfin reef squid ( Sepioteuthis lessoniana ). abstract: Pisciculture has been established as a strategic activity in the Amazon, with emphasis on the cultivation of tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum) and its hybrids. abstract: Climate change and global warming have significantly impacted the water cycle and water resources in the Himalayan region. This study focused on the effects of climate change and human intervention on water resources in the Ladakh region over the past decades. Changes in snowfall and glacial patterns, rapid runoff, and erratic rainfall due to changes in the snow season and an increase in temperature have resulted in water scarcity in this area. abstract: Abstract Radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating and dietary reconstruction of 28 cremated individuals excavated from the Ishibotoke-dani site in Taga Town, Shiga Prefecture, Japan, was performed to investigate the lifeways of a medieval Buddhist community. abstract: Habitat degradation and loss due to anthropogenic pressures are the primary threats to biodiversity, particularly in tropical forests. Monitoring bird communities provides valuable insights into the environmental status of both natural and human-modified ecosystems. In this study (February–April 2021), the point count method was used to assess avian species richness, diversity, and density in Amangarh Tiger Reserve (ATR)—a human-impacted forest area, aiming to understand its ecological importance and conservation potential. abstract: This study investigated the dynamics of land cover change in the Bhairabkunda region of Assam, with a focus on the emergence of grasslands resulting from flood-driven river course changes. The objective was to assess how flooding events and subsequent ecological succession influenced grassland formation and their role in supporting the ‘Critically Endangered’ Bengal Florican Houbaropsis bengalensis. title: Prospective life cycle assessment of redesigned airplane rudder with thermoplastic composites
abstract: Abstract The aviation industry is innovating to decrease its environmental impacts while maintaining high standards of safety. For example, new thermoplastic composite materials are being investigated to reduce weight and allow for material recycling (currently impossible with incumbent thermoset composites). abstract: Abstract Macrophytes are important in structuring various aquatic communities, particularly cladocerans. Our findings highlight that plant structural complexity and functional life forms (specifically free-floating and submerged species) act as key drivers of interaction density and network stability, providing essential microhabitats for cladocerans in tropical oxbow lakes. abstract: Abstract Citizen science data are increasingly used to infer species distributions and monitor biodiversity at large spatial scales. However, recording effort is often uneven across space, potentially biasing inferences about species’ distributions. We analysed 51,045 butterfly records submitted via the iRecord Butterflies app in Devon and Cornwall, in the southwest of the United Kingdom. abstract: Abstract Understanding how basin-scale heterogeneity influences phytoplankton in regulated reservoirs is essential for reconciling water management and conservation objectives. We analysed phytoplankton assemblages across five environmentally distinct basins and the Kis-Tisza of Lake Tisza during the exceptionally dry summer of 2022, when water levels were reduced to winter stage. abstract: Abstract Migratory bats remain poorly understood despite their ecological importance and increasing exposure to anthropogenic threats. We present twelve years of monitoring of Pipistrellus nathusii at Bedfont Lakes, the first bat box site in the UK to document use by this species. abstract: Abstract Beavers are keystone species that modify ecosystem structure and function through dam building, thereby creating a complex mosaic of lotic and lentic ecosystems. title: De Novo Discovery of Bioactive Cyclic Peptides via Cellular Selection of Genetically Encoded Libraries
abstract: Cellular selection has emerged as a powerful approach for high throughput de novo discovery of bioactive cyclic peptides (CPs). This strategy coexpresses genetically encoded CP libraries with the target of interest in cells and uses customizable selection systems to link desired CP activities to a selectable phenotype to directly identify functional inhibitors. Cellular selections have yielded many CP inhibitors against a diverse range of therapeutic targets and have been continuously empowered by expansions in the CP diversity and selection repertoire. title: Harnessing shrimp shell waste: enhanced chitinase production through optimization techniques for ecofriendly solutions using bacteria
abstract: Chitinous wastes, particularly shrimp shell residues, represent a major underutilized biomass resource with significant potential for bioconversion into high-value products. In this study, four thermophilic bacterial strains (Bacillus amyloliquefaciens BT 2022, Bacillus licheniformis Basma87, Priestia megaterium AMD 2024, and Streptomyces maritimus MSQ-2021) were screened for their ability to produce chitinase using shrimp shell waste (SSW) as the sole carbon and nitrogen source. title: Volatile Conduits Beneath Vulcano Island (Italy) Revealed by High‐Resolution Nodal Local Earthquake Tomography During Volcanic Unrest
abstract: Abstract Understanding shallow magmatic and hydrothermal systems at active volcanoes is essential for interpreting unrest and forecasting eruptions. We present the first high‐resolution three‐dimensional , , and models of Vulcano Island, Aeolian Islands, Italy, derived from a dense nodal seismic network. During 1 month of acquisition in 2021, coinciding with volcanic unrest, we detected and picked 1749 local earthquakes. title: Evaluating wildlife rehabilitation: successful return of rehabilitated gulls to the wild
abstract: Abstract The expansion of human activities has increased the need for animal rehabilitation, especially for urban-breeding species such as herring gulls (Larus argentatus) and lesser black-backed gulls (Larus fuscus), which now commonly nest on buildings and industrial sites. This study evaluates rehabilitation effectiveness by comparing survival and post-release reintegration, measured through habitat use and the degree of association with human-dominated environments, between rehabilitated and wild juvenile gulls along the Belgian coast. title: Baseline spatiotemporal patterns in the invertebrate diet of Eurasian Tree Sparrow Passer montanus chicks revealed using DNA metabarcoding
abstract: Capsule DNA metabarcoding revealed that the diet of Eurasian Tree Sparrow chicks at three sites in the UK was dominated by ground beetles Carabidae, suggesting parental foraging was predominantly ground-based.Aims Most bird species in temperate environments rely on invertebrates as a food resource, so widespread and substantial invertebrate declines are important in the context of avian conservation. title: 3D radial anisotropic imaging of magma plumbing systems beneath the Malani silicic igneous province in northwestern India
abstract: Abstract Imaging the plumbing systems of ancient silicic large igneous provinces (SLIPs) is inherently challenging due to the decay of thermal anomalies associated with SLIPs, and the erosion or masking of surface expressions by sediments. The plumbing architecture of the Neoproterozoic Malani SLIP, remains unresolved, due to limited geophysical evidence of magma conduits or sill complexes. We present the first 3D crustal isotropic shear velocity and radially anisotropic models obtained through ambient noise tomography beneath northwestern India. title: Effects of replacing fish oil with Antarctic krill oil on the growth and ovarian development of female Litopenaeus vannamei broodstock
abstract: This study examined how replacing fish oil with Antarctic krill oil affects the growth and reproduction of female Litopenaeus vannamei broodstock. Six isonitrogenous and isolipidic diet were formulated to replace fish oil with varying percentages of Antarctic krill oil, specifically at 0% (O1), 20% (O2), 40% (O3), 60% (O4), 80% (O5), 100% (O6). These diets were then administered to L. vannamei broodstock, which had an initial average weight of 24.74 ± 0.13 g, over a 70-day experimental period. title: The African Mole‐Rat Genus Cryptomys and Its Species: Distinct in Their Genes and Habitats
abstract: ABSTRACT The African mole‐rat genus Cryptomys comprises five morphologically cryptic lineages distributed across South Africa and in Zimbabwe, historically treated as subspecies of C. hottentotus ( C. h. hottentotus , C. h. mahali , C. h. natalensis , C. h. pretoriae and C. h. nimrodi ). Despite extensive ecological and physiological research, their taxonomic status and evolutionary relationships have remained unresolved because of limited genetic data. Here, we integrate mitochondrial and genome‐wide nuclear data, broad geographic sampling and environmental niche modelling to reassess species

title: Dynamic Land Use Change in SWAT +: A Novel Application of Scenario Decision Tables
abstract: ABSTRACT Land use and land cover (LULC) changes significantly impact hydrological processes, yet their dynamic representation in hydrological models remains a challenge. This paper introduces and pioneers the use of the newly implemented capability of SWAT+ to simulate dynamic LULC changes using “land use scenario decision tables”. Traditionally, LULC change assessments in hydrological modeling rely on a static “delta approach,” which often leads to inaccurate parameterization and limitations in capturing the true temporal evolution of hydrological responses. journal: JAWRA Journal of the American Water Resources Association

title: Malware detection using dynamic analysis with a modified Harris Hawk optimizer
abstract: The rapid advancement of technology has significantly enhanced innovation, productivity, and connectivity across industries but has also empowered cybercriminals to develop increasingly sophisticated malware. This advanced malware poses serious challenges to cybersecurity, as traditional detection methods often fail to recognize new, unknown, or obfuscated attacks. title: Profiling autofluorescence signatures of microplastics from commercial plastic products by flow cytometry and multivariate analysis
abstract: Microplastics exhibit autofluorescence, yet how this optical property varies among particles derived from commercial plastic products and its potential for stain-free differentiation remain poorly understood. This study investigated the autofluorescence signatures of polyethylene terephthalate, high-density polyethylene, polyvinyl chloride, polypropylene, and polystyrene fragmented from various packaging, household, and construction materials using multichannel flow cytometry. Autofluorescence was measured across eleven fluorescence detection channels alongside forward scatter and side scatter

title: Plant belowground traits indicate increased plant-mediated methane transport along a peatland permafrost thaw gradient
abstract: Permafrost thaw alters methane (CH 4 ) fluxes from subarctic peatland ecosystems. Collapsing permafrost palsas change hydrology, interstitial oxygen availability, and vegetation composition, and each of these factors contribute to net CH 4 flux by influencing CH 4 production, consumption and transport. Changes in plant-mediated CH 4 fluxes have mostly been estimated using aboveground characteristics, such as biomass and leaf area, leaving belowground parts (roots and rhizomes) understudied despite their direct contact to depth-dependent CH 4 flux processes. title: A foldable small-scale soft electromagnetic robot for multimodal navigation in confined and unstructured environments
abstract: Multimodal locomotion is crucial for an animal’s adaptability in unstructured wild environments. Analogously, in the human gastrointestinal tract, characterized by viscoelastic mucus, complex rugae, and narrow openings like the cardia, multimodal locomotion is also essential for a small-scale soft robot to conduct tasks. Here, we introduce a small-scale, compact, foldable, and robust soft electromagnetic robot with more than nine locomotion modes designed for such a scenario. title: Freeze–thaw processes influence shallow groundwater recharge sources and pathways in the Qinghai Lake Basin: insights from water isotopes
abstract: Groundwater plays a crucial role in maintaining baseflow in rivers and ensuring water supply, particularly in alpine regions where the freeze–thaw (FT) cycle exerts a strong influence on hydrological processes. However, a systematic understanding is still lacking regarding how FT processes affect the composition of groundwater recharge sources and the transitions among recharge pathways. title: Multicriteria optimization and decision making of ultrasound-assisted hydrothermal liquefaction process of Cladophora glomerata macro-algae for biooil production
abstract: This study optimizes ultrasound-assisted hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of Cladophora glomerata using response surface methodology (RSM), multi-objective optimization (MOO), and multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM). However, achieving high biooil yield while simultaneously minimizing the formation of biogas, hydrochar yield, and aqueous by-products remains a major challenge because of the complex interactions among HTL operating parameters. title: AVA‐MAPbI 3 Cap‐and‐Root Islands on Mesoporous TiO 2 Toward Neutral‐Color Semi‐Transparent Perovskite Solar Cells in Agrivoltaics
abstract: Semi‐transparent perovskite solar cells offer a route to agrivoltaics, combining electricity generation with controlled light transmission for crop cultivation. However, conventional perovskite films preferentially absorb blue photons, producing redshifted transmitted spectra that can affect plant photophysiology. This work presents quasi‐neutral‐color semi‐transparent perovskite films based on AVA‐MAPbI 3 islands rooted in mesoporous TiO 2 (mp‐TiO 2 ). title: Gastrointestinal Endoparasites in Captive Exotic Psittacines Birds: Prevalence and Associated Factors in Two Conservation in East Java, Indonesia
abstract: Gastrointestinal endoparasites infections in captive exotic psittacine birds (Psittaciformes) represent a significant health concern affecting avian well-being in managed environments. This study aimed to identify the parasitic species involved, determine the prevalence of infection, and analyze factors associated with gastrointestinal endoparasite infection, including husbandry management practices and environmental conditions, in conservation centers in Prigen and Batu, Indonesia Sampling was conducted over a six-month period using two approaches: direct collection of fresh fecal samples fro

title: Shallow Poroelastic Hydrothermal Deformation at Changbaishan Volcano Before the 2020 Unrest Revealed by Sentinel‐1 InSAR Time Series
abstract: Abstract Ground deformation of dormant volcanoes provides critical insights into subsurface processes and potential hazards. Here we present Sentinel‐1 Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) time series (2015–2020) for Changbaishan volcano, the largest intraplate volcanic system in East Asia. We detect persistent subsidence of up to 3.5 mm/yr on the eastern flank of the summit prior to minor unrest in December 2020. title: Design and realization of robust disturbance rejection decoupling control strategy for time delayed multi-variable process
abstract: Abstract This paper presents design and development of a robust decentralized PI controller exploiting an analytical model based approach for multi-variable system. In this work, a two-degree-of-freedom control approach is employed to tackle load disturbance rejection, enhance robustness against parametric uncertainties, and ensure precise set-point tracking. title: Bioelectrochemical treatment of untreated spent car catalyst: Effects of solids loading on platinum group metal redistribution and process limitations
abstract: Spent car catalyst (SCC) is a secondary source of platinum group metals (PGMs), but recovery commonly requires high-temperature smelting or aggressive chemical leaching. Bioelectrochemical treatment offers milder conditions, though most studies use dissolved metal salts rather than untreated catalyst solids, leaving their behaviour with real SCC poorly characterised. Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 was operated in dual-chamber microbial fuel cells with untreated SCC at 0; 10,000; 50,000; and 100,000 ppm for 168 h, with abiotic controls at each loading. title: Green stone, hidden life: Bacterial and fungal communities on the weathered serpentinite cladding of Florence Cathedral
abstract: Serpentinite is a metamorphic rock widely employed in architecture for its aesthetic value. In Tuscany (Italy), it acquired significant symbolic and cultural relevance during the Gothic and Renaissance periods, becoming a distinctive element of regional architectural identity. Within the region, Florence stands out for its extensive use in the characteristic polychrome cladding of several major monuments, including the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore (SMFC). abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we have designed and synthesized two novel metal‐free organic D‐π‐A dyes with 6‐methoxy‐N‐(4‐(methylthio)phenyl)‐N‐phenylnaphthalen‐2‐amine (SP‐3) and N‐(4‐(methylthio)phenyl)‐N‐phenylpyren‐2‐amine (SP‐4) as the donor moiety, cyanoacrylic acid as the anchoring unit and thiophene as the π‐spacer. title: Random amplified polymorphic DNA-based assessment of genetic variation in natural and cultivated allspice (Pimenta dioica (L.) Merr.) populations in Guatemala
abstract: The fruit of the allspice tree (Pimenta dioica (L.) Merr.) is a valuable non-timber forest product traded for its flavour, oils and secondary metabolites. Intense selection pressure from traditional harvesting methods has favoured low-height, high-yield phenotypes, potentially impacting genetic diversity. Although phenotypic variations have been observed, no baseline molecular genetic assessments have been conducted in Guatemala to evaluate the impact of these practices. title: Low-carbon ultra-high-performance concrete: raw materials, particle packing optimization, and data-driven performance assessment—a review
abstract: Ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) offers exceptional mechanical properties and durability; however, its cement-intensive formulations raise concerns regarding environmental sustainability. This study addresses this challenge by establishing quantitative relationships between UHPC mixture design, performance indicators, and embodied CO 2 emissions by coupling a literature survey with data-driven analysis of over 200 mixtures. title: The First Quantitative Evidence of Ontogenetic Growth in the Early Cambrian Ecdysozoan Worm Cricocosmia jinningensis Reveals the Earliest Energy Reallocation
abstract: Ontogeny is both biologically pivotal and ubiquitous among extant ecdysozoans. Ontogenetic data from the fossil record offer direct evidence for resolving questions of developmental evolution within this clade. However, such data remain exceedingly scarce, especially for ecdysozoan worms. Here, our study provides the first comprehensive analysis of the growth pattern of the early Cambrian ecdysozoan worm Cricocosmia jinningensis from the Chengjiang biota. title: Petrogenesis and geodynamic setting of Ediacaran rocks from the Sirwa massif, Central Anti-Atlas of Morocco
abstract: The geodynamic evolution of the post-Pan-African Anti-Atlas Orogeny (∼ 650 Ma) remains debated, particularly regarding the basement beneath the Central Anti-Atlas and the geological processes leading to the formation of the Ediacaran Saghro Group (SG) and Ouarzazate Group (OG). New LA-ICP-MS U-Pb ages of 575 ± 3 Ma and 564 ± 2 Ma were obtained from two OG magmatic rocks. title: Beyond GDP: Integrating the Total Economic Value of Wetland and Forest Ecosystem Services into Rwanda’s National Accounting System
abstract: Rwanda’s wetlands and forests deliver crucial socio-economic and environmental value, especially in building climate resilience and supporting livelihoods. Still, most of their macroeconomic contribution is omitted from national metrics like GDP, leading policies to focus on immediate economic returns, often to the detriment of these important natural infrastructures. To bridge this gap in measuring natural capital, we developed, established, and launched the Rwanda Integrated Valuation Framework (RIVF). title: Shallow lithosphere structure in the north-central region of the gulf of California, Mexico, from seismic noise and earthquake tomography
abstract: Summary The potential for geothermal resources and the tectonic activity of the north-central region of the Gulf of California, Mexico (GoC) offer a good opportunity to investigate the lithospheric structure of this region. We used one year of ambient seismic noise and 11 shallow earthquakes recorded by the Gulf of California Broadband Seismological Network (RESBAN) and stations from the Northwest Mexico Seismic Network (RESNOM) and the National Seismological Service (SSN) to estimate the three-dimensional S-wave velocity structure. title: Rock carving depth reflects carvers’ geological insight
abstract: Rock art serves as a remarkable window into Bronze Age societies and is usually interpreted through motif and setting. The exceptionally well-preserved art in Bohuslän is recognized as world heritage with a wide range of imagery engraved into the local Bohus granite. Here we connect the depth of these carvings with near surface structure of this granite by combining ultrasonic pulse-echo B-scans with Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry and DEM based depth modelling for five major panels. title: Complexome profiling of mitochondria in the myzozoan parasite of oysters, Perkinsus marinus
abstract: Mitochondrial complexes, such as the mitochondrial electron transport chain (mETC), the F1Fo-ATP synthase, the mitochondrial ribosome and the Translocase of the Outer Membrane (TOM) complex are centrally important for mitochondrial function and cell survival. Recently, an unexpected diversity in the composition of these complexes across unicellular eukaryotic lineages, with the apicomplexan parasites featuring prominently, has been revealed. title: From acclimation to risk: Increasing drought vulnerability of introduced Pinus strobus L. across central and Eastern Europe
abstract: Climate projections suggest major shifts in tree species distributions, with most conifers expected to lose suitable habitats. In this context, non-native species may offer potential substitutes for native taxa. The introduced Pinus strobus exhibits pronounced variability in growth responses across Europe, reflecting varying levels of adaptation to environmental conditions. The aim of this study was to analyze P. strobus responses to climatic factors along a latitudinal gradient from the Baltic region to the Balkans. title: Quasi‐Global Search Behaviour of Large‐Step Gradient‐Based Optimization in Full Waveform Inversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Full waveform inversion (FWI) iteratively updates the velocity model by minimizing the difference between observed and simulated data. However, because FWI typically relies on gradient‐based local optimizers, it is prone to cycle skipping when the initial velocity model is inaccurate and low‐frequency data are absent. In such cases, the mismatch between simulated and observed data can exceed half a wavelength, causing the optimization to converge to local minima. title: A Community-Oriented and Climate-Adaptive WASH Framework for Disaster Risk Mitigation and Recovery in Rural India
abstract: Climate change, uncontrolled land use, and environmental degradation have increased the frequency and severity of natural disasters, with a particular impact on rural Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) systems in countries like India. Floods, cyclones, droughts, and earthquakes frequently disrupt water supplies, destroy sanitation facilities, and hinder hygiene services, increasing disease risk and slowing recovery. title: Architecture of the cardiac transverse–axial tubular system across different mammalian species
abstract: Abstract Cardiac excitation–contraction coupling relies on a pancellular network of regular cardiomyocyte surface membrane invaginations, termed the transverse–axial tubular system (TATS). The TATS is ubiquitously present in adult mammalian cardiomyocytes, enabling efficient structural and functional coupling of sarcolemma and intracellular Ca 2+ stores. title: Creative ventures : reimagining place and storytelling through augmented and enhanced realities
abstract: This journal article uses a practice-led research methodology to examine case studies across education, creative practice and industry engagement that use augmented and extended reality (AR/XR) technologies and concepts to tell stories of place. The three co-authors developed a practice-led inquiry, which engaged undergraduate creative industries students in interdisciplinary collaborations with cultural institutions and communities to produce site-responsive digital interventions. title: Heavy Metal Characteristics and Their Association With Microbial Communities of Wetland Soils of Shengjin and Caizi Lakes, China
abstract: Wetland soils are among the ecosystems most vulnerable to anthropogenic disturbances, and they play critical roles in biogeochemical cycling and energy exchange. In this study, we investigated the characteristics of heavy metal distribution and microbial community structures in soil samples from Shengjin Lake and Caizi Lake in China. Analysis of soil physicochemical properties revealed a significant difference in soil pH between the two lakes, whereas no significant differences were detected in organic matter content or cation exchange capacity. title: Testing the Effect of Glow Sticks on Amphibian Captures: A Literature Review and Case Study from Vernal Ponds in Iowa
abstract: Amphibians are currently experiencing population declines at faster rates than any other vertebrate group. To effectively monitor amphibian populations for conservation purposes, it is important to maximize sampling efficiency to meet the assumptions required by population estimation models, but effective monitoring is challenging because many species are secretive and difficult to capture. title: Nanoscale Surface Roughness Induces Long‐Range Ordering of Interfacial Water Over Tens of Molecular Layers
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how far solid surfaces influence the structure of adjacent water remains a central challenge in interfacial science. Here, we demonstrate that nanoscale surface roughness can induce long‐range ordering of interfacial water extending over tens of molecular layers under ambient conditions. abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom photocatalysts offer a structurally defined platform for merging homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, yet their application in selective C─H functionalisation remains limited. In this study, we report a manganese‐based single‐atom photocatalyst (Mn@f‐g‐C 3 N 4 ) comprising atomically dispersed Mn─N x sites anchored on an arylamino‐functionalised graphitic carbon nitride support. abstract: Abstract Microalgal treatment can couple pharmaceutical attenuation with organic-matter and nutrient removal, but the operating windows for saline and freshwater species remain insufficiently defined. This laboratory study combined a central composite design, dual-detector confirmation of cortisone acetate (CA) removal, biomass mass balance, and artificial neural network (ANN) modelling and genetic algorithm (GA) optimisation to evaluate Tetraselmis chui ( T. chui ) and Scenedesmus obtusus ( S. obtusus ) under salinity, pH, and treatment-time variation. title: Geographic isolation promoted species divergence of two closely related Cycas species in distinct river basins
abstract: PREMISE: Understanding the process of species divergence and the mechanisms that drive genetic differentiation among closely related species is essential for explaining the origins of plant biodiversity. Geographic isolation and niche differentiation are key drivers of species divergence. Cycas chenii and C. guizhouensis are morphologically similar sister species from different river basins in Southwest China. title: Immersion-based morpholino delivery into Atlantic salmon eggs using a nona-arginine carrier
abstract: Delivering exogenous compounds into fish eggs is a powerful tool for early stage manipulation. However, efficient delivery is constrained by the chorion barrier, which restricts the passive entry of macromolecules and therefore limits non-invasive manipulation. Here, we demonstrate that bath immersion enables efficient delivery of fluorescently labeled morpholino oligomers (MOs) into Atlantic salmon eggs when conjugated to the guanidinium rich cell-penetrating peptide nona-arginine. title: Seismicity Parameters of the Westernmost Part of the North Anatolian Fault Zone (NAFZ)
abstract: This study characterizes seismicity and stress regime in the westernmost part of the North Anatolian Fault Zone (NAFZ), focusing on the Saros segment, where dextral strike-slip deformation transitions into the transtensional northern Aegean domain. Unlike previous regional studies that combine Marmara and broader Aegean datasets or focus on individual rupture sequences, this study isolates a coordinate-bounded transition window to quantify the intrinsic seismic behavior of the terminal NAFZ–North Aegean Trough (NAT) linkage zone within a completeness-controlled framework. abstract: Abstract Water plays a critical role in Earth's mantle dynamics and evolution, yet lower‐mantle storage mechanisms remain debated. δ‐AlOOH and SiO 2 phases have been independently proposed as high‐pressure water hosts. abstract: This paper examines the innovative financing mechanisms that are driving the shift toward a circular economy in agriculture, drawing on recent international research and documented practice. The analysis synthesizes findings from the European Environment Agency (EEA), the United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) and the Global Alliance on Circular Economy and Resource Efficiency (GACERE), together with peer-reviewed studies published in international journals. title: Postbiotic sequestration of micro- and nanoplastics: in vitro intestinal epithelial protection and proof of concept in the human mouth
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are ubiquitous dietary contaminants, yet practical strategies to reduce gastrointestinal exposure remain limited. title: Spent Artemisia arborescens as a Biowaste Filler for Melt‐Processed PBSA Biocomposites With Enhanced Disintegration and Aerobic Biodegradation
abstract: ABSTRACT Artemisia arborescens is a Mediterranean shrub widely used for essential oil production, generating significant amounts of spent biomass after extraction. This spent biomass, often underutilized, represents a valuable resource for sustainable biocomposites. This study focuses on the development of biocomposites using a biobased poly(butylene succinate‐ co ‐butylene adipate) (PBSA) as the matrix and spent Artemisia arborescens (AA) as a filler. title: After All, Size Does Matter: Size and Trachemys Scripta Reproduction Traits at the Western Limit of Its European Distribution
abstract: In invasive species, reproductive success may determine invasion outcomes and influence the choice of appropriate control and eradication. Trachemys scripta (Schoepff, 1792) is one of the world's most widespread invasive turtle species. Although some previous studies have focused on T. scripta reproduction, both in native and in non-native ranges, only one study has been carried out in Portugal, which reported clutch sizes. title: Two new species of Afrithelphusa Bott, 1969, from Sierra Leone, West Africa (Brachyura: Deckeniidae: Deckeniinae)
abstract: This work focuses on two new species of freshwater crabs from Sierra Leone, West Africa: Afrithelphusa outamba sp. nov., and A. mano sp. nov. These taxa are described based on newly collected material. Diagnoses, illustrations, and a distribution map are provided, and their conservation status is discussed. title: Arsenate reduction coupled to anaerobic oxidation of methane by members of the Methanoperedenaceae
abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic 'Candidatus Methanoperedenaceae' play a key role in mitigating methane emissions from freshwater sediments. Members of the family are metabolically versatile, with species coupling anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) to the reduction of nitrate, metal oxides and/or humic compounds. Metagenomic analyses have indicated further uncharacterised metabolic diversity, including the potential for AOM coupled to arsenate reduction (As-AOM). title: The MHC class II transactivator CIITA induction as a potential new tool to develop anti-tumor vaccines and predict the efficacy of immunotherapy
abstract: The MHC class II transactivator (CIITA) is the master regulator of MHC class II (MHC-II) genes expression. In fact, it promotes both constitutive and interferon gamma-inducible expression of all MHC-II genes and thus regulates the optimal activation of adaptive immunity, which depends on the proper activation of CD4 + T helper cells. title: A comprehensive study on ferredoxin isoforms in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
abstract: Ferredoxins are central to cellular metabolism by mediating electron flow in energy conversion reactions. The focus of this study was to systematically examine twelve ferredoxin and ferredoxin-like proteins from Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 to identify their properties, activities, and functions in electron transfer. Using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, we detected cluster types consistent with major ferredoxin families including plant-type [2Fe-2S], adrenodoxin, thioredoxin, and bacterial-type [4Fe-4S] ferredoxins.
