title: Characterisation of brown-rot decay in the historic Lejonström bridge using X-ray tomography and molecular identification of associated fungi
abstract: Abstract The deterioration of wooden heritage structures requires regular monitoring, particularly when pressure-impregnated Scots pine is exposed to moisture and biological degradation. This study assessed fungal degradation of structural elements of the Lejonström bridge in Skellefteå, Sweden’s oldest wooden bridge and a culturally significant monument. Non-destructive X-ray tomography identified internal decay based on reduced density, brown-rot characteristics, and microbial colonisation. Institute of Food Biotechnology and Genomics

title: Analysis of historical water availability and projected surface water trends for decision-making: the case of Mexico
abstract: Freshwater is a vital resource whose availability, quality, and accessibility have been affected by variability and climate change, population growth, land-use change, social inequality, and socio-environmental conflicts. In the face of these challenges, intersectoral collaboration is required to plan, implement, and monitor actions that ensure water security in Mexico. The aim of this study was to analyze historical water availability and projected surface water trends in Mexico, based on official concession data, hydrological and climate models, as well as spatially explicit maps to support

title: DESIGN OF BRAIN EMOTIONAL LEARNING BASED ON CEREBELLAR ARCHITECTURE FOR INVERTED PENDULUM CONTROL
abstract: A bio-inspired controller called Brain Emotional Learning (BEL) was developed through research on the limbic system of the mammalian brain. Based on BEL structure design of intelligent and cognitive controllers with different tuning algorithms has attracted more attention. In contrast to the traditional formulation of BEL, the paper analyzes and designs certain functions used in Brain Emotional Learning to improve the system's performance. title: Engineering a compact CgCas12n platform for efficient genome and base editing in mammalian cells
abstract: Type V CRISPR-Cas12 systems evolved from transposon-encoded TnpB proteins, with type V-U4 nucleases (Cas12n) as evolutionary intermediates linking TnpB to larger type V effectors. Despite their compact size, most Cas12n orthologs, including Corynebacterium glutamicum Cas12n (CgCas12n), exhibit low genome-editing activity in mammalian cells. Here, we engineered CgCas12n using an arginine enrichment strategy, generating a variant with approximately 60-fold enhanced editing efficiency. title: Temporal evolution and decline of seismicity associated with cyclic operations at the Serajeh underground gas storage, Iran
abstract: Abstract Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. We investigate seismicity around the Serajeh UGS in central Iran by combining 29,781 deep-learning-based single-station earthquake detections, multi-station relocation, centroid moment tensor inversion, and operational records. The relocated hypocentres form a compact cluster near the Serajeh structure, primarily at depths of 3–8 km, overlapping with and extending below the 2.4
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: The effect of lignocellulosic biomass pretreatment by-products on the fermentation activity of Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast, measured using indices of toxic stress
abstract: The use of lignocellulosic biomass as a renewable raw material for the production of cellulosic ethanol requires pretreatment. Unfortunately, this process can generate numerous by-products that have a toxic effect on yeasts. Understanding the response of yeast is crucial if measures are to be developed that allow adaptation under multifactorial stress conditions. The study objective was to determine the effect that inhibitors in the form of by-products of lignocellulose pretreatment have on yeast fermentation activity. The yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae was fermented in liquid media containing

title: Further records of Lycodon irwini Naveen, Mirza, Choure & Chandramouli, 2025 (Squamata, Colubridae) from Great Nicobar, India
abstract: We report additional records of the recently described, supposedly rare species of wolf snake, Lycodon irwini Naveen et al., 2025, known only from Great Nicobar Island, India. We report 14 sightings of this species from opportunistic encounters recorded during sporadic surveys over seven months. This highlights the limited extent of previous surveys in this region and suggests that this species is not as rare as previously assumed. title: Exploring male and female mate preferences using genetic algorithms and digital phenotypes
abstract: Abstract During mate choice, both males and females can exhibit choosiness when selecting a partner. The expression and measurement of preferences is typically constrained by the traits presented during mate-choice trials, which generally represent a subset of the phenotypic trait space and thus may not capture the full range of potential preferences. Here, we present a proof of concept for a novel method building on the commonly used experimental protocol of screen-based stimuli for examining mate preferences. title: Cooperative Regulation of Defect‐Mediated Molecular Recognition With Single‐Walled Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Defects are increasingly recognized as powerful modulators of the chemistry and photophysics of fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), enabling tunable optical responses toward exogenously introduced analytes. However, defect-mediated interactions arise not solely from defects, but from the interplay among multiple interconnected system variables, including defect type and density, analyte identity and size, corona composition and conformation, SWCNT chirality, and the surrounding environment. title: Effects of Aeration on Growth and Production of Carps in Chitwan, Nepal
abstract: An experiment was conducted to assess effects of aeration on water quality and yield of carps at farmer‘s pond of Kathar, Chitwan, Nepal for 225 days from 25 May 2018 to 10 January 2019. Experiment included three treatments: T1 - No aeration (control), T2 - 4 hours aeration (4:00 - 8:00 am) and T3 - 6 hours aeration (4:00 - 10:00 am) with four replications of each. Ponds were stocked with fingerlings of rohu (Labeo rohita), mrigal (Cirrhinus mrigala), common carp (Cyprinus carpio), silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix), bighead carp (Aristichthys nobilis) and grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon i
journal: Nepalese Journal of Aquaculture and Fisheries

title: Structural and Mechanistic Basis of Dual Substrate Promiscuity in the Acyltransferase AntB Enables Late‐Stage Diversification of Natural Products
abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic regioselective acylation is a powerful strategy for diversifying natural products and optimizing their pharmacological properties. Compared with plant acyltransferases (ATs), bacterial tailoring ATs remain poorly understood. AntB from the antimycin pathway was previously reported to possess acyl‐donor promiscuity toward limited acyl‐CoA thioesters, yet its acyl‐acceptor promiscuity, structural basis, and catalytic mechanism had not been elucidated. title: Nesting Success of the Commodore Park Great Blue Heron Colony, 2014–2023
abstract: Long-term and consistent data are necessary to understand phenomena such as the timing and success of reproduction. A Pacific Great Blue Heron (Ardea herodias fannini) colony in Seattle, Washington, was studied from 2014 to 2023. Community scientists observed the usage of 120 nest locations repeatedly throughout each nesting season. Between 38 and 76 nests were active in any year. Incubation began in the colony between March 7 and 21, depending on the year (mean = March 15). The start of incubation in individual nests differed strongly within years, often by multiple months. title: Mapping the Cryptococcus neoformans Hsp90 genetic interaction network identifies Ypk1 and Pkh202 as client proteins of the molecular chaperone
abstract: Hsp90 is a conserved molecular chaperone that orchestrates fungal stress responses by stabilizing proteins important for antifungal susceptibility and virulence. While targeting fungal-specific components within Hsp90 networks offers an attractive therapeutic strategy, the Hsp90 interaction network remains enigmatic in Cryptococcus neoformans , a leading cause of fatal meningitis in immunocompromised individuals. institutions: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center

title: Cold atmospheric plasma decontamination of indoor mold
abstract: Abstract Indoor molds damage building materials and can compromise occupant health. Correction of the moisture source and physical removal of contaminated material remain central to remediation, but inactivation of residual viable growth may be useful as an adjunct where heat or liquid biocides are unsuitable. Here we combine controlled building-material experiments with a nonlinear logistic inactivation model to test whether fungal response to cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) is governed by threshold behavior at the time of treatment. title: De los residuos a oportunidades: JTBD y SCAMPER para el emprendimiento sostenible universitario
abstract: El presente artículo tiene como objetivo describir y comunicar los cambios observados en las competencias emprendedoras sostenibles de estudiantes universitarios después de participar en un programa que integró Jobs to Be Done (JTBD), SCAMPER y el aprovechamiento de residuos valorizables para fortalecer sus capacidades emprendedoras sostenibles. title: Cultivating diversity: is the functional diversity of nursery stocks sufficient for the establishment of functionally diverse restored woodlands?
abstract: Abstract Introduction Ecological restoration projects often rely on nurseries (NU) to provide plants to restore ecological communities. However, the range of species available in NU may not represent the range of ecological function found in species in reference (natural) communities. Objectives We tested for differences in species and functional representation between national parks (NP; reference communities) and NU used to supply plants for restoration projects. title: First U-Pb detrital zircon ages from the Los Morteritos Unit (El Gigante Metamorphic Complex), Sierras Pampeanas, Argentina: new insights into the early Paleozoic evolution of SW Gondwana
abstract: The El Gigante Metamorphic Complex, in the homonymous range (Sierras Pampeanas, Argentina), consists of three lithostratigraphic units that, from bottom to top, are: Quebrada Grande (Mesoproterozoic protoliths), Loma Cortada (Ediacaran-early Cambrian sedimentary protoliths), and Los Morteritos (middle to late Cambrian protoliths), all reworked by the Famatinian orogeny. This study reports the first U–Pb detrital zircon data from a quartz–micaceous schist of the Los Morteritos Unit, which shows two main Mesoproterozoic peaks (~1350 and ~1070 Ma) and minor Cambrian ages. title: Prevalence and associated factors of traditional eyelash epilation among patients with trachomatous trichiasis in South Ethiopia
abstract: Trachoma remains the leading infectious cause of blindness globally, with Ethiopia bearing the highest disease burden. Trachomatous trichiasis (TT), the advanced stage of trachoma, requires surgical correction to prevent irreversible blindness. However, many affected patients rely on traditional eyelash epilation as an alternative to surgery. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of traditional eyelash epilation and identify factors associated with its practice among TT patients in South Ethiopia. title: Estimating home range size under spatial constraints: a comparative approach using the semi-aquatic European mink (Mustela lutreola)
abstract: Accurate home range knowledge is essential for conserving species that are highly constrained by spatial features. The critically endangered European mink ( Mustela lutreola ) is a wetland specialist whose movements are constrained along rivers or in wetlands. In dendritic landscapes, conventional home range estimators such as Minimum Convex Polygons tend to include unsuitable areas in estimated home ranges. title: Enhancing therapeutic efficacy through Kaempferol and docetaxel combination: integrative binding and molecular dynamics study targeting Bcl-2 protein in breast cancer
abstract: Bcl-2 inhibits apoptosis by sequestering pro-apoptotic proteins, thereby preventing mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization. Disruption of this interaction represents a promising strategy for restoring apoptosis signaling in cancer cells. This study investigated the binding affinity, conformational effects, and pharmacokinetic properties of docetaxel (DTX) and kaempferol (KAE) against Bcl-2. title: Deciphering the Evolutionary Dynamics: A Phylogenetic Analysis of Contemporary Tacheng Tick Virus Strains
abstract: Objectives This study aims to present the first molecular evidence of Tacheng tick virus-1 (TcTV-1) in Hyalomma aegyptium ticks collected from Turkey. It also seeks to characterise the genetic features of the Turkish TcTV-1 strain and identify its closest evolutionary relationship among known global TcTV-1 strains. title: Direct Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral β‐Hydroxy‐α‐Amino Amides via PLP ‐Inspired Biomimetic Aldol Reaction
abstract: Chiral β-hydroxy-α-amino amides represent important structural motifs ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules. Current synthetic approaches typically rely on multistep conversion from the corresponding β-hydroxy-α-amino acids, resulting in poor step-economy and potential α-racemization during amidation. However, direct asymmetric synthesis of these compounds via aldol reactions remains highly challenging because of the low reactivity of glycinamides and the instability of the corresponding aldol products. title: Distribution and Seasonal Variation of Snail Vector of Medical and Veterinary Importance in Communities Around Challawa Dam, Karaye Local Government Area, Kano State
abstract: Snail are generally aquatic upon found in almost all fresh water bodies ranging from rivers, lakes, streams, irrigation channels, lakes, streams, Ponds and marshes attached to the water plants. The epidemiology of schistosomiasis involves a mollucs (snail) as an intermediate host, various species of fresh water snails are known to act as intermediate host of schistosomiasis. title: Complete Pathway Refactoring and Combinatorial Biosynthesis of Anthracyclines for Modulation of Histone Eviction and DNA Damage Bioactivities
abstract: Anthracyclines including doxorubicin are cornerstone chemotherapeutic agents with high cytotoxic potency, but their use in cancer treatment is limited by irreversible dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. Recent investigations indicate that cardiotoxicity-free anthracyclines may be achieved through uncoupling DNA damage from chromatin damage. However, semi-synthetic derivatization is complicated by anthracycline structural complexity. title: Simulated visual attention modelling in digital tourism interfaces: an integrative approach to destination communication
abstract: This paper introduces a simulation-based methodological and conceptual study addressing a critical gap in tourism research: the fragmented treatment of spatial, sequential and temporal dimensions of visual attention. It proposes the Simulated Visual Attention Integrative (SVAI) Model, combining predicted saliency heatmaps, simulated scan paths and saccadic timing within a unified analytical framework. title: UAV-based RGB imagery for assessing vegetation status in a Mediterranean area affected by Xylella fastidiosa
abstract: Vegetation monitoring in areas affected by plant pathogens is essential for assessing the vulnerability of plant communities and supporting the management of infected territories. Although field surveys remain the cornerstone of vegetation monitoring, RGB UAV technology is increasingly proving its value at local and regional scales for mapping plant communities and detecting diagnostic species of Annex I habitats. title: Carbohydrate‐binding modules: powerful tools in the research and development of carbohydrates – a review
abstract: Carbohydrate-binding modules (CBMs) are independent domains generally appended in carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) with carbohydrate-binding functions. The primary roles of CBMs in CAZymes include targeting, proximity, disruption, and adhesion effects. Due to their capacity to recognize and bind to specific carbohydrate structures, CBMs have emerged as valuable tools with wide applications, greatly facilitating the research and development of carbohydrates. title: The Reactivity of Haloalkanes on Superatomic Niobium Clusters: Demethylation versus Dehydrogenation
abstract: The catalytic cleavage of C−H and C−X (X = Cl, Br, I) bonds in alkanes and their halides over transition metals has drawn considerable attention due to the broad applicability in synthesizing commodity and fine chemicals. However, the dynamic reaction mechanisms of halomethanes on nanometals are still not fully understood. title: Assessing Smoke Particle Contamination on Firefighter Personal Protective Equipment using Generative AI and Edge Detection Models
abstract: Firefighters at a wildland-oilfield interface (WOI) encounter complex smoke particle mixtures from biomass and hydrocarbons. These particulates settle onto Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) surfaces, remaining long after fire suppression activities. These attached smoke particles create a severe occupational hazard through secondary exposure during movement and the donning/doffing of contaminated gear. title: Phenotypic characterization of the traditional cashew (Anacardium occidentale L.) populations from Nachingwea and Newala districts, Tanzania
abstract: This study was conducted to assess phenotypic variation in traditional cashew populations from Nachingwea and Newala districts in Tanzania. A total of 120 traditional cashew trees were sampled from the two districts, with 60 samples from each study site. Morphological descriptors for cashew developed by the International Board for Plant and Genetic Resources (IBPGR) in 1986 were used for the phenotypic characterization of traditional cashew populations. title: Cyanobacteria: A sustainable platform for high-value biopharmaceutical protein production
abstract: Biopharmaceutical (therapeutic) proteins are biologically-derived drugs used to treat a variety of diseases. Producing these proteins naturally from mammalian cells presents significant challenges. As a result, non-native hosts, including plants, algae, yeast, and bacteria, have been employed to produce these proteins; however, the complex genetic reconstruction process, high cultivation costs, contamination risks, and regulatory hurdles have hampered commercial success. title: Characterising runoff processes for Australia: insights from a parsimonious rainfall-runoff event identification method
abstract: Rainfall-runoff events are widely used in hydrological applications, from flood estimation and flood forecasting, to understanding catchment responses in a climate/anthropogenic affected world. The majority of methods used to identify rainfall-runoff events are statistical in nature, relying on subjective, user-defined “rules” (i.e., parameters) that define a rainfall-runoff event. Since no ground-truth information is available to confirm the exact beginning and end of rainfall-runoff events, there is noticeable inconsistency (i.e. uncertainty) within the results. title: Complexation strength between organic carbon and transition metal ions dominates the photochemical conversion of SO 2 to sulfates
abstract: The photooxidation of SO 2 on organic carbon (OC) is a critical pathway for sulfate formation, yet the role of interactions between OC and transition metal ions (TMIs) in this process remains scarcely understood. We systematically investigated potential influences of TMIs (Fe 3+ , Cu 2+ and Mn 2+ ) on the conversion of SO 2 to sulfates on OC from coal combustion under irradiation. title: Participación de las MIPYMES en la contratación pública ecuatoriana y resultados económicos durante 2023 a 2024
abstract: Introducción: La contratación pública puede ampliar el acceso de las micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MIPYMES) a mercados institucionales, aunque su aprovechamiento depende de capacidades administrativas, liquidez y condiciones de competencia. El objetivo fue analizar su participación y los resultados económicos asociados en Ecuador durante 2023-2024. Metodología: Se desarrolló un estudio mixto, descriptivo-analítico y no experimental. journal: Sage Sphere of Technology Sciences Discoveries And Society

title: Elemental profiling of zebrafish (Danio rerio) across developmental stages using ion beam analytical techniques
abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of zebrafish as a biological model, comprehensive baseline elemental data across its developmental stages remain limited. In this work, ion beam analytical techniques were employed to establish the elemental composition of zebrafish larvae and adults under controlled vivarium conditions. The combined use of these techniques enables quantitative elemental analysis and spatially resolved elemental mapping of small biological samples within the same analytical framework, providing an integrated elemental baseline across zebrafish development. title: Assessing biogenic carbon dioxide resource for synthetic e-fuel production to decarbonise shipping
abstract: A high-level assessment of the production potential and costs of three synthetic e-fuels, methane, methanol and Fischer–Tropsch diesel, derived from renewable hydrogen and biogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) was conducted for maritime transport in the EU and Ireland for 2050. Biogenic CO 2 sources included by-products from biomethane production and ethanol fermentation (priced at €30/tonne), and emissions from biomass combustion (€80/tonne). title: Hippobosca equina as an emerging threat in northern temperate zones: Species distribution modelling under climate change
abstract: Climate change poses significant threats to arthropod vectors of veterinary importance. Hippobosca equina, the forest fly, is an obligate ectoparasite of ungulates with demonstrated capacity for pathogen transmission. We employed maximum entropy modelling to predict current and future global distribution patterns of H. equina under climate change scenarios. Using 1195 occurrence records and five bioclimatic variables, we generated models for present conditions and future projections (2050s and 2070s) under SSP 3-7.0 and SSP 5-8.5 scenarios. title: Dry farming for resilience: productivity and physiological drivers of organic common bean production
abstract: Abstract Water scarce agricultural regions are increasingly challenged to find practices and systems that reduce water use. One such approach is dry farming: the cultivation of drought-adapted crop varieties without irrigation but relying on residual soil moisture following seedling establishment. abstract: Se presenta una metodología de regionalización ecohidrológica basada en SIG para definir el espaciamiento diferenciado de zanjas de infiltración en doce Unidades Ecohidrológicas Homogéneas (UEH) de la cuenca endorreica de Lagunas de Tajzara, Tarija, Bolivia. title: Infra-Net: a robust parallel decision-making network for discriminating natural hazards and anthropogenic infrasound events via multi-view feature learning
abstract: The accurate classification of infrasound signals is a cornerstone of global geophysical monitoring, essential for both natural hazard early warning systems (e.g., volcanic eruptions, debris flows, and earthquakes) and the verification of the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty. However, the development of reliable automated systems is hindered by the inherent scarcity of representative event data, particularly for rare extreme events, as well as the presence of complex, non-stationary background interferences. title: Gravitational torque drives multidecadal variations in length of day
abstract: Multidecadal fluctuations in Earth’s length of day are shown to be driven by gravitational torque and resisted by electromagnetic and topographic forces, improving our understanding of the material properties and dynamics of Earth’s deep interior.

title: Wetlands birds in the transboundary floodplains of north-western Bangladesh and their conservation urgency
abstract: In perspective of the conservation of biodiversity in Bangladesh, transboundary river floodplains are ecologically important but those are beyond protected landscapes particularly in the western part of Bangladesh. The present study was conducted on bird community structure, habitat associations, seasonal dynamics, and conservation issues during July 2020 to June 2022 using direct field observations methods at urban, rural and beel ecosystems of the Chapainawabganj district- a transboundary floodplain of northwestern Bangladesh. title: Genetic diversity and conservation of a rare Miconia species (Melastomataceae) from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
abstract: Biodiversity is undergoing an unprecedented global decline, and genetic diversity plays a fundamental role in ensuring species persistence. Miconia ulei, an endemic species from the eastern Atlantic Forest in Santa Catarina, southern Brazil, is rare and has few known populations. We investigated genetic diversity and population structure using microsatellite markers and assessed its conservation status following IUCN guidelines and by incorporating genetic parameters in the evaluation. title: When psychedelic discourse meets local narrative: Selective uptake of psychedelic meanings surrounding mad honey in Nepal
abstract: AIMS: 'Mad honey' is produced when bees collect nectar from Rhododendron species containing grayanotoxins, naturally occurring diterpenoid toxins that can produce dose-dependent intoxication. It has long been embedded in Nepalese medicinal and ritual practices but has recently become part of global psychedelic discourse. This study examined how globally circulating discourse and local narrative practices interact in shaping meanings of intoxication, using mad honey as a case. title: Multi-elemental plagioclase-melt modeling unravels (dis)equilibrium crystal growth during dynamic magmatic processes
abstract: Assessing magma storage conditions relies critically on crystal-melt equilibrium models. However, natural rocks are replete with disequilibrium features that testify to open-system processes and episodic crystal growth. Interface kinetics at the crystal-melt boundary lag behind changes of physicochemical conditions determined by magma dynamics. title: The Evolution and Assessment of Intelligence Architectures in Nigerian Security: A Historical Analysis
abstract: This paper has discussed the development and evaluation of intelligence structures in Nigeria, and how these structures are effective in dealing with the modern internal security issues. The study follows the historical evolution of intelligence systems in Nigeria, which started with indigenous security establishments in the pre-colonial period and colonial surveillance systems, through the centralization of the systems in the post-independent era, expansions of the systems in the military era, and the reform in the democratic era. title: Bio-ecology of the harmful leafhopper Zyginidia sohrab Zachvatkin, 1947 (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) in maize fields of the Central Anatolia Region
abstract: Leafhoppers damage plants by piercing and sucking leaf tissues. Among the leafhopper species occurring in Central Anatolia, Zyginidia sohrab (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) is the most widespread and abundant species. This study was conducted under natural field conditions during the 2021 and 2022 growing seasons to investigate the bioecology of Z. sohrab in maize production areas. Z. sohrab overwinters as an adult and begins to emerge from overwintering sites in the last week of April as temperatures increase. title: Native-range origin predicts genomic contribution in an experimental Mimulus guttatus invasion
abstract: Biological invasions and range expansions act as natural experiments for understanding evolutionary processes at and beyond a species' range margin. However, unlike manipulative experiments, invasions and range expansions are less genetically tractable and often involve genotypes of uncertain origin that are subject to complex evolutionary pressures. Here, we replay the earliest stages of the colonisation of the widespread North American plant species Mimulus guttatus (synonym Erythranthe guttata) in the United Kingdom. title: Antimicrobial resistance in the monotreme microbiome
abstract: Context Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global health crisis requiring a One Health approach that recognises the interconnectedness of people, animals and the environment. Since wide adoption of the One Health framework, wildlife species have been identified as important potential reservoirs and vectors of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. title: Disrupting antimicrobial resistance in food systems from a One Health perspective: a complex systems analysis in Canada, Senegal and the Netherlands
abstract: BACKGROUND: Food systems are a key contributor to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Given the multi-sectoral nature of AMR, a One Health perspective has been advocated. Recent research situates AMR as an emerging property of a complex system, a perspective which can help identify root drivers of AMR and theorise the impacts of proposed solutions. This study aims to combine systems modelling and a One Health perspective to identify system-level dynamics and priority actions for addressing AMR in food systems. title: Unpacking Roman trade: a quantitative study of amphora circulation in the Western provinces
abstract: Ceramic amphorae provide clues to the movement of foodstuffs within the Roman Empire and can therefore act as a useful proxy for economic productivity. Here, the authors present the results of a large-scale quantitative analysis of amphora frequency data from 254 excavations conducted across the Western Roman provinces. By examining the distribution of 20 of the most common amphora types, which primarily served as olive-oil, garum and wine containers, they assess economic trends and temporal shifts in supply and consumption previously identified through other economic proxies, emphasising the

title: Biogeographic origins of the disjunct distribution of the chacoan Neotropical frog Pleurodema guayapae
abstract: Disjunct distributions, in which populations of a putative species are separated by large distances, represent an important, albeit poorly understood pattern in biogeography. Detailed study of these populations often reveals that they actually comprise more than one species resulting from prolonged restricted gene flow. The leptodactylid chacoan frog Pleurodema guayapae exhibits a striking disjunct distribution. Populations are well known to occur in north-central Argentina, whereas records from southern Bolivia are separated by ca. 820 km gap lacking confirmed records despite extensive survey
institutions: Museo de Historia Natural Noel Kempff Mercado

title: Role of yeast MIG1 gene in glycolysis, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and glycogen and trehalose biosynthesis in response to DNA damage
abstract: Background: In eukaryotic cells, under certain stress conditions, the diversion of carbohydrate flux, either downstream toward tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle or upstream toward the hexosamine biosynthesis and pentose phosphate pathways, is governed by the activation of key regulatory genes and glycolytic enzymes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the transcription factor Mig1 (encoded by the MIG1 gene) regulates respiration, glucose repression, and gluconeogenesis. title: A revised early Jurassic to Albian chronology for dinosaur evolution in tropical Asia
abstract: The Mesozoic deposits of the Khorat Plateau in Thailand have yielded a rich but chronologically unclear record of dinosaur evolution. Here, we use detrital zircon U-Pb dating to establish precise ages for these deposits. The Nam Phong Formation, once thought to include some of the oldest sauropodomorphs, is now dated to the Pliensbachian stage of the Early Jurassic (ca. 190 Ma), at least 20 million years younger than previously assumed. title: Habitat and landscape outweigh stand age as drivers of species composition in managed temperate forests dominated by Quercus robur L. and Quercus petraea (Matt.) Liebl
abstract: Abstract Key Message Managed oak stands with Quercus robur L. and Quercus petraea (Matt.) Liebl. supported a range of natural forest communities differing in species composition despite regular forest management. Habitat was the most influential driver shaping species composition, followed closely by landscape, whereas stand age showed a relatively small contribution. Soil fertility and the proportions of oak stands and deciduous stands in the research plot surroundings were the strongest independent determinants of species composition. title: Decarbonizing under water stress: Water-energy-land nexus insights from Chile's 2050 carbon neutrality pathway
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change is exacerbating water scarcity in Mediterranean climate regions, such as Central Chile, which already has a low annual precipitation rate, increasing the likelihood of a potentially permanent “mega-drought”. While carbon-neutrality policies often combine energy- and land-sector measures, their specific implications for water-energy-land interactions in Chile remain insufficiently explored. title: Widespread endocrine-disrupting pollutant alters male courtship behavior in a livebearing fish
abstract: Abstract Sexual selection is a potent evolutionary force shaping both pre-copulatory courtship behavior and post-copulatory sperm traits, with male reproductive effort often adjusted to social and mating context. Endocrine-disrupting contaminants are predicted to alter how males allocate reproductive effort, yet their behavioral effects across different mating contexts remain poorly understood. abstract: A systematic combinatorial study of anodic oxidation on Ti-Yb alloys was conducted along a compositional range of 7–27 at.% Yb. For this purpose, a thin-film library was produced by co-sputtering in a self-developed vacuum system. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy were employed to investigate the compositional spread and surface structure of the thin film alloys. This study aims to design an Arduino Uno-based pH and turbidity meter and evaluate its performance through multi-point calibration and real water sample testing. The system integrates an E-201C pH sensor, a turbidity sensor, a 16×2 LCD, an SD card module, and a buzzer. title: Human-made material use in urban European Blackbird nests varies with breeding characteristics and female age
abstract: Abstract Human activity has profoundly altered the environment, with anthropogenic material pollution posing serious threats to wildlife. In birds, the incorporation of human-made materials into nests may have harmful effects, such as reducing survival and reproductive success, or beneficial effects, including parasite deterrence or social signalling. We investigated the use of human-made materials in the nests of an urban population of European Blackbirds ( Turdus merula ). We found that the use of human-made materials was common. title: Photovoltaic Panels on Green Roofs: Optical, Thermal and Electrical Contributions in a Multi-Energy Model
abstract: As the transition to renewable energy accelerates, optimizing photovoltaic (PV) systems becomes essential by considering their interactions with physical and climatic environments. Additionally, urban architecture has evolved in recent decades with the advent of buildings featuring flat and green roofs. This research examines the integration of PV panels on green roofs through a coupled optical–thermal–electrical (multi-energy) model and an experimental validation under real operating conditions. title: Repurposed lives: shipping containers as contested sites of urban citizenship in Accra
abstract: This study investigates how shipping containers are repurposed as architecture in Accra, Ghana. The study reveals the spatial factors shaping the emergence of these adaptive structures. Rather than being randomly situated, containers cluster in strategic locations enabling access to livelihoods while also avoiding eviction threats. Their positioning highlights contradictions between top-down urban planning favouring elite interests and the needs of marginalised residents. title: Polish Consumer Preferences and Awareness about Products Containing Caffeine
abstract: Objective: The main objective of this article was the recognition of food choices, consumption of products containing caffeine and purchasing habits regarding products containing caffeine on the Polish market. The article characterises Polish consumers’ preferences toward caffeine-containing beverages (CCBs) such as coffee, tea, yerba mate and energy drinks. abstract: Nitrate ( $${{\rm{NO}}}_{3}^{-}$$ ) is a groundwater pollutant that is challenging to remediate. title: The plasma protease inhibitor ITIH4 forms oligomeric complexes and senses broader proteolytic activity
abstract: In self-perpetuating proteolytic cascades within the body, tight regulation by an excess of inhibitors is essential to maintain homoeostasis. The plasma protein inter-α-trypsin inhibitor heavy chain 4 (ITIH4) inhibits extracellular proteolytic pathways, including the contact system and the complement cascade, by a mechanism requiring cleavage of ITIH4 but without direct binding to the active site of the cleaving protease. title: Investigation of slurry erosion behaviour of additively manufactured polylactic acid
abstract: This study investigates the slurry erosion behaviour of additively manufactured polylactic acid (AM-PLA) under controlled slurry conditions. Both printing parameters and slurry erosion test conditions were varied to explore their combined effect. Test samples were printed with different infill densities (50–100%) and raster orientations (X, Y and diagonal). Slurry erosion tests were performed at three slurry velocities (20, 25 and 30 m/s) and a wide range of impingement angles (15°–90°). title: Magmatic U-Pb zircon ages west of the Domeyko Fault System, Collahuasi District (Chile): implications for its potential westward continuity
abstract: This study presents new high-precision U-Pb zircon age data to document previously unrecognized igneous bodies in a poorly explored sector in the western part of the Collahuasi District, northern Chile. By integrating these new geochronological constraints with detailed geological mapping, petrography, and mineralogical observations, the temporal and spatial patterns of magmatism west of the Domeyko Fault System, the most relevant tectonic structure in the zone, are refined. title: Ranking microbial risk of self-supplied groundwater in urban Indonesia
abstract: In Indonesia, 61% of urban households use self-supplied groundwater, with 24% relying on it as a primary drinking water source. Many self-supplied sources contain faecal contamination, posing health risks. Identifying locations with elevated contamination risk can help target piped-water investments and interim safety measures, but collecting sufficient water quality data is costly. This study develops and validates a method to rank contamination risk across Indonesian cities using secondary data alone. title: Flame morphology and infrared radiation of non-premixed H2-NH3 laminar flames under O2-enrichment
abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) and hydrogen (H 2 ) are promising carbon-free fuels for decarbonizing energy-intensive industries; however, their adoption is hindered by altered flame morphology and low radiative intensity compared to hydrocarbons. This study experimentally investigates the impact of O 2 -enrichment on the morphology and infrared radiation heat flux of non-premixed H 2 -NH 3 flames. title: Multifunctional Hydroxyapatite: Recent Progress and Future Prospects in Biomedicine and Materials Science
abstract: One of the most studied biomaterials for biomedical applications is hydroxyapatite (HAp), a bioactive ceramic (Ca-P) with structural and compositional similarity to the mineral phase of human bones and teeth. HAp is investigated for various applications, such as bone regeneration, dental implants, tissue engineering, implant coatings, and controlled drug delivery systems, due to its excellent biocompatibility, osteoconductivity, and ability to accommodate ionic substitutions. title: Exploratory Pollen and Starch Analysis at the Cloudman Site, Michigan, Shows Evidence for Maize ( Zea mays ) Cultivation and Wild Rice ( Zizania palustris ) Gathering From Early Late‐Woodland to Historic Times
abstract: Here we report exploratory pollen (and spores) and starch analyses of soils/sediments from the Cloudman site, encompassing the Early Late‐Woodland ( ad 500/600−1000) to modern times. Pollen results reflect the regional Late Holocene vegetation dominated by the Pinaceae, with angiosperm forest trees less represented. Consistently moderate amounts of grass (Poaceae) pollen in many samples reflect the local alvar vegetation, and charcoal particles, Taraxacum ‐type pollen, and bracken ( Pteridium aquilinum ) spores also in many samples suggest vegetation fires set by people. abstract: Passive radiative cooling, which reflects solar irradiation while emitting heat through the atmospheric window, provides a sustainable solution for zero-energy thermal management. title: Temperate bacteriophages shape intraspecies competition during Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infection
abstract: Temperate bacteriophages are increasingly recognized as important drivers of microbial evolution. However, their role in mediating competition among members of the same species during infection remains poorly defined. Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa), an opportunistic pathogen associated with acute and chronic infections, frequently exhibits clonal dominance within infected individuals, suggesting the existence of effective mechanisms for excluding conspecific competitors. title: Olfactory context and memory across the adult lifespan: effects on mnemonic discrimination and olfactory function
abstract: Odor is a powerful contextual cue that can influence memory and is closely linked to brain regions involved in episodic memory, including the hippocampus. Age-related olfactory dysfunction is among the earliest behavioral changes associated with cognitive decline and may contribute to memory impairments in older adults. Hippocampal pattern separation, or the process of reducing interference among similar experiences, provides a sensitive measure of age-related memory decline, yet little is known about how olfactory context influences mnemonic discrimination. title: Experimental validation and dynamic optimization of H-25 gas turbine control for power stability during fuel transitions
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of mitigating transient power fluctuation during fuel switching in the H-25 gas turbine, particularly during the shift between gas and diesel fuel. Utilizing a dynamic simulation model developed in MATLAB-Simulink, the research identifies critical factors contributing to instability, primarily focusing on the timing of gas and diesel fuel valve operations. title: The status quo is imperiled: Acknowledging the issue of range‐shifting wildlife species
abstract: Rapid climate and land-use change are reshaping wildlife distributions, forcing managers to confront difficult decisions that challenge the traditional “status quo” approach. Range contractions of snow-dependent species such as the snowshoe hare (Lepus americanus; left photo) may increasingly require practitioners to recognize and plan for unavoidable loss in particular regions. abstract: Fe-based metallic glasses readily passivate in chloride-rich environments. However, the combined influence of boron and carbon on passive-film properties remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is a valuable fruit crop whose development is heavily controlled by cultivar selection and crop management strategies. The current study assessed the interactive impacts of biostimulants and mulching on the vegetative growth and biomass production of two cultivars of strawberry grown in the field. title: Enhanced alkene productivity in methanol-to-hydrocarbons conversion using a secondary catalyst component and hydrogen co-feeds
abstract: Abstract The methanol-to-hydrocarbons conversion over unidimensional 10-membered ring zeolites offers an attractive route to produce C 3 –C 5 alkenes, central building blocks for the production of sustainable aviation fuels. However, the application of such zeolites is limited by a rapid deactivation due to coke formation. title: Organic compounds as Photosystem II inhibitors and Cu2+ ligands: insights from primary screening
abstract: The search for novel organic compounds as PSII inhibitors and copper (Cu2+) ligands addresses key agricultural challenges. Three novel compounds were synthesized and evaluated for PSII photochemical activity inhibition and Cu2+-chelating ability. Primary screening was performed by recording effects on minimal and maximal chlorophyll fluorescence levels in isolated thylakoids. title: ParetoPick-R: An interactive tool for boosting the interpretability of multi-objective optimisation outputs
abstract: This study presents ParetoPick-R, an R Shiny application for post-processing multi-objective optimisation (MOO) results in environmental modelling. Although MOO is widely used in environmental management, its multi-dimensional and abstract outputs are often hard to interpret and apply directly. abstract: Introduction Abietinella , a dominant genus in the understory, only comprises two species Abietinella abietina (Hedw.) Fleisch. and Abietinella hystricosa (Mitt.) Broth. They can influence forest regeneration and development. However, research on the geographical distribution patterns of Abietinella is limited, which led to the absence of a method that can help explore how climate change affects the progress of species speciation and species diversity and their ecological functions for Abietinella . title: Atrial natriuretic peptide may inhibit motion sickness through reducing aldosterone-induced increase in endolymph volume of the inner ear
abstract: Previous studies have suggested that aldosterone is potentially involved in the development of motion sickness and that atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) may inhibit it. Therefore, the present study was conducted to investigate the inhibitory effects of ANP on aldosterone activity in motion sickness and on aldosterone-induced changes in endolymph volume in the inner ear. We found that rotatory stimulation induced an elevation in plasma aldosterone levels, intraperitoneal aldosterone injection caused motion sickness-like responses in both guinea pigs and mice, and ANP inhibited these responses.

title: Community Perceptions of Rubble-Filled Gabion Walls in Post-Conflict Reconstruction (Syria, Palestine): An Exploratory Social Study
abstract: In recent years, the massive urban destruction of Syrian and Palestinian cities created huge amounts of concrete rubble, which requires sustainable post-war reconstruction paradigms. Although reusing or recycling this concrete waste could be economically and ecologically sustainable, the psychosocial consequences associated with refitting war ruins are not fully examined. title: Integrating evolutionary signals and predicted protein structure reveals localized molecular divergence in Cereus lineages
abstract: Understanding how positive selection shapes molecular evolution at the protein level remains a major challenge, particularly in non-model species. Here, we integrated phylogenetic evidence from candidate genes evolving under lineage-specific positive selection with comparative structural and biophysical analyses to investigate patterns of molecular divergence in the Cereus fernambucensis-C. insularis clade, which occupies contrasting island and continental environments. title: Deciphering temporal antifungal dynamics of a rare actinomycete via integrated omics
abstract: ABSTRACT Fungal phytopathogens pose a persistent threat to global crop production, and widespread use of fungicides has driven resistance development and environmental concerns, necessitating sustainable alternatives. Actinomycetes produce diverse bioactive metabolites, yet natural product discovery has disproportionately focused on Streptomyces , leaving rare actinomycete taxa underexplored. title: Using soundscapes to examine the impacts of urbanisation on spatial and temporal patterns of avian acoustic activity along a riparian corridor
abstract: Abstract Background Biodiversity may correlate with acoustic indices, potentially offering insights into urban soundscapes both spatially (identifying areas with higher or lower biodiversity) and temporally (depicting daily patterns of biological activity, such as the avian dawn chorus). title: Isolation, characterization, and optimization of extracellular laccase-producing bacteria from dye-contaminated textile wastewater for dye decolonization
abstract: Textile industries are important in both the global economy and our daily lives. They are, however, simultaneously becoming one of the main sources of environmental pollution in the world. It needs a greater amount of water for wet textile operations such as dyeing, and as a result, produces significant dosages of wastewater. Textile wastewater is highly colorful and contains dyes that are highly harmful to living creatures, and is discharged to the environment every day. title: OP392 - Status, Distribution, Morphology, and Genetics of Sigmodon fulviventer dalquesti in the Chihuahuan Desert Ecoregion
abstract: The tawny-bellied cotton rat, Sigmodon fulviventer dalquesti, is a Texas endemic subspecies reported only from a collection that occurred in 1991 near the town of Fort Davis in the TransPecos region. The current population, distribution, and evolutionary origin of S. f. dalquesti is enigmatic, and its taxonomic status is uncertain. title: A Risk-Based Safety Resilience Framework for Brownfield Projects
abstract: Brownfield projects combine construction hazards with residual process risk, temporary systems, changing plant states and simultaneous operations. This framework-development paper proposes the Risk-Based Safety Resilience Index (RSRI) as a structure for organizing evidence, not as a validated measure of safety performance. title: Beating and coupling in pulsating stars: A unified Fourier description and observational diagnostics
abstract: Long-term amplitude and phase variations in pulsating stars produce side peaks or multiplets in the Fourier spectrum of the light curves around the pulsation frequency and its harmonics. Such structures are often attributed to modulation, although linear beating and the non-linear coupling of close oscillations can also produce similar patterns. We developed a unified analytical Fourier description of these alternatives and identify observational relations that retain discriminatory power when their frequency patterns overlap. title: Synergistic impact of cotton-legume intercropping and integrated weed management on soil health and productivity
abstract: Cotton is a globally important crop that serves as a major source of fibre and edible oil while supporting millions of livelihoods. With increasing demand for sustainable materials, improving cotton productivity in an eco-friendly way has become essential. One promising approach is the integration of legume intercropping with efficient weed management to reduce the potential yield loss of up to 86 % caused by weed competition. institutions: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University

title: Trichloroethylene and perchloroethylene metabolites have fetal sex-specific RNA expression impacts in a full term placental villous explant model
abstract: Exposure to volatile organic chemicals (VOCs) like trichloroethylene (TCE) and perchloroethylene (PCE) has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes. We conducted an analysis of gene expression responses to the TCE metabolite S-(1,2-dichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine (DCVC) and the PCE metabolite S-(1,2,2-trichlorovinyl)-L-cysteine (TCVC) in placental explants. Explants from placentas with male and female fetuses were treated with either metabolite at 10 μM or 20 μM (n=4). title: Phage genomes are enriched with genes to overcome diverse bacterial immune systems
abstract: Abstract Phages and bacteria are engaged in an evolutionary arms race, where phages continually evolve new strategies to overcome bacterial defenses. To systematically investigate the functions of all genes within phage genomes, we constructed a gene deletion library of the Escherichia coli phage phiDruSM1, belonging to the Queuovirinae subfamily, the Seuratvirus genus, whose morphotype is siphovirus morphology, encompassing 105 open reading frames ( orfs ). By infecting various E. coli clinical isolates with 73 orf knockout phages, we demonstrated that each gene is essential for host range me

title: Assessing the impact of stack degradation and replacement on the levelized cost of hydrogen over multi-decadal horizons
abstract: How progressive stack degradation, replacement timing, and operational flexibility interact over multi-decadal plant lifetimes is not well understood. Project developers therefore rely on ad-hoc lifetime heuristics rather than economically grounded replacement strategies. This work develops a degradation-inclusive levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) optimization methodology that captures hourly electricity price dynamics, progressive efficiency loss, and an ex-post evaluation of stack replacement policies over a 20-year horizon. title: Structure and Biosynthesis of Mangotoxin Produced by the Plant Pathogen Pseudomonas syringae
abstract: Pathogenic bacteria interfere with plant metabolism through specialized metabolites and mechanisms. Mangotoxin was identified in 2003 from Pseudomonas syringae pv. syringae, which causes devastating diseases globally in various crops, including mango. Mangotoxin was found to inhibit arginine biosynthesis in tomato and Escherichia coli; however, its chemical structure remained unknown. We determined the structure of mangotoxin from the native bacterial producer P. syringae to be an alanine-citrulline dipeptide that contains an internal alkyne on citrulline. title: Straw incorporation lowers DGT-labile cadmium despite acidification in polyurethane microplastic-exposed soil
abstract: Straw incorporation may acidify soil and has conventionally been expected to increase cadmium (Cd) mobility, but this response may change in microplastic-affected soils. This study used diffusive gradients in thin films (DGT), diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (DTPA) extraction, and sequential extraction to explore how straw treatment affects soil Cd behavior in the presence of polyurethane (PU) microplastics, while concurrently measuring soil physicochemical properties and plant Cd accumulation. Relative to the PU-only treatment, maize and wheat straw decreased soil pH from 6.5 to 6.0 and 5.

title: Many-to-one mapping of locomotor mode: a case study in the pelvic morphology of two basal hyaenodonts
abstract: Abstract Extant carnivorans are often used as ecological analogs for hyaenodonts because of their similar size and diet. However, it is unclear whether this comparison extends to locomotor mode. Unlike carnivorans, hyaenodonts have relatively short limbs and revolute lumbar articulations. These systematic anatomical differences across clades can skew the results of ecomorphological analyses if only carnivorans are used. title: Place names reflect the adaptation of human to environmental changes: taking the Erhai Lake Basin in China as an example
abstract: Under the global context of climate change, understanding the adaptation mechanisms of human societies to the environment has become a crucial issue for achieving sustainable development goals. The ecological wisdom embedded in traditional knowledge is increasingly valued for addressing environmental changes. This study takes the Erhai Lake Basin in China, as a case to explore the value of toponyms as carriers of local knowledge in revealing environmental changes and human adaptation strategies. Through a systematic analysis of the toponyms and their spatial distribution patterns related to se

title: Physiological and transcriptomic insights into the roles of growth and defense hormones in bermudagrass shade tolerance
abstract: Bermudagrass ( Cynodon dactylon ) is widely used in ecological restoration, soil conservation, industrial landscaping, and potentially bioenergy, ethanol, and biochar production. Shading critically influences bermudagrass growth and survival. However, current knowledge on bermudagrass responses to shade from a hormonal perspective, particularly regarding growth and defense mechanisms, remains limited. We investigated shade responses in bermudagrass with two accessions, shade-tolerant (C792) and shade-sensitive (GZ), through morphological, physiological (hormone profiling by UPLC-MS), and trans
institutions: Institute of Botany, Jiangsu Province and Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Indicator-based assessment of multidimensional vulnerability to multiple hazards in Dollo Ado Woreda, Somali Region, Ethiopia
abstract: Multi-hazard vulnerability is shaped by interacting social, physical, economic, and environmental conditions that vary across livelihood systems. This study assessed multidimensional vulnerability to multiple hazards among pastoral and agropastoral households in Dollo Ado Woreda, Somali Region, Ethiopia, using a cross-sectional mixed-methods design combining a household survey with focus group discussions and key informant interviews. Household-level vulnerability was operationalized using 67 indicators representing social, physical, economic, and environmental dimensions. Principal Component

title: Enhancing Solubility Predictions of Plastic Additives in Depolymerization Solvents Using Quantum Chemical Conformer Analysis and COSMO-RS
abstract: Abstract The success of recycling plastics by means of depolymerization requires the selective purification of regenerated monomers from complex mixtures. This can be assisted by accurate prediction of the phase behavior of large, flexible, and multifunctional additive molecules, which remains a challenge for current thermodynamic models. In this study, the solubility of 11 representative additives and three PET monomers was measured in two common depolymerization solvents, water and ethylene glycol, covering a wide range from practically insoluble (<1 ppm) to 41.6 wt %. title: Seismic Versus Sub‐Seismic Experimental Mirror‐Like Fault Surfaces in Bituminous Dolostones
abstract: Abstract Mirror‐like Surfaces (MSs) are ultra‐polished surfaces frequently found in exhumed seismogenic fault zones in carbonates. They form over a wide range of pressure‐temperature conditions and slip rates, from seismic (≈1 m/s) to sub‐seismic (≈0.1–100 μm/s), reflecting distinct phases of the seismic cycle. Motivated by the abundance of MSs in bituminous dolostones from the Central Apennines (Italy), we performed rotary‐shear experiments at seismic and sub‐seismic slip rates on incohesive samples under water‐dampened and room‐humidity conditions, to determine the conditions favoring MSs fo
journal: Journal of Geophysical Research Solid Earth

title: Victims of rumour: British Channel Islanders under German occupation in the second world war
abstract: After the entry of the United States into the Second World War, American psychologists undertook the first studies of rumour, in which they analysed and defined its social functions in a country at war. But rumours are themselves a useful lens through which to look at the societies which produced them, and in the German-occupied Channel Islands there is an opportunity to gain a much deeper understanding of a wartime society, whose experience of the war was fundamentally different to that of the United Kingdom and the United States. As small as they are, these islands have produced a large body

title: Canada as a clean energy ‘superpower’? Green hydrogen, between deployment and disavowal
abstract: Canada’s potential to generate more renewable energy than it needs has led to visions of it becoming a leader in low-carbon hydrogen. In the Atlantic provinces, this has involved proposals aimed at producing ‘green’ hydrogen and its derivatives, predominantly for export to Europe. Despite trade being a contributor to carbon emissions, green hydrogen offers an alternative vision where trade is used to spur a clean energy transition and decarbonize hard-to-abate industries, driving growth, jobs and investment. While critics expose the contradictions of hydrogen, they often fail to recognize the

title: MORPHOLOGICAL DISAMBIGUATION FOR THE KAZAKH LANGUAGE USING TRANSFORMER-BASED MODELS
abstract: Morphological ambiguity constitutes a significant challenge for natural language processing in agglutinative languages, as a single word form might include many grammatical categories. The Kazakh language features productive suffixation, vowel harmony, and intricate morphophonological patterns, which considerably hinder automatic morphological analysis. This work presents a transformer-based methodology for morphological disambiguation in Kazakh texts, with the objective of identifying the appropriate morphological interpretation of word forms within context. title: Anthropogenic and Geogenic Factors Affecting Groundwater Arsenic and Potential Drinking Water Exposure in the San Luis Valley, Colorado
abstract: Abstract Groundwater arsenic is a serious health threat in many regions with limited surface water drinking supplies. In the San Luis Valley, Colorado, USA, where most residents rely on groundwater for drinking water, elevated groundwater arsenic concentrations (≥5 μg/L) were observed in 19.8% of private wells. Many recent studies have leveraged data science methods to estimate the spatial variability of arsenic at local, regional, and global scales. title: Tandem Synthesis and Photophysical Behavior of Pyrazolo[3,4‐ h ][1,6]naphthyridines: A Theoretical–Experimental Approach
abstract: A microwave‐assisted tandem synthesis of pyrazolo[3,4‐ h ][1,6]naphthyridines bearing substituents with diverse stereoelectronic character (i.e., alkyl, aryl, CN, and MeO) is reported. Products were obtained in good yields by reacting 5‐aroyl‐pyrazolo[3,4‐ b ]pyridines with malononitrile in methanol, where the expected Knoevenagel reaction does not proceed. Instead, a solvent molecule drives a tandem reaction that affords three tricyclic N ‐heteroaromatic compounds. title: Steady-state parameter-space analysis for interpretable fault diagnosis of centrifugal pumps
abstract: This paper investigates a steady-state parameter-space approach for interpretable fault diagnosis of centrifugal pumps under controlled benchmark conditions. The analysis assesses whether physically interpretable coefficients derived from pump head and shaft-torque relations can provide an informative diagnostic representation within the tested steady-state scope. A semi-empirical model is formulated for the pump head and shaft torque, and six trial-wise coefficients are estimated by least squares from repeated steady-state measurements. title: Dung Beetle Functional Response and Dung Removal Rates Along an Altitudinal Gradient in Neotropical Rainforests
abstract: ABSTRACT Dung beetles are a vital component of ecosystems, providing essential ecosystem services. However, the factors that regulate the functional response of dung beetles and dung removal across altitudinal gradients have been scantily explored. Along an altitudinal gradient in rainforests of the Talamanca Cordillera of Costa Rica, we assessed the structure, composition, functional diversity, and dung removal rates of the dung beetle assemblage. title: Identificação de fases deformacionais pré-cambrianas na região de Tejuçuoca - CE
abstract: Apresentamos novos dados obtidos em um levantamento geológico de detalhe realizado em Tejuçuoca-CE. A área de estudo se localiza no domínio Ceará Central, 30km ao sudeste do Arco Magmático Santa Quitéria (AMSQ), onde predominam as rochas do Complexo Canindé do Ceará (Paleoproterozóico) e do Grupo Ceará (Neoproterozóico). title: Evaluation of LiDAR‐based canopy trait estimation in Midwestern row crops
abstract: Abstract Stand count, the number of plants per unit ground area, and leaf area index (LAI), the ratio of leaf area to ground area, are critical traits for crop research but are traditionally measured using labor‐intensive methods. While new sensing technologies are being developed, quantifying improvement in measurement efficiency and data quality, relative to traditional techniques, is lacking. title: La trayectoria de la transición verde en Emiratos Árabes Unidos
abstract: Este artículo analiza la trayectoria de la transición verde en Emiratos Árabes Unidos (EAU), atendiendo a su carácter extractivo o inclusivo y a su estabilidad. Ello es pertinente por la singularidad de las relaciones entre el Estado y la sociedad y su elevada dependencia del petróleo en este país. Se exploran los intereses de distintos actores a favor o en contra de la transición y, en relación con la estabilidad, las dinámicas de poder, la coordinación entre los diferentes actores y sus intereses. title: Attempts to investigate what words trivia experts focus on in quiz questions: Human-AI comparison through “LLM-as-a-judge” approach
abstract: Computational capacity and knowledge of humans are more limited than those of large language models (LLMs). However, in buzzer quizzes, human trivia experts can often identify the correct answer even from insufficient information such as only a few words. Investigating how they can make fast and accurate judgments is expected to highlight new characteristics of human intelligence, but little is known about that. title: Analysis of Surface Deformations in Bursa and Its Surroundings Using the InSAR method
abstract: This study investigates surface deformation in the Bursa region using semi-monthly Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) analysis from both ascending and descending satellite tracks. The cumulative deformation time series reveal widespread and significant subsidence across much of the study area over an observation period of approximately three years. title: Novel highly potent and environmentally benign molluscicides for Pomacea canaliculata control: Discovery, mechanism, and field validation
abstract: The Pomacea canaliculata is a globally invasive freshwater pest that poses significant threats to both agriculture and aquatic ecosystems; however, conventional molluscicides, such as niclosamide, exhibit high toxicity toward non-target organisms, leading to substantial ecological risks. To develop highly potent and environmentally benign molluscicides, we designed and synthesized a series of 15 novel compounds, among which D-1 emerged as the most promising candidate. title: Low-density ablator response to induction plasmatron aerothermal environments
abstract: Abstract The aerothermal response of low-density charring ablators for atmospheric entry is investigated in dissociated air and nitrogen plasmas. NASA’s Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator, and its carbon preform, FiberForm, were subjected to aerothermal environments relevant to Earth and Titan atmospheric entry in the Plasmatron X inductively coupled plasma wind tunnel. The response of these materials across a range of heat fluxes (80–250 W/cm 2 ) and stagnation pressures (1900–7300 Pa) was studied using a combination of in situ imaging and post-test characterizations. title: The parallel mediation role of social entrepreneurship orientation in the nexus between climate change awareness and green entrepreneurial intention: a hybrid PLS-SEM-NCA approach
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how climate change awareness influences green entrepreneurial intention within a developing country context, with a focus on the parallel mediation role of social entrepreneurship orientation (SEO). Empirical data were collected from 426 students across three Ghanaian universities who were actively involved in social enterprise initiatives or had previously launched such ventures. title: How Socio-Cultural Structures Shape Strategies of Climate-Resilient Social Protection Pathways in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
abstract: Low-income households in Sub-Saharan Africa have limited resilience to climate change shocks despite the region's unique socio-cultural support structures. This article explores how socio-cultural structures such as gender norms, social networks, social cohesion, trust, indigenous knowledge, customs and traditions, and cultural values of reciprocity shape climate-resilient social protection pathways among low-income households. journal: Journal of arts, humanities and social science.

title: Mitotic bypass and continued endocycling promote cancer cell survival after genotoxic chemotherapy
abstract: Abstract Genotoxic chemotherapies are central components of the treatment regimen for most cancers but are rarely curative. Drug-tolerant persister cells (DTPs) evade cell death during these treatments by accessing transient adaptive states and can contribute to cancer progression after treatment. Here, we demonstrate that cancer cells can survive genotoxic chemotherapy-induced stress by accessing a DTP state wherein stress-induced bypass of mitosis precipitates continued endocycling which promotes survival by allowing cells to evade mitotic catastrophe and cell death. title: Bibliometric Review on the Role of Microbial Fertilizers in Soil Health Enhancement
abstract: Soil degradation caused by intensive land use (e.g., compaction, acidification, salinization, and continuous cropping obstacles) is a major constraint on the biological function and sustainable productivity of terrestrial agroecosystems. Microbial fertilizers (biofertilizers), which deploy beneficial functional microorganisms, are increasingly considered a promising biotic intervention to improve degraded soils by restoring microbial-driven ecosystem services. title: Coupling Atomic Confinement With CO 2 Pressure for Selective and Stable CO 2 Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical reduction of CO 2 (CO 2 RR) offers a promising route to convert waste carbon into valuable chemical feedstocks while mitigating greenhouse emissions. However, achieving high activity and selectivity in CO 2 RR remains challenging due to the low solubility of CO 2 in aqueous electrolytes and competing hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) that limit efficiency under practical conditions. title: SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in Long COVID: an exploratory randomized phase 2a mechanistic trial
abstract: Abstract Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 has been proposed as a biological driver of Long COVID, a disabling chronic illness with no proven treatments. We conducted an exploratory, placebo-controlled, double-blind, 2:1 randomized mechanistic trial (NCT05877508) of the SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in 36 participants who met the World Health Organization case definition of Long COVID. After baseline characterization, participants received a single infusion and were followed for 360 days. title: Bridging the Gap: An Evaluation of the Philippine National Police-Anti Cybercrime Group and the Community Partnership For Cybercrime Prevention
abstract: This study examined the collaborative efforts between the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) and the community in the prevention of cybercrime. Specifically, it sought to evaluate the nature and effectiveness of their partnership by examining the mechanisms of collaboration, the extent of community participation, and the efficacy of their joint initiatives in mitigating cyber-related risks. journal: International Journal of Multidisciplinary Applied Business and Education Research

title: Effects of Internal Corporate Social Responsibility Activities on Social Performance: The Employee Perspective
abstract: Internal corporate social responsibility (ICSR) has gained recognition as a strategic strategy to enhancing organizational sustainability and employee well-being in recent years. It encompasses employee-centered policies like empowerment, diversity, skill development, job stability, a positive work atmosphere, and work-life balance. These programs are thought to improve social performance by encouraging long-term dedication and positive workplace behavior. However, there is no empirical data on how ICSR affects social performance from the viewpoint of employees in the Nepalese corporate sector

title: 32-bit SPI interface design between Texas Instruments MCU and Intel FPGA enabling real-time intelligent control applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) communication system between a Texas Instruments TMS320F28335 Microcontroller Unit (MCU) and an Intel Altera Cyclone V 5CSEMA5F31C6N Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). The system demonstrates high-speed, reliable, full-duplex communication between heterogeneous processing platforms for real-time intelligent control and embedded system applications. title: Functional–Taxonomic Scaling Resolves Conflicting Average Genome Size Estimates Across Environmental Gradients
abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. Here, we introduce and validate a framework that adjudicates conflicting AGS estimates by testing which estimate yields a gap between scaled functional diversity and scaled taxonomic diversity that is consistent with the expected positive association between genome size and gene functional breadth. title: Debt relief as climate policy: the role of personal insolvency law
abstract: Abstract Climate impacts extend beyond physical destruction to include widespread financial distress. This article explores the role that debt relief policies – particularly personal insolvency or bankruptcy law – might play within a range of measures to raise the capacity of individuals to withstand climate-related shocks. Through the cancellation of unpayable debt, personal insolvency acts as a form of insurance against the unavoidable risks inherent in a volatile and unpredictable economy. title: Mutant ASXL1 Cooperates with MECOM and BRD4 to Drive Transcriptional Dysregulation in Human Hematopoiesis
abstract: Mutations in the epigenetic regulator ASXL1 are common in myeloid malignancies and portend a near-universally poor prognosis. While multiple mechanisms for mutant ASXL1-dependent oncogenesis have been proposed, none have been functionally validated in the context of the human hematopoietic stem cell, where these mutations almost certainly arise. Here, we extensively characterized a CRISPR-engineered human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell model of ASXL1 mutations. title: Behaviour of the Eurasian otter at latrines along a gradient of anthropogenic landscape context
abstract: Abstract Increasing human pressure on fluvial ecosystems can alter wildlife behaviour, particularly where human activities modify habitat structure and the conditions under which behaviours are expressed at key communication sites. In this study, we examined how environmental and proxies of anthropogenic variables influence behavioural expression of the Eurasian otter Lutra lutra at latrine sites, which function as key locations for chemical communication. title: Harnessing Potential: A Systematic Investigation of How and Why Learning Happens in a Health System
abstract: ABSTRACT Background The ability to learn is central to innovation and performance across industries, and it is the hallmark feature of the rapidly growing movement toward Learning Health Systems. While learning drivers—such as experimentation, risk‐taking, participative decision‐making, dialogue, and interaction with the external environment—are well defined, they have received little attention in healthcare contexts. title: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer
abstract: Abstract Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a sensitive, noninvasive tool for monitoring the genomic landscape, heterogeneity, and evolution of cancer, aggregating genetic information from multiple metastatic sites. Here, we study 15,564 cfDNA samples from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer (MBC). We classify samples, deep-sequenced with Guardant360, into MBC subtypes using our trained random forest model. title: Nocturnal Lepidoptera Larvae in Mega‐Project: Habitat and Environmental Factors Over Construction Effects
abstract: Mega-projects are large-scale developments that profoundly transform landscapes while delivering infrastructure and socio-economic benefits. However, they are also major drivers of biodiversity loss through multiple direct and indirect impacts. Among these, artificial light at night (ALAN) is increasingly recognised as a threat to biodiversity, including nocturnal Lepidoptera, which play crucial ecological roles. title: Las tecnologías de la información como espacios de deliberación para los mecanismos de participación ciudadana en México
abstract: A partir de los hallazgos de la investigación doctoral del autor, el texto plantea que las herramientas de la democracia participativa pueden ayudar a que el actuar del Estado se dirija hacia el desarrollo de ciertos derechos o principios constitucionales. La opinión vertida en el ensayo es que la deliberación democrática se logra mediante la discusión ciudadana en espacios públicos y podría contribuir a que las soluciones que se propongan adquieran una mayor legitimidad democrática, bajo el argumento de que las instituciones del Estado deben ajustarse para integrar la deliberación democrática

title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Exposes Conserved Antimicrobial Resistance Elements and Diverse Secretion Systems in Serratia proteamaculans
abstract: Serratia proteamaculans is an environmentally widespread member of the genus Serratia isolated from aquatic animals, food products, plants, insects, environmental habitats and clinical sources. Ecologically broadly distributed, little is known about its genomic diversity and factors associated with antimicrobial resistance and virulence. The present study reports a comparative genomic analysis of 38 publicly available S. proteamaculans genomes to explore genomic diversity, antimicrobial resistance determinants, integrons, and bacterial secretion systems.
