title: Occupational branches of Japan’s ruling party: building linkages while hedging clientelist exposure
abstract: Abstract Reassessing the underappreciated grassroots of Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), I argue that the party’s localized institutions not only mobilize votes but also mitigate the risks of clientelism. Informed by field research and relying on documentary evidence, descriptive statistics, and financial records, I identify mechanisms that link the party to citizens, even in the periphery. Such mechanisms have received too little scholarly attention due to persisting notions that membership in the LDP is spurious and that the party’s local linkages are weak or narrowly transactional. title: Sustainable cotton fabric-based microfluidic platform for smartphone-assisted flow characterization and colorimetric iron detection
abstract: Increasing need of low-cost and portable analytical devices have motivated search for inexpensive materials as substrates for performing chemical assays. In this study, fabric-based microfluidic platform was developed using cotton substrate through a facile patterned cutting-based fabrication method for smartphone assisted colorimetric detection of iron in water. Both the spot-test and flow-test device configurations were designed without relying on sophisticated instruments. title: How can digital media be studied in times of information deluge? The TUCANO methodological protocol applied to documentary research on online news
abstract: Este artigo apresenta o TUCANO (Técnicas Unificadas de Categorização e Análise de Notícias Online), protocolo metodológico híbrido para análise de corpora de notícias online em português. Desenvolvido para enfrentar um desafio das amostragens não probabilísticas em Ciências Sociais, o TUCANO busca delimitar, organizar e explorar conjuntos de notícias sem perder a densidade interpretativa da análise qualitativa. title: Brechas de interoperabilidad y adopción de salud digital en los establecimientos sanitarios del Perú
abstract: The digital transformation of the Peruvian healthcare system faces challenges relating to interoperability, infrastructure, connectivity and training, which limit the secure and timely exchange of clinical information. The coexistence of incompatible platforms between the Ministry of Health (MINSA), EsSalud, the Armed Forces, the National Police and the private sector fragments care, hinders longitudinal patient follow-up and contributes to the duplication of tests, diagnostic delays, clinical errors and administrative overload. title: Determination of yield and plant part ratios of some silage maize varieties under Kahramanmaraş conditions
abstract: Silage maize (Zea mays L.) yields high biomass and fermentable carbohydrates per unit area, so it is the primary forage crop in ruminant livestock systems across Türkiye. Cultivar performance varies by location, and yield data for Kahramanmaras are limited. This study compared four silage maize cultivars (DKC7240, 30B74, Colonia, Gladius) for morphological traits, green forage yield, and plant part ratios over the 2024 and 2025 growing seasons in Kahramanmaras. title: Seasonal shifts in the daily vocal activity of a nocturnal tropical bird, the great eared nightjar ( Lyncornis macrotis )
abstract: Abstract Many tropical birds occupy permanent territories and use vocalizations for year-round defense, yet they typically exhibit a seasonal peak in vocal activity associated with breeding. abstract: We investigate the cross-sectional pricing of the exposure to pollution news for individual stocks. abstract: Rodent control in urban areas is an important public health measure, among other reasons, for their capacity of harboring several zoonotic pathogens. Efficient, evidence-based control programs must consider both rodent and pathogen ecology, to achieve both rodent population and pathogen transmission risk reduction. title: Overwintering Strategies Drive Climate Change Impacts on Body Mass in Northern Mammals
abstract: Climate change drives variable shifts in mammalian body sizes, yet the mechanisms underlying this variation remain unclear. Two explanations prevail: (1) higher temperatures reduce thermal constraints, favouring smaller bodies; or (2) warming enhances primary productivity, supporting larger bodies. abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based hydrogels in previous research demonstrated as promising biomimetic scaffolds. abstract: The recent spread of wolves into highly human-modified landscapes in Europe is an important example of large carnivore recovery and illustrates their ability to live in environments very different from those usually considered suitable for the species. This study aimed to evaluate how wolf feeding habits vary over time and across space by comparing diet composition, trophic niche breadth, and key prey consumption between the historical Apennine range and the recently colonized Po Plain in north-western Italy, based on scat samples collected between 2021 and 2025. abstract: El cambio climático plantea desafíos significativos para la gestión sostenible de los recursos hídricos, particularmente en países en desarrollo donde las capacidades institucionales y normativas suelen ser limitadas. abstract: Introduction In a social dominance hierarchy, dominant and subordinate individuals can exhibit dramatic differences in behavioral, physiological, and neural phenotypes. abstract: Catamaran sailing and windsurfing are nature-based sports that require physical risk-taking, balance, attention, and endurance. We analyzed interactions between wolves and red foxes Vulpes vulpes at red deer Cervus elaphus carcasses in the Stelvio National Park (Italian Alps). abstract: The development of advanced coolant media is increasingly important for improving thermal regulation in proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks while addressing concerns related to material use, operational durability, and environmental sustainability. abstract: Existing camouflaged object detection (COD) models are computationally demanding, which limits their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. abstract: This study examines the strategic dilemmas posed by China's global rise for the European Union (EU). In this context, it focuses on how Europe balances its geopolitical autonomy with protecting its economic interests in the face of China. The theoretical framework is based on realism and liberalism approaches, and also analyzed from a structuralist perspective emphasizing the EU's identity construction and normative aspects. title: An improved approach for rainfall-runoff simulation under anthropogenic influence
abstract: Human activities significantly influence the rainfall-runoff process, leading to pronounced fluctuations in runoff data and presenting substantial challenges for accurate simulation. In this study, the Water Allocation and Simulation (WAS) model was adopted and enhanced to simulate rainfall-runoff under the impact of human activities. title: Calibration using downscaled and bias-corrected satellite soil-moisture data can improve watershed model representation of soil-moisture variability
abstract: Watershed streamflow is often the focus of hydrological model calibration and evaluation, despite other potential objectives, including water quality management, flood protection, or agricultural management. When hydrological models are calibrated on streamflow, intermediate processes such as those affecting soil-moisture are not necessarily well represented. abstract: ABSTRACT Organoselenophosphates and tellurophosphates represent important structural motifs in organochalcogenophosphorus chemistry and exhibit unique electronic properties, distinctive biological activities, and versatile synthetic utility. This review provides a systematic overview of recent methodological advances in the synthesis of these two classes of compounds, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic features of key transformations. title: Influence of black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.) larval frass manure on plant growth, soil health and economics of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.)
abstract: Black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.; BSF) larval frass has recently been considered a superior organic nutrient source for sustainable crop production because of its balanced nutrient content, which facilitates the conversion of organic waste into effective fertiliser that enhances residue recycling. The present study aimed to compare the effects of BSF larval frass, vermicompost, farmyard manure (FYM) and chemical fertilisers on the growth, yield, soil health and economics of sunflower (Helianthus annus L.) during the rabi season of 2024–25 at the College Farm, Agricultural College, Jagti

abstract: Cette étude approfondit l’analyse des facteurs de vulnérabilité des populations aux maladies d’origine hydrique dans la ville de Kenge, chef-lieu de la province du Kwango, en République Démocratique du Congo. En s’appuyant sur des données de surveillance sanitaire collectées sur une période de dix ans (2016-2025) dans cinq aires de santé, la recherche identifie la diarrhée, la typhoïde et la dysenterie comme les pathologies dominantes. abstract: The northern Eastern Cordillera (EC) in the Colombian Andes is a high-elevation subduction-related orogenic plateau above a flattened subduction zone. Previous constraints on crustal thickness have shown a shift from a thickened central region (~50–65 km) to a thinner northern part (~40–55 km). title: A bacterial pangenome association study identifies a role for polyamine metabolism and alkaline tolerance in middle ear infections
abstract: Infection of the middle ear, or otitis media (OM), is a disease that commonly afflicts children, and Haemophilus influenzae is the most prevalent OM-associated bacterium. We sought new insights into mechanisms of pathogenesis by identifying bacterial genes associated with OM disease. We whole-genome sequenced >200 clinical isolates collected over time from 9 healthy and 12 OM-prone children. abstract: Abstract Intracontinental deformation records how early Eocene India–Asia collisional stress propagated into continental interiors. title: A (p,q,r)-spherical fuzzy CODAS framework for sustainable crop selection in agriculture
abstract: Crop selection is an important decision problem in precision agriculture and sustainable farm management, particularly in environmentally diverse and climate-sensitive regions. This paper proposes a (p,q,r)-spherical fuzzy ((p,q,r)-SF) extension of the combinative distance-based assessment (CODAS) method for evaluating crop alternatives under uncertain expert judgments. title: Species interactions, not Richness: How does long-term pastoral land use alter Mediterranean mammal communities?
abstract: Abstract Pastoralism, a common land use worldwide, plays a significant ecological role in Mediterranean ecosystems, where it has been present for millennia. However, its long-term effects on mammal communities, community composition, and interspecific interactions are not fully understood. We carried out a camera-trap study at four nature reserves in northern Israel, comparing medium-sized mammal communities between paired grazed (pastoral) and non-pastoral habitats. title: HeaTrace: A Parametric Design‐to‐Fabrication Workflow for Thermally Programmable Soft Robots
abstract: Inspired by the multifunctional bodies of natural organisms, soft robotic systems are advancing toward integrated body architectures that combine shape change, tunable compliance, and visual feedback within compact, material‐embedded structures. Thermal actuation provides a viable route to this multifunctionality by locally delivering heat from embedded Joule heaters to thermoresponsive materials. title: Hybrid Renewable Energy Supply System for Remote Villages of Grid in Madagascar Using Linear Programming by Simplex Method and Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper details the development of a linear model to optimize the sizing of a hybrid renewable energy supply system (HRESS) for remote rural villages in developing countries. The model studied is defined by its energy supply versatility to rural household consumers. It includes electrical energy, thermal energy for cooking, and also muscular energy used for transport and manual work related to the HRESS and agriculture. abstract: Raman spectra of RNA nucleotide strands extracted from 20 SARS-CoV-2 strains, including the original Japanese isolate, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Lambda, Theta, Mu, and 12 Omicron subvariants, were systematically collected, deconvoluted, and converted into Raman barcodes. title: Meta-transcriptomic profiling of Ixodes ricinus and Ixodes persulcatus ticks from Finland reveals diverse RNA viromes, community structuring, and emerging viral lineages
abstract: Tick-borne viruses (TBVs) threaten human and animal health in northern Europe, where Ixodes ricinus and Ixodes persulcatus are expanding their range. In Finland, the genetic diversity, population structure, and tick-associated RNA virome of these species remain insufficiently characterized. Characterizing tick-borne viruses in Finland is essential to detect emerging pathogens at the northern edge of tick expansion, where climate-driven ecological change may facilitate the spread of novel viruses with potential risks to human and animal health. title: Military Discourse during the Gaza War via Digital Platforms: A Comparative Analytical Study of Palestinian Resistance and Israeli Military Discourse
abstract: This study aims to identify the nature of military-media discourse circulated on digital platforms during the Gaza war and its impact on international relations, through a comparative analytical study of the speeches of the Palestinian resistance spokesperson (Abu Ubeida) and the Israeli army spokesperson (Daniel Hagari). The study belongs to descriptive research and employs the survey method based on content analysis of a sample of 40 military speeches: 17 by the resistance spokesperson and 23 by the Israeli army spokesperson, from Oct. 7, 2023, to early January 2024. title: Comparative niche modelling identifies conservation and cultivation opportunities for two Harpagophytum species in southern Africa
abstract: Overharvesting of wild medicinal plants is a major driver of biodiversity loss, particularly in semi-arid regions of southern Africa where commercially valuable species such as Harpagophytum procumbens (Burch.) DC. ex Meisn. and Harpagophytum zeyheri Decne. are extensively harvested. title: Canopy functional composition as an indicator of bird traits, taxonomy, and vulnerability in tropical Peruvian forests
abstract: Tropical forests harbour exceptional biodiversity, yet anthropogenic change is rapidly altering forest composition and structure in ways that shape species' ecological strategies and persistence. While advances in remote sensing now allow detailed characterisation of canopy function, links between forest functional diversity and animal traits remain poorly understood. abstract: This study analyzes survivor exporters – firms that export continuously every year – in shaping Türkiye's intensive and extensive export margins from 2011 to 2022. abstract: Rubia cordifolia L. is an important Himalayan medicinal plant valued for its diverse therapeutic properties. The present study investigated the influence of altitude, habitat conditions, and edaphic factors on nutritional composition, phytochemicals, and antioxidant activity of R. cordifolia populations collected from different habitats (open grassy, shady, and moist shady) in the western Himalaya. abstract: In this article, we examine the nexus of Southern African community newspapers’ sceptical AI integration and grassroots democracy. The sceptical approach to AI integration in marginalised media markets of Southern African community newspapers’ news ecosystems is interrogated. title: Human behaviour in wildfire emergencies: insights from evacuation decision-making and timing across Canada, Australia, and the United States
abstract: Wildfires often require rapid evacuation to save lives, leading residents to make quick and context-specific transportation decisions that may differ across countries and cultures. This study examines intended evacuation behaviours during wildfires, focusing on promptness, departure time, and cross-country differences. title: Analysis of annual honey production in Kenya as influenced by weather parameters and atmospheric constituents
abstract: The contribution of weather parameters and atmospheric constituents on honey production in Kenya is little understood. We studied the influence of average national diurnal 2-m temperature range, consecutive dry days, summer days, daytime relative humidity, night-time relative humidity, precipitation rate, number of days with precipitation, surface buoyancy, surface wind speed, Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) and soil moisture content, on annual honey harvest. title: A comparative multi-criteria decision analysis framework for strategic energy storage investments: From data to decisions
abstract: Energy storage is increasingly recognised as a critical enabler of Europe’s clean energy transition, yet Member States display heterogeneous levels of readiness to integrate and scale storage solutions. This study introduces the Investment Planning Tool, a multi-criteria, interactive decision-support framework designed to evaluate alternatives under diverse uncertainty levels, weighting schemes, and behavioural profiles. abstract: Accurate prediction and classification of transportation-related metrics such as CO 2 emissions and road fatalities are vital for sustainable urban planning and public safety. Using data from 30 major Chinese cities, this study introduces a comprehensive methodology that integrates the XGBoost algorithm with 16 distinct metaheuristic optimization techniques to compare algorithms performance in both regression and classification tasks. title: Heterogeneity in cancer: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies
abstract: Cancer heterogeneity drives therapeutic failure, resistance, and relapse and encompasses variation across genetic, cellular, tissue, organ, and systemic scales. Existing frameworks define malignant capabilities and tumor-microenvironment interactions but less explicitly address how heterogeneity propagates across scales and informs therapeutic design. abstract: El presente estudio examina las brechas de género en la producción científica y en la composición de los comités editoriales de revistas chilenas de ingeniería y matemáticas indexadas en Scopus durante el período 2014–2023. abstract: Estudiar los territorios de las aves permite conocer sus requerimientos y la limitación de sus poblaciones. abstract: Flowers are expected to exhibit lower trait variability than vegetative traits, thereby enhancing precise pollination and reproductive success, especially in self-incompatible species that rely on cross-pollination. This is particularly important in distylous plants, which have two co-dependent flower morphs with reciprocal positioning of sexual structures (L- and S-morph). abstract: Abstract In descriptions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), companies often anthropomorphise their innovations by attributing human-associated characteristics or capabilities to them, e.g. intelligence, understanding or reasoning. I argue that anthropomorphism can become a structuring part of sociotechnical imaginaries—visions of desirable futures attainable through advances in science and technology. title: Global patterns of disaster-related injuries: A 50-year epidemiological analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective This research aims to identify the global epidemiological profile of disaster-related injuries over the last 50 years and examine their distribution across natural, technological, and human-caused disasters. title: Llamadas repetitivas en la Ratona Común Sudamericana: la información codificada en el número y tasa de repetición de los llamados de alarma
abstract: Las aves frecuentemente utilizan señales acústicas de alarma para alertar a co- y heterospecíficos de la presencia cercana de una amenaza. Los emisores pueden usar una señal única o largas secuencias de llamados repetitivos las cuales pueden producir un efecto sostenido en el comportamiento de los receptores de la señal. title: The Strait of Hormuz and the Geopolitics of Energy Security: International Relations Implications of the US-Iran Conflict
abstract: The Strait of Hormuz is a vital strategic chokepoint within the global energy system due to its geographical position and the substantial quantity of oil and natural gas transported through it. Its importance to international energy supplies also makes it susceptible to geopolitical tensions, especially conflicts between states with competing strategic and national interests. title: Role of Extracellular Vesicles in Shaping Immune Responses in the Lymph Node Microenvironment
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EV) secreted by living cells are important players in cell-to-cell communication, particularly in the diffuse immune system, where they contribute to local and systemic coordination. title: Innovation and economic performance in the EU: an integrated framework for analysis
abstract: Innovations are important for the economic growth, but such impact varies significantly across regions and the EU countries. Existing researches often adopt a sectoral perspective, overlooking the long- term effects of innovations and the need for a comprehensive framework to measure its influence on GDP. abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of large language model (LLM)-powered value-integrated story cards in English vocabulary instruction using a convergent mixed methods design with 30 sixth-grade middle school students over a four-week intervention. Story cards embedding universal values (empathy, responsibility, honesty, and cooperation) were developed via systematic prompt engineering with GPT-4, a generative AI (GenAI) tool, reviewed by domain experts, and applied within a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design. abstract: Cyclobutane‐fused heterocycles represent a distinctive class of structurally constrained scaffolds with significant relevance in natural products and medicinal chemistry. abstract: Abstract Predicted climate change will cause higher temperatures, less rainfall, and aridification of the most extensive tropical dry forest region in South America (Caatinga) as this century progresses. abstract: Abstract This article examines how the Common Concern of Humankind (CCH), developed in international environmental law, can inform transboundary digital governance. title: Revelando un patrón complejo de variación del canto en Zonotrichia capensis australis en el este de Patagonia
abstract: La subespecie patagónica del Chingolo (Zonotrichia capensis australis) es la más diferenciada morfológicamente, careciendo de líneas negras en su corona. Estudios en el noreste de Patagonia mostraron que los cantos carecen de trino e incluyen un pretema, pero recientemente mostramos que esto no ocurre en el sudeste patagónico. Para estudiar la variación vocal en el este de Patagonia, grabamos y analizamos los cantos de alrededor de 500 Chingolos desde Santa Rosa (provincia de La Pampa) hasta el Parque Nacional Monte León (provincia de Santa Cruz). title: Assessing the deviation in building energy performance predicted by historical typical weather files from recent local climates
abstract: Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data are widely used in building energy simulations but may no longer represent current urban climate conditions under climate change. title: Multi-scale drivers shape bird taxonomic and functional diversity in Mediterranean urban forests
abstract: Abstract Urban green spaces provide critical habitat and support biodiversity within cities, and birds serve as sensitive bioindicators of environmental quality. Identifying which urban drivers most strongly affect biodiversity is essential for planning resilient and eco-friendly cities. This study aimed to identify the relative contribution of local forest and landscape-scale factors in shaping taxonomic and functional dimensions of urban bird diversity, and to determine whether different biodiversity components respond to environmental drivers operating at different spatial scales. title: Analysis of drought carry-over effect on apple trees using the Leafiness-LiDAR index
abstract: Apple trees ( Malus × domestica Borkh.) are widely grown in Mediterranean regions, where drought-induced irrigation restrictions can impair canopy development and productivity. title: Integration of the D‐Genome Reshapes Gene Transcription, Chromatin Architecture, and Metabolome of Allohexaploid Wheat, Leading to Enhanced Environmental Adaptability
abstract: The hybridization-led integration of the D-genome into domesticated tetraploid wheat gave rise to allohexaploid wheat, the most cultivated wheat globally grown across diverse environmental conditions. However, the regulatory mechanisms by which this genomic integration confers increased environmental adaptability in allohexaploid remains largely unexplored. title: Onboard Vision and MPC Navigation for Underwater Robots: An Open BlueROV2 Platform for Multi-Robot Experiments & Docking
abstract: Autonomous underwater robots require robust perception, estimation and control to operate in confined environments. This paper presents an open-source BlueROV2 platform combining onboard vision with nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) for autonomous navigation and docking. The platform integrates an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX and an Intel RealSense D435i stereo camera in a modular pressure housing. title: SeA-RVINS: Semantic-Aware Tightly Coupled RTK-Visual-Inertial System with Correlation-Preserving Robust Estimation for Urban Navigation
abstract: Reliable absolute pose estimation in urban environments is undermined by outlier measurements and incorrect temporal associations that can persist in tightly coupled estimators. Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations provide globally referenced measurements but are prone to multipath effects. Visual-inertial sensing supplies local motion constraints, but false visual associations can corrupt the estimator. title: H-SPAR: Hydrodynamic-aware Simulation for Particle Transport and Autonomous Robots
abstract: Environmental robotic sampling requires considering the dual influence of water currents on robotic motion and particle transport. Existing marine robotics simulators generally model flow, autonomy, and sampling targets separately, limiting joint evaluation of mission cost and sampling performance. H-SPAR integrates spatially and temporally varying velocity fields, Lagrangian particle transport, probabilistic sampling, and ROS 2/Gazebo-based uncrewed surface vehicle (USV) autonomy. title: Resummation-scale uncertainties in PDF determinations
abstract: We investigate the impact of resummation-scale variations on parton distribution function (PDF) determinations. These variations introduce an additional source of theoretical uncertainty related to the evolution of PDFs and strong coupling $α_s$ that has never previously been accounted for in PDF fits. Using the open-source xFitter framework, we quantify this uncertainty in fits to HERA deep-inelastic scattering data and examine its implications for predictions of top-quark pair production at the LHC. title: Phoenix: A Modular and Versatile Framework for C/C++ Pointer Analysis
abstract: We present Phoenix, a modular pointer analysis framework for C/C++ that unifies multiple alias analysis algorithms behind a single, stable interface. Phoenix addresses the fragmentation of today’s C/C++ pointer analysis ecosystem by cleanly separating IR construction, constraint generation, solver backends, and client-facing queries—making analyses easy to compare, swap, and compose while exposing explicit precision–performance trade-offs. title: Omnidirectional Amphibious Locomotion via Internal Mass Actuation
abstract: Field robots must traverse varied terrain and obstacles while remaining robust to water, debris, vegetation, and physical contact. We present MARBLE, a fully enclosed omnidirectional amphibious rolling robot driven entirely by internal mass redistribution. Three mutually orthogonal linear sliders shift internal masses to generate body rotation, while an orientation-aware controller maps planar velocity commands into slider positions. title: Phase diagram morphology shapes droplet propulsion in chemical gradients
abstract: Droplets in complex environments often encounter compositional gradients that drive their propulsion. For example, surfactant gradients induce surface-tension-driven propulsion via the Marangoni effect. Here, we show that such propulsion emerges generically, even in the absence of surfactants. title: A Quasi-Direct-Drive Underactuated Asymmetric Hand for Dexterous and Efficient Grasping and Manipulation
abstract: In this paper, we present the Berkeley QUAD (Quasi-direct-drive, Underactuated, Asymmetric Design) Hand, a four-finger anthropomorphic robotic hand with 11 degrees of freedom and 8 degrees of actuation. The design utilizes QDD actuation at the base of each finger, enabling high force transparency for dexterous, adaptive performance. However, the low torque density of these actuators traditionally presents major issues with size, weight, and thermal limits. title: The LZ event with a two-state dark matter halo
abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a single nuclear-recoil candidate at $E_R \simeq 248$keV. LZ interprets it in terms of inelastic dark matter that scatters endothermically from its ground state, $χ_1 N \to χ_2 N$. In pseudo-Dirac models the excited state $χ_2$ can survive to the present day, and exothermic scattering, $χ_2 N \to χ_1 N$, is then also open. The published LZ intervals do not describe this case. title: Design and Validation of an Antagonistic Tendon-Driven Dexterous Robotic Hand with Bidirectional Operation
abstract: Dexterous robotic hands typically reproduce human hand morphology but inherit its one-sided grasping workspace, requiring wrist or arm reorientation to grasp from the opposite side. Existing reversible hands generally rely on non-anthropomorphic, soft, or task-specific finger arrangements, whereas conventional five-digit anthropomorphic hands remain designed primarily for palmar-side grasping. title: Life-time patterns of reinfections: epidemic cohorts as traveling waves
abstract: Infectious disease models that allow for reinfection, such as the SIS or SIRS frameworks, typically treat all infections as exchangeable and independent, erasing the temporal structure of individual reinfection histories. Here, we introduce a minimal "chain SIR" model that resolves this limitation by indexing compartments by reinfection count and allowing transmission, recovery, and waning rates to depend on that count. title: Cosserat Modeling of Trimmed Helicoid Soft Arms with a Separated-Section Constitutive Law
abstract: Cosserat rod models for soft robots usually construct sectional stiffness by summing material properties over a common cross-section. This assumption becomes inaccurate for trimmed helicoid arms, where load-bearing helix domains are separated and connected only through sparse fused crossings. This paper formulates a separated-section constitutive law that evaluates each helix domain in its local frame and pulls its constitutive response back to the backbone, yielding an effective backbone stiffness. title: Heavy Inert Doublet Reconciles LZ and IceCube
abstract: We show that the inert doublet dark matter can reconcile the purported LZ direct detection signal and IceCube constraints. The preferred dark matter mass is 11.3--20.3~TeV, an order of magnitude heavier than the standard higgsino target. The smaller number density at a high mass can reproduce the LZ event given the exponential sensitivity to the velocity, while suppressing the capture rate in the Sun because of the higher infall velocity. title: The Canonical Parallel Form as a Substrate for Parallelizing Compilers and Agentic Optimizers
abstract: Imperative code fixes an execution order the computation does not require, and a parallelizing compiler must prove which parts of that order it can remove.
